questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A YOUNG FEMALE COMES TO THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT AFTER INGESTING 10 TABLETS OF
PHENOBARBITAL. WHICH OF THESE COMPONENTS OF THE ETC IS INHIBITED BY THIS DRUG?
questions.explanation:
PHENOBARBITAL IS A BARBITURATE THAT INHIBITS COMPLEX I TO Q OF THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN.
COMPLEX I OF THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN IS NADH-Q OXIDOREDUCTASE. IT OXIDIZES NADH AND
REDUCES COENZYME Q. PHENOBARBITAL INHIBITS COMPLEX I TO Q SO THAT THE ELECTRONS WILL NOT BE ABLE
TO BE TRANSFERRED FROM NADH TO COENZYME Q, WHICH IS THE FIRST STEP IN THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT
CHAIN. AS A RESULT, THE RATE OF OXYGEN CONSUMPTION WILL DECREASE.
THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (ETC) REPRESENTS THE FINAL PATHWAY THROUGH WHICH ELECTRONS,
ORIGINATING FROM THE OXIDATION OF CARBOHYDRATES, FATTY ACIDS, AND AMINO ACIDS, ARE CHANNELED
TOWARD A FINAL REACTION WITH OXYGEN TO PRODUCE WATER AND ATP. THE ETC COMPLEXES ARE EMBEDDED
IN THE INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE.
THE OXIDATION OF COMPOUNDS BY ETC COMPLEXES LEADS TO THE RELEASE OF FREE ENERGY. THIS IS USED TO
PUMP H+ TO THE INTERMEMBRANE SPACE. THIS RESULTS IN THE FORMATION OF A PROTON MOTIVE FORCE THAT
IS USED FOR THE PHOSPHORYLATION OF ADP TO ATP. THUS, OXIDATION IS COUPLED WITH PHOSPHORYLATION
TO GENERATE ATP. NADH GENERATES 2.5 ATP AND FADH2 GENERATES 1.5 ATP.
THE TABLE BELOW SUMMARIZES THE INHIBITORS OF THE ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN.
965
COMPLEXES OF ETC INHIBITORS

UCTASE
PIERICIDIN A,PHENOBARBITAL, R
OTENONE

CTASE
TTFA (THENOYLTRIFLUOROACETON
E), CARBOXIN, MALONATE
COMPLEX III:Q- CYT C OXIDORE
DUCTASE
BAL (BRITISH ANTI-LEWISITE), A
NTIMYCIN A
COMPLEX IV:CYT C OXIDASE HYDROGEN SULFIDE, CARBON MO
NOXIDE, CYANIDE
COMPLEX V:ATP SYNTHASE ATRACTYLOSIDE, OLIGOMYCIN

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A CHILD PRESENTS TO YOU WITH BONE PAIN, HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY, AND PANCYTOPENIA. A TREPHINE
BIOPSY ASPIRATE SHOWS THE FOLLOWING FINDING. WHICH OF THESE IS THE MOST LIKELY ENZYME
DEFICIENT IN THE PATIENT DESCRIBED?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF A CHILD WITH BONE PAIN, HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY, AND TREPHINE BIOPSY
SHOWING GAUCHER'S CELL WITH A CHARACTERISTIC CRUMPLED TISSUE PAPER APPEARANCE IS SUGGESTIVE OF
GAUCHER'S DISEASE. THE DEFICIENT ENZYME IS GLUCOCEREBROSIDASE (ALSO KNOWN AS BETA-GLUCOSIDASE).
GAUCHER'S DISEASE IS AN INBORN ERROR OF METABOLISM CAUSED DUE TO A DEFICIENCY OF
BETA-GLUCOCEREBROSIDASE. IT IS THE MOST COMMON LYSOSOMAL STORAGE DISORDER AND THE MODE OF
INHERITANCE IS AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE. THERE IS AN ACCUMULATION OF LIPID-LADEN MACROPHAGES IN THE
SPLEEN, LIVER, AND OTHER TISSUES.
THERE ARE THREE CLINICAL SUBTYPES - TYPE I (CHRONIC NON-NEURONOPATHIC), TYPE II (ACUTE
NEURONOPATHIC), AND TYPE III (INTERMEDIATE). CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE ANEMIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA,
HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY, AND NEUROLOGICAL FEATURES DEPENDING ON THE SUBTYPE.
GAUCHER'S CELLS ARE FORMED AS A RESULT OF THE ACCUMULATION OF MASSIVE AMOUNTS OF
GLUCOCEREBROSIDES WITHIN THE PHAGOCYTES. THE CELLS HAVE A FIBRILLARY CYTOPLASM AND GIVE A CRUMPLED
TISSUE PAPER APPEARANCE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A 32-YEAR-OLD LADY COMES WITH COMPLAINTS OF ERYTHEMATOUS SCALY RASH, LOOSE STOOLS, AND
COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION. THE RASH INVOLVED HER FOREARM, NECK, AND FACE. SHE SEEMS TO HAVE
DIFFICULTY REMEMBERING THINGS FROM THE RECENT PAST. HER ELECTROLYTES ARE WITHIN NORMAL RANGE.
SHE ADMITS TO HAVING SHIFTED TO A CORN-BASED DIET DUE TO ECONOMIC REASONS. WHICH OF THESE WOULD IMPROVE HER SYMPTOMS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL FEATURES SUGGESTS THE DIAGNOSIS OF PELLAGRA, DUE TO HER CORN-BASED DIET. ORAL
NICOTINAMIDE SUPPLEMENTS CAN IMPROVE HER SYMTPOMS.
NIACIN CAN BE SYNTHESIZED IN THE BODY FROM TRYPTOPHAN. TWO COMPOUNDS, NICOTINIC ACID AND
NICOTINAMIDE, HAVE THE BIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY OF NIACIN. THE NICOTINAMIDE RING OF THE COENZYMES
NICOTINAMIDE ADENINE DINUCLEOTIDE (NAD) AND NICOTINAMIDE ADENINE DINUCLEOTIDE PHOSPHATE
(NADP) PARTICIPATE IN OXIDATION/REDUCTION REACTIONS.
THE INITIAL SYMPTOMS OF PELLAGRA INCLUDE LOSS OF APPETITE, GENERALIZED WEAKNESS, IRRITABILITY,
ABDOMINAL PAIN, AND VOMITING. THIS IS FOLLOWED BY BRIGHT RED GLOSSITIS AND A CHARACTERISTIC
PIGMENTED, SCALY SKIN RASH IN SUN-EXPOSED AREAS. THIS RASH IS KNOWN AS CASAL’S NECKLACE WHEN IT
FORMS A RING AROUND THE NECK.
THE 4DS OF PELLAGRA:
966
- DIARRHEA
- DERMATITIS
- DEMENTIA, LEADING TO
- DEATH
IT IS DIAGNOSED BY MEASURING URINARY LEVELS OF 2-METHYL NICOTINAMIDE AND 2-PYRIDONE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: THIAMINE (VITAMIN B1) DEFICIENCY LEADS TO CONDITIONS LIKE BERIBERI AND
WERNICKE-KORSAKOFF SYNDROME, WHICH ARE CHARACTERIZED BY SYMPTOMS SUCH AS MUSCLE WEAKNESS,
PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY, CARDIOVASCULAR ISSUES, AND CONFUSION. WHILE COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION CAN
RESULT FROM THIAMINE DEFICIENCY, RASH AND LOOSE STOOLS DO NOT FIT WITH THIAMINE DEFICIENCY.
THEREFORE, THIAMINE WOULD NOT ADDRESS THE FULL SPECTRUM OF THIS PATIENT’S SYMPTOMS.
OPTION C: VITAMIN C DEFICIENCY CAUSES SCURVY, WHICH IS ASSOCIATED WITH SYMPTOMS LIKE BLEEDING
GUMS, BRUISING, JOINT PAIN, AND FATIGUE. SCURVY IS NOT ASSOCIATED WITH A RASH LIKE THE ONE DESCRIBED,
NOR DOES IT TYPICALLY CAUSE COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION OR DIARRHEA. HENCE, HIGH-DOSE VITAMIN C WOULD
NOT IMPROVE THIS PATIENT’S SYMPTOMS.
OPTION D: CORN-BASED DIETS ARE LOW IN NIACIN AND TRYPTOPHAN, LEADING TO PELLAGRA OVER TIME,
ESPECIALLY IF THE DIET IS NOT BALANCED WITH OTHER NIACIN-RICH FOODS. WHILE STOPPING THE CORN-BASED
DIET COULD PREVENT FURTHER NIACIN DEFICIENCY, IT WILL NOT IMMEDIATELY ADDRESS THE EXISTING DEFICIENCY
AND SYMPTOMS LIKE RASH, DIARRHEA, AND COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION. THE PATIENT WOULD STILL NEED NIACIN
SUPPLEMENTATION TO RESOLVE THE CURRENT SYMPTOMS.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A 3-MONTH-OLD CHILD WAS BROUGHT TO THE CLINIC WITH A HISTORY OF DIFFICULTY IN FEEDING AND FAILURE
TO THRIVE. UPON EXAMINATION, THE CHILD IS FLOPPY, 48 CM IN LENGTH AND WEIGHS 2.8 KG. THERE IS
GENERALIZED HYPOTONIA, MACROGLOSSIA AND HEPATOMEGALY. THE CHEST X-RAY OF THE CHILD IS PROVIDED BELOW. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE CHILD WITH A CLINICAL HISTORY OF DIFFICULTY FEEDING AND FAILURE TO THRIVE WITH GENERALISED
HYPOTONIA, MACROGLOSSIA, HEPATOMEGALY AND CHEST X-RAY FINDINGS OF MASSIVE CARDIOMEGALY SUGGEST
A DIAGNOSIS OF POMPE'S DISEASE.
POMPE'S DISEASE IS A GLYCOGEN STORAGE DISORDER(TYPE II) CAUSED BY A DEFICIENCY OF LYSOSOMAL ACID
MALTASE (ALPHA-GLUCOSIDASE) WHICH LEADS TO THE ACCUMULATION OF GLYCOGEN IN THE LYSOSOMES OF THE
LIVER (HEPATOMEGALY), SKELETAL MUSCLES IN THE FORM OF LARGE VACUOLES (HYPOTONIA AND WEAKNESS),
CARDIAC MUSCLES (HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY). THE CHILD GENERALLY DIES BY THE AGE OF 2 YEARS DUE
TO CARDIAC FAILURE. THE ADULT FORM PRESENTS WITH MUSCLE DYSTROPHIES.
LABORATORY FINDINGS SHOW ELEVATED LEVELS OF SERUM CREATINE KINASE (CK), ASPARTATE TRANSAMINASE
(AST), ALANINE TRANSAMINASE (ALT), AND LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE (LDH). URINE GLUCOSE
TETRASACCHARIDE, A GLYCOGEN BREAKDOWN METABOLITE, IS A RELIABLE BIOMARKER FOR DISEASE SEVERITY AND
TREATMENT RESPONSE. TREATMENT INCLUDES ENZYME REPLACEMENT THERAPY WITH RECOMBINANT ENZYME
A-GLUCOSIDASE ALFA (MYOZYME).
GIVEN BELOW IS THE IMAGE OF MUSCLE BIOPSY SHOWING GLYCOGEN-POSITIVE VACUOLES.
967
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A- EBSTEIN'S ANOMALY IS THE TERATOGENIC EFFECT OF MATERNAL LITHIUM CONSUMPTION WHICH
CAUSES A CYANOTIC HEART DISEASE IN THE NEWBORN WITH ATRIALIZATION OF THE RIGHT VENTRICLE AND
CONDUCTION DEFECTS. THE CHEST X-RAY WILL SHOW A BOX-SHAPED ENLARGEMENT OF THE RIGHT ATRIUM AND
PULMONARY OLIGEMIA.
OPTION C- TRANSPOSITION OF GREAT VESSELS IS CYANOTIC CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE WHERE THERE IS A
SWITCH IN THE POSITION OF TWO MAIN ARTERIES I.E. PULMONARY ARTERY AND AORTA. X-RAY SHOWS OF
EGG-ON-STRING APPEARANCE WITH PULMONARY PLETHORA.
OPTION D- VON GIERKE DISEASE OCCURS DUE TO A DEFICIENCY OF GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATASE. PATIENTS
PRESENT COMMONLY IN 3-4 MONTHS OF AGE WITH HYPOGLYCEMIA, LACTIC ACIDOSIS, HEPATOMEGALY, GROWTH
RETARDATION, HYPERURICEMIA, AND HYPERLIPIDEMIA.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH MULTIPLE YELLOWISH RAISED PLAQUES ON EYELIDS, XANTHOMAS ON THE
ACHILLES TENDON. SPECIFY THE LIKELY CAUSE FOR THE PATIENT'S PRESENTATION.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION WITH YELLOWISH, RAISED PLAQUES ON EYELIDS, AND TENDON XANTHOMAS POINTS
TO A DIAGNOSIS OF FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA (FH).
FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA (TYPE IIA HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA) IS AN INHERITED DISORDER DUE TO
DEFECTS IN LDL RECEPTORS AND APO B100. THIS DECREASES THE UPTAKE OF LOW-DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN AND
CHOLESTEROL LEADING TO THEIR INCREASED LEVELS IN THE BLOOD. THE INCREASED LDL ACCUMULATES IN THE
BLOOD VESSELS CAUSING ATHEROSCLEROSIS (PREMATURE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE)AND IN THE ACHILLES
TENDON CAUSING TENDON XANTHOMAS. XANTHOMAS ARE TUMOROUS MASSES PRODUCED BY FOAMY CELL
CLUSTERS (LIPID-LADEN MACROPHAGES) FOUND IN THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE OF THE SKIN AND TENDONS. PATIENTS
CAN ALSO HAVE YELLOWISH PLAQUES AROUND THE EYES (XANTHELASMA) AND CORNEAL ARCUS.
TREATMENT INCLUDES LIFESTYLE CHANGES, RESTRICTION OF A FATTY DIET, AND PHARMACOTHERAPY WITH STATINS
IN HETEROZYGOUS FH PATIENTS.
THE IMAGES BELOW SHOW ACHILLES TENDON XANTHOMA AND XANTHELASMA RESPECTIVELY:
968
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: TANGIER’S DISEASE IS A HYPOLIPOPROTEINEMIA CAUSED BY A MUTATION OF THE ABCA1 GENE.
ENLARGED ORANGE TONSILS ARE PATHOGNOMONIC. LOW HDL LEVELS ARE SEEN. THERE IS AN INCREASED RISK
FOR ATHEROSCLEROSIS.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS ENLARGED YELLOW-ORANGE COLOURED TONSILS IN TANGIER'S DISEASE.
969
OPTION C: XANTHOMATOSIS IS THE DEPOSITION OF LIPIDS IN VARIOUS PARTS OF THE BODY LIKE TENDON
XANTHOMAS, XANTHELASMA, ERUPTIVE AND TUBEROUS XANTHOMAS. THIS IS A SIGN OF UNDERLYING LIPID
METABOLISM DISORDERS.
OPTION D: FABRY'S DISEASE IS A LYSOSOMAL STORAGE DISORDER WITH A DEFECT IN ALPHA-GALACTOSIDASE. IT
CAUSES ANGIOKERATOMAS, HYPOHIDROSIS AND CHARACTERISTIC MALTESE CROSS DEPOSITS IN URINE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A CHILD PRESENTED TO THE OPD WITH COMPLAINTS OF FATIGUE AND MUSCLE WEAKNESS WHILE
EXERCISING. LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS FOUND THAT LCFA OXIDATION WAS AFFECTED. A MUSCLE
BIOPSY WAS DONE WHICH SHOWED THE PRESENCE OF FAT VACUOLES. SPECIFY THE PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO OF A CHILD WITH FATIGUE AND MUSCLE WEAKNESS ON EXERCISE WITH LABORATORY
FINDINGS OF LCFA OXIDATION DEFICIENCY AND FAT VACUOLES ON MUSCLE BIOPSY SUGGESTS A DIAGNOSIS OF
CARNITINE DEFICIENCY.
CARNITINE DEFICIENCY IS A DEFECT IN FATTY ACID OXIDATION THAT LEADS TO HYPOKETOTIC HYPOGLYCEMIA AND
HYPERAMMONEMIA. CARNITINE TRANSPORTS ACTIVATED LCFA (LONG CHAIN FATTY ACYL COA) FROM THE
CYTOPLASM TO THE MITOCHONDRIA FOR BETA-OXIDATION (AS THEY CANNOT CROSS THE MITOCHONDRIAL
MEMBRANE), CARNITINE DEFICIENCY IMPAIRS THIS TRANSPORT CAUSING ACCUMULATION OF LIPIDS (SKELETAL
MUSCLE WEAKNESS). THIS EXCESS FATTY ACID INHIBITS THE UREA CYCLE CAUSING HYPERAMMONEMIA. SINCE
BETA-OXIDATION CANNOT OCCUR, ENERGY PRODUCTION IS REDUCED, AND THERE IS HYPOGLYCEMIA WITHOUT A
CORRESPONDING INCREASE IN KETONE BODIES (HYPOKETOTIC) DURING TIMES OF GLUCOSE DEPLETION SUCH AS
EXERCISE.
THE ROLE OF CARNITINE IN THE METABOLISM OF FATTY ACIDS IS DEMONSTRATED IN THE IMAGE BELOW:
970
CLINICAL FEATURES OF CARNITINE DEFICIENCY BEGIN IN CHILDHOOD AND INCLUDE POOR FEEDING, LETHARGY,
LIVER DYSFUNCTION AND HEPATOMEGALY, HYPOTONIA, AND DILATED CARDIOMYOPATHY. TREATMENT INVOLVES
ORAL SUPPLEMENTATION OF CARNITINE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: AN INCREASE IN LDL CAN CAUSE HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA, AND REDUCED LDL CAN CAUSE
DEFECTIVE ABSORPTION OF FAT-SOLUBLE VITAMINS.
OPTION B: LPL IS INVOLVED IN HYDROLYSIS OF LIPOPROTEINS IN THE BLOOD TO FREE FATTY ACID AND GLYCEROL
WHICH ARE THEN TAKEN UP BY THE TISSUES. A DEFECTIVE LPL CAN CAUSE TYPE 1 FAMILIAL CHYLOMICRONEMIA
SYNDROME PRESENTING AS PANCREATITIS.
OPTION C: FATTY ACID SYNTHASE IS A MULTIENZYME COMPLEX INVOLVED IN FATTY ACID SYNTHESIS IN THE
CYTOSOL WHICH WHEN DEFECTIVE MAY IMPAIR ENERGY PRODUCTION, ESSENTIAL FATTY ACIDS, AND AFFECT
METABOLIC PATHWAYS. THERE IS NO ACCUMULATION OF FAT VACUOLES SINCE FATTY ACIDS ARE NOT SYNTHESISED.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A MOTHER CAME BACK HOME TO SEE HER CHILD SUFFERING FROM DIFFICULTY BREATHING. THE CHILD HAD
CONTACT WITH ROTENONE WHILE TRYING TO BATHE THEIR PET. THE CHILD WAS TAKEN TO THE EMERGENCY
DEPARTMENT AND SHE LATER PASSED AWAY. INHIBITION OF WHICH OF THESE ENZYMES WAS THE
LIKELY CAUSE OF HER DEATH?
questions.explanation:
IN THE GIVEN CLINICAL VIGNETTE, INHIBITION OF NADH-Q OXIDOREDUCTASE BY ROTENONE WAS THE LIKELY
CAUSE OF BREATHLESSNESS, FOLLOWED BY DEATH IN THIS CHILD.
ROTENONE INHIBITS COMPLEX I, THEREBY INHIBITING THE RESPIRATORY CHAIN, SO ELECTRONS CANNOT BE
TRANSFERRED TO OXYGEN. THIS HALTS ATP PRODUCTION, LEADING TO AN ENERGY DEFICIT IN THE CELLS,
EVENTUALLY CAUSING CELL DEATH. THE ETC CONSTITUTES FOUR ENZYME COMPLEXES:
- COMPLEX I: NADH-Q OXIDOREDUCTASE
- COMPLEX II: SUCCINATE-Q REDUCTASE
- COMPLEX III: Q-CYTOCHROME C OXIDOREDUCTASE
- COMPLEX IV: CYTOCHROME C OXIDASE
971
COMPONENTS OF COMPLEX I ARE FMN AND FE-S COMPLEX. NADH-Q OXIDOREDUCTASE CATALYSES THE
TRANSFER OF ELECTRONS FROM NADH TO COENZYME Q, ALONG WITH THE TRANSFER OF FOUR H+ ACROSS THE
MEMBRANE.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt:
A CHILD SUFFERING FROM PHENYLKETONURIA WAS STARTED ON NECESSARY DIETARY MODIFICATIONS BUT THE
NEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS PERSISTED. PHENYLALANINE HYDROXYLASE LEVELS IN THE SERUM ARE NORMAL.
WHICH OF THESE ENZYMES IS LIKELY TO BE DEFICIENT IN THIS SITUATION?
questions.explanation:
THIS CHILD WITH PHENYLKETONURIA WITH NEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS NOT IMPROVING DESPITE DIETARY
MODIFICATIONS AND NORMAL SERUM PHENYLALANINE HYDROXYLASE LEVEL IS SUGGESTIVE OF
TETRAHYDROBIOPTERIN (BH4) SYNTHASE DEFICIENCY.
A DIET LOW IN PHENYLALANINE (EG: TAPIOCA) IS THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT FOR CLASSIC PHENYLKETONURIA
BUT MAY NOT BE SUFFICIENT IN BH4 DEFICIENCY WHERE SUPPLEMENTATION WITH BH4 AND DEFICIENT
NEUROTRANSMITTER PRECURSORS (L-DOPA) IS REQUIRED TO OVERCOME THE BLOCK.
PHENYLKETONURIA (PKU) IS AN INBORN ERROR OF METABOLISM SEEN DUE TO A DEFECT IN THE
ENZYME PHENYLALANINE HYDROXYLASE (CLASSIC PHENYLKETONURIA) AND LESS COMMONLY, DUE TO A DEFECT
IN BH4 SYNTHASE (NON-CLASSICAL). THESE DEFECTS RESULT IN THE IMPAIRED CONVERSION OF PHENYLALANINE
TO TYROSINE. THE PATIENT DEVELOPS CLINICAL FEATURES DUE TO ELEVATED LEVELS OF PHENYLALANINE
METABOLITES AND DECREASED LEVELS OF TYROSINE. THE EXCESS PHENYLALANINE IN THE BLOOD IS METABOLIZED
TO PHENYLPYRUVATE (POSITIVE FERRIC CHLORIDE) AND PHENYLACETATE (MOUSY ODOUR) WHICH ARE EXCRETED
IN THE URINE. INFANTS APPEAR NORMAL AT BIRTH AND GRADUALLY DEVELOP SYMPTOMS OF HYPERREFLEXIA,
SEIZURES, HYPOPIGMENTATION, LOW IQ, HYPERACTIVITY, AND TREMORS.
TANDEM MASS SPECTROSCOPY IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE. GUTHRIE TEST IS A SCREENING TEST THAT
SHOWS WITH ABSENCE OF GROWTH OF BACILLUS SUBTILIS. THE FERRIC CHLORIDE TEST IS POSITIVE WITH THE
DEVELOPMENT OF A TRANSIENT BLUE-GREEN COLOUR.
OTHER OPTIONS -
OPTION A: TYROSINE HYDROXYLASE IS THE RATE-LIMITING ENZYME IN THE SYNTHESIS OF EPINEPHRINE,
CONVERTS TYROSINE TO DOPA, ITS DEFICIENCY DOES NOT CAUSE PHENYLKETONURIA
OPTION B: HOMOGENTISIC ACID OXIDASE CONVERTS HOMOGENTISIC ACID TO MALEYLACETOACETIC ACID IN THE
TYROSINE DEGRADATION PATHWAY AND ITS DEFICIENCY CAUSES ALKAPTONURIA WITH A DARK COLOUR OF URINE
ON STANDING, BLUISH-BLACK PIGMENTATION IN CONNECTIVE TISSUE (OCHRONOSIS) AND ARTHRITIS.
OPTION D: DOPA DECARBOXYLASE IS ANOTHER ENZYME INVOLVED IN THE SYNTHESIS OF EPINEPHRINE. IT
CONVERTS DOPA TO DOPAMINE IN THE PRESENCE OF VITAMIN B6. WHILE ENZYMES INVOLVED IN
EPINEPHRINE SYNTHESIS CAUSE NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION, THEY DO NOT CAUSE PHENYLKETONURIA AS SUCH.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.prompt: WHICH MICRONUTRIENT IS MOST LIKELY DEFICIENT IN A PATIENT WITH THE RADIOGRAPHIC FINDINGS PROVIDED BELOW ALONG WITH ANEMIA, NEUTROPENIA, DEPIGMENTED HAIR AND SKIN?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL FEATURES OF ANAEMIA AND NEUTROPENIA, ALONG WITH DEPIGMENTED HAIR AND SKIN AND
THE RADIOLOGICAL FINDINGS SUGGESTIVE OF PELKAN SPURS, TRUMMERFELD ZONE, FRENKEL'S LINE, AND
WIMBERGER'S RING SIGN POINT TO THE DIAGNOSIS OF MENKE'S DISEASE. PATIENTS WITH THIS CONDITION HAVE
LOW SERUM LEVELS OF COPPER.
MENKE'S DISEASE OR MENKE-KINKY HAIR SYNDROME IS AN X-LINKED RECESSIVE CONDITION CAUSED DUE TO A
MUTATION IN THE ATP7A GENE ON CHROMOSOME X. THIS CAUSES IMPAIRED TRANSPORT OF DIETARY COPPER
972
FROM THE SMALL INTESTINE TO THE LIVER LEADING TO LOW LEVELS OF COPPER-CONTAINING ENZYMES.
THE FINAL STEP OF COLLAGEN SYNTHESIS INVOLVES THE FORMATION OF COVALENT CROSS-LINKS. THIS IS DONE BY
THE ENZYME LYSYL OXIDASE, A COPPER-CONTAINING PROTEIN. THIS IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE STRENGTH AND
RIGIDITY OF COLLAGEN. AS A RESULT OF DEFICIENCY OF COPPER IN MENKES DISEASE, THIS STEP OF COLLAGEN
SYNTHESIS IS AFFECTED.
THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH DEPIGMENTED KINKY HAIR, FAILURE TO THRIVE, NEURODEGENERATIVE SYMPTOMS
(LOSS OF DEVELOPMENTAL MILESTONES, TRUNCAL HYPOTONIA, EPILEPSY), MULTIPLE FRACTURES, ANAEMIA DUE

questions.prompt:
A CHILD PRESENTED WITH RECURRENT ABDOMINAL PAIN, VOMITING, AND DIARRHEA FOLLOWING INGESTION
OF MILK-BASED PRODUCTS. INDICATE WHICH ENZYME IS LIKELY TO BE DEFICIENT.
questions.explanation:
973
THE GIVEN SCENARIO INDICATES INTOLERANCE OF MILK-BASED PRODUCTS IN THIS CHILD, HENCE, THE ENZYME
LIKELY TO BE DEFICIENT IS LACTASE.
LACTASE IS THE ENZYME THAT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR BREAKING DOWN LACTOSE, A DISACCHARIDE FOUND IN MILK
AND DAIRY PRODUCTS. WHEN THIS ENZYME IS DEFICIENT, IT CAN LEAD TO THE ACCUMULATION OF LACTOSE IN
THE INTESTINAL LUMEN WHERE IT IS FERMENTED BY INTESTINAL BACTERIA TO LACTATE WHICH PRODUCES
SYMPTOMS OF LACTOSE INTOLERANCE, INCLUDING RECURRENT ABDOMINAL PAIN, VOMITING, AND DIARRHEA
AFTER CONSUMING LACTOSE-RICH FOOD ITEMS. LACTASE AND MALTASE ARE PRESENT IN THE INTESTINAL BRUSH
BORDER.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A- LIPASES ARE INVOLVED IN THE HYDROLYSIS OF DIETARY TRIGLYCERIDES TO FREE FATTY ACIDS AND
GLYCEROL. IT IS DEFICIENT IN EXOCRINE PANCREATIC DEFICIENCY STATES SUCH AS CHRONIC PANCREATITIS, CYSTIC
FIBROSIS, AND CROHN'S. ALTHOUGH IT MIGHT ALSO PRESENT WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN AND DIARRHEA, THE STOOLS
ARE FOUL-SMELLING(DUE TO GUT BACTERIA) AND GREASY DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF FAT (STEATORRHEA) AND ARE
ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH FAT-SOLUBLE VITAMIN DEFICIENCY.
OPTION B- MALTASE BREAKS DOWN MALTOSE WHICH IS A DISACCHARIDE INTERMEDIATE OF STARCH
BREAKDOWN.
OPTION C- AMYLASE HYDROLYSES STARCH WHICH IS A GLUCOSE HOMOPOLYMER AND IS PRESENT IN
GERMINATING CEREALS, POTATOES, LEGUMES, AND MALT.

questions.prompt:
IN THE GIVEN LINEWEAVER-BURK PLOT, THE BLUE LINE REPRESENTS THE ACTION OF AN ENZYME, AND THE
RED LINE REPRESENTS THE ACTION OF THE SAME ENZYME IN THE PRESENCE OF AN INHIBITOR. SPECIFY THE
TYPE OF INHIBITION SHOWN HERE.
options:
ALLOSTERIC INHIBITION
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN GRAPH SHOWS COMPETITIVE INHIBITION, IN WHICH THE VALUE OF VMAX REMAINS CONSTANT AND
THE KM VALUE INCREASES. THE INTERCEPT ON THE Y-AXIS REMAINS UNCHANGED WHILE THE INTERCEPT ON THE
X-AXIS SHIFTS CLOSE TO ZERO FORMING A STEEPER SLOPE.
COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS WHEN THE INHIBITOR BINDS REVERSIBLY TO THE SUBSTRATE-BINDING SITE AND
COMPETES WITH THE SUBSTRATE FOR THE ACTIVE ENZYME-BINDING SITE. THIS EFFECT OF COMPETITIVE
INHIBITION CAN BE OVERCOME BY INCREASING THE SUBSTRATE CONCENTRATION BY WHICH MAXIMUM VELOCITY
CAN STILL BE ACHIEVED. THEREFORE, VMAX (MAXIMUM VELOCITY OF THE REACTION) IS UNALTERED IN THIS TYPE
OF INHIBITION. HOWEVER, THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE HALF OF THE
MAXIMUM VELOCITY IS INCREASED. THEREFORE, KM IS INCREASED IN THIS CONDITION.
THE GRAPH BELOW SHOWS THE CHANGES IN VMAX AND KM IN COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.
974
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION IS BY BINDING INHIBITORS TO ENZYMES IN LOCATIONS
REMOTE FROM THE ACTIVE SITE. INCREASING THE CONCENTRATION OF THE SUBSTRATE DOES NOT OVERCOME
NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION. THUS, NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS DECREASE THE VMAX OF THE REACTION.
THEY DO NOT INTERFERE WITH THE BINDING OF THE SUBSTRATE TO THE ENZYME. THUS, THE ENZYME SHOWS
THE SAME KM IN THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF NONCOMPETITIVE INHIBITORS.
THE GRAPH SHOWS THE CHANGES IN VMAX AND KM IN NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION.
OPTION C: IN UNCOMPETITIVE INHIBITION, INHIBITORS BIND WITH THE ENZYME-SUBSTRATE INTERMEDIATE
COMPLEX, AND INHIBIT IT. THIS LEADS TO A DECREASE IN BOTH VMAX AND KM. AN EXAMPLE IS THE
INHIBITION OF PLACENTAL ALKALINE PHOSPHATE (ALP) BY PHENYLALANINE.
OPTION D: IN ALLOSTERIC INHIBITION, INHIBITORS BIND TO A SITE OTHER THAN THE ACTIVE SITE I.E. ALLOSTERIC
SITE, AND INDUCE A CONFORMATIONAL CHANGE (CHANGE IN THE SHAPE OF THE ACTIVE SITE UNLIKE IN
NON-COMPETITIVE INHIBITION) THUS, INHIBITING THE ENZYME. ATP IS AN ALLOSTERIC INHIBITOR OF
975
PHOSPHOFRUCTOKINASE IN GLYCOLYSIS.

ACETONE FREE METHANOL IS USED IN FIXATION (PRESERVATION OF BIOLOGICAL TISSUES FROM DECAY WHICH ACTS
BY PREVENTING METABOLIC AND ENZYME ACTIVITY AND NOT BY FIXING THE CELLS TO THE SLIDE).
ACETONE (LIPID SOLVENT) IS NOT USED AS IT CAUSES SHRINKAGE AND DESTRUCTION OF CELL MEMBRANE

- IMMERSION OF SPECIMEN IN FIXATIVE
- PERFUSING VASCULAR SYSTEM WITH A FIXATIVE
THE MOST COMMONLY USED FIXATIVE IS 10% NEUTRAL BUFFERED FORMALIN.

questions.prompt:
A 30-YEAR-OLD WOMAN PRESENTED WITH PAINFUL BLISTERS ON THE SKIN AND ORAL MUCOSA. DIRECT
IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE IS PROVIDED BELOW. WHICH OF THESE IS FALSE CONCERNING THE SAME?
options: SUPRABASAL ACANTHOLYTIC BLISTER IS A CHARACTERISTIC FEATURE
questions.explanation:
ANTIBODIES AGAINST HEMIDESMOSOMES IS THE FALSE STATEMENT AS THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS A
CHARACTERISTIC FISH-NET APPEARANCE ON DIRECT IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE, WHICH IS DIAGNOSTIC OF
PEMPHIGUS VULGARIS. THE ANTIBODIES ARE AGAINST THE DESMOSOMAL ADHESION PROTEINS SUCH AS
DESMOGLEINS 1 AND 3.
THIS PATTERN IS DUE TO INTRAEPIDERMAL INTERCELLULAR DEPOSITION OF IGG AND C3.
THE FIRST-LINE INVESTIGATION IN PEMPHIGUS VULGARIS IS THE TZANCK SMEAR. IT ALLOWS US TO VISUALIZE THE
HISTOLOGY BY COLLECTING MATERIAL FROM THE FLOOR OF A FRESH BLISTER THAT IS STAINED WITH GIEMSA OR ANY
ROMANOWSKY STAIN. TZANCK CELLS ARE SEEN ON MICROSCOPY.
1823
DIRECT IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY (DIF) IS THE MOST ACCURATE TEST.
ANTIBODIES AGAINST HEMIDESMOSOMES THAT LINK BASAL KERATINOCYTES TO THE UNDERLYING BASEMENT
MEMBRANE ARE SEEN IN BULLOUS PEMPHIGOID.

questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE STAIN DONE ON A SECTION OF LIVER DISPLAYED BELOW?
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE STAIN DEMONSTRATES RETICULAR FIBERS OF THE LIVER AND HENCE HAS TO BE RETICULIN STAIN.
RETICULIN STAIN
- STAINED BY 2 PROCEDURES, GORDON AND SWEET’S RETICULIN STAIN (MOST COMMON) AND GOMORI
RETICULIN STAIN.
- THEY DEMONSTRATE RETICULIN FIBERS AND BASEMENT MEMBRANE.
- RETICULIN FIBERS: THIN, TYPE 3 COLLAGEN, WIDESPREAD IN CONNECTIVE TISSUE
- BASEMENT MEMBRANE: TYPE 4 COLLAGEN FIBERS AND LAMININ.
RETICULIN STAIN IS USED TO SHOWS THE NORMAL ARCHITECTURE OF THE LIVER AND THEREBY HELP DETECT
DISRUPTED ARCHITECTURE IN HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA AND HEPATOCELLULAR PROLIFERATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THESE IS TRUE CONCERNING THE INTERNAL IRON HOMEOSTASIS IN IRON-DEFICIENCY
ANAEMIA?
options:
FERRITIN MRNA CONCENTRATION IRON-RESPONSIVE ELEMENT INCREASES AND FERRITIN SYNTHESIS
DECREASES

TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR 1 IRON-RESPONSIVE ELEMENTS INCREASES TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR MRNA
CONCENTRATION AND SYNTHESIS

TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR 1 IRON RESPONSIVE ELEMENTS DECREASES TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR MRNA
CONCENTRATION AND SYNTHESIS

FERRITIN MRNA CONCENTRATION IRON RESPONSIVE ELEMENT DECREASES AND FERRITIN SYNTHESIS
INCREASES
questions.answer:
TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR 1 IRON-RESPONSIVE ELEMENTS INCREASES TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR MRNA
CONCENTRATION AND SYNTHESIS
questions.explanation:
IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA, THERE IS AN INCREASE IN TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR MRNA CONCENTRATION AND
SYNTHESIS.
IRON ABSORBED THROUGH DIET OR WHICH IS RELEASED FROM CIRCULATION IS BOUND TO TRANSFERRIN (IRON
TRANSFER PROTEIN). WHEN ERYTHROPOIESIS IS STIMULATED, IRON-TRANSFERRIN COMPLEXES ACT AS TRANSFERRIN
RECEPTORS ON THE SURFACE OF BONE MARROW ERYTHROID CELLS. THROUGH RECEPTOR-MEDIATED ENDOCYTOSIS,
THIS COMPLEX IS INTERNALISED.
THIS IRON IS THEN MADE AVAILABLE FOR HEME SYNTHESIS WHILE THE TRANSFERRIN-RECEPTOR COMPLEX IS
RECYCLED TO THE SURFACE OF THE CELL, FROM WHERE THE TRANSFERRIN IS RELEASED BACK INTO CIRCULATION AND
THE TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR RE-ANCHORS INTO THE CELL MEMBRANE. THE EXCESS IRON AFTER HEMOGLOBIN
SYNTHESIS BINDS TO APOFERRITIN (STORAGE PROTEIN), FORMING FERRITIN.
SENESCENT RBCS UNDERGO PHAGOCYTOSIS IN THE CELLS OF THE RETICULOENDOTHELIAL SYSTEM. THE
HEMOGLOBIN IS BROKEN DOWN, THE GLOBIN AND OTHER PROTEINS ARE RETURNED TO THE AMINO ACID POOL,
AND THE IRON IS SHUTTLED BACK TO THE SURFACE OF THE RETICULOENDOTHELIAL CELL, WHERE IT IS TAKEN UP BY
TRANSFERRIN VIA FERROPORTIN (IRON EXPORT CHANNEL).
THERE IS NO REGULATED EXCRETORY PATHWAY FOR IRON, AND THE ONLY MECHANISMS BY WHICH IRON IS LOST
ARE BLOOD LOSS (VIA GASTROINTESTINAL BLEEDING, MENSTRUATION, OR OTHER FORMS OF BLEEDING) AND THE
LOSS OF EPITHELIAL CELLS FROM THE SKIN, GUT, AND GENITOURINARY TRACT. THE NORMAL DAILY IRON LOSS FROM
THE BODY IS 1-2 MG.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: ALL ARE REDUCED IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA EXCEPT
questions.explanation:
IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA, TOTAL IRON BINDING CAPACITY(TIBC) IS INCREASED IN ORDER TO
COMPENSATE TO THE DEFICIENT STATE.
- DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA INCLUDE OF IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA INCLUDE :
- HYPOCHROMIC AND MICROCYTIC RED CELL INDICES
- LOW SERUM FERRITIN(<15MG/DL) AND IRON LEVELS(<30MG/DL)
- LOW TRANSFERRIN SATURATION(<15%)
- INCREASED TOTAL IRON-BINDING CAPACITY
- THE PLATELET COUNT OFTEN IS ELEVATED
- ERYTHROPOIETIN LEVELS ARE ELEVATED, BUT THE MARROW RESPONSE IS BLUNTED BY THE IRON DEFICIENCY;
THUS, MARROW CELLULARITY USUALLY IS ONLY SLIGHTLY INCREASED.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH ANTICOAGULANT IS USED FOR ELECTROLYTE ESTIMATION.
questions.explanation:
LITHIUM HEPARIN IS USED FOR ELECTROLYTE ESTIMATION.
HEPARIN
- IT IS THE ANTICOAGULANT CAUSING THE LEAST INTERFERENCE WITH THE TEST.
- IT IS THE BEST ANTICOAGULANT TO USE WHEN MINIMAL HEMOLYSIS IS DESIRED E.G. FOR SODIUM AND
POTASSIUM.
- HEPARIN ACCELERATES THE ACTION OF ANTITHROMBIN III WHICH NEUTRALIZES THROMBIN AND THUS PREVENTS
THE FORMATION OF FIBRIN FROM FIBRINOGEN.
- HEPARIN IS ADDED (0.2 MG /ML OF BLOOD) OR A DROP OF HEPARIN IS DRAWN INTO THE SYRINGE.
- USUALLY FOUND AS GREEN TOP TUBES
- DRAWBACKS
- IT INHIBITS THE ACID PHOSPHATASE ACTIVITY.
- IT GIVES A BLUE BACKGROUND FOR WRIGHT’S STAIN SMEARS SO NOT GOOD FOR PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR
INTERPRETATION.
- IT ALSO AFFECTS THE BINDING OF TRIIODOTHYRONINE AND THYROXINE TO THEIR CARRIER PROTEIN AND PRODUCES
A HIGHER FREE CONCENTRATION OF THESE HORMONES.
- IT INTERFERES WITH BINDING OF CALCIUM TO EDTA.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHEN YOU ADD CALCIUM AND THROMBOPLASTIN TO PLATELET POOR PLASMA WHICH PATHWAY IS
ASSESSED?
questions.explanation:
- PLATELET POOR PLASMA IS USED IN ASSESSING COAGULATION PATHWAY.
1833
- THROMBOPLASTIN (FACTOR III) BINDS WITH FACTOR VII. WHEN CALCIUM IS ADDED, IT GEARS UP THE
COAGULATION PROCESS VIA EXTRINSIC PATHWAY.
- COAGULATION PARAMETERS USED TO ASSESS :
- EXTRINSIC PATHWAY - PROTHROMBIN TIME (PT)
- INTRINSIC PATHWAY - ACTIVATED PARTIAL THROMBOPLASTIN TIME (APTT)
- COMMON PATHWAY - BOTH PT AND APTT

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS ORIGIN OF B CELL IN CLL/SLL?
options: NAIVE B CELLS IN INTERFOLLICULAR ZONES
questions.answer: NAIVE B CELLS IN INTERFOLLICULAR ZONES
questions.explanation:
IN CLL/SLL, B CELLS ORIGINATE FROM NAIVE B CELL OR PRE/POST GERMINAL CENTRE MEMORY B CELL. CLL
ARISES IN THE LYMPH NODE.
DNA SEQUENCING HAS REVEALED THAT THE IG GENES OF SOME CLL/SLL ARE SOMATICALLY HYPERMUTATED,
WHEREAS OTHERS ARE NOT, SUGGESTING THAT THE CELL OF ORIGIN MAY BE EITHER A POSTGERMINAL CENTER
MEMORY B CELL OR A NAIVE B CELL. FOR UNCLEAR REASONS, TUMORS WITH UNMUTATED IG SEGMENTS (THOSE
PUTATIVELY OF NAIVE B-CELL ORIGIN) PURSUE A MORE AGGRESSIVE COURSE.
CENTROCYTES ARE PRESENT IN GERMINAL CENTRE. THEY ARE NOT THE ORIGIN OF CLL.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD MAN REPORTS FACIAL PUFFINESS AND FROTHY URINE. PROVIDED BELOW
IS THE HISTOLOGICAL IMAGE OF THE CONDITION. WHAT DO YOU THINK IS THE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE IS CHARACTERISTIC OF MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY. THE GIVEN HEMATOXYLIN AND EOSIN
(H&E)-STAINED IMAGE SHOWS UNIFORM, DIFFUSE THICKENING OF THE GLOMERULAR CAPILLARY WALL.
(INTENSE PINK COLOR)
MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON CAUSES OF NEPHROTIC SYNDROME IN OLDER
ADULTS, WITH A PEAK INCIDENCE IN 30–50 YEARS AND A MALE:FEMALE RATIO OF 2:1.
IT IS A FORM OF CHRONIC IMMUNE-COMPLEX-MEDIATED DISEASE.
IT CAN BE PRIMARY (75% OF CASES) OR SECONDARY (ASSOCIATED WITH SYSTEMIC DISEASES/IDENTIFIABLE
ETIOLOGIC AGENTS).
MICROSCOPY:
- LIGHT MICROSCOPY: DIFFUSE THICKENING OF THE GLOMERULAR CAPILLARY WALL WITHOUT CELLULAR
PROLIFERATION. IRREGULAR SPIKES PROJECTING FROM THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE ARE BEST SEEN WITH SILVER
STAINS.
- IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY: GRANULAR DEPOSITS CONTAINING IG AND COMPLEMENT ALONG THE
GLOMERULAR BASEMENT MEMBRANE
- ELECTRON MICROGRAPH: ELECTRON-DENSE SUBEPITHELIAL DEPOSITS (EPIMEMBRANOUS SPIKES) AND
EFFACEMENT OF FOOT PROCESSES OF PODOCYTES
IMAGE: THE SILVER STAIN OF THE GLOMERULUS HIGHLIGHTS THE PROTEINACEOUS BASEMENT MEMBRANES IN
BLACK. THERE ARE CHARACTERISTIC "SPIKES" OF BASEMENT MEMBRANE BETWEEN THE IMMUNE DEPOSITS OF
MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY. THE BLACK BASEMENT MEMBRANE MATERIAL SHOWN HERE APPEARS
AS PROJECTIONS IN THE CAPILLARY LOOPS.
1835

questions.prompt:
A 50-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTED WITH THE BLURRING OF VISION. URINE EXAMINATION SHOWED
PROTEINURIA. FUNDUS EXAMINATION SHOWED DOT AND BLOT HEMORRHAGES, MICROANEURYSMS, AND

questions.explanation:
HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE SHOWS ACELLULAR PERIODIC ACID SCHIFF (PAS)-POSITIVE NODULES SUGGESTIVE
OF NODULAR GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS/INTERCAPILLARY GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS/KIMMELSTIEL–WILSON DISEASE,
WHICH OCCURS IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETIC NEPHROPATHY.
THESE LESIONS APPEAR AS OVOID OR SPHERICAL, OFTEN LAMINATED, PAS-POSITIVE NODULES WITHIN THE
MESANGIAL CORE OF THE GLOMERULAR LOBULES.
THESE NODULAR LESIONS ARE FREQUENTLY ACCOMPANIED BY PROMINENT ACCUMULATIONS OF HYALINE
MATERIAL IN CAPILLARY LOOPS (“FIBRIN CAPS”) OR ADHERENT TO BOWMAN CAPSULES (“CAPSULAR DROPS”).
RENAL FAILURE IS THE SECOND COMMON CAUSE OF DEATH IN DIABETES MELLITUS, THE FIRST BEING MYOCARDIAL
INFARCTION.
THREE RENAL LESIONS ARE ENCOUNTERED IN DIABETIC NEPHROPATHY:
1. GLOMERULAR LESIONS:
- CAPILLARY BASEMENT MEMBRANE THICKENING
- DIFFUSE MESANGIAL SCLEROSIS
- NODULAR GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS/KIMMELSTIEL–WILSON DISEASE
2. RENAL VASCULAR LESIONS, PRINCIPALLY HYALINE ARTERIOLOSCLEROSIS
3. PYELONEPHRITIS, INCLUDING NECROTIZING PAPILLITIS
RENAL HISTOPATHOLOGY IN
- AMYLOIDOSIS: GLOMERULAR DEPOSITS APPEARING AS THICKENINGS OF THE MESANGIAL MATRIX, FORMING
INTERLACING BROAD RIBBONS OF AMYLOID
- LUPUS NEPHRITIS: IMMUNE COMPLEX DEPOSITS IN THE MESANGIUM OR ALONG THE ENTIRE BASEMENT
MEMBRANE (WIRE LOOP LESIONS), WITH MESANGIAL CELL PROLIFERATION
1836
- FOCAL SEGMENTAL GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS: FOCAL AND SEGMENTAL HYALINOSIS AND SCLEROSIS OF THE CAPILLARY
WALL; LIPID DROPLETS IN THE SCLEROSED AREA.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IF THE RB GENE IS HYPOPHOSPHORYLATED, WHICH OF THESE WILL HAPPEN?
options: CELL CYCLE WILL STOP AT G2
CELL CYCLE WILL STOP AT G1
THERE WILL BE NO EFFECT ON CELL CYCLE AS RB GENE PHOSPHORYLATION IS NOT NEEDED
THE CELL CYCLE PROGRESSES AND CELL DIVIDES
questions.answer: CELL CYCLE WILL STOP AT G1
questions.explanation:
IF THE RETINOBLASTOMA (RB) GENE IS HYPOPHOSPHORYLATED, IT IS ACTIVE AND THE CELL CYCLE WILL STOP AT
G1.
RB IS A CELL-CYCLE REGULATOR BECAUSE IT BINDS TO AND INACTIVATES A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR (E2F). THIS IS
NECESSARY FOR THE TRANSCRIPTION OF CERTAIN GENES NECESSARY FOR THE PROGRESSION FROM THE G1 TO S
PHASE. THE PHOSPHORYLATION OF RB RESULTS IN THE RELEASE OF E2F. THIS ACTIVATES GENE TRANSCRIPTION
AND CELL-CYCLE PROGRESSION OCCURS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE CELL CYCLE REGULATION BY RB GENE.

GASTROINTESTINAL ENDOSCOPY WAS DONE, AND THE BIOPSY RESULT IS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE

questions.explanation:

THE HISTOLOGICAL IMAGE ABOVE SHOWS THE TRANSITION BETWEEN NORMAL SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM AND THE

BARRETT’S ESOPHAGUS IS A COMPLICATION OF CHRONIC GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE (GERD)

PREMALIGNANT CONDITION THAT CONFERS AN INCREASED RISK OF ESOPHAGEAL ADENOCARCINOMA.
HENCE, PATIENTS DIAGNOSED WITH BARRETT’S ESOPHAGUS MUST BE SUBJECTED TO A REGULAR SURVEILLANCE
ENDOSCOPY ANNUALLY OR WITH 2-YEAR INTERVALS, PROVIDED NO DYSPLASIAS HAVE BEEN DETECTED. THE
PRESENCE OF DYSPLASIA IS ASSOCIATED WITH PROLONGED SYMPTOMS, LONGER SEGMENT LENGTH, INCREASED
PATIENT AGE, AND CAUCASIAN RACE.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 32 YEAR OLD FEMALE WITH HISTORY OF BACK ACHE AND POLYARTHRALGIA WAS INVESTIGATED AND FOUND
TO HAVE NUCLEOLAR PATTERN IN IF. WHICH OF THESE IS THE BEST FIT IN HER CASE?
options: JOINT PAINS WITH NODULES ON SKIN
questions.explanation:
THE NUCLEOLAR PATTERN ON IF (IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE) IS SUGGESTIVE OF RNA ANTIBODIES WHICH POINT
TOWARDS THE DIAGNOSIS OF SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS. HENCE, RAYNAUD PHENOMENON AND SCLERODACTYLY ARE
THE BEST FIT IN THE GIVEN CASE.
THE NUCLEOLAR PATTERN IN IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE:
SOME SCLERODACTYLY PATIENTS DEVELOP A COMBINATION CALLED THE CREST SYNDROME:
- CALCINOSIS
- RAYNAUD PHENOMENON
- ESOPHAGEAL DYSMOTILITY
- SCLERODACTYLY
- TELANGIECTASIA
PATIENTS WITH THIS SYNDROME HAVE RELATIVELY LIMITED INVOLVEMENT OF SKIN, OFTEN CONFINED TO FINGERS,
FOREARMS, AND FACE, AND CALCIFICATION OF THE SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUES. INVOLVEMENT OF THE VISCERA MAY
NOT OCCUR AT ALL OR OCCUR LATE. IN GENERAL, THESE PATIENTS LIVE LONGER THAN THOSE WITH SYSTEMIC
SCLEROSIS WITH DIFFUSE VISCERAL INVOLVEMENT AT THE OUTSET.

SHOWED RS CELLS WITH VAGUE NODULE FORMATION AND A BACKGROUND OF REACTIVE T-LYMPHOCYTES.

LYMPHOMA (NLPHL).
AXIAL GROUP (CERVICAL) LYMPHADENOPATHY AND ALONG WITH THE L&H VARIANT OF REED-STERNBERG
CELLS IS CHARACTERISTIC.
RS CELLS ARE NEOPLASTIC GIANT CELLS. IN NLPHL, THE CELLS HAVE VAGUE NODULAR FORMATION.
IMMUNOPHENOTYPING IS POSITIVE FOR CD20 (B CELL-ASSOCIATED), LCA (CD45), EMA (EPITHELIAL

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS A TOOL USED IN GENE EDITING:
questions.explanation:
GUIDE RNAS CALLED CRISPRS HELP TO SELECTIVELY ALTER OR CORRECT DNA SEQUENCES.
CRISPR IS CLUSTERED REGULARLY INTERSPACED SHORT PALINDROMIC REPEATS
- CRISPR-CAS9 IS A GENOME EDITING TOOL AND THIS SYSTEM ENABLES SELECT BACTERIA TO RESPOND TO AND
ELIMINATE INVADING GENETIC MATERIAL.
- CRISPRS ARE TRANSCRIBED INTO AN RNA SEQUENCE THAT DIRECTS THE CAS9 TO A SEQUENCE LEADING TO ITS
CLEAVAGE.
- GENE EDITING USES AN ARTIFICIAL GUIDE RNA THAT BINDS CAS9 AND IS COMPLEMENTARY TO A DNA
SEQUENCE OF INTEREST AND CAS9 INDUCES THE BREAK OF DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA.
ONE OF THE FIRST SUCCESSFUL DISEASES USED ON EXPERIMENTAL BASIS IS SICKLE CELL ANEMIA.
OTHER GENE EDITING TOOLS ARE:
- ZINC-FINGER NUCLEASES (ZNFS)
- TRANSCRIPTION-ACTIVATOR LIKE EFFECTOR NUCLEASES (TALEN)
- MEGANUCLEASES

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 37-YEAR-OLD PRESENTED WITH FEVER. UPON EXAMINATION,■ HE HAD ENLARGED AND ULCERATED TONSILS.
HIS PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR SHOWED LYMPHOCYTOSIS. MONOSPOT TEST WAS NEGATIVE.
TONSILLECTOMY WAS DONE AND IT SHOWED LARGE CELLS MIXED WITH LYMPHOCYTES. THE CELLS WERE
POSITIVE FOR CD20, EBV LMP1, MUM1, CD 79A. BACKGROUND CELLS WERE POSITIVE FOR CD3. THE
CELLS ARE NEGATIVE FOR CD15. WHAT IS YOUR MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO SUGGESTS A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS OF EBV POSITIVE DLBCL, NOS (EPSTEIN BARR
VIRUS-POSITIVE DIFFUSE LARGE B CELL LYMPHOMA, NOT OTHERWISE SPECIFIED).
1840
THE GIVEN SLIDE SHOWS SHEETS OF LARGE LYMPHOID CELLS WITH IRREGULAR VESICULAR NUCLEI AND PROMINENT
NUCLEOLI TYPICAL OF DLBCL.
APPROACH TO THE QUESTION:
- IN THE GIVEN CASE, MONOSPOT TEST NEGATIVE RULES OUT INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS AND THE
IDENTIFICATION OF REED-STERNBERG CELL AND THEIR VARIANT IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF HODGKIN
LYMPHOMA, WHICH CAN ALSO BE RULED OUT.
- EBV-POSITIVE MUCOCUTANEOUS ULCER IS A LOCALIZED LYMPHOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDER IN
IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENTS. IT IS A SELF-LIMITING ULCER WHICH REVERTS ON TREATMENT IN
IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PEOPLE. HISTOLOGICALLY CHARACTERIZED BY ATYPICAL LARGE B CELLS WITH RS
CELL-LIKE MORPHOLOGY. HENCE, THIS IS ALSO RULED OUT.
- EBV POSITIVE DLBL(DIFFUSE LARGE B CELL LYMPHOMA) OCCURS IN PATIENTS MORE THAN 50 YEARS OF
AGE AND WITHOUT A PREVIOUS HISTORY OF LYMPHOMA. DLBCL TYPICALLY PRESENTS AS A RAPIDLY ENLARGING
MASS AT A NODAL OR EXTRANODAL SITE.
- IMMUNOHISTOCHEMICAL STUDIES INDICATE THAT EBV+ DLBCL, NOS IS MOLECULARLY HETEROGENEOUS
WITH A PROMINENT BACKGROUND OF T LYMPHOCYTES. THE CELLS ARE POSITIVE FOR CD 20, CD 79A,
IRF4/MUM1. EBV LMP-1(LATENT MEMBRANE PROTEIN-1) IS POSITIVE IN ABOUT 2/3RDOF CASES, WHILE
EBNA-2 (EPSTEIN-BARR NUCLEAR ANTIGEN) IS POSITIVE IN THE REMAINING 1/3RD OF CASES. IT IS NEGATIVE
FOR CD10 AND BCL6.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
THE SCRAPING OF A PAINLESS GENITAL ULCER, WHEN STAINED WITH GRAM STAIN AND VIEWED UNDER THE
MICROSCOPE, SHOWS A GRAM-NEGATIVE COCCOBACILLUS SURROUNDED BY NEUTROPHILS. WHAT IS YOUR
DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE DESCRIPTION OF A GRAM STAIN SHOWING GRAM-NEGATIVE COCCOBACILLUS SURROUNDED BY
NEUTROPHILS IS SUGGESTIVE OF KLEBSIELLA GRANULOMATIS.
GRANULOMA INGUINALE, OR DONOVANOSIS, IS A SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE
CAUSED BY KLEBSIELLA GRANULOMATIS, A MINUTE, ENCAPSULATED, COCCOBACILLUS. IT CAN EXHIBIT A
CHARACTERISTIC SAFETY PIN APPEARANCE ON MICROSCOPY.
KLEBSIELLA GRANULOMATIS IS DIFFICULT TO CULTURE AND DIAGNOSIS NEEDS VISUALIZATION OF DARK-STAINING
DONOVAN BODIES ON TISSUE CRUSH PREPARATION OR BIOPSY. THE ORGANISMS ARE DEMONSTRABLE IN
GIEMSA-STAINED SMEARS OF THE EXUDATE AS A MINUTE, ENCAPSULATED COCCOBACILLI (DONOVAN BODIES) IN
MACROPHAGES.
OPTIONS 1, 4: GRAM-NEGATIVE DIPLOCOCCI
OPTION 2: SCHOOL OF FISH APPEARANCE

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHEN PAPAIN ACTS ON A MOLECULE OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN, WHICH OF THESE ARE THE END
PRODUCTS?
questions.explanation:
WHEN PAPAIN ACTS ON A MOLECULE OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN, THE END PRODUCTS ARE 1 FC AND 2 FAB
FRAGMENTS.
IF AN ANTIBODY MOLECULE IS DIGESTED WITH PAPAIN, CLEAVAGE OCCURS ABOVE THE DISULFIDE BONDS THAT
HOLD THE HEAVY CHAINS TOGETHER. THIS GENERATES 3 SEPARATE FRAGMENTS, TWO OF WHICH ARE CALLED FAB
(FRAGMENT ANTIGEN BINDING), AND ONE OF WHICH IS CALLED FC (FRAGMENT CRYSTALLIZABLE).
1841
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE CLEAVAGE OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN BY PAPAIN.
CLEAVAGE OF THE ANTIBODY MOLECULE WITH PEPSIN GENERATES ONE LARGE FRAGMENT CALLED F(AB´)2 AND A
DIGESTED FC FRAGMENT.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE CLEAVAGE OF IMMUNOGLOBULIN BY PEPSIN.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
DURING DEVELOPMENT, THYMIC CELLS RECOGNIZING SELF-ANTIGENS ARE REMOVED TO PREVENT
AUTOIMMUNITY. WHICH GENE AMONG THESE IS INVOLVED IN THE PROCESS?
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE PROCESS IS CALLED CENTRAL TOLERANCE AND THE AIRE (AUTOIMMUNE REGULATOR) PROTEIN IS
NECESSARY FOR THIS PROCESS.
IMMATURE SELF-REACTIVE T AND B LYMPHOCYTE CLONES RECOGNIZE SELF-ANTIGENS DURING THEIR MATURATION
IN THE CENTRAL LYMPHOID ORGANS (THYMUS FOR T CELLS, BONE MARROW FOR B CELLS). THEY ARE KILLED OR
RENDERED HARMLESS.
THE REMOVAL OF SELF REACTING T LYMPHOCYTES IN THE THYMUS IS CALLED NEGATIVE SELECTION/ DELETION. FOR
THIS PROCESS, AIRE PROTEIN IS NEEDED. MUTATIONS IN THE AIRE GENE RESULTS IN AUTOIMMUNE
DISORDERS (AUTOIMMUNE POLYENDOCRINOPATHY).
B CELLS UNDERGO A PROCESS CALLED RECEPTOR EDITING. WHEN DEVELOPING B CELLS ENCOUNTER AN ANTIGEN, IT
FORMULATES A CHANGE IN THE RECEPTOR THAT MAKES THE ANTIGEN UNRECOGNIZABLE. SELF-REACTING B CELLS
CAN ALSO UNDERGO APOPTOSIS.

questions.prompt: AMONG THESE, WHICH CELLS HAVE MHC CLASS II?
options: B CELLS, DENDRITIC CELLS, MONONUCLEAR PHAGOCYTES

PLATELETS
Answer Key

questions.answer: B CELLS, DENDRITIC CELLS, MONONUCLEAR PHAGOCYTES
questions.explanation:
CLASS II MAJOR HISTOCOMPATIBILITY COMPLEX (MHC) MOLECULES ARE MAINLY EXPRESSED
ON MACROPHAGES, B LYMPHOCYTES, AND DENDRITIC CELLS. THESE CELLS PRESENT INGESTED ANTIGENS TO
T-CELLS.
THE FUNCTION OF MHC MOLECULES IS TO DISPLAY PEPTIDE FRAGMENTS OF PROTEIN ANTIGENS FOR RECOGNITION
BY ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC T CELLS. IN HUMANS, THE MHC MOLECULES ARE CALLED HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGENS
(HLA) BECAUSE THEY WERE INITIALLY DETECTED ON LEUKOCYTES BY THE BINDING OF ANTIBODIES. THE
COMBINATION OF HLA ALLELES IN EACH INDIVIDUAL IS CALLED THE HLA HAPLOTYPE.
THE GENES ENCODING HLA MOLECULES ARE CLUSTERED ON THE SHORT ARM OF CHROMOSOME 6.
USES OF MHC/ HLA TYPING INCLUDE:
- ANTHROPOLOGY
- TRANSFUSION
- PATERNITY TESTING
- FORENSIC SCIENCE
- TRANSPLANTATION
- DISEASE CORRELATION

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: TOLUIDINE BLUE STAINING IS USED IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF WHICH OF THESE CELLS?
questions.explanation:
TOLUIDINE BLUE IS THE SPECIAL STAIN FOR MAST CELLS.
IT STAINS THE MAST CELLS VIOLET IN A BLUE BACKGROUND.
MAST CELLS MAY BE DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE FROM LYMPHOCYTES IN ROUTINE, HEMATOXYLIN, AND
EOSIN–STAINED SECTIONS, AND SPECIAL METACHROMATIC STAINS (TOLUIDINE BLUE OR GIEMSA) ARE USED TO
VISUALIZE THEIR GRANULES.
OTHER OPTIONS:
MELANOCYTES CAN BE IDENTIFIED USING MELAN A/ MART-1, MITF, S100, HMB45.
MACROPHAGES CAN BE IDENTIFIED USING MITF, SOX 10, CD31, CD68.
FIBROBLAST CAN BE IDENTIFIED USING FIBROBLAST SURFACE ANTIGEN, VIMENTIN, HSP47,
FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC PROTEIN 1.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: T(11,22) IS BEST DIAGNOSED BY _______
questions.explanation:
T(11,22) CAN BE BEST DETECTED USING FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH).
T(11,22) IS A CHARACTERISTIC TRANSLOCATION GIVING RISE TO EWING'S SARCOMA. IN 85 TO 90 PERCENT OF
CASES OF EWING SARCOMA FAMILY OF TUMORS (EFT), A RECURRENT CHROMOSOMAL TRANSLOCATION,
T(11;22)(Q24;Q12), FUSES THE 5' PORTION OF THE EWSR1 GENE ON CHROMOSOME 22 TO THE 3' PORTION OF
THE FLI1 GENE ON CHROMOSOME 11.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: GAMMA DELTA T CELL(γδ TCRS) RECEPTORS RECOGNIZES
questions.explanation:
γδ TCRS (T-CELL RECEPTORS) HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO RECOGNIZE LIPID ANTIGENS PRESENTED BY CD1D IN AN
MHC-INDEPENDENT MANNER
T LYMPHOCYTES DEVELOP IN THE THYMUS FROM PRECURSORS THAT ARISE FROM HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS.
MATURE T CELLS ARE FOUND IN THE BLOOD, WHERE THEY CONSTITUTE 60% TO 70% OF LYMPHOCYTES, AND IN
T-CELL ZONES OF PERIPHERAL LYMPHOID ORGANS.
- EACH T CELL RECOGNIZES A SPECIFIC CELL-BOUND ANTIGEN BY MEANS OF AN ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC T-CELL
RECEPTOR (TCR).
- IN APPROXIMATELY 95% OF T CELLS, THE TCR CONSISTS OF A DISULFIDE-LINKED HETERODIMER MADE UP OF
α AND β POLYPEPTIDE CHAIN, EACH HAVING A VARIABLE (ANTIGEN-BINDING) REGION AND A CONSTANT REGION.
1853
- THE αβ TCR RECOGNIZES PEPTIDE ANTIGENS THAT ARE PRESENTED BY MAJOR HISTOCOMPATIBILITY COMPLEX
(MHC) MOLECULES ON THE SURFACES OF ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS. BY LIMITING THE SPECIFICITY OF T CELLS
FOR PEPTIDES DISPLAYED BY CELL SURFACE MHC MOLECULES, CALLED MHC RESTRICTION, THE IMMUNE SYSTEM
ENSURES THAT T CELLS SEE ONLY CELL-ASSOCIATED ANTIGENS.
-
- A SMALL POPULATION OF MATURE T CELLS EXPRESSES ANOTHER TYPE OF TCR COMPOSED OF γ AND δ
POLYPEPTIDE CHAINS. THE γδ TCR RECOGNIZES LIPIDS, AND SMALL MOLECULES, WITHOUT A REQUIREMENT FOR
DISPLAY BY MHC PROTEINS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS CANCER THAT LEAST COMMONLY SPREADS BY LYMPHATIC ROUTE?
questions.explanation:
BASAL CELL CARCINOMA IS A LOCALLY AGGRESSIVE TUMOR THAT RARELY SPREADS BY THE LYMPHATIC ROUTE.
MUTATIONS IN SONIC HEDGEHOG PATHWAY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH IT.
IT PRESENTS AS SMALL, SLOWLY GROWING PEARLY NODULE, OFTEN WITH TORTUOUS TELANGIECTATIC VESSELS ON ITS
SURFACE, ROLLED BORDERS, AND A CENTRAL CRUST (NODULAR BCC).
THE OCCASIONAL PRESENCE OF MELANIN IN THIS VARIANT OF NODULAR BCC (PIGMENTED BCC) MAY LEAD TO
CONFUSION WITH MELANOMA.
THE MOST COMMON SITE IS THE INNER CANTHUS OF THE EYE.
BASAL CELL CARCINOMA DOES NOT SHOW LYMPHATIC OR HEMATOGENOUS METASTASIS. IT IS PRIMARILY LOCALLY
INVASIVE.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS CORRECT CONCERNING TRANSFUSION OF THE BLOOD RECEIVED FROM BLOOD BANK?
options: IT SHOULD BE STARTED WITHIN 4 HOURS OF RECEIVING IT FROM THE BLOOD BANK.
IT SHOULD BE COMPLETED WITHIN 4 HOURS OF RECEIVING FROM THE BLOOD BANK.
NO SUCH TIME RESTRAINT AND CAN BE DONE ANYTIME.
IT SHOULD BE COMPLETED WITHIN 6 HOURS OF RECEIVING FROM THE BLOOD BANK.
questions.answer: IT SHOULD BE COMPLETED WITHIN 4 HOURS OF RECEIVING FROM THE BLOOD BANK.
questions.explanation:
BLOOD RECEIVED FROM BLOOD BANK SHOULD BE COMPLETELY TRANSFUSED WITHIN 4 HOURS OF RECEIVING.
PRINCIPLES OF BLOOD ADMINISTRATION:
- ALL BLOOD PRODUCTS SHOULD BE GIVEN THROUGH AN APPROPRIATE BLOOD ADMINISTRATION SET CONTAINING A
FILTER.
- A CAREFUL ASEPTIC TECHNIQUE SHOULD BE PRACTISED AT ALL TIMES.
- VITAL SIGNS SHOULD BE DOCUMENTED BEFORE AND AFTER TRANSFUSION AND AS CLINICALLY REQUIRED. FOR THE
FIRST 15 MINUTES AFTER THE INFUSION HAS BEGUN, THE PATIENT SHOULD BE KEPT UNDER CLOSE OBSERVATION
TO DETECT ANY SIGNS OF A SERIOUS TRANSFUSION REACTION. IF NONE IS OBSERVED, THE INFUSION RATE MAY BE
INCREASED.
- ONE UNIT OF RED CELLS IS OFTEN GIVEN IN 1 TO 4 HOURS, DEPENDING ON THE AMOUNT TO BE TRANSFUSED
AND ON THE PATIENT’S CARDIOVASCULAR STATUS. INFUSION OF A UNIT FOR LONGER THAN 4 HOURS IS NOT
RECOMMENDED, AS THERE IS A RISK OF BACTERIAL PROLIFERATION BECAUSE THE OPENED UNIT IS AT ROOM
TEMPERATURE.
- NO OTHER SOLUTION AND NO MEDICATION SHOULD BE ADDED TO OR INFUSED THROUGH THE SAME TUBING AS A
BLOOD PRODUCT.
1854
- RINGER’S LACTATE OR OTHER SOLUTIONS CONTAINING CALCIUM MUST NEVER BE ADDED TO A BLOOD PRODUCT
BECAUSE THE CALCIUM PRESENT LEADS TO COAGULATION.
- AFTER THE TRANSFUSION HAS BEEN COMPLETED, THE TRANSFUSION TAG OR RECORD SHOULD BECOME PART OF
THE PATIENT’S CHART.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WORKING IN A FACTORY PRESENTED WITH LUNG FIBROSIS AND THICKENING OF PLEURA. BIOPSY
WAS DONE. WHAT IS DIAGNOSIS FROM THE HISTOPATHOLOGY PICTURE?
questions.explanation:
THIS CLINICAL SCENARIO AND IMAGE SHOWING TYPICAL ASBESTOS BODIES ARE SUGGESTIVE OF ASBESTOSIS.
ASBESTOSIS IS A TYPE OF PNEUMOCONIOSIS ASSOCIATED WITH ASBESTOS EXPOSURE. THE DISEASE-CAUSING
CAPABILITIES OF THE DIFFERENT FORMS OF ASBESTOS DEPEND ON CONCENTRATION, SIZE, SHAPE, AND
SOLUBILITY. THIS CONDITION IS MARKED BY DIFFUSE PULMONARY INTERSTITIAL FIBROSIS.
ASBESTOS BODIES ARE A TYPICAL FINDING. THEY ARE GOLDEN BROWN, FUSIFORM, OR BEADED RODS WITH A
TRANSLUCENT CENTER. THEY CONSIST OF ASBESTOS FIBERS COATED WITH AN IRON-CONTAINING PROTEINACEOUS
MATERIAL AND ARISE WHEN THESE FIBERS ARE PHAGOCYTOSED BY MACROPHAGES.
1855
OTHER INORGANIC PARTICULATES MAY BECOME COATED WITH SIMILAR IRON-PROTEIN COMPLEXES AND ARE
CALLED FERRUGINOUS BODIES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 65-YEAR-OLD HIV-POSITIVE MAN PRESENTED WITH FEVER AND BREATHLESSNESS FOR 2 WEEKS. IMAGING
SHOWS DENSE INFILTRATION IN THE LOWER LOBE AND THE LUNG BIOPSY SHOWED THE FOLLOWING FINDING.
SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS A CYTOMEGALIC PNEUMOCYTE CONTAINING CHARACTERISTIC INTRANUCLEAR
BASOPHILIC INCLUSION SURROUNDED BY A CLEAR HALO KNOWN AS OWL’S EYE APPEARANCE. ALONG WITH THE
GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO, IT IS SUGGESTIVE OF CYTOMEGALOVIRUS (CMV) PNEUMONIA.

- IMMUNOCOMPETENT INDIVIDUALS - ASYMPTOMATIC OR MONONUCLEOSIS-LIKE INFECTION
- NEONATES - DEVASTATING SYSTEMIC INFECTIONS
- IMMUNOSUPPRESSED INDIVIDUALS - SERIOUS, LIFE-THREATENING, DISSEMINATED CMV INFECTIONS OF THE
LUNGS (PNEUMONITIS) AND GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT (COLITIS)

questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS A TRUE STATEMENT CONCERNING APOPTOSIS?
options: THERE IS ENZYMATIC DIGESTION OF CELLULAR CONTENTS
IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH ADJACENT INFLAMMATION
questions.explanation:
THE PLASMA MEMBRANE REMAINS INTACT IN APOPTOSIS.
APOPTOSIS LITERALLY MEANS FALLING-OFF IN GREEK. IT IS A PATHWAY OF PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH.
APOPTOTIC CELLS BREAK UP INTO FRAGMENTS CALLED APOPTOTIC BODIES. THESE APOPTOTIC BODIES HAVE
INTACT PLASMA MEMBRANE BUT ALTERED STRUCTURES. HENCE, THEY ARE SUBJECTED TO PHAGOCYTOSIS WITHOUT
ELICITING INFLAMMATION.
NECROSIS IS AN UNPROGRAMMED FORM OF CELL DEATH THAT INCLUDES:
- ENZYMATIC DIGESTION
- ADJACENT INFLAMMATION
- KARYOLYSIS

questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH ABDOMINAL DISTENSION AND INTERMITTENT FEVER. PERIPHERAL SMEAR
FINDINGS ARE NORMAL. A TUMOR IS RESECTED AND THE HISTOPATHOLOGY IMAGE OF THE RESECTED LYMPH

questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE SHOWING FOLLICULAR HYPERPLASIA OF LYMPH
NODES ARE SUGGESTIVE OF CASTLEMAN DISEASE.
CASTLEMAN DISEASE (ANGIOFOLLICULAR LYMPH NODE HYPERPLASIA) IS A LYMPHOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDER THAT
CAN BE ASSOCIATED WITH HHV-8 (MULTICENTRIC CASTLEMAN DISEASE OR MCD) OR IDIOPATHIC (UNICENTRIC
CASTLEMAN DISEASE OR UCD)
THERE ARE 3 MAJOR HISTOLOGICAL SUBTYPES:
- HYPERVASCULAR (UCD) -
- LOLLIPOP APPEARANCE - ATROPHIC GERMINAL CENTERS WITH RADIALLY PENETRATING BLOOD VESSELS
- ONION SKIN APPEARANCE OF MANTLE ZONE AROUND GERMINAL CENTERS
- PLASMA CELL SUBTYPE (UCD OR MCD) - HYPERTROPHIC GERMINAL CENTERS, INCREASED VASCULARITY
- MIXED VARIANT (MCD) - MIX OF HYPERVASCULAR AND PLASMA CELL SUBTYPE FEATURES IN THE SAME LYMPH
NODE
THE CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE:
- MULTIPLE ENLARGED LYMPH NODES
- NIGHT SWEATS
- WEIGHT LOSS
- WEAKNESS AND FATIGUE
- HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY
AS THIS CONDITION IS ASSOCIATED WITH ELEVATED LEVELS OF IL-6, THE TREATMENT INVOLVES IL-6 INHIBITORS
LIKE SILTUXIMAB AND TOCILIZUMAB.
NOTE: HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA HAS CHARACTERISTIC REED-STERNBERG CELLS IN THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL
SECTION OF LYMPH NODES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS INVOLVED IN RECOGNITION AND CLEARANCE OF NECROTIC CELLS?
questions.explanation:
INFLAMMASOMES ARE INVOLVED IN THE RECOGNITION AND CLEARANCE OF NECROTIC CELLS.
INFLAMMASOMES ARE INVOLVED IN PYROPTOSIS, A PROCESS OF PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH DISTINCT FROM
APOPTOSIS AND NECROSIS. THIS PROCESS IS DEPENDENT ON CASPASES 1, 4, AND 5 AND IS RESPONSIBLE FOR
KILLING OF INFECTED CELLS. IT OCCURS IN THE FOLLOWING SEQUENCE:
- ACTIVATION OF INFLAMMASOME COMPLEX BY INFECTED CELLS
- THIS CAUSES ACTIVATION OF CASPASE-1
- THIS RESULTS IN GENERATION OF IL-1, WHICH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR FEVER, INFLAMMATION, LEUKOCYTE
RECRUITMENT
OPTION B: TOLL-LIKE RECEPTORS (TLR)- RECOGNIZES MOLECULES SHARED BY PATHOGENS
OPTION C: P-SELECTINS - AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE INITIAL RECRUITMENT OF WBCS AT THE SITE OF
INFLAMMATION & IN PLATELET RECRUITMENT AND AGGREGATION AT THE SITE OF INJURY.

questions.prompt: WHAT IS NARP SYNDROME?
questions.explanation:
NARP SYNDROME - NEUROPATHY ATAXIA RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA SYNDROME IS DESCRIBED AS
A MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION DISORDER.
NARP SYNDROME IS DUE TO A POINT MUTATION OF THE MITOCHONDRIAL ATPASE-6 GENE. IT HAS 2
PHENOTYPES:
- NARP
- MATERNALLY INHERITED LEIGH SYNDROME (MILS)
IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY MODERATE, DIFFUSE CEREBRAL AND CEREBELLAR ATROPHY AND SYMMETRIC LESIONS OF
THE BASAL GANGLIA ON MRI. THE SEVERITY OF THE SYNDROME CORRESPONDS TO THE MUTANT MITOCHONDRIAL
DNA LOAD IN THE TISSUES.

questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE MAXIMUM DURATION FOR TRALI TO OCCUR AFTER BLOOD TRANSFUSION.
questions.explanation:
THE MAXIMUM DURATION FOR TRALI (TRANSFUSION-RELATED ACUTE LUNG INJURY) TO OCCUR AFTER BLOOD
TRANSFUSION IS UPTO 6 HOURS. TRALI IS SUDDEN-ONSET RESPIRATORY FAILURE THAT OCCURS DURING OR SOON
AFTER BLOOD TRANSFUSION.
THE PATHOGENESIS INVOLVES A TWO-HIT HYPOTHESIS:
- PRIMING EVENT - INCREASED SEQUESTRATION AND SENSITIZATION OF NEUTROPHILS IN THE MICROVASCULATURE
OF THE LUNG
- SECOND HIT - THE FACTOR (MOST COMMONLY MHC CLASS I ANTIGENS) PRESENT IN THE TRANSFUSED BLOOD
PRODUCT ACTIVATES THE PRIMED NEUTROPHILS

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LONG-TERM LIMITATION OF CARDIAC TRANSPLANTATION?
questions.explanation:
THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LONG-TERM LIMITATION OF CARDIAC TRANSPLANTATION IS ALLOGRAFT
ARTERIOPATHY.
COMPLICATIONS FOLLOWING CARDIAC TRANSPLANTATION:
1938
ALLOGRAFT REJECTION: IT IS THE PRIMARY CONCERN THAT REQUIRES CLOSE SURVEILLANCE. BOTH CLASSIC CELLULAR
REJECTION AND ANTIBODY-MEDIATED REJECTION IS RECOGNIZED. CELLULAR REJECTION IS CHARACTERIZED BY
INTERSTITIAL LYMPHOCYTIC INFLAMMATION, WITH ASSOCIATED MYOCYTE DAMAGE.
ALLOGRAFT ARTERIOPATHY: IT IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LONG-TERM LIMITATION FOR CARDIAC
TRANSPLANTATION. IT IS A LATE, PROGRESSIVE, DIFFUSELY STENOSING INTIMAL PROLIFERATION IN THE CORONARY
ARTERIES, LEADING TO ISCHEMIC INJURY. IT CAN LEAD TO SILENT MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION SINCE TRANSPLANT
PATIENTS HAVE DENERVATED HEARTS AND DO NOT EXPERIENCE ANGINA. PROGRESSIVE CONGESTIVE HEART
FAILURE AND SUDDEN CARDIAC DEATH CAN ALSO OCCUR.
OTHER POSTOPERATIVE PROBLEMS INCLUDE INFECTION AND MALIGNANCIES, ESPECIALLY EPSTEIN–BARR
VIRUS-ASSOCIATED B-CELL LYMPHOMAS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS ALLOGRAFT ARTERIOPATHY. THERE IS SEVERE DIFFUSE CONCENTRIC INTIMAL

PENTACHROME STAIN, ELASTIN BLACK)

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF AGRANULOCYTOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF AGRANULOCYTOSIS IS DRUG TOXICITY.
CAUSES OF AGRANULOCYTOSIS INCLUDE:
- INADEQUATE OR INEFFECTIVE GRANULOPOIESIS -
- SUPPRESSION OF HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS - APLASTIC ANEMIA, INFILTRATIVE MARROW DISORDERS
1940
- SUPPRESSION OF COMMITTED GRANULOCYTIC PRECURSORS
- INEFFECTIVE HEMATOPOIESIS - MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA, MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROMES
- CONGENITAL CONDITIONS - KOSTMANN SYNDROME
- INCREASED DESTRUCTION OR SEQUESTRATION OF NEUTROPHILS -
- IMMUNOLOGICAL INJURY TO NEUTROPHILS - IDIOPATHIC, SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS, DRUG EXPOSURE
- INCREASED PERIPHERAL UTILIZATION - BACTERIAL, FUNGAL, OR RICKETTSIAL INFECTIONS
- SPLENOMEGALY

questions.prompt: ALL OF THESE ARE CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES OF PANCREATIC CARCINOMA EXCEPT:
options: CIGARETTE SMOKING IS A RISK FACTOR
CARCINOMA OF BODY OF PANCREAS OFTEN PRESENT WITH JAUNDICE
questions.answer: CARCINOMA OF BODY OF PANCREAS OFTEN PRESENT WITH JAUNDICE
questions.explanation:
PATIENTS WITH CARCINOMA OF THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS DEVELOP JAUNDICE DUE TO OBSTRUCTION OF THE
BILIARY TRACT.
CIGARETTE SMOKING DOUBLES THE RISK OF PANCREATIC CANCER AND IS THE LEADING PREVENTABLE CAUSE. THE
CLINICAL FEATURES DEPEND ON THE LOCATION OF THE TUMOR.
- HEAD - PAINLESS, PALPABLE GALLBLADDER WITH MILD JAUNDICE IS SUGGESTIVE OF MALIGNANCY (ACCORDING
TO COURVOISIER'S LAW)
- BODY AND TAIL - MAY REMAIN ASYMPTOMATIC UNTIL LATER STAGES AS THEY DO NOT IMPINGE ON THE BILIARY
TRACT AND DO NOT CAUSE JAUNDICE
OTHER COMMON PATHOLOGICAL FEATURES OF THIS CONDITION ARE:
- DESMOPLASTIC REACTION - GROWTH OF FIBROUS OR CONNECTIVE TISSUE
- PERINEURAL INVASION, AS WELL AS LYMPHATIC AND LARGE VESSEL INVASION

IT IS A BACTERIAL INFECTION CAUSED BY BARTONELLA HENSELAE. IT IS ACQUIRED FOLLOWING CONTACT WITH

- FOLLICULAR HYPERPLASIA WITH CIRCUMSCRIBED CENTRAL STELLATE NECROSIS WITH NEUTROPHILS
- SURROUNDED BY PALISADING HISTIOCYTES (SUPPURATIVE GRANULOMAS)
- SINUSES PACKED WITH MONOCYTOID B CELLS
- USUALLY, THERE ARE NO PERIFOLLICULAR AND INTRAFOLLICULAR EPITHELIOID CELLS

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE MOST CONSISTENT AND PERSISTENT FEATURE OF BLADDER CARCINOMA?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST CONSISTENT AND PERSISTENT FEATURE OF CARCINOMA BLADDER IS PAINLESS HEMATURIA.
BLADDER TUMORS PRODUCE A WIDE RANGE OF CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDING:
- PAINLESS HEMATURIA - CLASSICAL FEATURE AND MAY BE THE ONLY CLINICAL MANIFESTATION
- IRRITATIVE URINARY SYMPTOMS (FREQUENCY, URGENCY, DYSURIA) - DIFFUSE TUMORS OR TUMORS AT THE

- PYELONEPHRITIS OR HYDRONEPHROSIS - WHEN THE URETERAL ORIFICE IS INVOLVED

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: FEVER OCCURS DURING INFLAMMATION DUE TO ALL EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
HISTAMINE IS INVOLVED IN THE MEDIATION OF VASCULAR EVENTS OF INFLAMMATION, NOT FEVER.
FEVER IS CHARACTERIZED BY AN ELEVATION OF BODY TEMPERATURE, USUALLY BY 1° TO 4°C. IT IS ONE OF THE
MOST PROMINENT MANIFESTATIONS OF THE ACUTE-PHASE RESPONSE, ESPECIALLY IF ASSOCIATED WITH
INFECTION.
SUBSTANCES THAT INDUCE FEVER ARE CALLED PYROGENS. THEY MAY BE EXOGENOUS OR ENDOGENOUS.
- ENDOGENOUS PYROGENS - IL-1, TNF, PROSTAGLANDINS
- EXOGENOUS PYROGENS -
- LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDES OF BACTERIAL WALLS
- THEY STIMULATE LEUKOCYTES TO RELEASE ENDOGENOUS PYROGENS (IL-1 AND TNF)
CYTOKINES RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN CYCLOOXYGENASES THAT CONVERT ARACHIDONIC ACID INTO
PROSTAGLANDINS. THESE PROSTAGLANDINS ARE PRODUCED IN THE VASCULAR AND PERIVASCULAR CELLS OF THE
1943
HYPOTHALAMUS. IN THE HYPOTHALAMUS, THEY STIMULATE THE PRODUCTION OF NEUROTRANSMITTERS THAT
RESET THE TEMPERATURE SETPOINT TO A HIGHER LEVEL. THIS IS ESPECIALLY BY PGE2.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: ANAPLASIA REFERS TO:
options: VARIATION IN CELL SIZE AND SHAPE
REPLACEMENT OF ONE TYPE OF CELL BY OTHER
questions.explanation:
ANAPLASIA REFERS TO A LACK OF DIFFERENTIATION.
THE TERM ANAPLASIA MEANS TO FORM BACKWARD IMPLYING A REVERSAL OF DIFFERENTIATION TO A MORE
PRIMITIVE LEVEL. THE EXTENT TO WHICH NEOPLASTIC CELLS RESEMBLE NORMAL CELLS, BOTH MORPHOLOGICALLY
AND FUNCTIONALLY, IS CALLED DIFFERENTIATION.
ANAPLASIA IS AN IMPORTANT MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURE OF MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION.
THE MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES OF MALIGNANCY INCLUDE:
- ANAPLASIA
- PLEOMORPHISM - VARIATION IN THE SIZE AND SHAPE OF CELLS
- INCREASED N: C RATIO (NUCLEUS: CYTOPLASMIC RATIO) - AROUND 1:4 IN NORMAL CELLS, INCREASES TO 1:1 IN
MALIGNANT CELLS
- HYPERCHROMASIA - COARSELY CLUMPED AND DARKLY STAINED CHROMATIN WITHIN IRREGULAR NUCLEI
- INCREASED MITOSIS - ATYPICAL, BIZARRE MITOTIC FIGURES
- LOSS OF POLARITY - SHEETS OR LARGE MASSES OF TUMOR CELLS GROW IN AN ANARCHIC, DISORGANIZED FASHION

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS AN OPSONIN?
questions.explanation:
C3B FUNCTIONS AS AN OPSONIN.
OPSONIZATION IS THE PROCESS OF COATING A FOREIGN PARTICLE AND PREPARING IT FOR PHAGOCYTOSIS. THE
SUBSTANCES INVOLVED IN THIS PROCESS ARE CALLED OPSONINS AND INCLUDE:
- MANNOSE-BINDING LECTIN
- C3B, C4B, C5B
- IGM AND FC RECEPTOR OF IGG
- CRP
- FIBRINOGEN
ELIE METCHNIKOFF WAS THE FIRST PERSON TO DESCRIBE THE PROCESS OF PHAGOCYTOSIS, AND IS HENCE KNOWN
AS THE FATHER OF INNATE IMMUNITY.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: CD-59 IS INVOLVED IN ____________.
questions.explanation:
CD-59 IS INVOLVED IN PAROXYSMAL NOCTURNAL HEMOGLOBINURIA (PNH).
1944
FACTORS REGULATING COMPLEMENTARY PATHWAYS:
- DAF OR CD-55 INHIBITS C3 ACTIVATION
- MIRL OR CD-59 INHIBITS THE MEMBRANE-ACTIVATING COMPLEX
IN PNH, DAF AND MIRL ARE ABSENT. HENCE, THERE WILL BE UNREGULATED COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF PNH INCLUDE:
- INTRAVASCULAR HEMOGLOBINURIA - COLA-COLORED URINE
- PANCYTOPENIA + HYPERCELLULAR BONE MARROW
- THROMBOSIS (IF HEPATIC VEIN INVOLVED → BUDD–CHIARI SYNDROME)
DIAGNOSIS OF PNH IS BY THE FOLLOWING METHODS:
- HAM’S TEST - ACIDIFIED SERUM LYSIS
- SUCROSE LYSIS TEST
- FLOW CYTOMETRY - ABSENCE OF CD 55 AND CD 59 ON RBC
ECULIZUMAB IS USED TO ALLEVIATE THE HEMOLYSIS ASSOCIATED WITH PNH AND ITS SEQUELAE. ECULIZUMAB
DOES NOT ALTER THE UNDERLYING DEFECT OF THE DISEASE.
NOTE: FDA HAS RECENTLY APPROVED PEGCETACOPLAN FOR ADULTS WITH PNH WHICH ACTS BY BINDING TO
COMPLEMENT PROTEIN C3 AND INCREASING HEMOGLOBIN CONCENTRATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: LEIDEN MUTATION IS OF FACTOR:
questions.explanation:
LEIDEN MUTATION IS A SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE MUTATION THAT OCCURS IN FACTOR V. THIS IS NAMED AFTER THE
CITY IN THE NETHERLANDS WHERE IT WAS DISCOVERED.
OF THE INHERITED CAUSES OF HYPERCOAGULABILITY, POINT MUTATIONS IN THE FACTOR V GENE AND
PROTHROMBIN GENE ARE THE MOST COMMON.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THESE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT DETERMINANT OF MALIGNANT POTENTIAL IN THE
PAPILLARY TYPE OF RENAL TUMOR?
options:
PART OF KIDNEY INVOLVED
Answer Key

questions.explanation:
THE MOST IMPORTANT DETERMINANT OF MALIGNANT POTENTIAL IN THE PAPILLARY TYPE OF RENAL TUMOR IS THE
SIZE OF THE TUMOR.
THE PAPILLARY TYPE OF RENAL TUMORS INCLUDES:
- RENAL PAPILLARY ADENOMA (≤ 1.5 CM)
- PAPILLARY TYPE OF RENAL CELL CARCINOMA (RCC) - > 1.5 CM
SMALL RENAL PAPILLARY GROWTHS ARE FAIRLY COMMON AND INCIDENTALLY FOUND. RULING OUT OF MALIGNANCY
IS ONE OF THE PROCESSES CARRIED OUT DURING THE EVALUATION OF DONOR TRANSPLANT KIDNEYS.
1945
PAPILLARY RENAL CELL CARCINOMA (RCC) IS THE SECOND MOST COMMON TYPE OF RENAL CELL CARCINOMA AND
IT ARISES FROM PROXIMAL TUBULES. IT CAN BE MULTIFOCAL OR BILATERAL. IT IS TYPICALLY HEMORRHAGIC AND
CYSTIC, ESPECIALLY WHEN LARGE.
IT IS OFTEN A CIRCUMSCRIBED TUMOR COMPOSED OF PAPILLAE FORMED BY DELICATE FIBROVASCULAR CORES THAT
OFTEN CONTAIN FOAMY MACROPHAGES AND PSAMMOMA BODIES.
IT HAS TWO HISTOLOGICAL TYPES:
- TYPE 1 PAPILLARY RCC - SINGLE LAYER OF CELLS ON THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE AND LOW-GRADE NUCLEAR
FEATURES
- TYPE 2 PAPILLARY RCC - PSEUDOSTRATIFICATION OF CELLS AND USUALLY HAS HIGH-GRADE NUCLEAR FEATURES

questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT AN INTERMEDIATE FILAMENT?
questions.explanation:
TUBULIN IS A PART OF MICROTUBULES AND IS NOT AN INTERMEDIATE FILAMENT.
THERE ARE THREE MAJOR CLASSES OF CYTOSKELETAL PROTEINS: MICROFILAMENTS, INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS, AND
MICROTUBULES.
1. ACTIN MICROFILAMENTS:
THESE FIBRILS FORMED FROM THE GLOBULAR PROTEIN ACTIN (G-ACTIN) NONCOVALENTLY POLYMERIZE INTO LONG
FILAMENTS (F-ACTIN) THAT INTERTWINE TO FORM DOUBLE-STRANDED HELICES.
2. INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS:
THESE ROPE-LIKE INTERMEDIATE FILAMENT FIBERS ARE FOUND PREDOMINANTLY IN A POLYMERIZED FORM
WITHIN CELLS AND DO NOT POSSESS THE QUALITY OF ACTIVE REORGANIZATION LIKE ACTIN AND MICROTUBULES.
THEY ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR CELLULAR TENSILE STRENGTH, WHICH ALLOWS THE CELLS TO BEAR MECHANICAL STRESS.
3. MICROTUBULES:
THESE ARE FORMED BY NON-COVALENT POLYMERIZATION OF A DIMER OF TWO GLOBULAR PROTEINS,
ALPHA-TUBULIN, AND BETA-TUBULIN. THE MICROTUBULES IN MOST CELLS EXTEND OUTWARD FROM A
MICROTUBULE-ORGANIZING CENTER (MTOC), IN WHICH THE MINUS ENDS OF MICROTUBULES ARE ANCHORED.1878

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH TEST EVALUATES THE EXTRINSIC PATHWAY.
questions.explanation:
PROTHROMBIN TIME (PT) EVALUATES THE EXTRINSIC PATHWAY OF COAGULATION.
PT MEASURES THE CLOTTING TIME OF PLASMA IN THE PRESENCE OF AN OPTIMAL CONCENTRATION OF TISSUE
EXTRACT (THROMBOPLASTIN). THIS INDICATES THE OVERALL EFFICIENCY OF THE EXTRINSIC CLOTTING SYSTEM.
CAUSES OF PROLONGED PT:
- ADMINISTRATION OF ORAL ANTICOAGULANT DRUGS - VITAMIN K ANTAGONISTS
- LIVER DISEASE - OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE
- VITAMIN K DEFICIENCY
- DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULATION
- PREVIOUSLY UNDIAGNOSED FACTOR VII, X, V OR PROTHROMBIN DEFICIENCY OR DEFECT (RARE)
ACTIVATED PARTIAL THROMBOPLASTIN TIME (APTT) MEASURES THE CLOTTING TIME OF PLASMA AFTER THE
ACTIVATION OF CONTACT FACTORS AND THE ADDITION OF PHOSPHOLIPID AND CACL2, BUT WITHOUT ADDED TISSUE
THROMBOPLASTIN. IT INDICATES THE OVERALL EFFICIENCY OF THE INTRINSIC PATHWAY.
CAUSES OF PROLONGED APTT:
- DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULATION
- LIVER DISEASE
- MASSIVE TRANSFUSION WITH PLASMA-DEPLETED RED BLOOD CELLS
- ADMINISTRATION OF OR CONTAMINATION WITH HEPARIN OR OTHER ANTICOAGULANTS
- A CIRCULATING ANTICOAGULANT (INHIBITOR)
- DEFICIENCY OF A COAGULATION FACTOR OTHER THAN FACTOR VII
- INTAKE OF ORAL ANTICOAGULANT DRUGS
- VITAMIN K DEFICIENCY

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 58-YEAR-OLD MAN DIED 24 HOURS AFTER THE ONSET OF SUBSTERNAL CHEST PAIN RADIATING TO THE LEFT
ARM. ON AUTOPSY, AN ATHEROMATOUS PLAQUE WAS SEEN OBSTRUCTING THE LEFT ANTERIOR DESCENDING
ARTERY. INDICATE WHICH TYPE OF CALCIFICATION IS MOST LIKELY TO BE SEEN IN THIS CONDITION.
questions.explanation:
ATHEROMATOUS PLAQUES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH DYSTROPHIC CALCIFICATION. THIS IS SEEN IN THE PRESENCE
OF NORMAL CALCIUM LEVELS IN THE SERUM.
THE DEPOSITION OF CALCIUM IN DEAD OR DYING TISSUES IS CALLED DYSTROPHIC CALCIFICATION. ALTHOUGH IT
OCCURS IN THE PRESENCE OF NORMAL SERUM CALCIUM, IT CAN BE WORSENED BY HYPERCALCEMIA.
DYSTROPHIC CALCIFICATION IS SEEN IN AREAS OF NECROSIS OF ANY TYPE. SOME EXAMPLES INCLUDE ATHEROMAS
OF ADVANCED ATHEROSCLEROSIS AND AREAS OF CASEOUS NECROSIS IN TUBERCULOSIS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: HEPCIDIN INHIBITS IRON TRANSFER FROM THE ENTEROCYTE TO THE PLASMA BY BINDING TO ________
questions.explanation:
1880
HEPCIDIN INHIBITS IRON TRANSFER FROM THE ENTEROCYTE TO PLASMA BY BINDING TO FERROPORTIN.
HEPCIDIN IS RELEASED BY THE LIVER IN RESPONSE TO INCREASES IN INTRAHEPATIC IRON LEVELS. IT INHIBITS
IRON TRANSFER FROM THE ENTEROCYTE TO PLASMA BY BINDING TO FERROPORTIN AND CAUSING IT TO BE
ENDOCYTOSED AND DEGRADED. AS A RESULT, IRON BECOMES TRAPPED WITHIN DUODENAL CELLS IN THE FORM OF
MUCOSAL FERRITIN AND IS LOST AS THESE CELLS ARE SLOUGHED.
NOTE: IN HEREDITARY HEMOCHROMATOSIS, THERE WILL BE IMPAIRED HEPCIDIN SYNTHESIS RESULTING IN
INCREASED IRON ABSORPTION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A CKD PATIENT HAD TO UNDERGO DIALYSIS AND HIS HB WAS 5.2GM/DL. SO TWO BLOOD TRANSFUSIONS
WERE TO BE GIVEN. THE FIRST BAG WAS COMPLETED IN 2 HOURS. THE SECOND WAS STARTED AND IN THE
MIDWAY, HE DEVELOPED SHORTNESS OF BREATH AND HYPERTENSION. VITALS WERE BP - 180/120 MMHG
AND PULSE RATE - 110/MIN. SPECIFY THE CAUSE.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF TRANSFUSION-ASSOCIATED CIRCULATORY OVERLOAD (TACO).
TACO IS CAUSED BY RAPID OR EXCESS TRANSFUSION OF RED CELL PREPARATIONS OR PLASMA PRODUCTS. THIS
CONDITION IS CHARACTERIZED BY:
- DYSPNEA WITH O2% <90 AT ROOM AIR
- BILATERAL INFILTRATES ON CHEST X-RAY
- SYSTOLIC HYPERTENSION
- ELEVATION OF BRAIN NATRIURETIC PEPTIDE, 1.5 TIMES THAT OF PRE-TRANSFUSION LEVELS
IT CAN BE PREVENTED BY ADMINISTERING THE TRANSFUSION SLOWLY, AT THE RATE OF 1 TO 2 ML OF BLOOD/KG OF
BODY WEIGHT PER HOUR. DIURETICS ARE ALSO USED IF NECESSARY.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WHO RECEIVES RECURRENT TRANSFUSIONS FOR THALASSEMIA DEVELOPS FEVER AND CHILLS DURING
THIS TIME. THERE IS NO EVIDENCE OF HEMOLYSIS. WHICH OF THESE MEASURES CAN DECREASE
THE RATE OF TRANSFUSION REACTIONS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF FEBRILE NON-HEMOLYTIC TRANSFUSION REACTION (FNHTR). SUCH
REACTIONS CAN BE PREVENTED BY USING LEUKOREDUCED RBCS.
1881
REMOVAL OF LEUKOCYTES FROM THE BLOOD IS CALLED LEUKOREDUCTION. IT IS DONE BEFORE STORAGE TO
PREVENT CYTOKINE FORMATION.
FNHTR MAY OCCUR DUE TO THE FOLLOWING:
- SENSITIZATION TO THE WBC ANTIGENS BY PREVIOUS BLOOD TRANSFUSIONS OR PREGNANCY
- CYTOKINES PRODUCED BY THE DONOR LEUKOCYTES DURING STORAGE
- BACTERIAL CONTAMINATION
NOTE: LUSPATERCEPT IS AN ERYTHROID MATURATION AGENT, A RECEPTOR FUSION PROTEIN CONSISTING OF A
MODIFIED EXTRACELLULAR DOMAIN OF HUMAN ACTIVIN RECEPTOR TYPE-2B LINKED TO THE HUMAN IG-G1 FC
DOMAIN. THE DRUG WAS RECENTLY APPROVED BY THE FDA FOR THE TREATMENT OF TRANSFUSION-DEPENDENT
THALASSEMIA.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IF DNA IS DAMAGED IN THE CELL CYCLE, WHAT GENE CAUSES CELL CYCLE ARREST?
questions.explanation:
IF THE DNA IS DAMAGED IN THE CELL CYCLE, THE P53 GENE CAUSES ARREST OF THE CELL CYCLE IN G1 PHASE TO
PROVIDE TIME FOR DNA REPAIR. IN CASE THE DNA DAMAGE COULD NOT BE REPAIRED, P53 TRIGGERS
APOPTOSIS.
IN CONDITIONS WHERE THERE IS MUTATION IN P53 GENE, THE CELLS WITH DAMAGED DNA CONTINUE TO
REPLICATE AND THUS MAY UNDERGO NEOPLASTIC TRANSFORMATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT A HEMOSTATIC AGENT?
questions.explanation:
BORIC ACID IS NOT A HEMOSTATIC AGENT.
TOPICAL HEMOSTATIC AGENTS USED IN PRACTICE INCLUDE:
- HEMOSTATIC FIELD DRESSINGS
- SURGICAL HEMOSTATIC AGENTS
1. THE HEMOSTATIC FIELD DRESSINGS ARE THE GRANULAR AND GAUZE-BASED AGENTS WHICH ARE USED TO
FACILITATE COAGULATION AND HEMOSTASIS. THE ACTIVE INGREDIENTS USED IN VARIOUS HEMOSTATIC FIELD
DRESSINGS ARE KAOLIN, MINERAL ZEOLITE, AND CHITOSAN.
2. THE SURGICAL HEMOSTATIC AGENTS ARE FURTHER DIVIDED INTO THE FOLLOWING GROUPS BASED ON THE
NATURE OF THE AGENT:
- CAUSTIC AGENTS: THEY ACT BY CAUSING LOCAL TISSUE DESTRUCTION, WHICH LEADS TO PROTEIN COAGULATION
AND PRECIPITATION. THIS FURTHER LEADS TO THROMBUS FORMATION AND SEALING OF THE SMALL BLOOD VESSELS.
THE AGENTS INCLUDE MONSEL SOLUTION (A20% FERRIC NITRATE SOLUTION), SILVER NITRATE, AND ALUMINUM
CHLORIDE.
- BIOLOGICAL PHYSICAL AGENTS: THEY ACT BY PROMOTING PLATELET ACTIVATION AND FORMATION OF
THREE-DIMENSIONAL MATRIX FOR THE FORMATION OF CLOTS. THESE AGENTS ARE USED IN SEVERAL OPERATIONS
INCLUDING NEUROSURGICAL, ORTHOPEDIC, THORACIC, ABDOMINAL, AND VASCULAR PROCEDURES. THE AGENTS
INCLUDE GELATIN, OXIDIZED CELLULOSE, AND MICROFIBRILLAR COLLAGEN.
1882
- PHYSIOLOGIC AGENTS: THESE AGENTS ACTIVATE A SPECIFIC STEP OF THE COAGULATION CASCADE AND PROMOTES
THE CLOT FORMATION. THESE AGENTS INCLUDE THROMBIN AND FIBRIN GLUE/SEALANT.
- COMBINATION OR POLYMER AGENTS: THESE AGENTS INCLUDE SEVERAL DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF THE
ABOVE AGENTS AND VARIOUS SYNTHETIC HEMOSTATIC AGENTS. EXAMPLES INCLUDE GELATIN-THROMBIN AGENT,
POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL HYDROGEL, AND GLUTARALDEHYDE CROSS-LINKED ALBUMIN.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: ACUTE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE IS NOT SEEN IN:
questions.explanation:
AN INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE IS NOT SEEN IN APOPTOSIS. IN THIS PROCESS, THE CELL MEMBRANE REMAINS
INTACT. HENCE, THERE IS NO LEAKAGE OF CELL CONTENTS AND NO SURROUNDING INFLAMMATION.
ON THE OTHER HAND, OTHER FORMS OF CELL DEATH INCLUDING NECROSIS, NECROPTOSIS, AND
PYROPTOSIS INVOLVE THE DISINTEGRATION OF THE CELL MEMBRANE. THIS CAUSES THE CELL CONTENTS TO LEAK
OUT OF THE CELL LEADING TO AN ACUTE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
AN AFFECTED MALE DOES NOT HAVE AFFECTED CHILDREN BUT AN AFFECTED FEMALE ALWAYS HAS AFFECTED
CHILDREN. TYPE OF INHERITANCE?
questions.explanation:
IN MITOCHONDRIAL INHERITANCE, IF THE MOTHER IS AFFECTED AND THE FATHER IS NORMAL, THEN ALL THEIR
CHILDREN (BOTH MALE AND FEMALE) WILL BE AFFECTED. HOWEVER, CHILDREN BORN TO AN AFFECTED FATHER AND
A NORMAL MOTHER WILL NOT BE AFFECTED.
THE MITOCHONDRIAL INHERITANCE PATTERN IS AS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE BELOW:
1883
THE UNIQUE FEATURE OF MITOCHONDRIAL INHERITANCE IS MATERNAL INHERITANCE, AS THE DISEASE IS
TRANSMITTED THROUGH THE AFFECTED MITOCHONDRIAL DNA (MTDNA), WHICH IS DERIVED FROM THE
MATERNAL MITOCHONDRIA.
THE OVUM CONTAINS SEVERAL MITOCHONDRIA, WHILE THE SPERMATOZOA HAS VERY FEW MITOCHONDRIA IF
PRESENT. HENCE, THE MITOCHONDRIAL DNA OF THE ZYGOTE IS ENTIRELY DERIVED FROM THE OVUM.
THEREFORE, AFFECTED MOTHER TRANSMITS THE DISEASE TO ALL THE OFFSPRINGS (BOTH MALE AND FEMALE), AND
ONLY THE DAUGHTERS OF THE AFFECTED MOTHER, WILL FURTHER TRANSMIT THE DISEASE.
CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES OF MITOCHONDRIAL INHERITANCE:
- THE MITOCHONDRIAL DNA ENCODES ENZYMES REQUIRED FOR OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION. THEREFORE,
ORGANS THAT ARE MOST DEPENDENT ON THE OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION ARE THE ONES MOST AFFECTED IN
DISEASES DUE TO MUTATIONS IN MTDNA. THESE ORGANS INCLUDE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, SKELETAL
MUSCLE, CARDIAC MUSCLE, LIVER, AND KIDNEYS.
- THERE ARE SEVERAL THOUSANDS OF COPIES OF MTDNA IN EACH MITOCHONDRIA, OF WHICH ONLY A FEW
COPIES ARE AFFECTED IN CASE OF MUTATION. THEREFORE, A DISEASED INDIVIDUAL POSSESSES COPIES OF BOTH
WILD TYPE MTDNA AND MUTANT MTDNA IN EACH MITOCHONDRIA THIS PHENOMENON IS CALLED
HETEROPLASMY.
- THE DISEASE MANIFESTS IF A MINIMUM NUMBER OF COPIES OF MUTANT MTDNA ARE PRESENT IN THE
MITOCHONDRIA THAT CAN LEAD TO OXIDATIVE DYSFUNCTION, CALLED THE THRESHOLD EFFECT. IN MOST CASES,
THIS THRESHOLD EFFECT IS REACHED IN THE ORGANS AS MENTIONED ABOVE.
- ALSO, DURING A CELL DIVISION, THE WILD AND MUTANT COPIES OF THE MTDNA ARE UNEQUALLY DISTRIBUTED
AMONG THE DAUGHTER CELLS. AS A RESULT, THE EXPRESSION OF THE DISEASE VARIES EVEN AMONG DIFFERENT

questions.explanation:
ANAPHYLACTOID REACTIONS ARE THOSE REACTIONS THAT ARE SIMILAR TO THE ANAPHYLACTIC REACTIONS BUT ARE

REACTION CAN OCCUR EVEN ON THE FIRST EXPOSURE. THE MOST COMMON AGENTS THAT CAN CAUSE AN
ANAPHYLACTOID REACTION INCLUDE NSAIDS AND RADIOCONTRAST MEDIA.
IN 2014, WORLD ALLERGY ORGANISATION HAS INTRODUCED TWO NEW TERMS:
- IMMUNOLOGIC ANAPHYLAXIS - IT INCLUDES ANAPHYLACTIC REACTIONS MEDIATED BY IGE, IGG (IN ANIMALS),
AND IMMUNE COMPLEX/ COMPLEMENT-MEDIATED REACTIONS.
- NON-IMMUNOLOGIC ANAPHYLAXIS (PREVIOUSLY CALLED ANAPHYLACTOID REACTION) - IT INCLUDES REACTIONS
CAUSED BY AGENTS WHICH CAUSE MASSIVE DEGRANULATION OF MAST CELLS OR BASOPHILS IN THE ABSENCE OF
IMMUNOGLOBULIN.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: HEPCIDIN INHIBITS IRON TRANSFER FROM THE ENTEROCYTE TO THE PLASMA BY BINDING TO _____
questions.explanation:
HEPCIDIN INHIBITS IRON TRANSFER FROM THE ENTEROCYTES INTO THE PLASMA BY BINDING TO FERROPORTIN,
WHICH IS AN IRON EFFLUX CHANNEL IN THE ENTEROCYTE.
IRON METABOLISM IS REGULATED BY HEPCIDIN, A PROTEIN AND ACUTE PHASE REACTANT PRODUCED BY THE
LIVER. IT BINDS TO FERROPORTIN AND DEGRADES IT. THIS INHIBITS THE TRANSFER OF IRON FROM THE ENTEROCYTE
TO THE PLASMA VIA FERROPORTIN. AS A RESULT, IRON BECOMES TRAPPED WITHIN THE DUODENAL CELLS
(ENTEROCYTES) IN THE FORM OF MUCOSAL FERRITIN AND IS LOST IN FECES WHEN THESE CELLS ARE SHED OFF.
TRANSCRIPTION OF HEPCIDIN IS INCREASED BY THE FOLLOWING FACTORS:
- INCREASED LEVELS OF IRON
- INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES
TRANSCRIPTION OF HEPCIDIN IS DECREASED BY THE FOLLOWING FACTORS:
- IRON DEFICIENCY
- HYPOXIA
- INEFFECTIVE ERYTHROPOIESIS
HEPCIDIN IS ENCODED BY THE HAMP GENE AND ITS MUTATIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH HEREDITARY
HEMOCHROMATOSIS.
1891

THERE ARE TWO TYPES OF T CELLS: γ■ T-CELLS AND αβ T-CELLS.
THE FUNCTIONS OF γ■ T-CELLS:
- PROVIDE PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIA BY DIRECT KILLING OF INFECTED MACROPHAGES
- KILLS EXTRACELLULAR BACTERIA BY GRANULYSIN AND PERFORIN
- PLAYS A ROLE IN MAINTAINING SELF-TOLERANCE
- CAPABLE OF RECOGNISING AND LYSING DIVERSE CANCERS IN AN MHC-UNRESTRICTED MANNER
αβ T-CELLS HAVE MHC RESTRICTED ACTION.

- EVALUATION OF UNEXPLAINED ANEMIA, LEUKOPENIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA, PANCYTOPENIA

- SEVERE HEMOPHILIA

- SEVERE BLEEDING DISORDERS
PROCEDURE FOR BONE MARROW BIOPSY:
PRONE OR LATERAL POSITION IS CHOSEN FOR THE PROCEDURE. POSTERIOR SUPERIOR ILIAC SPINE IS IDENTIFIED.
AFTER DISINFECTION AND LOCAL ANAESTHESIA, THE PATIENT IS ASKED TO INHALE SLOWLY THROUGH THE NOSE AND
EXHALE SLOWLY THROUGH THE MOUTH TO RELIEVE ANXIETY .THE NEEDLE IS INSERTED AND ROTATED ON ITS AXIS.
ON REACHING THE DESIRED DEPTH, THE STYLET IS REMOVED AND NEEDLE IS ADVANCED. THE NEEDLE IS ROTATED
IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO LOOSEN THE SPECIMEN. IT IS THEN WITHDRAWN USING THE SAME ROTATIONAL
MOVEMENT.

IS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PHENOMENON OF ANTICIPATION, WHERE THE DISEASE PHENOTYPE WORSENS OVER
GENERATIONS WITHIN A FAMILY.
THE AFFECTED MALES ARE MENTALLY RETARDED, WITH AN IQ IN THE RANGE OF 20 TO 60.

- LONG FACE WITH A LARGE MANDIBLE

PREDOMINANTLY OSTEOBLASTIC SECONDARIES ARE SEEN IN PROSTATE CARCINOMA.
METASTATIC TUMORS OF BONE:
METASTATIC TUMORS ARE THE MOST COMMON FORM OF SKELETAL MALIGNANCY, GREATLY OUTNUMBERING
PRIMARY BONE CANCERS.
SKELETAL METASTASES ARE TYPICALLY MULTIFOCAL. HOWEVER, CARCINOMAS OF THE KIDNEY AND THYROID MAY
PRESENT WITH SOLITARY LESIONS. MOST METASTASES INVOLVE THE AXIAL SKELETON (VERTEBRAL COLUMN, PELVIS,
RIBS, SKULL, AND STERNUM). THE RED MARROW IN THESE AREAS, WITH ITS RICH CAPILLARY NETWORK AND SLOW
BLOOD FLOW, FACILITATES IMPLANTATION AND GROWTH OF THE TUMOR CELLS.
THE RADIOGRAPHIC APPEARANCE OF METASTASES MAY BE PURELY LYTIC (BONE DESTROYING), PURELY BLASTIC
(BONE FORMING), OR MIXED LYTIC AND BLASTIC. FURTHERMORE, SOME CANCERS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH
PREDOMINANTLY ONE PATTERN OR THE OTHER.
FOR EXAMPLE, PROSTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA IS PREDOMINANTLY BLASTIC WHEREAS CARCINOMAS OF THE
KIDNEY, LUNG, AND GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT AND MALIGNANT MELANOMA PRODUCE LYTIC LESIONS.

ABSORPTION. IRON OVERLOAD LEADS TO THE ACCUMULATION OF IRON IN PARENCHYMAL ORGANS SUCH AS THE
LIVER AND PANCREAS FOLLOWED BY THE HEART, JOINTS, AND ENDOCRINE ORGANS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: α1-ANTITRYPSIN IS THE MAJOR INHIBITOR OF THE ENZYME ________.
questions.explanation:
α1-ANTITRYPSIN IS THE MAJOR INHIBITOR OF THE ENZYME NEUTROPHIL ELASTASE.
- LYSOSOMAL ENZYMES, IF UNCHECKED, CAN POTENTIATE FURTHER INFLAMMATION BY DAMAGING TISSUES.
- THESE HARMFUL PROTEASES, HOWEVER, ARE NORMALLY CONTROLLED BY A SYSTEM OF ANTIPROTEASES IN THE
SERUM AND TISSUE FLUIDS.
- α1-ANTITRYPSIN IS THE PROTOTYPE MEMBER OF THE SERINE PROTEASE INHIBITOR (SERPIN) SUPERFAMILY OF
PROTEINS.
CLINICAL CORRELATE:
- ALPHA 1 ANTI-TRYPSIN DEFICIENCY (α1-ATD) IS CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN THE SERPINA1 GENE LOCATED IN
THE LONG ARM OF CHROMOSOME 14.
- THIS GENETIC DEFECT ALTERS THE CONFIGURATION OF THE α1-ANTITRYPSIN MOLECULE AND PREVENTS ITS
RELEASE FROM HEPATOCYTES.
- AS A RESULT, SERUM LEVELS OF α1-ANTITRYPSIN ARE DECREASED, LEADING TO LOW ALVEOLAR CONCENTRATIONS,
WHERE THE α1-ANTITRYPSIN MOLECULE NORMALLY WOULD PROVIDE PROTECTION AGAINST PROTEASES SUCH

IN AMOEBIASIS, AMOEBA ATTACH THEMSELVES TO THE COLONIC EPITHELIUM, INDUCES APOPTOSIS, INVADE
CRYPTS, AND BURROW LATERALLY INTO THE LAMINA PROPRIA. THIS RECRUITS NEUTROPHILS AND CAUSES TISSUE
DAMAGE, RESULTING IN FLASK-SHAPED ULCERS WITH A NARROW NECK AND BROAD BASE.
CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS:
- AMEBIC COLITIS
- COLICKY ABDOMINAL PAINS AND FREQUENT BOWEL MOVEMENTS.
- DIARRHEA ASSOCIATED WITH TENESMUS AND HEME-POSITIVE STOOL.
- TROPHOZOITES INVADE THE INTESTINAL MUCOSA, PRODUCE FLASK-SHAPED ULCERS.
- AMEBIC LIVER ABSCESS
- FEVER IS THE HALLMARK OF AMEBIC LIVER ABSCESS
- IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN, ABDOMINAL DISTENTION, AND ENLARGEMENT AND TENDERNESS OF
THE LIVER.

questions.explanation:
STEM CELLS ARE THE CELLS LINING THE ISTHMUS OF THE GASTRIC PITS.
ISTHMUS IS THE NARROW, UPPER-THIRD SEGMENT OF THE GASTRIC GLAND. THIS REGION HAS STEM CELLS AND
MUCOUS NECK CELLS. MOST STEM CELLS CONSTANTLY REGENERATE AND PRIMARILY MATURE TO FORM MUCOUS

STEM CELLS DO NOT DIVIDE WITHOUT ANY REGULATORY STIMULUS.
STEM CELLS GIVE RISE TO ALL THE VARIOUS DIFFERENTIATED TISSUES. IN ADULTS, STEM CELLS REPLACE DAMAGED
CELLS AND MAINTAIN TISSUE POPULATIONS.
THE PROPERTIES OF STEM CELLS ARE:
- SELF-RENEWAL
- ASYMMETRIC DIVISION - IN WHICH ONE DAUGHTER CELL ENTERS A DIFFERENTIATION PATHWAY AND GIVES RISE
TO MATURE CELLS, WHILE THE OTHER REMAINS UNDIFFERENTIATED AND RETAINS ITS SELF-RENEWAL CAPACITY.
THE TYPES OF STEM CELLS ARE:
- EMBRYONIC STEM CELLS WHICH ARE TOTIPOTENT
- ADULT STEM CELLS PRESENT IN STEM CELL NICHES
THE PLURIPOTENCY OF STEM CELLS IS DUE TO FACTORS LIKE:
1908
- OCT3/4
- KLF 4
- SOX 2
- CMYC
