questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome classically includes:
options: Aortic aneurysm, lens dislocation, and tall stature
Dry eyes, dry mouth, and lymphoma only
questions.explanation: WAS affects cytoskeletal responses in hematopoietic cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Chediak-Higashi syndrome is associated with:
options: Defective lysosomal trafficking and giant granules
Complete absence of leukocyte beta-2 integrins
Selective deletion of purine nucleoside phosphorylase
questions.answer: Defective lysosomal trafficking and giant granules
questions.explanation: LYST mutation causes abnormal granule fusion and impaired microbial killing.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: C3 deficiency predisposes especially to:
questions.explanation: C3 is central to opsonization and complement activation.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: An infant develops recurrent bacterial infections after maternal IgG wanes. Tonsils and lymph nodes are very small, mature B cells are absent, and serum immunoglobulins of all classes are markedly reduced. T-cell numbers are preserved. Which defect is most likely?
options: X-linked agammaglobulinemia due to BTK mutation
questions.answer: X-linked agammaglobulinemia due to BTK mutation
questions.explanation: BTK deficiency blocks pre-B-cell maturation, causing absent mature B cells and antibodies.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A newborn has chronic diarrhea, thrush, Pneumocystis pneumonia, and failure to thrive. Both cellular immunity and antibody responses are poor, and lymphocyte numbers are very low. Which category best describes the disease?
questions.explanation: SCID causes profound T-cell deficiency with secondary impairment of B-cell immunity.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: The first line of defense that is ready before antigen exposure is called:
questions.explanation: Innate immunity is constitutively present and responds rapidly to microbes and damaged cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Bacterial peptides containing N-formylmethionine are detected by leukocyte G-protein-coupled receptors. Neutrophils then migrate up the concentration gradient toward the infected tissue. Which innate immune function is being illustrated?
questions.explanation: N-formylated bacterial peptides act as chemoattractants for innate leukocytes.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Which cells are the principal rapid phagocytes recruited from blood during innate immune responses?
questions.explanation: Neutrophils and monocytes/macrophages are central innate phagocytes.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Epithelia contribute to innate immunity mainly by:
options: Providing barriers and producing antimicrobial peptides
Presenting exogenously derived peptides on MHC class I
questions.answer: Providing barriers and producing antimicrobial peptides
questions.explanation: Skin and mucosal epithelia block entry and secrete defensins and other antimicrobial products.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Toll-like receptors are important because they:
options: Generate somatic recombination of antigen receptors
Directly induce target cell lysis via perforin release
Serve as circulating opsonins for encapsulated bacteria
Recognize microbial products and induce inflammation
questions.answer: Recognize microbial products and induce inflammation
questions.explanation: TLRs are pattern-recognition receptors for microbial PAMPs and damage signals.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: The inflammasome promotes inflammation chiefly by increasing production of:
questions.explanation: Inflammasomes activate caspase-1, which processes pro-IL-1 beta into active IL-1.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Natural killer cells kill abnormal cells when:
options: Inhibitory killer Ig-like receptors bind intact MHC I
Activating signals exceed inhibitory MHC class I signals
Target cells express high levels of beta-2 microglobulin
Circulating antibodies cross-link high-affinity Fc receptors
questions.answer: Activating signals exceed inhibitory MHC class I signals
questions.explanation: NK cells integrate activating stress ligands and inhibitory recognition of self MHC I.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity by NK cells depends on:
questions.explanation: NK-cell CD16 recognizes IgG-coated targets and triggers killing.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A virus-infected cell downregulates MHC class I and expresses stress-induced ligands on its surface. A nearby lymphocyte lacks a TCR but contains cytotoxic granules and secretes IFN-gamma. Which cell is best suited to eliminate this target?
questions.explanation: Loss of MHC I removes NK inhibition, while stress ligands activate NK-cell cytotoxicity.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A patient has recurrent fever attacks from excessive inflammasome activity but no autoantibodies or antigen-specific T-cell response. Symptoms improve dramatically with IL-1 blockade. This pattern is best classified as:
questions.explanation: Autoinflammatory syndromes arise from dysregulated innate immunity, often IL-1 driven.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: IL-2 produced by activated T cells primarily functions as:
questions.explanation: IL-2 drives clonal expansion of antigen-stimulated T cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A child has recurrent mucocutaneous fungal infections due to impaired IL-17 signaling. Neutrophil numbers are normal, but epithelial chemokine responses are weak. Which helper T-cell subset function is most impaired?
options: Th1 classical macrophage activation via interferon-gamma
Th2-mediated eosinophil recruitment and IgE switching
Th17 recruitment of neutrophils and barrier defense
questions.answer: Th17 recruitment of neutrophils and barrier defense
questions.explanation: Th17 cells are crucial for neutrophil-rich responses at mucosal barriers, especially against fungi.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Th1 cells characteristically secrete:
questions.explanation: Th1 cells activate macrophages through IFN-gamma.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Th2 cells are especially important in defense against:
questions.explanation: Th2 cytokines promote IgE, eosinophils, mast cells, and anti-helminth responses.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Th17 cells promote inflammation mainly by:
questions.explanation: Th17 cytokines induce chemokines and recruit inflammatory leukocytes.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: CD40 ligand on helper T cells is important because it:
options: Directly binds class I MHC molecules on target cells
Induces proteasomal processing of cytosolic antigens
Activates macrophages and helps B-cell class switching
Inhibits all costimulatory signals on dendritic cells
questions.answer: Activates macrophages and helps B-cell class switching
questions.explanation: CD40L-CD40 interactions are central to T-cell help for macrophages and B cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes kill infected cells mainly using:
options: Major basic protein and eosinophil cationic protein
questions.explanation: CTL granules induce apoptosis in antigen-bearing target cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Affinity maturation of antibodies occurs in:
questions.explanation: Somatic hypermutation and selection in germinal centers increase antibody affinity.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A patient with a CD40L mutation has recurrent pyogenic and opportunistic infections with very high IgM but little IgG, IgA, or IgE. Germinal centers are poorly developed. Which failed process best explains this syndrome?
options: Dendritic cell migration to lymph nodes
questions.explanation: CD40L deficiency causes hyper-IgM syndrome by blocking class switching and germinal center reactions.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A macrophage contains viable intracellular mycobacteria. A nearby CD4+ T cell recognizes microbial peptide on MHC II, expresses CD40L, and secretes IFN-gamma. What is the main intended result?
options: Alternative macrophage activation with tissue repair
Immediate mast cell degranulation and vasodilation
Classical macrophage activation with microbicidal killing
B-cell apoptosis and somatic hypermutation cessation
questions.answer: Classical macrophage activation with microbicidal killing
questions.explanation: Th1 CD40L and IFN-gamma activate macrophages to kill ingested microbes.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Systemic lupus erythematosus is classically associated with antibodies against:
questions.explanation: ANA and anti-dsDNA/anti-Sm antibodies are characteristic of SLE.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A patient develops tight skin of the fingers, Raynaud phenomenon, dysphagia from esophageal fibrosis, and pulmonary hypertension. The disease involves endothelial injury and fibroblast activation rather than immune complex deposition alone. Which disease fits best?
questions.explanation: Systemic sclerosis is marked by vasculopathy and progressive fibrosis of skin and organs.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: The most specific antibody for SLE among common tests is:
questions.explanation: Anti-Sm is highly specific, though not very sensitive, for SLE.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Sjögren syndrome primarily affects:
questions.explanation: Autoimmune destruction of exocrine glands causes dry eyes and dry mouth.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Anti-dsDNA antibodies in SLE correlate especially with:
questions.explanation: Anti-dsDNA immune complexes are associated with renal involvement.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Libman-Sacks endocarditis in SLE is characterized by:
options: Large destructive bacterial vegetations with perforation
Sterile vegetations on either side of valve leaflets
Ulcerated atherosclerotic plaques along aortic root
questions.answer: Sterile vegetations on either side of valve leaflets
questions.explanation: SLE can cause sterile verrucous endocarditis.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Sjögren syndrome increases risk of:
questions.explanation: Chronic B-cell stimulation in Sjögren syndrome predisposes to MALT-type lymphoma.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Systemic sclerosis is characterized by:
options: Isolated cutaneous IgE-mediated mast cell disease
Congenital failure of T-cell receptor rearrangement
questions.explanation: Scleroderma combines vascular injury, immune activation, and collagen deposition.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A woman has photosensitive malar rash, arthritis, low complement, and proteinuria. Renal biopsy shows granular deposits of IgG and complement in glomeruli. Which mechanism best explains the nephritis?
options: Type III immune complex disease from anti-nuclear antibodies
Type II linear anti-glomerular basement membrane nephritis
Type I immediate hypersensitivity with mast cell degranulation
Type IV delayed cell-mediated interstitial granulomatosis
questions.answer: Type III immune complex disease from anti-nuclear antibodies
questions.explanation: SLE nephritis is largely immune complex-mediated, producing granular deposits.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A patient has dry eyes, dry mouth, parotid enlargement, anti-SSA antibodies, and a monoclonal B-cell proliferation in salivary tissue. Which long-term complication is most directly linked to the chronic autoimmune process?
questions.explanation: Sjögren syndrome may evolve into extranodal marginal zone lymphoma from chronic B-cell activation.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: The major barrier to organ transplantation is mismatch in:
questions.explanation: HLA polymorphism is the main determinant of graft recognition.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: After bone marrow transplantation, a recipient develops rash, jaundice, diarrhea, and mucosal ulceration. The graft contains mature donor T cells, and the recipient is immunosuppressed. Which immunologic event is central?
options: Recipient IgE against donor mast cells
Preformed recipient antibodies to kidney endothelium
Donor T cells reacting against recipient antigens
questions.answer: Donor T cells reacting against recipient antigens
questions.explanation: GVHD occurs when donor T cells recognize host alloantigens.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Hyperacute rejection is usually mediated by:
options: De novo donor-specific cytotoxic T cells
questions.explanation: Preexisting antibodies cause immediate endothelial injury and thrombosis.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Graft-versus-host disease occurs when:
options: Donor T cells attack recipient tissues
Recipient antibodies attack donor RBCs only
questions.answer: Donor T cells attack recipient tissues
questions.explanation: Immunocompetent donor T cells react against host antigens.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Acute cellular rejection is mediated mainly by:
questions.explanation: Recipient T cells attack graft parenchyma and vessels.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Acute antibody-mediated rejection primarily targets:
questions.explanation: Antibodies to donor antigens injure graft vessels through complement and inflammation.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Chronic rejection is characterized by:
options: Sudden microvascular thrombosis and cortical necrosis
questions.explanation: Chronic rejection causes graft ischemia and fibrosis over months to years.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Direct allorecognition means recipient T cells recognize:
options: Intact donor MHC molecules on donor APCs
Donor peptides presented by recipient MHC molecules
Soluble donor antibodies deposited along graft capillaries
questions.answer: Intact donor MHC molecules on donor APCs
questions.explanation: Direct recognition is a strong T-cell response to foreign MHC itself.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Minutes after kidney transplantation, the graft becomes cyanotic and fails to perfuse. Histology shows neutrophils, fibrin thrombi, and endothelial injury. The recipient had circulating antibodies against donor blood group/HLA antigens. What is the rejection pattern?
questions.explanation: Preformed antibodies cause immediate complement-mediated vascular thrombosis.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Months after transplant, a patient develops gradual renal graft dysfunction. Biopsy shows intimal smooth muscle proliferation, luminal narrowing, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis. There is no sudden thrombosed graft. Which process is most likely?
questions.explanation: Chronic rejection is dominated by vascular occlusion and fibrosis.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: The most reliable feature proving malignancy in a solid tumor is:
questions.explanation: Metastasis is unequivocal evidence of malignancy in solid tumors.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: A large uterine smooth muscle tumor has infiltrative edges, hemorrhage, necrosis, numerous atypical mitoses, and pleomorphic cells. A small well-circumscribed smooth muscle mass elsewhere in the uterus lacks these findings. Which feature most supports leiomyosarcoma?
options: Abundant uniform elongated smooth muscle bundles
Well-circumscribed margins with a thick fibrous capsule
Invasion with cytologic atypia and abnormal mitoses
Estrogen receptor positivity with menstrual cyclic changes
questions.answer: Invasion with cytologic atypia and abnormal mitoses
questions.explanation: Malignant smooth muscle tumors show infiltrative growth, atypia, necrosis, and mitoses.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Differentiation refers to:
options: Capacity of neoplastic cells to metastasize
Degree of vascularization within tumor stroma
Resemblance of tumor cells to normal cells
Extent of ischemic necrosis across the tumor
questions.answer: Resemblance of tumor cells to normal cells
questions.explanation: Differentiation measures morphologic and functional similarity to normal tissue.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Anaplasia means:
questions.explanation: Anaplasia is a hallmark of many malignant tumors.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Carcinoma in situ means malignant epithelial cells:
options: Full-thickness dysplasia without basement membrane invasion
Superficial microinvasion into underlying lamina propria
Widespread metastatic dissemination to regional lymph nodes
Benign hyperplastic architectural distortion of epithelium
questions.answer: Full-thickness dysplasia without basement membrane invasion
questions.explanation: In situ carcinoma shows cytologic malignancy but remains above the basement membrane.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Dysplasia is most often recognized by:
options: Orderly maturation with uniform polarized nuclei
Disordered epithelial growth with cytologic atypia
Pure stromal edema without nuclear enlargement
Dense keloidal collagen deposition without atypia
questions.answer: Disordered epithelial growth with cytologic atypia
questions.explanation: Dysplasia is premalignant epithelial disordered growth.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Benign tumors usually grow by:
options: Diffuse infiltration of all adjacent structures
questions.explanation: Benign tumors often push aside adjacent tissue rather than invade it.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: Which feature favors malignancy over benignity?
options: Uniform small nuclei with abundant cytoplasm
Slow circumscribed expansile pattern of growth
Tumor giant cells with abnormal mitoses
questions.answer: Tumor giant cells with abnormal mitoses
questions.explanation: Marked pleomorphism and atypical mitoses suggest anaplasia and malignancy.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: A cervical biopsy shows full-thickness epithelial atypia, loss of maturation, hyperchromatic nuclei, and mitoses above the basal layer. The basement membrane is intact, and no stromal invasion is identified. Which diagnosis best matches these findings?
questions.explanation: Full-thickness dysplasia without basement membrane invasion is carcinoma in situ.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Characteristics of Benign and Malignant Neoplasms
questions.prompt: A smoker’s bronchial biopsy shows replacement of ciliated columnar epithelium by squamous epithelium. A later biopsy shows pleomorphic basal-like cells and abnormal mitoses, but no invasion. Which sequence best describes the progression?
options: Metaplasia to dysplasia to carcinoma in situ
questions.answer: Metaplasia to dysplasia to carcinoma in situ
questions.explanation: Chronic injury can cause metaplasia, then dysplasia, then preinvasive carcinoma.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: Tumor grade is based mainly on:
options: Tumor diameter and depth of tissue invasion
Presence of regional lymph node metastases
Degree of cytologic atypia and differentiation
questions.answer: Degree of cytologic atypia and differentiation
questions.explanation: Grade estimates biologic aggressiveness from histology.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: A man with pancreatic carcinoma loses marked weight despite adequate caloric intake and no mechanical obstruction. He has muscle wasting, anorexia, and elevated inflammatory mediators. Which mechanism best explains this systemic effect?
options: Simple caloric starvation and dietary deprivation
Cancer cachexia mediated by cytokines and metabolic changes
questions.answer: Cancer cachexia mediated by cytokines and metabolic changes
questions.explanation: Cachexia is a cytokine-driven wasting syndrome not fully reversed by nutrition.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: Tumor stage is based mainly on:
options: Nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic frequency only
Presence of intracytoplasmic mucin or keratin
Size and local extent, nodal spread, and metastasis
questions.answer: Size and local extent, nodal spread, and metastasis
questions.explanation: Stage describes anatomic spread, often by TNM.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: For most solid tumors, prognosis correlates better with:
questions.explanation: Anatomic extent is usually more prognostically important than grade.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: Cachexia in cancer is driven partly by:
options: Suppression of all hepatic acute-phase reactants
questions.explanation: Cancer cachexia involves systemic inflammation and metabolic wasting.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: Paraneoplastic syndromes are symptoms caused by:
options: Symptoms caused exclusively by physical tumor compression
Complications directly resulting from regional nodal spread
Effects not explained by local tumor spread or hormones
Adverse reactions secondary to antineoplastic chemotherapy
questions.answer: Effects not explained by local tumor spread or hormones
questions.explanation: Paraneoplastic syndromes are remote effects of cancer.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: A classic paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome in small cell lung carcinoma is:
options: Growth hormone secretion by renal cell carcinoma
questions.explanation: Small cell carcinoma may secrete ACTH or ADH.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: A definitive cancer diagnosis most often requires:
options: Nonspecific rise in erythrocyte sedimentation rate
questions.explanation: Tissue diagnosis remains central to tumor classification.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: A colon cancer invades through muscularis propria and has metastases in regional lymph nodes but no distant metastasis. Another colon cancer is poorly differentiated but confined to mucosa. Which parameter usually has greater prognostic weight?
options: Presence of a capsule in all cancers
questions.explanation: Stage generally predicts outcome better than grade in most solid tumors.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Clinical Features, Grading, Staging, and Laboratory Diagnosis
questions.prompt: A patient with lung cancer develops hypercalcemia, but imaging shows no bone metastases. Laboratory testing reveals tumor production of a parathyroid hormone-related peptide. Which clinical category best explains this finding?
questions.explanation: PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia is a paraneoplastic endocrine syndrome.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Defective DNA repair predisposes to cancer by causing:
questions.explanation: Failure to repair DNA damage increases mutation rates.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: A woman with inherited BRCA1 mutation develops high-grade serous carcinoma. The tumor is defective in homologous recombination repair, making it vulnerable to PARP inhibition through synthetic lethality. Which lesion is normally repaired by BRCA pathways?
questions.explanation: BRCA1/2 are essential for homologous recombination repair of double-strand DNA breaks.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Mismatch repair defects are associated with:
questions.explanation: Mismatch repair loss causes length changes in microsatellite repeats.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: BRCA1 and BRCA2 participate in repair of:
options: Double-strand DNA breaks by homologous recombination
Ultraviolet pyrimidine dimers by nucleotide excision
Base deamination by base excision repair enzymes
questions.answer: Double-strand DNA breaks by homologous recombination
questions.explanation: BRCA proteins help high-fidelity double-strand break repair.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Lynch syndrome is caused by germline defects in:
questions.explanation: Inherited mismatch repair defects predispose to colon and endometrial cancers.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective:
questions.explanation: XP impairs repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Microsatellite instability is most useful as a marker of:
questions.explanation: MSI reflects insertion/deletion errors at short repeats due to MMR loss.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: Cancers with high mutation burdens may be more responsive to immune checkpoint blockade because they:
questions.explanation: More mutations can create tumor-specific peptides recognized by T cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: A young patient develops colon cancer, and tumor testing shows loss of MLH1/MSH2 function with length variation in multiple microsatellite markers. The tumor has numerous frameshift mutations in growth-regulatory genes. Which inherited syndrome is most likely?
questions.explanation: Lynch syndrome is caused by germline mismatch repair defects and MSI.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: DNA Repair Defects and Genomic Instability
questions.prompt: A child develops multiple skin cancers on sun-exposed areas, severe photosensitivity, and inability to repair UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. The underlying defect lies in excising bulky helix-distorting lesions. Which repair pathway is abnormal?
questions.explanation: Xeroderma pigmentosum involves nucleotide excision repair defects.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Cancer is fundamentally caused by:
options: Chronic hydrostatic vascular congestion and edema
Genetic and epigenetic alterations in a cell clone
questions.answer: Genetic and epigenetic alterations in a cell clone
questions.explanation: Neoplasms arise from heritable changes that confer growth and survival advantages.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: A small carcinoma remains clinically dormant until a clone emerges that secretes VEGF, degrades basement membrane, and survives in blood. The new clone expands because it has a selective advantage within the tumor. What process best explains this evolution?
options: Reversible cellular adaptation to chronic ischemia
questions.explanation: Tumors evolve by selection of subclones with advantageous mutations.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Driver mutations are mutations that:
options: Occur exclusively in benign connective tissue
Arise only as artifacts during tissue fixation
questions.explanation: Drivers provide selective growth, survival, or invasion advantages.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Passenger mutations are:
options: Essential mutations required for metastatic colony formation
Incidental mutations not directly contributing to tumor growth
Germline mutations that initiate hereditary cancer syndromes
Specific translocations that generate chimeric oncoproteins
questions.answer: Incidental mutations not directly contributing to tumor growth
questions.explanation: Passenger mutations accumulate but do not drive cancer phenotype.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: A core hallmark of cancer is:
options: Permanent dependence on normal growth control
questions.explanation: Cancer cells acquire autonomous growth signaling.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Cancer cells evade growth suppression by altering:
questions.explanation: Loss of RB, TP53, and related pathways removes brakes on proliferation.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Cancer cells acquire limitless replicative potential largely through:
options: Inactivation of vascular endothelial growth factors
Suppression of glycolytic aerobic respiration pathways
Downregulation of antiapoptotic BCL2 family proteins
questions.explanation: Telomere maintenance prevents senescence during repeated division.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: Angiogenesis helps tumors by:
options: Inducing permanent growth arrest and cellular senescence
Supplying nutrients and oxygen for expanding tumor mass
Preventing tumor cells from accessing circulating vessels
Promoting uniform differentiation of malignant blast cells
questions.answer: Supplying nutrients and oxygen for expanding tumor mass
questions.explanation: Tumors require new vessels beyond small diffusion-limited sizes.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: A tumor biopsy shows many mutations, but only a small subset repeatedly appears in independent samples and activates pathways controlling growth, survival, and invasion. The remaining mutations vary randomly between regions. Which term applies to the recurrent selected mutations?
questions.explanation: Driver mutations are selected because they contribute to malignant behavior.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.topic: Molecular Basis and Hallmarks of Cancer
questions.prompt: A cancer cell grows without exogenous growth factors, ignores antigrowth signals, resists apoptosis after DNA damage, induces blood vessels, and invades basement membrane. Which framework best integrates these diverse acquired properties?
questions.explanation: The hallmarks summarize acquired capabilities needed for malignant growth and spread.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Tumor neoantigens are often generated by:
questions.explanation: Cancer mutations can create new peptides recognized by T cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Aflatoxin B1 exposure in food leads to a characteristic TP53 mutation and greatly increases hepatocellular carcinoma risk, especially with hepatitis B infection. Which broad carcinogenic mechanism is most relevant?
options: Insertional viral oncogenesis without somatic mutations
IgE-dependent mast cell activation and tissue injury
Chemical carcinogenesis with mutational DNA damage
questions.answer: Chemical carcinogenesis with mutational DNA damage
questions.explanation: Aflatoxin is an indirect chemical carcinogen producing DNA adducts and TP53 mutations.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: The main antitumor effector lymphocyte is:
questions.explanation: CTLs recognize tumor peptides on MHC I and kill tumor cells.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Immune checkpoint blockade commonly targets:
questions.explanation: Checkpoint inhibitors release brakes on antitumor T-cell responses.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Tumors evade immunity by downregulating:
questions.explanation: Loss of MHC I impairs CD8 T-cell recognition.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Chemical carcinogenesis typically includes:
questions.explanation: Initiation causes mutation; promotion drives clonal expansion.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Direct-acting carcinogens require:
questions.explanation: Direct-acting agents are intrinsically carcinogenic.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Indirect-acting chemical carcinogens are often activated by:
questions.explanation: Procarcinogens require metabolic conversion to ultimate carcinogens.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A melanoma responds to anti-PD-1 therapy after biopsy shows many mutation-derived neoantigens and T cells at the tumor edge. The treatment does not kill tumor cells directly but restores exhausted T-cell activity. Which mechanism is being targeted?
questions.explanation: PD-1 blockade reinvigorates antitumor T-cell responses.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A chemical produces no tumor by itself after a single exposure, but later application of a nonmutagenic irritant causes clonal expansion of initiated cells and papilloma formation. Which stage does the irritant represent?
questions.explanation: Promoters are nonmutagenic stimuli that expand initiated mutant clones.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Metastasis means:
options: Spread of malignant tumor to distant sites
Benign expansile proliferation with intact capsule
Reversible replacement of columnar by squamous cells
questions.answer: Spread of malignant tumor to distant sites
questions.explanation: Metastasis is discontinuous spread of cancer.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A renal cell carcinoma grows as a long tumor thrombus up the renal vein into the inferior vena cava, yet widespread metastases are initially absent. What concept from Robbins does this illustrate?
options: Venous tumor thrombi invariably indicate incurable dissemination
Intravascular extension can occur without widespread metastasis
Benign adenomas routinely invade deep systemic venous conduits
Carcinoma in situ frequently embolizes to pulmonary capillaries
questions.answer: Intravascular extension can occur without widespread metastasis
questions.explanation: Some tumors, especially renal cell carcinoma, show striking venous growth without parallel dissemination.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Carcinomas most commonly spread initially by:
questions.explanation: Lymphatic spread is typical of carcinomas.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Sarcomas more often spread by:
questions.explanation: Hematogenous spread is common in sarcomas.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Loss of E-cadherin promotes invasion by reducing:
options: Basement membrane collagen synthesis and cross-linking
Angiogenic vascular sprouting driven by hypoxia
Tumor cell adhesion to neighboring epithelial cells
questions.answer: Tumor cell adhesion to neighboring epithelial cells
questions.explanation: Reduced adhesion permits dissociation and invasion.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Matrix metalloproteinases help metastasis by:
options: Degrading extracellular matrix and basement membrane
Phosphorylating retinoblastoma protein to promote G1-S
Activating complement cascades on endothelial cells
questions.answer: Degrading extracellular matrix and basement membrane
questions.explanation: MMPs facilitate invasion through tissue barriers.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Ovarian carcinoma commonly spreads by:
questions.explanation: Ovarian cancers often exfoliate cells into the peritoneal cavity.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: Portal venous drainage helps explain why colon carcinoma often metastasizes first to:
questions.explanation: Blood from colon drains through portal circulation to liver.
questions.subject: Pathology

questions.prompt: A breast carcinoma loses E-cadherin expression, degrades basement membrane with proteases, migrates through stroma, enters lymphatics, and forms deposits in axillary nodes. Which step sequence best describes this event?

questions.explanation:
VIRAL CULTURE FROM CORNEAL SCRAPINGS IS USED TO CONFIRM DIAGNOSIS.
MULTIPLE TESTS IN SUCCESSION/SIMULTANEOUSLY ARE THE BEST. USUALLY DIRECT FLUORESCENT ANTIBODY TEST
FOLLOWED BY VIRUS ISOLATION/CULTURE IS USEFUL.
VIRUS ISOLATION THROUGH CULTURE: BEST SPECIMENS ARE BRAIN AND SALIVA. CSF, CORNEAL SMEARS AND
CENTRIFUGED URINE CAN ALSO BE USED.
OPTION A: SEROLOGICAL TESTS LIKE INDIRECT IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE ARE INSENSITIVE.
OPTION B: NEGRI BODIES CAN ONLY BE DEMONSTRATED IN BRAIN (PYRAMIDAL CELLS OF AMMON’S HORN, AND
THE PURKINJE CELLS OF THE CEREBELLUM ARE THE MOST COMMON SITE).
OPTION D: REAL TIME-PCR AMPLIFICATION DETECTION OF RABIES VIRUS RNA IS HIGHLY SENSITIVE AND
SPECIFIC. THIS TECHNIQUE CAN DETECT VIRUS IN FRESHSALIVA SAMPLES, SKIN, CSF, AND BRAIN TISSUES.
HOWEVER IT IS NOT CONFIRMATORY TEST.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE PARASITE FROM THE GIVEN LIFE CYCLE.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN LIFE CYCLE BELONGS TO FASCIOLA HEPATICA.
FASCIOLA HEPATICA (SHEEP LIVER FLUKE) CAUSES DISEASE PRIMARILY IN SHEEP AND OTHER DOMESTIC
ANIMALS. HUMANS ARE INFECTED BY EATING WATERCRESS (OR OTHER AQUATIC PLANTS) CONTAMINATED BY
LARVAE (METACERCARIAE) THAT EXCYST IN THE DUODENUM, PENETRATE THE GUT WALL, AND REACH THE LIVER,
WHERE THEY MATURE INTO ADULTS.
THE ADULT FLUKES IN THE BILE DUCTS PRODUCE EGGS, WHICH ARE EXCRETED IN THE FECES. THE EGGS HATCH IN
FRESHWATER AND MIRACIDIA ENTER THE SNAILS. MIRACIDIA DEVELOP INTO CERCARIAE, WHICH THEN ENCYST ON
AQUATIC VEGETATION. SHEEP AND HUMANS EAT THE PLANTS, THUS COMPLETING THE LIFE CYCLE. MOST
INFECTIONS ARE ASYMPTOMATIC. HALZOUN IS A PAINFUL PHARYNGITIS CAUSED BY THE PRESENCE OF ADULT
FLUKES ON THE POSTERIOR PHARYNGEAL WALL AFTER EATING RAW SHEEP LIVER. OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE CAN
OCCUR MONTHS OR YEARS LATER.
DIAGNOSIS IS MADE BY IDENTIFICATION OF THE EGGS IN THE FECES.

questions.prompt: THE LIFE CYCLE PROVIDED BELOW IS OF WHICH OF THESE:
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN LIFE CYCLE IS OF ENTAMOEBA HISTOLYTICA.
ITS LIFE CYCLE INCLUDES 2 STAGES - THE MOTILE TROPHOZOITE AND THE NON-MOTILE CYST, BOTH OF WHICH ARE
SEEN IN THE IMAGE SHOWN ABOVE. THE TRANSMISSION IS PRIMARILY BY THE FECAL-ORAL ROUTE. THERE IS NO
ANIMAL RESERVOIR. THE MOST FREQUENT SITE OF SYSTEMIC DISEASE IS THE LIVER.
THE INGESTED CYSTS DIFFERENTIATE INTO TROPHOZOITES IN THE ILEUM WHICH INVADE THE COLONIC
EPITHELIUM. THE TROPHOZOITES PENETRATE THE SUBMUCOSAL LAYER AND FORM ABSCESSES WHICH BREAK
DOWN TO FORM FLASK-SHAPED ULCERS.
1347
THE TROPHOZOITES MULTIPLY BY BINARY FISSION AND PRODUCE CYSTS, AND BOTH STAGES ARE PASSED IN THE
FECES. TROPHOZOITES ARE RAPIDLY DESTROYED OUTSIDE THE BODY. CYSTS SURVIVE IN THE EXTERNAL
ENVIRONMENT AND ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR TRANSMISSION.
NOTE: THE GENUS ENTAMOEBA HAS FOUR MORPHOLOGICALLY IDENTICAL SPECIES - E. HISTOLYTICA, E. DISPAR,
E. BANGLADESHI, AND E. MOSHKOVSKII. E. MOSHKOVSKII WHICH WAS INITIALLY THOUGHT TO BE
NON-PATHOGENIC HAS RECENTLY BEEN SHOWN TO BE A CAUSATIVE AGENT OF NON-INVASIVE DIARRHEA.

questions.prompt: THE GIVEN LIFE CYCLE IS SUGGESTIVE OF WHICH OF THESE VIRUSES?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN LIFE CYCLE IS OF THE HEPATITIS B VIRUS.
STEPS:
- THE INFECTIOUS VIRION ATTACHES TO CELLS AND UNCOATING OCCURS.
- CELL ENZYMES IN THE HEPATOCYTES CONVERT DSDNA TO COVALENTLY CLOSED CIRCULAR DOUBLE-STRANDED
DNA (CCCDNA)
- HBV MRNA AND PRE-GENOME RNA IS SYNTHESIZED USING CCCDNA AS A TEMPLATE.
- PRE-GENOME RNA IS ENCAPSIDATED BY PACKAGING SIGNAL INTO NEW CORE PARTICLES.
- THESE NEW CORE PARTICLES ARE TEMPLATES FOR HBV REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE.
- NEGATIVE-STRAND DNA IS SYNTHESIZED BY VIRAL POLYMERASE BY REVERSE TRANSCRIPTION.
- THE CORES BUD FROM THE PRE-GOLGI MEMBRANES, ACQUIRING HBSAG-CONTAINING ENVELOPES.
- ONCE VIRAL PARTICLES ARE ASSEMBLED, THEY EITHER EXIT THE CELL OR CAUSE REINFECTION OF THE SAME CELL.

questions.prompt: SELECT THE FOLLOWING?

THE ABOVE IMAGE SHOWS GIARDIA LAMBLIA.
CYSTS ARE RESISTANT FORMS AND ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR TRANSMISSION OF GIARDIASIS. BOTH CYSTS AND
TROPHOZOITES CAN BE FOUND IN THE FECES (DIAGNOSTIC STAGES). THE CYSTS ARE HARDY AND CAN SURVIVE
SEVERAL MONTHS IN COLD WATER.
INFECTION OCCURS BY THE INGESTION OF CYSTS IN CONTAMINATED WATER, FOOD, OR BY THE FECAL-ORAL ROUTE
(HANDS OR FOMITES).
IN THE SMALL INTESTINE, EXCYSTATION RELEASES TROPHOZOITES (EACH CYST PRODUCES TWO TROPHOZOITES).
TROPHOZOITES MULTIPLY BY LONGITUDINAL BINARY FISSION, REMAINING IN THE LUMEN OF THE PROXIMAL
SMALL BOWEL WHERE THEY CAN BE FREE OR ATTACHED TO THE MUCOSA BY A VENTRAL SUCKING DISK.
ENCYSTATION OCCURS AS THE PARASITES TRANSIT TOWARD THE COLON. THE CYST IS THE STAGE FOUND MOST
COMMONLY IN NONDIARRHEAL FECES. BECAUSE THE CYSTS ARE INFECTIOUS WHEN PASSED IN THE STOOL OR
SHORTLY AFTERWARD, PERSON-TO-PERSON TRANSMISSION IS POSSIBLE.
GIARDIA LAMBLIA EXISTS IN :
- INFECTIVE FORM – QUADRINUCLEATE CYST
- TENNIS RACKET SHAPED TROPHOZOITE IS ACTIVELY MOTILE WITH CENTRAL AXOSTYLE WITH PAIR OF NUCLEI
- OVAL SHAPED CYST DENOTED WITH CYST WALL

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: BEST METHOD OF DIAGNOSIS FOR CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE?
questions.explanation:
NUCLEIC ACID AMPLIFICATION TESTS, INCLUDING PCR ASSAYS, FOR C. DIFFICILE TOXIN A OR B GENE IN STOOL
HAVE BEEN APPROVED FOR DIAGNOSTIC PURPOSES OF CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION DUE TO HIGH
SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY AND RAPID TURNAROUND TIME.
THE DIAGNOSIS OF CDI IS BASED ON A COMBINATION OF CLINICAL CRITERIA:
(1) DIARRHEA (≥3 UNFORMED STOOLS PER 24 H FOR ≥2 DAYS) WITH NO OTHER RECOGNIZED CAUSE PLUS
(2) TOXIN A OR B DETECTED IN THE STOOL, TOXIN- PRODUCING C. DIFFICILE DETECTED IN THE STOOL BY PCR OR
CULTURE, OR PSEUDOMEMBRANES SEEN IN THE COLON.
OTHER DIAGNOSTIC METHODS INCLUDE :
- STOOL CULTURE IN SELECTIVE MEDIA
- DEMONSTRATING TOXIN BY HEP-2 CELL CULTURES
- TOXIN GENE IDENTIFICATION BY ENZYME IMMUNOASSAY
- COLONSCOPY OR SIGMOIDOSCOPY

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE ORGANISMS IS REPRESENTED BY THE GIVEN FORM OF REPLICATION?

THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS GENERATION OF MRNA FROM NEGATIVE SENSE RNA WITHIN THE NUCLEUS. THIS
OCCURS DURING THE REPLICATION OF INFLUENZA VIRUS.
ORTHOMYXOVIRUSES (INFLUENZA VIRUS) CONTAIN SEGMENTED (8 SEGMENTS) NEGATIVE SENSE SSRNA THAT IS
REPLICATED IN THE NUCLEUS. STAGES OF VIRAL REPLICATION INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING:
- ATTACHMENT, PENETRATION, UNCOATING: THE VIRUS ATTACHES TO CELL-SURFACE SIALIC ACID VIA
HEMAGGLUTININ. IT IS THEN INTERNALIZED BY RECEPTOR-MEDIATED ENDOCYTOSIS. THERE IS FUSION OF THE
VIRAL ENVELOPE AND CELL MEMBRANE, RESULTING IN UNCOATING OR RELEASE OF NUCLEOCAPSID INTO THE HOST
CELL CYTOPLASM.
- TRANSCRIPTION AND TRANSLATION: MRNAS ARE PRODUCED FROM NUCLEOCAPSIDS VIA A VIRUS-ENCODED
POLYMERASE. THIS PROCESS OCCURS IN THE NUCLEUS. THE MRNAS THUS PRODUCED ARE TRANSLATED INTO
VIRAL PROTEINS IN THE CYTOPLASM.
- VIRAL RNA REPLICATION: THE VIRAL GENOME IS REPLICATED BY THE SAME VIRUS-ENCODED POLYMERASE
INVOLVED IN TRANSCRIPTION. THE NEGATIVE SENSE RNA IS CONVERTED TO ITS POSITIVE SENSE FORM. THE
POSITIVE SENSE COPIES SERVE AS TEMPLATES FOR REPLICATION OF THE VIRAL GENOME.
- MATURATION: THE VIRUS MATURES BY BUDDING FROM THE SURFACE OF THE CELL.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE HELMINTH FROM THE LIFE CYCLE PROVIDED BELOW.
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS THE LIFE CYCLE OF STRONGYLOIDES STERCORALIS.
STRONGYLOIDES STERCORALIS IS THE SMALLEST NEMATODE KNOWN TO CAUSE HUMAN INFECTION. IT HAS BOTH A
FREE-LIVING AND A PARASITIC LIFE CYCLE. ITS NATURAL HOST IS MAN. THE INFECTIVE FORM TO MAN IS THE
FILARIFORM LARVA. INFECTION OCCURS THROUGH PENETRATION OF THE SKIN BY LARVAE IN THE SOIL. THEN, THE
LARVAE MIGRATE TO THE SMALL INTESTINE. THEY MOLT TWICE AND BECOME ADULT FEMALE WORMS IN THE
SMALL INTESTINE. THE EGGS LAID IN THE MUCOSA OF THE INTESTINE HATCH IMMEDIATELY RELEASING THE
RHABDITIFORM LARVA (L1 STAGE). THUS, IT IS OVOVIVIPAROUS. THESE RHABDITIFORM LARVAE IN THE BOWEL CAN
DEVELOP DIRECTLY INTO FILARIFORM LARVAE THAT PENETRATE THE COLONIC WALL OR PERIANAL SKIN AND ENTER
THE CIRCULATION TO REPEAT THE MIGRATION. THIS ESTABLISHES ONGOING INTERNAL REINFECTION.
THE RHABDITIFORM LARVA CAN ALSO BE PASSED IN THE STOOL. IT MAY DIRECTLY METAMORPHOSE TO THE
INFECTIVE FILARIFORM LARVA IN THE SOIL, OR DEVELOP INTO ADULT WORMS. THE FREE-LIVING ADULT WORMS THEN
PASS EGGS, WHICH HATCH AND MATURE TO FORM INFECTIVE FILARIFORM LARVAE.
IN ANCYLOSTOMA DUODENALE INFESTATION, EGGS CONTAINING SEGMENTED OVA (NOT RHABDITIFORM LARVAE)
ARE PASSED IN THE STOOL. THE RHABDITIFORM LARVA HATCHES 2 DAYS AFTER THE EGGS ARE PASSED IN THE SOIL.
NOTE: BASED ON THE METHOD OF REPRODUCTION, NEMATODES ARE CLASSIFIED AS FOLLOWS:
- OVIPAROUS - THEY LAY EGGS:
- UNSEGMENTED EGGS: ASCARIS LUMBRICOIDES, TRICHURIS TRICHURIA
- SEGMENTED EGGS: ANCYLOSTOMA DUODENALE, NECATOR AMERICANUS
- EGGS CONTAINING LARVA: ENTEROBIUS VERMICULARIS
- VIVIPAROUS - THEY PRODUCE LARVAE. E.G., TRICHINELLA SPIRALIS, WUCHERERIA BANCROFTI, BRUGIA MALAYI
- OVOVIVIPAROUS – THEY LAY EGGS CONTAINING FULLY FORMED LARVAE THAT HATCH IMMEDIATELY. E.G.,
STRONGYLOIDES STERCORALIS

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: THE FOLLOWING IMAGE DEPICTS:
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE DEPICTS THE PRODUCTION OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES BY HYBRIDOMA TECHNOLOGY.
THE FOLLOWING ARE THE STEPS INVOLVED IN HYBRIDOMA TECHNOLOGY:
- MICE ARE IMMUNIZED WITH AN ANTIGEN. AFTER SEVERAL WEEKS OF IMMUNIZATION, BLOOD SAMPLES ARE
OBTAINED FROM MICE FOR MEASUREMENT OF SERUM ANTIBODIES.
- WHEN THE ANTIBODY TITER IS HIGH ENOUGH, MICE ARE COMMONLY BOOSTED BY INJECTING ANTIGEN,
WITHOUT ADJUVANT, INTRAPERITONEALLY OR INTRAVENOUSLY. THEN THE MICE ARE EUTHANIZED AND THEIR
SPLEENS REMOVED FOR IN VITRO HYBRIDOMA CELL PRODUCTION.
- FUSING ANTIBODY-PRODUCING SPLEEN CELLS, WHICH HAVE A LIMITED LIFE SPAN, WITH MYELOMA CELLS
(DERIVED FROM AN IMMORTAL TUMOR OF LYMPHOCYTES) RESULTS IN A HYBRIDOMA THAT IS CAPABLE OF
UNLIMITED GROWTH.
- THE CELLS ARE CULTURED IN A MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE, AMINOPTERIN, AND THYMIDINE (HAT
MEDIUM) WHICH ALLOWS ONLY THE FUSED CELLS TO SURVIVE IN CULTURE.
- MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES ARE THEN HARVESTED.

ALBERT’S, NEISSER’S, AND PONDER’S STAIN ARE USED TO DEMONSTRATE THE METACHROMATIC

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE INFECTION PRESENTS WITH MUCUS IN STOOLS AND ABDOMINAL PAIN?
questions.explanation:
STOOLS WITH MUCUS AND ABDOMINAL PAIN ARE SEEN IN INFECTION DUE TO ENTAMOEBA.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF INTESTINAL AMEBIASIS:
- ACUTE INTESTINAL AMEBIASIS PRESENTS AS DYSENTERY ACCOMPANIED BY LOWER ABDOMINAL DISCOMFORT
AND FLATULENCE. STOOLS USUALLY HAVE BLOOD AND MUCUS.
- CHRONIC AMEBIASIS PRESENTS WITH LOW-GRADE SYMPTOMS SUCH AS OCCASIONAL DIARRHEA, WEIGHT LOSS,
AND FATIGUE.
- A GRANULOMATOUS LESION CALLED AN AMEBOMA MAY FORM IN THE CECAL OR RECTOSIGMOID AREAS OF THE
COLON WHICH CAN RESEMBLE AN ADENOCARCINOMA OF THE COLON.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A - GIARDIA IS OFTEN ASYMPTOMATIC, BUT IN SOME CASES CAN LEAD TO FAT MALABSORPTION, DULL
EPIGASTRIC PAIN, AND FLATULENCE.
OPTION C - CAMPYLOBACTER PRESENTS WITH FEVER, PAIN AND BLOODY OR WATERY DIARRHEA. STOOL CONTAINS
LEUCOCYTES AND BLOOD.
OPTION D - STAPHYLOCOCCAL FOOD POISONING IS TOXIN-MEDIATED AND PRESENTS WITH NAUSEA, VOMITING,
AND DIARRHEA.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT'S PLASMA HAS HIGH LEVELS OF INTERFERON BETA. HE MOST LIKELY HAS AN INFECTION DUE TO
_____
questions.explanation:
INTERFERON-BETA IS SECRETED DURING INFECTION DUE TO VIRUSES.
INTERFERONS ARE CLASSIFIED AS CYTOKINES. INTERFERONS ARE NON-TOXIC, NON-ANTIGENIC AND
SPECIES-SPECIFIC MOLECULES. THEY ARE INACTIVATED BY PROTEASES. THEY ARE STABLE AT PH OVER 2-10,
EXCEPT INF-γ (LABILE AT PH 2) AND ARE NON-DIALYSABLE AND NON-SEDIMENTABLE.
THERE ARE THREE TYPES OF INTERFERONS - α, β AND γ. IFN-α OR LEUKOCYTE INTERFERON IS PRODUCED BY
LEUCOCYTES. IT HAS ANTIVIRAL ACTIVITY, IS IMMUNOREGULAOTRY AND ANTIPROLIFERATIVE. IFN-β OR FIBROBLAST
INTERFERON IS PRODUCED BY FIBROBLASTS AND EPITHELIAL CELLS. IT HAS ANTIVIRAL ACTIVITY AND IS THUS
INCREASED IN VIRAL INFECTIONS. IT ENHANCES MHC CLASS 1 AND NK CELL ACTIVITY. IFN-γ OR IMMUNE
INTERFERON IS PRODUCED BY T-LYMPHOCYTES, NK CELLS . IT ACTIVATES MACROPHAGES, INCREASES NEUTROPHIL
FUNCTION, ENHANCES BOTH MHC CLASS 1 AND CLASS II EXPRESSION AND HAS ANTI-PROLIFERATIVE
(ANTI-TUMOUR) FUNCTIONS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS THE MOST POTENT STIMULATOR OF NAIVE T-CELLS?
questions.explanation:
MATURE DENDRITIC CELLS ARE THE MOST POTENT STIMULATOR OF NAIVE T CELLS.
NAIVE CD4+ T CELLS ARE ACTIVATED WHEN THEY COME IN CONTACT WITH TWO LIGANDS - MHC CLASS II AND A
COSTIMULARY MEMBRANE PROTEIN (EG: CD28). BOTH OF THESE ARE PRESENT IN ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS,
THE MOST POTENT OF WHICH IS THE MATURE DENDRITIC CELL. OTHER PROFESSIONAL ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS
INCLUDE MACROPHAGES AND B LYMPHOCYTES (OPTION C).
OTHER OPTIONS:
1381
OPTION B: FOLLICULAR DENDRITIC CELLS ARE FUNCTIONALLY DIFFERENT FROM DENDRITIC CELLS. THEY ARE NOT
ANTIGEN-PRESENTING-CELLS AND DO NOT ACTIVATE NAIVE T CELLS.
OPTION D: NK CELLS DO NOT STIMULATE NAIVE T CELLS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS AN IMMUNOLOGICALLY PRIVILEGED SITE?
questions.explanation:
THE SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES ARE AN IMMUNOLOGICALLY PRIVILEGED SITE.
IMMUNOLOGICALLY PRIVILEGED SITES CAN TOLERATE THE INTRODUCTION OF ANTIGENS WITHOUT ELICITING AN
IMMUNE RESPONSE. THIS ALLOWS A HIGHER LIKELIHOOD OF GRAFT SURVIVAL, EVEN WITHOUT PERFECT HLA
MATCHING. AS A RESULT, AN ALLOGRAFT CAN BE PLACED IN THESE SITES WITHOUT ENDANGERING A REJECTION
REACTION.
THE UNIQUE IMMUNE TOLERANCE IN THESE REGIONS IS PRIMARILY DUE TO THE LACK OF EFFECTIVE LYMPHATIC
DRAINAGE, WHICH PREVENTS ANTIGEN PRESENTATION TO THE IMMUNE SYSTEM, AND THE PRESENCE OF
BLOOD-TISSUE BARRIERS THAT RESTRICT IMMUNE CELL INFILTRATION. LOW VASCULARITY CONTRIBUTES TO IMMUNE
PRIVILEGE BY MINIMISING ANTIGEN EXPOSURE AND IMMUNE CELL RECRUITMENT.
EXAMPLES OF IMMUNE-PRIVILEGED SITES ARE THE ANTERIOR CHAMBER OF THE EYE, CORNEA, TESTES, AND
BRAIN.
NOTE: ALTHOUGH PART OF THE BRAIN, THE BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER IS ABSENT AT THE AREA POSTREMA, THEREFORE
IT IS NOT AN IMMUNE-PRIVILEGED SITE.

questions.answer: BUFFY COAT IS USED TO DIAGNOSE THE PARASITE
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS THE AMASTIGOTE FORM OF LEISHMANIASIS LOCATED INTRACELLULARLY IN
MACROPHAGES. BUFFY COAT IS USED TO DIAGNOSE THE PARASITE.
VISCERAL LEISHMANIASIS (KALA-AZAR) IS A SLOWLY PROGRESSING INDIGENOUS DISEASE CAUSED BY A
PROTOZOAN PARASITE OF GENUS LEISHMANIA. LEISHMANIASIS IS A PARASITIC DISORDER TRANSMITTED BY THE
1382
BITE OF AN INFECTED FEMALE PHLEBOTOMUS SANDFLY IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES. THE DISEASE IS TRANSMITTED
BY SAND FLIES, WHICH INOCULATE THE FLAGELLATED PROMASTIGOTES INTO THE SKIN OF THE HOST.
IN HUMAN BEINGS, THE DISEASE PRESENTS IN FOUR DIFFERENT FORMS WITH A BROAD RANGE OF CLINICAL
MANIFESTATION:
- VISCERAL LEISHMANIASIS, OR KALA-AZAR,
- CUTANEOUS LEISHMANIASIS,
- MUCOCUTANEOUS LEISHMANIASIS, AND
- DIFFUSE CUTANEOUS LEISHMANIASIS.
THE LIFE CYCLE OF LEISHMANIA INVOLVES TWO FORMS,
- THE PROMASTIGOTE WHICH DEVELOPS AND LIVES EXTRACELLULARLY IN THE SANDFLY VECTOR AND
- THE AMASTIGOTE WHICH MULTIPLIES INTRACELLULARLY IN THE RETICULOENDOTHELIAL CELLS OF THE HOST.
IT LOWERS IMMUNITY, CAUSES PERSISTENT FEVER, ANEMIA, LIVER AND SPLEEN ENLARGEMENT, AND IF LEFT
UNTREATED, DEATH MAY OCCUR DUE TO OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTION.
DIAGNOSIS:
- RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TEST: RK39 RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TEST AND KALA AZAR DIPSTICK TEST STRIP.
- PARASITOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS: DEMONSTRATION OF LD BODIES IN BUFFY COAT SMEAR - CONFIRMATORY.
- ALDEHYDE TEST OF NAPIER: WIDELY USED FOR SURVEILLANCE.
- SEROLOGICAL TESTS FOR DIAGNOSIS: RAPID DIPSTICK TEST, DIRECT AGGLUTINATION TEST, ELISA, INDIRECT
FLUORESCENT ANTIBODY TEST
- LEISHMANIN (MONTENEGRO) TEST: INDURATION OF 5MM OR MORE IS CONSIDERED POSITIVE, USUALLY
POSITIVE 4-6 WEEKS AFTER ONSET IN CUTANEOUS LEISHMANIASIS, VALUABLE FOR DISTINGUISHING IMMUNE
FROM NONIMMUNE SUBJECTS AND ENDEMICITY.
DRUGS USED IN THE TREATMENT OF VISCERAL LEISHMANIASIS ARE SODIUM STIBOGLUCONATE, MILTEFOSINE, AND
AMPHOTERICIN. LIPOSOMAL AMPHOTERICIN SINGLE DOSE 10MG/KG IV IS THE FIRST LINE OF TREATMENT IN
INDIA.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: NUDE MICE ARE NOT RESISTANT TO XENOGRAFT DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF _______
questions.explanation:
NUDE MICE ARE NOT RESISTANT TO XENOGRAFT DUE TO ABSENCE OF T CELL.
A XENOGRAFT IS A TISSUE GRAFT OR ORGAN TRANSPLANT FROM A DONOR OF A DIFFERENT SPECIES.
NUDE MICE LACK BODY HAIR, HENCE THE NAME. THEY LACK A THYMUS AND THUS CANNOT GENERATE MATURE
T LYMPHOCYTES. THE ABSENCE OF T-LYMPHOCYTES MAKES THEM UNABLE TO MOUNT ADAPTIVE IMMUNE
RESPONSES REQUIRING HELPER T CELLS AND CYTOTOXIC T CELLS. THE ABSENCE OF FUNCTIONING T CELLS ALSO
PREVENTS THE REJECTION OF ALLOGRAFTS & XENOGRAFTS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS BURKHOLDERIA CEPACIA RESISTANT TO?
questions.explanation:
BURKHOLDERIA CEPACIA IS RESISTANT TO CEFOTETAN.
B. CEPACIA COMPLEX STRAINS ARE INTRINSICALLY RESISTANT TO AMINOGLYCOSIDES, POLYMIXIN, FIRST AND
SECOND-GENERATION CEPHALOSPORINS (E.G. CEFOTETAN) AND CARBOXYPENICILLINS. THIS ANTIMICROBIAL
RESISTANCE IS MEDIATED BY EFFLUX PUMPS, ANTIMICROBIAL DEGRADATION, MODIFYING ENZYMES OR ALTERED
1448
MEMBRANE FUNCTIONS.
B. CEPACIA IS A GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLUS WHICH CAN CAUSE SEVERE NECROTIZING PNEUMONIA IN PATIENTS
WITH CHRONIC GRANULOMATOUS DISEASE. IT CAN LEAD TO FATAL SEPTICEMIA IN PATIENTS WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS.
ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS THAT ARE EFFECTIVE AGAINST B. CEPACIA COMPLEX INCLUDE MEROPENEM,
CEFTAZIDIME, TRIMETHOPRIM-SULFAMETHOXAZOLE, PIPERACILLIN AND TEMOCILLIN.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE ORGANISMS CAUSES SCOMBROID FISH POISONING?
questions.explanation:
SCOMBROID FISH POISONING IS ASSOCIATED WITH PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA.
IT FOLLOWS THE CONSUMPTION OF BOTH SCOMBROID (MACKEREL-LIKE) FISH AND NONSCOMBROID FISH THAT
HAVE NOT BEEN REFRIGERATED PROPERLY. THE MUSCULATURE OF THESE DARK- OR RED-FLESHED FISH UNDERGOES
DECOMPOSITION BY MORGANELLA MORGANII, ESCHERICHIA COLI, PROTEUS SPECIES, KLEBSIELLA SPECIES, AND
PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA. THERE IS CONSEQUENT DECARBOXYLATION OF THE AMINO ACID L-HISTIDINE TO
FORM HISTAMINE.
A SECOND COMPOUND IS THOUGHT TO PLAY A CAUSATIVE ROLE IN THIS INTOXICATION BECAUSE LARGE DOSES OF
ORAL HISTAMINE DO NOT REPRODUCE THE AFFLICTION. THE TOXIN OR TOXINS INVOLVED ARE HEAT STABLE AND ARE
NOT DESTROYED BY COOKING OR FREEZING.
SYMPTOMS DEVELOP WITHIN 15–90 MIN OF INGESTION. MOST CASES ARE MILD, WITH TINGLING OF LIPS AND
MOUTH, MILD ABDOMINAL DISCOMFORT, AND NAUSEA. THE MORE SEVERE AND COMMONLY DESCRIBED
PRESENTATION INCLUDES FLUSHING, CONJUNCTIVAL HYPEREMIA, PRURITUS, URTICARIA, AND
ANGIOEDEMA. WITHOUT TREATMENT, THE SYMPTOMS GENERALLY RESOLVE WITHIN 8–12 H.

CMV IS THE MOST COMMON VIRUS TO AFFECT RECIPIENTS AFTER ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION (KIDNEY, HEART,

LEUKOPENIA, HEPATOSPLENOMEGALY, MYALGIA, AND ARTHRALGIA. ANTIVIRAL PROPHYLAXIS WITH GANCICLOVIR

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: SABIN-FELDMAN DYE TEST IS USED FOR DIAGNOSIS OF WHICH OF THESE CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
SABIN-FELDMAN DYE TEST IS USED FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF TOXOPLASMOSIS.
IT IS BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE THAT THE PRESENCE OF ANTI-TOXOPLASMA ANTIBODIES IN THE PATIENT'S
SERUM INHIBITS THE STAINING OF TROPHOZOITES BY ALKALINE METHYLENE BLUE DYE. TOXOPLASMA
TROPHOZOITES AND COMPLEMENT ARE ADDED TO THE PATIENT'S SERUM WHICH IS THEN INCUBATED FOR AN
HOUR AT 37°C. AFTER INCUBATION, METHYLENE BLUE DYE IS ADDED.
- IF ANTI-TOXOPLASMA ANTIBODIES ARE PRESENT IN THE SERUM, THESE ARE ACTIVATED BY COMPLEMENT AND
THE PARASITE MEMBRANE IS LYSED. THUS, THE TROPHOZOITES ARE NOT STAINED (POSITIVE RESULT).
- IF THERE ARE NO ANTIBODIES, TROPHOZOITES WILL TAKE UP THE STAIN AND APPEAR BLUE UNDER THE
MICROSCOPE (NEGATIVE RESULT).
THE DILUTION OF THE TEST SERUM AT WHICH 50% OF THE TACHYZOITES ARE NOT STAINED IS REPORTED AS THE
ANTIBODY TITER OF THE TEST SERUM. THE TEST IS HIGHLY SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC. HOWEVER, IT CANNOT
DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN RECENT OR PAST INFECTIONS AS IT DETECTS ONLY IGG ANTIBODIES.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS CALLED AS AUSTRALIA ANTIGEN?
questions.explanation:
HBSAG (HEPATITIS B SURFACE ANTIGEN) IS ALSO KNOWN AS THE AUSTRALIA ANTIGEN. IT IS CALLED SO BECAUSE
IT WAS FIRST ISOLATED FROM THE SERUM OF AN AUSTRALIAN PERSON.
SERA FROM HEPATITIS B PATIENTS WHEN OBSERVED UNDER AN ELECTRON MICROSCOPE SHOW THREE TYPES OF
PARTICLES:
- A SPHERICAL PARTICLE: 22NM, MOST ABUNDANT, CONTAINS ONLY HBSAG.
- FILAMENTOUS OR TUBULAR PARTICLE: 22NM, CONTAINS ONLY HBSAG.
- A DOUBLE-WALLED SPHERICAL STRUCTURE: 42NM DIAMETER, IS THE COMPLETE HEPATITIS B VIRUS. IT WAS
DESCRIBED BY DANE AND IS CALLED DANE PARTICLE.
1450

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: BACTERIAL TRANSDUCTION OCCURS BY
options: UPTAKE OF GENETIC MATERIAL BY OTHER BACTERIA.
questions.explanation:
BACTERIAL TRANSDUCTION OCCURS BY BACTERIOPHAGES.
TRANSDUCTION IS A PROCESS OF ACQUIRING BACTERIAL DNA FROM A BACTERIOPHAGE (VIRUS) THAT HAS
INCORPORATED BACTERIAL DNA FROM PREVIOUS HOST BACTERIA.
OTHER METHODS OF EXCHANGE OF GENETIC MATERIAL ARE TRANSFORMATION AND
CONJUGATION. TRANSFORMATION INVOLVES THE UPTAKE OF GENETIC MATERIAL FROM THE ENVIRONMENT, WHICH
IS RELEASED BY OTHER BACTERIA. CONJUGATION IS THE DIRECT TRANSFER OF DNA FROM ONE BACTERIAL CELL TO
ANOTHER BACTERIAL CELL THROUGH A SEX PILUS OR BRIDGE. THE TRANSFERRED DNA IS A PLASMID, A CIRCLE OF
DNA THAT IS DISTINCT FROM THE MAIN BACTERIAL CHROMOSOME.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt:
INDICATE WHICH FUNGUS IS MOST COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH ORBITAL CELLULITIS IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETIC
KETOACIDOSIS .
questions.explanation:
RHIZOPUS IS THE MOST COMMON FUNGUS ASSOCIATED WITH ORBITAL CELLULITIS IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETIC
KETOACIDOSIS.
DIABETIC PATIENTS ARE IMMUNOCOMPROMISED AND SO PRONE TO DEVELOP OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS LIKE
MUCORMYCOSIS - CAUSED BY RHIZOPUS AND MUCOR SPP. RHINO-ORBITAL- CEREBRAL DISEASE IS THE MOST
COMMON FORM OF MUCORMYCOSIS. IT MOSTLY OCCURS IN DIABETICS. PATIENTS INITIALLY PRESENT WITH EYE OR
FACIAL PAIN, FACIAL NUMBNESS, CONJUNCTIVAL SUFFUSION AND SWELLING, AND BLURRY VISION. INFECTION THEN
SPREADS FROM THE ETHMOID SINUS TO THE ORBIT, LEADING TO PROPTOSIS AND ORBITAL CELLULITIS.
RHIZOPUS IS ANGIOINVASIVE, AND THUS THE INFECTION MAY SPREAD TO THE FRONTAL LOBE AND CAVERNOUS
SINUS, LEADING TO SEPTICEMIA AND THROMBOSES. THE SINUS TISSUE IN SUCH PATIENTS OFTEN DEVELOPS INTO
A BLACK NECROTIC ESCHAR.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: THE ADULT FORM OF ECHINOCOCCUS IS SEEN IN WHICH OF THESE?
questions.explanation:
THE ADULT FORM OF ECHINOCOCCUS IS SEEN IN DOGS AND OTHER CANIDS, WHICH ARE ITS DEFINITIVE HOSTS.

AND MAN. MAN ACTS AS AN ACCIDENTAL INTERMEDIATE HOST (DEAD END). HUMAN INFECTION FOLLOWS THE
INGESTION OF EGGS DUE TO THE INTIMATE HANDLING OF DOGS OR BY EATING RAW VEGETABLES OR OTHER FOOD
CONTAMINATED WITH DOG FECES.
NOTE: HUMANS CAN BECOME ACCIDENTAL DEFINITIVE HOSTS, SECOND INTERMEDIATE HOSTS, OR PARATENIC
HOSTS FOR SPIROMETRA. THESE ARE CESTODES BELONGING TO THE DIPHYLLOBOTHRIIDAE FAMILY. THEY CAUSE A
CONDITION CALLED SPARAGNOSIS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE CAN GROW IN AN ACIDIC PH?
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS, LACTOBACILLI IS THE ONE THAT CAN GROW IN AN ACIDIC PH.
IT IS A GRAM-POSITIVE, FACULTATIVELY ANAEROBIC, NON-MOTILE, NON–SPORE-FORMING BACTERIUM.
LACTOBACILLUS DERIVES LACTIC ACID FROM GLUCOSE, CREATING AN ACIDIC ENVIRONMENT, AND CAN GROW IN AN
ACIDIC MEDIUM. IT IS FOUND IN THE VAGINA AS PART OF ITS NORMAL MICROBIOTA.

questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWN IS OF THE LEISHMAN-DONOVAN BODIES WHOSE PRESENCE ARE DIAGNOSTIC OF KALA AZAR.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS TB TEST DONE ONLY ON WHOLE BLOOD SAMPLE?
questions.explanation:
1452
TB TEST DONE ON A WHOLE BLOOD SAMPLE IS THE INTERFERON-GAMMA RELEASE ASSAY. IT HAS BEEN USED FOR
THE DIAGNOSIS OF LATENT TUBERCULOSIS IN PATIENTS WITH HIV(WHO FREQUENTLY HAVE A NEGATIVE MANTOUX
TEST).
INTERFERON-GAMMA RELEASE ASSAYS INCLUDE:
- QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD
- T-SPOT.TB
QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD QUANTITATES THE AMOUNT OF IFN-γ PRODUCED BY CD4+ T CELLS IN RESPONSE TO
THE ANTIGENS FROM MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD PLUS (QFT- PLUS) IS AN
IMPROVED VERSION OF THE QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD TEST. QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD DETECTS ONLY
TB-SPECIFIC CD4+ RESPONSES. HOWEVER, QUANTIFERON-TB GOLD PLUS DETECTS BOTH CD8+ AND CD4+
T-CELL RESPONSES TO TB-SPECIFIC ANTIGENS.
T-SPOT.TB DETERMINES THE TOTAL NUMBER OF INDIVIDUAL EFFECTOR T CELLS EXPRESSING IFN-γ.
THE TRUENAT TB TEST IS A NEW MOLECULAR TEST THAT CAN DIAGNOSE TB IN ONE HOUR AS WELL AS TEST FOR
RIFAMPICIN RESISTANCE. THIS TEST USES A SPUTUM SAMPLE TAKEN FROM THE PATIENT. ONLY ABOUT 0.5 ML OF
THE SAMPLE IS REQUIRED. GENE XPERT IS ALSO A MOLECULAR METHOD OF TESTING THAT CANNOT USE BLOOD AS
A SAMPLE. (OPTION A AND B)

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: BY WHICH OF THE LISTED OPTIONS ARE MULTIPLE ABSCESSES WITH DISCHARGING SINUSES, DEMONSTRATING SULPHUR GRANULES IN PUS, CAUSED?
questions.explanation:
MULTIPLE ABSCESSES WITH DISCHARGING SINUSES, DEMONSTRATING SULFUR GRANULES IN PUS, ARE
CHARACTERISTIC OF ACTINOMYCOSIS CAUSED BY ACTINOMYCES.
ACTINOMYCOSIS IS A CHRONIC GRANULOMATOUS INFECTION CHARACTERIZED BY INDURATED SWELLINGS IN
THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE WITH SUPPURATION AND DISCHARGE OF SULFUR GRANULES. THE MOST COMMON
CAUSATIVE AGENT IS ACTINOMYCES ISRAELLI.
VARIOUS CLINICAL FORMS OF ACTINOMYCOSIS INCLUDE CERVICOFACIAL, THORACIC, ABDOMINAL, AND PELVIC
ACTINOMYCOSIS. AMONG THEM, ORAL-CERVICOFACIAL ACTINOMYCOSIS IS MOST COMMON, PRESENTING AS A
SOFT TISSUE SWELLING, ABSCESS, OR MASS LESION INVOLVING THE ANGLE OF THE JAW.

CANINUM.

WART-LIKE WITH EXTENSION ALONG THE DRAINING LYMPHATICS.
HISTOLOGICALLY, THE LESIONS ARE GRANULOMATOUS AND THE DARK SCLEROTIC BODIES MAY BE SEEN WITHIN
LEUKOCYTES OR GIANT CELLS CALLED MEDLAR/COPPER PENNY BODIES.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: CHOOSE THE WRONG STATEMENT CONCERNING PLASMODIUM SPECIES:
options: DRUG RESISTANT FALCIPARUM IS SEEN IN INDIA
PRESENCE OF DUFFY BLOOD GROUP ANTIGEN IS PROTECTIVE AGAINST VIVAX
SEVERE MALARIA WITH SHOCK IS CALLED ALGID MALARIA
RELAPSE IS SEEN IN P. OVALE
questions.answer: PRESENCE OF DUFFY BLOOD GROUP ANTIGEN IS PROTECTIVE AGAINST VIVAX
questions.explanation:
THE ABSENCE, NOT THE PRESENCE, OF THE DUFFY BLOOD GROUP ANTIGEN, IS PROTECTIVE AGAINST P. VIVAX
BECAUSE THE DUFFY ANTIGEN NORMALLY SERVES AS THE RECEPTOR FOR PLASMODIUM VIVAX.
DRUG EFFLUX PUMPS ARE THE PRIMARY MODE OF RESISTANCE FOR CHLOROQUINE. IT IS MEDIATED BY AN ABC
TRANSPORTER ENCODED BY P. FALCIPARUM MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE GENE 1 (PFMDR1). THE RESISTANCE OF P.
FALCIPARUM TO CHLOROQUINE INCREASED OVER TIME AND IS PRESENT ACROSS ALL REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY.
1393
ALGID MALARIA IS A RARE COMPLICATION OF SEVERE MALARIA CHARACTERIZED BY HEMODYNAMIC COLLAPSE
MANIFESTING AS SHOCK WITH PRONOUNCED METABOLIC CHANGES AND HYPOTHERMIA.
RELAPSE IS SEEN IN CASES OF PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND PLASMODIUM OVALE.
MALARIA RELAPSE :
TRUE RELAPSE IS CAUSED DUE TO HYPNOZOITES.
THESE ARE RESTING FORMS.
IN THE CASE OF PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND OVALE TWO KINDS OF SPOROZOITES ARE SEEN, SOME OF WHICH :
- MULTIPLY INSIDE HEPATIC CELLS TO FORM - SCHIZONTS
- OTHERS PERSIST AND REMAIN DORMANT AS - HYPNOZOITES
FROM TIME TO TIME SOME ARE ACTIVATED TO BECOME SCHIZONTS AND RELEASE MEROZOITES, WHICH GO
ON INFECTING RBCS PRODUCING CLINICAL RELAPSE.
IN THE CASE OF PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM AND PLASMODIUM MALARIAE, THE INITIAL TISSUE PHASE
DISAPPEARS COMPLETELY AND NO HYPNOZOITES ARE FOUND, HENCE TECHNICALLY RELAPSE IS NOT SEEN.

POSITIVE CRYPTOSPORIDIUM PARVUM.

questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE IMAGE SHOWS CUTANEOUS LARVA MIGRANS. BEING A KENNEL WORKER IS A RISK FACTOR FOR THIS
JOB AS EXPOSURE TO ANIMAL FECES IS HIGH.
AS LARVAE ARE FOUND ON SANDY BEACHES, AND UNDER DWELLINGS, SWIMMING IN NATURAL WATER BODIES
WOULD BE A RISK AND NOT ARTIFICIAL ONES LIKE SWIMMING POOLS.
CLM IS CAUSED BY VARIOUS ANIMAL HOOKWORM SPECIES (E.G., ANCYLOSTOMA BRAZILIENSES), AND THE
PARASITE IS ACQUIRED FROM DIRECT SKIN CONTACT WITH SOIL CONTAMINATED BY DOG OR CAT FECES. THE
PARASITIC INFECTION USUALLY BEGINS WITH AN INFLAMED PAPULE, OFTEN LOCATED BETWEEN THE TOES, WHERE
THE HOOKWORM SPECIES (E.G., ANCYLOSTOMA BRAZILIENSES) LARVAE ENTER THE SKIN.
SERPENTINE OR LINEAR SINGLE-TRACK LINES LATER MARK THE COURSE OF THE LARVAE AS THEY MIGRATE THROUGH
THE EPIDERMIS OF THE TRUNK AND LOWER EXTREMITIES.
IVERMECTIN IS THE FIRST-LINE DRUG FOR THE TREATMENT OF CUTANEOUS LARVA MIGRANS, TAKEN AS A SINGLE
200 µG/KG ORAL DOSE.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: TRANSMISSION ASSESSMENT SURVEY IS CARRIED OUT FOR:
questions.explanation:
TRANSMISSION ASSESSMENT SURVEY IS CARRIED OUT FOR FILARIASIS.
MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION IS USED TO REDUCE INFECTION IN THE COMMUNITY TO LEVELS BELOW A
THRESHOLD AT WHICH MOSQUITOES ARE UNABLE TO CONTINUE SPREADING THE PARASITES FROM PERSON TO
PERSON AND THUS NEW INFECTIONS ARE PREVENTED.
THE TRANSMISSION ASSESSMENT SURVEY (TAS) IS USED TO DETERMINE WHEN INFECTIONS HAVE BEEN
REDUCED BELOW TARGET THRESHOLDS AND MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION CAN STOP. ONCE MDA HAS STOPPED,
TAS IS USED AS A SURVEILLANCE TOOL TO DETERMINE THAT INFECTION LEVELS ARE SUSTAINED BELOW TARGET
THRESHOLDS.

questions.prompt:
A HOSPITAL HAS REPORTED AN OUTBREAK OF MRSA INFECTION. ON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS FOUND OUT
THAT A STAFF NURSE HAD NASAL CARRIAGE OF MRSA. WHICH OF THESE DRUGS HELPS IN THE
REMOVAL OF COLONIZATION OF BACTERIA?
questions.explanation:
TOPICAL MUPIROCIN IS THE PREFERRED AGENT FOR THE ELIMINATION OF NASAL CARRIERS OF MRSA.
AS MUPIROCIN HAS NO STRUCTURAL SIMILARITIES WITH EXISTING SYSTEMIC ANTIBIOTICS THAT MIGHT LEAD TO
THE DEVELOPMENT OF CROSS-RESISTANCE AND HAS MINIMAL TOXICITY IN ITS TOPICAL FORM, IT IS APPROVED FOR
THE PREVENTION OF MRSA OUTBREAKS
MIXED THERAPY WITH SYSTEMIC AGENTS IS NOT PREFERRED AS IT WOULD CAUSE UNNECESSARY ANTIBIOTIC
EXPOSURE POTENTIALLY PAVING WAY FOR DRUG RESISTANCE.

questions.prompt:
A 25-YEAR OLD MAN PRESENTS WITH A HISTORY OF URETHRAL DISCHARGE FOR THE PAST THREE DAYS. A GRAM

GONORRHOEAE INFECTION. NEISSERIA IS NOT AN OBLIGATE INTRACELLULAR ORGANISM, IT CAN ALSO OCCUR
EXTRACELLULARLY I.E, IT IS A FACULTATIVE INTRACELLULAR ORGANISM. THE OTHER NEISSERIA THAT ARE FOUND AS
NORMAL INHABITANTS OF THE HUMAN RESPIRATORY TRACT OCCUR EXTRACELLULARLY.
NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE IS A GRAM-NEGATIVE, NON-SPORULATING, NON-MOTILE DIPLOCOCCUS THAT
IS AEROBIC BUT MAY GROW ANAEROBICALLY ALSO. IT IS OXIDASE AND CATALASE-POSITIVE.
ALTHOUGH NEISSERIA ARE NON-MOTILE ORGANISMS, THEY SHOW TWITCHING MOTILITY. THIS IS A
FLAGELLA-INDEPENDENT FORM OF BACTERIAL TRANSLOCATION OVER MOIST SURFACES THAT OCCURS BY THE

ATTACHMENT TO HOST CELLS AND INHIBITING PHAGOCYTOSIS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt:
THE CLED MEDIUM IS PREFERRED OVER MACCONKEY AGAR FOR THE CULTURE OF ORGANISMS IN CASE OF
UTI BECAUSE:
options: IT PROMOTES THE GROWTH OF CANDIDA, STREPTOCOCCUS AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS
IT DIFFERENTIATES BETWEEN LACTOSE-FERMENTING AND NON-LACTOSE FERMENTING BACTERIA
IT PROMOTES THE GROWTH OF PSEUDOMONAS
questions.answer: IT PROMOTES THE GROWTH OF CANDIDA, STREPTOCOCCUS AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS
questions.explanation:
CLED (CYSTEINE LACTOSE ELECTROLYTE-DEFICIENT) MEDIUM IS PREFERRED OVER MACCONKEY AGAR FOR THE
CULTURE OF ORGANISMS INVOLVED IN URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS BECAUSE IT IS LESS INHIBITORY AND PROMOTES
THE GROWTH OF GRAM-POSITIVE BACTERIA (EXCEPT β HEMOLYTIC STREPTOCOCCUS) AND CANDIDA.
A COMBINATION OF BLOOD AGAR AND MACCONKEY AGAR IS USED FOR THE PROCESSING OF URINE SPECIMENS.
CLED MEDIUM IS USED AS AN ALTERNATIVE FOR THIS COMBINATION. IT CAN ALSO PREVENT SWARMING OF
PROTEUS, AND IS THUS DIFFERENT FROM BLOOD AGAR. LIKE MACCONKEY AGAR, IT DIFFERENTIATES BETWEEN
LACTOSE FERMENTERS AND NON-FERMENTERS. LACTOSE FERMENTERS CHANGE THE COLOUR OF THE MEDIUM FROM
GREEN TO YELLOW. HOWEVER, THESE TWO FACTS ARE NOT THE REASON IT IS BETTER THAN MACCONKEY AGAR FOR
EVALUATION OF UTI.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE ORGANISMS CAUSE MULTIPLE ALVEOLAR-LIKE LESIONS IN THE LIVER?
questions.explanation:
ECHINOCOCCUS MULTILOCULARIS CAUSES MULTIPLE ALVEOLAR-LIKE LESIONS IN THE LIVER.
E. MULTILOCULARIS LEADS TO THE FORMATION OF A MULTILOCULAR HYDATID CYST, MOST COMMONLY AFFECTING
THE LIVER. IT PRESENTS AS MULTIPLE SMALL CYSTS IN THE LIVER.
1398
ECHINOCOCCUS GRANULOSUS CAUSES A HOLLOW FLUID-FILLED UNILOCULAR CYST IN THE LIVER. THE CT BELOW
SHOWS WATER LILY SIGN, WHICH IS SEEN IN THE HYDATID DISEASE OF THE LUNG. IT IS CAUSED
BY ECHINOCOCCUS GRANULOSUS. (OPTION B)
THE WATER-LILY SIGN OCCURS DUE TO THE DETACHMENT OF THE ENDOCYST MEMBRANE FROM THE CYST WALL,
GIVING THE APPEARANCE OF FLOATING MEMBRANES WITHIN THE PERICYST. THIS MIMICS THE APPEARANCE OF A
WATER LILY. IT IS CLASSICALLY VISUALISED ON PLAIN RADIOGRAPHS (MAINLY CHEST X-RAY) WHEN THE COLLAPSED
MEMBRANES ARE CALCIFIED BUT MAY BE SEEN ON ULTRASOUND, CT, OR MRI.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: ALL OF THESE CAN BE SEEN INTRACELLULARLY IN HEPATOCYTES EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
BABESIA IS AN INTRACELLULAR PARASITE OF RBCS, NOT OF THE HEPATOCYTES.
ITS TROPHOZOITES INVADE THE RBCS.
THE LIVER IS USUALLY NOT AFFECTED AS BABESIA LACK AN EXOERYTHROCYTIC PHASE.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt:
A GIEMSA STAIN OF A THIN PERIPHERAL SMEAR IS PREPARED. WHICH OF THESE CANNOT BE
DIAGNOSED?
questions.explanation:
THE DIAGNOSIS OF COXIELLA BURNETII CANNOT BE DONE USING A GIEMSA STAIN OF A THIN PERIPHERAL SMEAR.
IT IS DONE MAINLY BY SEROLOGY, WHICH SHOWS A RISE IN THE TITER OF SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES TO C. BURNETII.
MICROORGANISMS SUCH AS HISTOPLASMA, LEISHMANIA, TOXOPLASMA, AND PNEUMOCYSTIS CAN ALSO BE
DETECTED WITH GIEMSA, AND IN GASTRIC TISSUES, HELICOBACTER PYLORI (H. PYLORI) APPEAR THIN AND
DISTINCTLY BLUE. GIEMSA’S STAIN IS FREQUENTLY USED FOR DIAGNOSTIC PURPOSES IN HAEMATOLOGY TO
DIFFERENTIATE THE NUCLEAR AND CYTOPLASMIC MORPHOLOGY OF PLATELETS, RBCS, WBCS, AND PARASITES.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS FALSE WITH RESPECT TO INFLUENZA?
options: VIRUS SHEDDING IS PRESENT BEFORE SYMPTOMS BEGINS
5-12 YEARS IS A HIGH RISK GROUP
questions.answer: 5-12 YEARS IS A HIGH RISK GROUP
questions.explanation:
1399
CHILDREN <5-YEARS, ESPECIALLY THOSE <2-YEARS OF AGE ARE AT THE HIGHEST RISK OF SERIOUS
COMPLICATIONS RELATED TO INFLUENZA INFECTION.
OTHER HIGH-RISK GROUPS FOR INFLUENZA INCLUDE ADULTS ≥60 YEARS OF AGE, PERSONS WITH CHRONIC

OPTION A: THE VIRUS IS SHED IN RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS A DAY BEFORE THE ONSET OF ILLNESS AND FOR 3-4

OPTION C: BIRDS, ESPECIALLY AQUATIC BIRDS ACT AS RESERVOIRS OF INFLUENZA VIRUSES.
OPTION D: SECONDARY ATTACK RATE IS 5- 15%.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: β 1-3 GLUCAN ASSAY IS USED TO DIAGNOSE ALL EXCEPT?
questions.explanation:
THE β-1-3 GLUCAN ASSAY CANNOT BE USED TO DIAGNOSE MUCORMYCOSIS. THIS CONDITION IS USUALLY
DIAGNOSED BASED ON CLINICAL FEATURES AND CULTURE.
THE β-1-3 GLUCAN ASSAY DETECTS THE PRESENCE OF (1-3)-β-D-GLUCAN (BDG), AN ABUNDANT CELL WALL
POLYSACCHARIDE FOUND IN MOST FUNGI. IT IS A CHROMOGENIC, QUANTITATIVE ENZYME IMMUNOASSAY (EIA)
DESIGNED TO DETECT BETA-D-GLUCAN BY USING PURIFIED, LYSED HORSESHOE CRAB (LIMULUS POLYPHEMUS)
AMEBOCYTES. 1,3 BETA D GLUCAN LEVEL OF ≥80 PG/ML IS CONSIDERED A POSITIVE RESULT.
FUNGI THAT DO NOT CONTAIN BDG IN THEIR CELL WALLS INCLUDE CRYPTOCOCCUS NEOFORMANS, ZYGOMYCETES
LIKE RHIZOPUS AND MUCOR AND BLASTOMYCES DERMATITIDIS. MUCORMYCOSIS IS AN OPPORTUNISTIC MYCOSIS
CAUSED BY ZYGOMYCETES, WHICH DO NOT CONTAIN (1-3)-β-D-GLUCAN, AND HENCE, THE β 1-3 GLUCAN ASSAY
CANNOT BE USED FOR ITS DIAGNOSIS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS A XENODIAGNOSTIC METHOD?
options: RABBIT ILEAL LOOP ASSAY FOR ETEC
INJECTING AEDES THORAX WITH BLOOD OF A PATIENT WITH SUSPECTED DENGUE
INJECTING A HAMSTER WITH SPLENIC BIOPSY FOR DIAGNOSIS OF LEISHMANIASIS

INTRADERMAL TEST ON GUINEA PIGS FOR TOXIGENICITY OF CORYNEBACTERIUM DIPHTHERIA
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.answer: INJECTING AEDES THORAX WITH BLOOD OF A PATIENT WITH SUSPECTED DENGUE
questions.explanation:
INJECTING AEDES THORAX WITH BLOOD OF A PATIENT WITH SUSPECTED DENGUE IS THE XENODIAGNOSTIC
METHOD AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS.
XENODIAGNOSIS (XENOS- FOREIGN) IS AN INDIRECT METHOD OF IDENTIFYING THE INFECTIOUS DISEASE AGENTS
(I.E. THE PATHOGEN). IN XENODIAGNOSIS, THE VECTOR OF A PATHOGENIC AGENT IS INFECTED AND THE PATHOGEN
IS ALLOWED TO MULTIPLY IN THE VECTOR. THE VECTOR ACTS AS THE “FOREIGN” HOST. LATER, THE VECTOR IS
EXAMINED FOR THE PRESENCE OF THE PATHOGEN.
THIS METHOD WAS FIRST USED BY BRUMPT FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF CHAGAS DISEASE. LABORATORY BRED
REDUVIID BUGS (VECTOR/ FOREIGN HOST) ARE ALLOWED TO FEED ON THE SUSPECTED PATIENTS (ORIGINAL HOST).
AFTER 4-5 WEEKS, THE FECES OF THE BUGS ARE MICROSCOPICALLY EXAMINED FOR AMASTIGOTE FORMS OF
TRYPANOSOMA CRUZI (PATHOGEN).
ANOTHER METHOD OF XENODIAGNOSIS IS THE INTRATHORACIC INOCULATION OF THE MOSQUITOES (VECTOR) WITH
VIRUSES (PATHOGEN). THE VIRUS MULTIPLIES IN DIFFERENT ORGANS OF THE MOSQUITO AND CAN BE EASILY
DEMONSTRATED. AEDES AEGYPTI, AEDES ALBOPICTUS, AND TOXORHYNCHITES MOSQUITOES ARE USED FOR THE
IDENTIFICATION OF THE DENGUE VIRUS.
IN TRICHINELLA SPIRALIS INFECTION, MUSCLE BIOPSY BITS FROM SUSPECTED PATIENTS ARE FED TO LABORATORY
RATS (VECTOR FOR T. SPIRALIS). THE LARVAE OF T. SPIRALIS CAN BE DEMONSTRATED IN THE MUSCLES OF THE
1400
INFECTED LAB RATS.
ADVANTAGE OF XENODIAGNOSIS: IT IS USEFUL IN CASES WHERE A DIRECT MICROSCOPIC DIAGNOSIS IS DIFFICULT
DUE TO THE LOW COUNT OF PATHOGENS IN THE BLOOD OF THE HOST/PATIENT.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: RABBIT ILEAL LOOP ASSAY FOR ETEC IS A METHOD OF DETECTION OF TOXIGENICITY/ VIRULENCE
TESTING.
OPTION C: INJECTING A HAMSTER WITH SPLENIC BIOPSY FOR DIAGNOSIS OF LEISHMANIASIS IS A METHOD OF
ANIMAL INOCULATION.
OPTION D: INTRADERMAL TEST ON GUINEA PIGS FOR TOXIGENICITY OF CORYNEBACTERIUM DIPHTHERIA IS A
METHOD OF VIRULENCE TESTING.
1401

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH GASTROINTESTINAL PROBLEMS INCLUDING ABDOMINAL PAIN AND DISTENSION,
BLOODY AND MUCUS-FILLED DIARRHEA, AND TENESMUS, WITH RECTAL PROLAPSE. A STOOL EXAMINATION
REVEALS THE PRESENCE OF TYPICAL BARREL-SHAPED EGGS. SPECIFY THE POSSIBLE CAUSATIVE AGENT.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL PICTURE AND THE BARREL-SHAPED EGGS ARE SUGGESTIVE OF INFECTION WITH TRICHURIS
TRICHIURA (WHIPWORM).
THE CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES OF WHIPWORM EGGS ARE:
- EGGS ARE BARREL-SHAPED IN THE MIDDLE WITH A PROJECTING MUCUS PLUG AT EACH POLE CONTAINING AN
UNSEGMENTED OVUM. THE PLUGS ARE COLORLESS.
- THEY FLOAT IN THE SATURATED SALT SOLUTION.
- IT HAS A TRIPLE SHELL, THE OUTERMOST LAYER OF WHICH IS STAINED BROWN.
THE BELOW IMAGE SHOWS THE EGG OF TRICHURIS TRICHIURA.
1465
IN MODERATE INFECTIONS OF 20 ADULT WORMS OR LESS, THE WORMS ARE CONFINED TO THE CAECUM AND
ASCENDING COLON. THE SYMPTOMS INCLUDE EPIGASTRIC AND LOWER ABDOMINAL PAIN, DIARRHEA (RARELY
BLOODY), VOMITING, FLATULENCE AND DISTENTION, WEIGHT LOSS, AND INCREASED BLOOD AND IRON LOSS.
IN HEAVY INFECTIONS OF 200 ADULTS WORMS OR MORE (TRICHURIS DYSENTERY SYNDROME), THE WORMS ARE IN
THE DISTAL COLON AND RECTUM. THE SYMPTOMS INCLUDE BLOODY DIARRHEA WITH PROFUSE MUCUS,
ABDOMINAL PAIN, TENESMUS, WEIGHT LOSS LEADING TO CACHEXIA, SEVERE ANEMIA, AND RECTAL PROLAPSE. ON
EXAMINATION, CLUBBING MAY BE PRESENT. BLOOD INVESTIGATIONS MAY SHOW MODERATE EOSINOPHILIA.
CHRONIC INFECTION LEADS TO GROWTH RETARDATION AND NUTRITIONAL DEFICIENCIES. AROUND 0.005 ML OF
BLOOD IS LOST PER DAY PER WORM. IN HEAVY INFECTIONS, AS MUCH AS 4 TO 5 ML CAN BE LOST PER DAY PER
WORM.
TREATMENT IS MEBENDAZOLE OR ALBENDAZOLE.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHAT IS VIRAL INFECTION MIMICKING ERYTHROBLASTOSIS FETALIS?
questions.explanation:
PARVOVIRUS B19 INFECTION MIMICS ERYTHROBLASTOSIS FETALIS.
PARVOVIRUS B19, BELONGING TO THE PARVOVIRUS GROUP CONSISTING OF THE SMALLEST ANIMAL DNA VIRUSES,
PRIMARILY INFECT IMMATURE CELLS OF THE ERYTHROID LINEAGE. IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH ERYTHEMA INFECTIOSUM
(FIFTH DISEASE), TRANSIENT APLASTIC CRISIS, PURE RED CELL APLASIA AND HYDROPS FETALIS.
DURING PREGNANCY, INFECTION WITH PARVOVIRUS B19 CAN LEAD TO SEVERE ANEMIA, NON-IMMUNE HYDROPS
FETALIS AND FETAL DEATH. THIS IS BECAUSE PARVOVIRUS PREFERENTIALLY INFECTS RBC PROGENITOR CELLS. THIS
MIMICS ERYTHROBLASTOSIS FETALIS, IN WHICH MATERNAL ANTIBODIES AGAINST FETAL RBCS CAUSE VARYING
DEGREES OF ANEMIA AND IMMUNE-MEDIATED HYDROPS FETALIS IN SEVER CASES.
PICORNAVIRUS, EPSTEIN-BARR VIRUS AND HSV INFECTIONS DO NOT MIMIC ERYTHROBLASTOSIS FETALIS.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE INVESTIGATIONS DOES NOT USE ANTIBODY MARKING?
questions.explanation:
THE HEMAGGLUTINATION TEST IS NOT BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF ANTIBODY MARKING.
IN TESTS BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF ANTIBODY MARKING, THE ANTIGENS OR ANTIBODIES ARE LABELLED OR
MARKED WITH ENZYMES, FLUORESCENT DYES, RADIOISOTOPES ETC. IN RADIOIMMUNOASSAY, FIXED AMOUNTS
OF ANTIBODY AND RADIOLABELLED ANTIGEN REACT IN THE PRESENCE OF UNLABELLED ANTIGEN. THE LABELLED AND
UNLABELLED ANTIGENS COMPETE FOR BINDING SITES ON THE ANTIBODY. THUS, THE CONCENTRATION OF THE TEST
ANTIGEN CAN BE CALCULATED FROM THE RATIO OF THE BOUND AND TOTAL ANTIGEN COUNTS USING A STANDARD
DOSE-RESPONSE CURVE. IN IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE, FLUORESCENT DYES ARE CONJUGATED TO ANTIBODIES OR
ANTIGENS. THE LABELLED ANTIBODIES OR ANTIGENS CAN THEN BE USED TO IDENTIFY ANTIGENS AND ANTIBODIES,
RESPECTIVELY. IN ELISA, AN ADSORBING MATERIAL - CELLULOSE, AGAROSE, POLYSTYRENE, POLYVINVYL ETC - IS
USED TO BIND TO EITHER ANTIGENS OR ANTIBODIES.
WHEN ANTIBODIES BIND TO ANTIGENS ON THE SURFACE OF RED BLOOD CELLS, THE RESULTANT CLUMPING
REACTION IS REFERRED TO AS HEMAGGLUTINATION. IT IS ROUTINELY PERFORMED TO TYPE RED BLOOD CELLS IN
ABO BLOOD-TYPING. THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS HEMAGGLUTINATION.
1468
NOTE: IF NO HEMAGGLUTINATION OCCURS IT MEANS THE PATIENT’S SERUM HAS ANTI-HAEMAGGLUTININ
ANTIBODIES THAT BIND TO HEMAGGLUTININ AND PREVENT THE CLUMPING REACTION. THIS HEMAGGLUTINATION
INHIBITION REACTION IS A METHOD OF DETECTION OF VIRUSES AND ANTIVIRAL-ANTIBODIES AND IS USED TO
MAKE A DIAGNOSIS OF INFLUENZA.

A 3-YEAR-OLD CHILD PRESENTS WITH A HISTORY OF REPEATED SINOPULMONARY INFECTIONS CAUSED BY
