questions.subject: General Medicine
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD FEMALE PATIENT WITH A KNOWN CASE OF MYASTHENIA GRAVIS ON MYCOPHENOLATE
MOFETIL AND PYRIDOSTIGMINE NOW PRESENTS WITH BREATHING DIFFICULTIES. HER CALCIUM LEVELS WERE
13.5G/DL. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE FOR THE INCREASE IN CALCIUM.
questions.explanation:
THE CAUSE OF HYPERCALCEMIA IN THE FEMALE WITH MYASTHENIA GRAVIS ON MYCOPHENOLATE MOFETIL AND
PYRIDOSTIGMINE IS LIKELY TO BE A PARATHYROID ADENOMA.
PARATHYROID ADENOMAS CAUSE PRIMARY HYPERPARATHYROIDISM AND MAY PRESENT AS A SOLITARY
ADENOMA OR AS A PART OF GENETIC SYNDROMES LIKE MEN SYNDROMES(PARATHYROID HYPERPLASIA).
ELEVATED PARATHYROID HORMONE INCREASES BLOOD CALCIUM VIA BONE RESORPTION, INTESTINAL ABSORPTION
AND RENAL REABSORPTION.
PRIMARY HYPERPARATHYROIDISM IS MOSTLY ASYMPTOMATIC. HOWEVER, IT MAY ALSO PRESENT AS PAINFUL
BONES (SUBPERIOSTEAL RESORPTION, OSTEITIS FIBROSA CYSTICA), RENAL STONES, ABDOMINAL GROANS (PAIN,
NAUSEA, VOMITING, HEARTBURN), NEUROPSYCHIATRIC (IRRITABILITY, PARANOID DELUSION, DEPRESSION),
FATIGUE, AND PROXIMAL MUSCLE WEAKNESS. EXCESS CALCIUM CAN ALSO DEPOSIT IN THE CORNEA
4635
(BAND-SHAPED KERATOPATHY), BLOOD VESSELS (CALCIPHYLAXIS), AND EXTRAVASCULAR TISSUES (CALCINOSIS).
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTIONS A AND D: SMALL CELL CARCINOMA AND ADENOCARCINOMA OF THE LUNG ARE NOT ASSOCIATED WITH
HYPERCALCEMIA. SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA IS ASSOCIATED WITH HYPERCALCEMIA DUE TO PTHRP.
OPTION B: MYCOPHENOLATE MOFETIL OR PYRIDOSTIGMINE ARE NOT KNOWN TO CAUSE HYPERCALCEMIA.

questions.subject: General Medicine
questions.prompt:
A 35-YEAR-OLD FEMALE WITH A HISTORY OF HYPERTENSION PRESENTS WITH PALPITATIONS, DYSPNEA,
BILATERAL BASAL CRACKLES AND IRREGULARLY IRREGULAR PULSE. ECG IS PROVIDED BELOW. WHICH AMONG THESE MANAGEMENT IS LEAST USEFUL?
options: CARDIOVERSION IN A HAEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE PATIENT
BETA BLOCKERS IS TO BE GIVEN FOR RATE CONTROL IF PATIENT IS INTOLERANT TO CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS
IV DIGOXIN FOR VENTRICULAR RATE CONTROL
questions.answer: BETA BLOCKERS IS TO BE GIVEN FOR RATE CONTROL IF PATIENT IS INTOLERANT TO CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS
questions.explanation:
IN THIS PATIENT PRESENTING WITH PALPITATIONS, DYSPNEA BILATERAL BASAL CRACKLES AND IRREGULAR RR
INTERVALS WITH ABSENT P WAVES ON ECG, THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IS ACUTE DECOMPENSATED HEART
FAILURE WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. BETA-BLOCKERS ARE NOT EMPLOYED FOR RATE CONTROL IN PATIENTS WITH
ACUTE HEART FAILURE.
BETA-BLOCKERS AND CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS ARE NEGATIVE IONOTROPIC DRUGS. THEY CAUSE DECREASED
CARDIAC OUTPUT, DECREASED BLOOD PRESSURE, AND INCREASED LEFT VENTRICULAR FILLING PRESSURE THEREBY
WORSENING ACUTE HEART FAILURE. BETA-BLOCKERS ARE FIRST-LINE THERAPY FOR RATE CONTROL FOR ATRIAL
FIBRILLATION IN PATIENTS WITHOUT ACUTE HEART FAILURE.
ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (AF) IS A SUPRAVENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA CAUSED BY ECTOPIC FOCI OR SMALL REENTRY
CIRCUITS WITHIN THE ATRIA. IT HAS AN ATRIAL RATE OF 400-600/MIN AND A VENTRICULAR RATE OF
100-160/MIN.
RISK FACTORS FOR DEVELOPING AF INCLUDE:
- AGE- USUALLY ABOVE 60 YEARS OF AGE
- UNDERLYING HEART DISEASE
- HYPERTENSION
- DIABETES MELLITUS
- OBESITY
- SLEEP APNEA
- POST-CARDIAC SURGERY
- INFLAMMATORY PERICARDITIS
- ACUTE ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION.
FEATURES INCLUDE HEART RATE TYPICALLY RANGING FROM 110-160 BEATS/MINUTE. IT IS IRREGULAR AND RAPID.
PRESYNCOPE AND SYNCOPE CAN BE SEEN. THROMBUS FORMATION CAN OCCUR AND THROMBOEMBOLIC EVENTS
CAN TAKE PLACE.
TYPICALLY, ECG SHOWS AN ABSENT P WAVE AND IRREGULAR RR INTERVALS.
MANAGEMENT IS MAINLY BY CONTROLLING THE RATE BY USING DRUGS LIKE β BLOCKERS (SUCH AS METOPROLOL)
AND CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS (SUCH AS DILTIAZEM AND VERAPAMIL). REVERSION TO SINUS RHYTHM CAN
BE DONE ELECTRICALLY OR USING MEDICATIONS. PHARMACOLOGICAL CARDIOVERSION CAN BE DONE USING
IBUTILIDE, DOFETILIDE AND AMIODARONE (CLASS III ANTIARRYHTHMICS) OR FLECAINIDE AND PROPAFENONE
(CLASS IC DRUGS).
4636
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: SYNCHRONIZED CARDIOVERSION IS THE TREATMENT OF CHOICE IN HAEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE
PATIENTS.
OPTION B: ATRIAL FIBRILLATION PREDISPOSES RISK FOR THROMBUS FORMATION, THEREFORE APPROPRIATE
ANTICOAGULATION HAS TO BE STARTED. DIRECT-ACTING ORAL ANTICOAGULANTS (DOACS) ARE PREFERRED OVER
WARFARIN FOR ANTICOAGULATION. HOWEVER, WARFARIN IS THE PREFERRED DRUG IF THE PATIENT HAS A
MECHANICAL PROSTHETIC VALVE, ADVANCED CKD OR MODERATE-SEVERE MITRAL STENOSIS.
OPTION D: INTRAVENOUS DIGOXIN CAN BE USED TO CONTROL THE VENTRICULAR RATE IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION,
ESPECIALLY IN PATIENTS WITH HEART FAILURE OR THOSE WHO ARE NOT SUITABLE FOR BETA-BLOCKERS OR CALCIUM
CHANNEL BLOCKERS. HOWEVER, DIGOXIN IS NOT ALWAYS THE FIRST-LINE TREATMENT FOR RATE CONTROL.

questions.subject: General Medicine
questions.prompt:
A 25-YEAR-OLD MALE PRESENTS WITH HYPERTHERMIA, AUTONOMIC INSTABILITY, CONFUSION,
HYPERREFLEXIA, MUSCLE RIGIDITY, AND DILATED PUPILS. THE PATIENT TAKES SERTRALINE AND WAS
RECENTLY PRESCRIBED AMITRYPTILINE AND SUMATRIPTAN FOR DEPRESSION AND MIGRAINES, RESPECTIVELY.
INDICATE WHICH MEDICATION IS MOST LIKELY TO BE EFFECTIVE IN TREATING THIS PATIENT'S CURRENT CONDITION.
questions.explanation:
4637
THIS PATIENT WITH A HISTORY OF DEPRESSION TREATED WITH SERTRALINE AND NOW AMITRYPTILINE MOST LIKELY
HAS DEVELOPED SEROTONIN SYNDROME. SEROTONIN SYNDROME IS TREATED WITH CYPROHEPTADINE (5-HT2
RECEPTOR ANTAGONIST). CYPROHEPTADINE CAN EFFECTIVELY TREAT SEROTONIN SYNDROME BY BLOCKING THE
EFFECTS OF EXCESS SEROTONIN.
SEROTONIN SYNDROME IS CHARACTERIZED BY A TRIAD OF:
- AUTONOMIC INSTABILITY - HYPERTHERMIA, HYPERTENSION, TACHYCARDIA, DIAPHORESIS, VOMITING,
DIARRHEA.
- ALTERED MENTAL STATUS - AGITATION, CONFUSION, DELIRIUM.
- NEUROMUSCULAR HYPERACTIVITY - TREMOR, HYPERREFLEXIA, MYOCLONUS.
SEROTONIN SYNDROME RARELY OCCURS WITH A SINGLE SEROTONERGIC DRUG USED AT THERAPEUTIC DOSES. MORE
COMMONLY, IT OCCURS DUE TO THE COMBINED SIDE EFFECTS WITH ANY DRUG THAT INCREASES SERUM
SEROTONIN LEVELS LIKE MAOIS (MONOAMINE OXIDASE INHIBITORS), SSRIS (SELECTIVE SEROTONIN REUPTAKE
INHIBITORS), SNRIS (SEROTONIN-NOREPINEPHRINE REUPTAKE INHIBITORS), TCAS (TRICYCLIC
ANTIDEPRESSANTS), TRAMADOL, ONDANSETRON, TRIPTANS, LINEZOLID, MDMA (AMPHETAMINE),
DEXTROMETHORPHAN, ETC.

Excessive intravascular hemolysis with high free plasma hemoglobin

questions.explanation: Visible cyanosis reflects a sufficient amount of reduced hemoglobin.

questions.explanation: Exertional syncope is a red flag for structural or rhythm-related cardiovascular disease.

Narrow pulse pressure with harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur
Low pulse pressure with opening snap and mid-diastolic rumbling murmur
Normal pulse pressure with continuous machinery murmur across systole

Is accompanied by severe dysphagia and improves promptly with antacids

options: Acute coronary occlusion produces extensive LV necrosis
Severe aortic regurgitation creates massive volume overload
Massive pulmonary embolism increases right ventricular afterload

options: Systolic pump failure with ventricular dilation
Severe isolated diastolic filling restriction with rigid walls
Asymmetric septal hypertrophy with dynamic outflow tract gradient
Primary fibrocalcific pericardial constriction without dilation

questions.explanation: Dilated cardiomyopathy impairs contraction and enlarges ventricular chambers.
questions.subject: General Medicine

options: Fixed coronary stenosis causing demand ischemia during exertion
Acute plaque rupture with occlusive intracoronary thrombosis
Coronary artery vasospasm occurring spontaneously at rest
Diffuse microvascular inflammation without epicardial narrowing
questions.answer: Fixed coronary stenosis causing demand ischemia during exertion
questions.explanation: Stable angina is predictable ischemic discomfort due to supply-demand mismatch.

Elevated cardiac troponin levels confirming acute myocyte necrosis

Persistent ST-segment elevation in two contiguous leads
Normal serial cardiac biomarkers and unchanged baseline ECG
Isolated PR-segment depression with diffuse concave ST elevation

Medial smooth muscle calcification without intimal lipid deposition
Acute adventitial neutrophilic vasculitis causing microaneurysms
Disruption of the internal elastic lamina by primary vasospasm

questions.prompt: The most important modifiable risks for coronary disease include

High serum ferritin and isolated transferrin saturation

questions.prompt: A high-intensity statin reduces coronary risk mainly by
options: Lower LDL cholesterol and stabilizing atherosclerotic plaque
Directly inhibiting cardiac myocyte beta-1 adrenergic receptors
Selectively reducing serum triglyceride levels via PPAR-alpha
Inhibiting cyclooxygenase-1 to suppress platelet thromboxane

Pain only when lying down after meals

questions.explanation: Claudication is reproducible muscle ischemia during walking.

questions.prompt: Critical limb ischemia is suggested by
options: Rest pain, ulcers or gangrene from severe arterial obstruction
Mild exertional calf tightness relieved within five minutes of rest
Dependent ankle pitting edema with stasis brown hyperpigmentation
Nocturnal lower extremity muscle cramps during warm hydration

questions.explanation: Rest pain and tissue loss indicate severe limb-threatening ischemia.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: An acutely painful pale cold pulseless leg requires
options: Emergency evaluation for acute limb ischemia and revascularization
Graduated compression stockings and oral venoactive bioflavonoids
Outpatient venous duplex scanning scheduled within two weeks

Empiric high-dose thoracic radiotherapy prior to obtaining histological diagnosis
Blind percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy without computed tomography guidance

The test must detect every benign histologic variation in the general public
The screening procedure should be applicable to all ages regardless of risk
The cost of individual screening tests should exceed diagnostic confirmatory care
questions.answer: The test should reduce morbidity or mortality in the target population
questions.explanation: Screening must show meaningful outcome benefit and acceptable harms.

Administer oral calcium carbonate supplements with active 1,25-vitamin D
Initiate high-dose thiazide diuretic therapy to promote urinary calcium loss

Anterior horn motor neuron acetylcholine synthesis

Isolated severe prolongation of prothrombin time with normal aPTT
Severe profound thrombocytopenia with platelet count below 20,000

Normal PT and aPTT, severe isolated thrombocytosis and elevated fibrinogen
Isolated prolongation of aPTT with normal platelet count and normal D-dimer
Prolonged bleeding time with normal PT, normal aPTT and normal fibrinogen

questions.prompt: Bioavailability refers to the fraction of administered drug that

questions.prompt: An elderly patient develops digoxin toxicity after dehydration and acute kidney injury. The main pharmacokinetic reason is
options: Reduced renal clearance increases drug accumulation
Enhanced hepatic microsomal enzyme clearance of digoxin
Decreased intestinal absorption of orally administered digoxin
Increased volume of distribution lowering serum concentration

questions.explanation: Digoxin is substantially renally cleared, so AKI raises serum levels and toxicity risk.

questions.prompt: Volume of distribution is increased when a drug
options: Leaves plasma extensively and distributes into tissues
Binds extensively and avidly to circulating plasma albumin
Has high molecular weight and remains confined to vascular space
Is highly ionized at physiologic pH and excluded from lipid membranes
questions.answer: Leaves plasma extensively and distributes into tissues
questions.explanation: Large apparent volume of distribution reflects extensive tissue binding or partitioning.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The loading dose of a drug is mainly determined by
options: Target concentration and volume of distribution
Total body clearance and elimination half-life
Renal creatinine clearance and fraction excreted unchanged
Rate of hepatic microsomal cytochrome oxidation
questions.answer: Target concentration and volume of distribution
questions.explanation: Loading dose quickly fills the apparent distribution space to achieve a target level.

questions.prompt: Maintenance dose is most directly related to
options: Drug clearance and target steady-state concentration
Apparent volume of distribution and peak target level
Rate of gastrointestinal dissolution and bioavailability
Protein-binding percentage and lipid partition coefficient
questions.answer: Drug clearance and target steady-state concentration
questions.explanation: Maintenance dosing replaces drug removed per unit time.

questions.prompt: A patient receiving vancomycin has rising trough levels after creatinine doubles. The best response is to
options: Extend the dosing interval or reduce dose based on renal function and levels
Increase the dose and shorten the interval to overcome declining clearance
Maintain current dose and interval unchanged while monitoring fever curve
Discontinue all therapeutic drug monitoring until renal function normalizes

questions.explanation: Renally cleared drugs need dose adjustment and monitoring when kidney function worsens.

questions.prompt: Steady state is usually reached after about

questions.prompt: A drug with zero-order elimination has
options: A constant amount eliminated per unit time
A constant fraction eliminated per unit time
Elimination independent of dose at all concentrations

questions.explanation: Zero-order kinetics occur when elimination pathways are saturated.

questions.prompt: A patient on phenytoin has disproportionate toxicity after a small dose increase. The explanation is
options: Saturable metabolism causing nonlinear rise in concentration
First-order linear elimination with constant half-life kinetics
Induction of hepatic CYP enzymes accelerating phenytoin clearance
Decreased gastrointestinal absorption resulting in subtherapeutic levels
questions.answer: Saturable metabolism causing nonlinear rise in concentration
questions.explanation: Phenytoin can show capacity-limited metabolism, so small dose changes may sharply raise levels.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Potency refers to the
options: Dose or concentration needed to produce a given effect
Maximum clinical efficacy achievable by a drug at receptor saturation
Time required for fifty percent of circulating drug to be cleared by liver
Ratio between the therapeutic dose and the toxic dose in animal trials
questions.answer: Dose or concentration needed to produce a given effect
questions.explanation: Potency compares how much drug is required for an effect.

questions.prompt: Efficacy refers to the
options: Maximum effect achievable by a drug
Concentration required to produce half-maximal response
Fraction of administered dose reaching systemic circulation
Total duration of action following a single oral dose
questions.answer: Maximum effect achievable by a drug
questions.explanation: Efficacy reflects maximal response, independent of dose needed to reach it.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient taking nitrates for angina develops severe hypotension after sildenafil. The mechanism is
options: Suppression of endogenous nitric oxide synthase
questions.explanation: PDE-5 inhibitors amplify nitrate-mediated vasodilation and can cause dangerous hypotension.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A competitive antagonist shifts an agonist dose-response curve
options: To the right with preserved maximum response if enough agonist is present
Downward with marked depression of maximum response that cannot be overcome
To the left with increased agonist potency and heightened intrinsic activity
Downward and to the left with non-surmountable suppression of all receptor binding
questions.answer: To the right with preserved maximum response if enough agonist is present
questions.explanation: Surmountable competitive antagonism reduces apparent potency but not maximal effect.

questions.prompt: A partial agonist has lower intrinsic activity than a full agonist and can
options: Antagonize a full agonist in the same receptor system
Produce a greater maximal response than the full agonist at saturation
Irreversibly inactivate the receptor through covalent disulfide bonding
Bind only to allosteric sites without occupying the orthosteric pocket
questions.answer: Antagonize a full agonist in the same receptor system
questions.explanation: Partial agonists occupy receptors but produce submaximal activation.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Idiosyncratic drug reactions are usually
options: Unpredictable reactions not explained by usual pharmacologic action
Dose-dependent predictable extensions of primary pharmacologic target effects
Expected toxic manifestations occurring consistently at supratherapeutic doses
Immune-mediated type I hypersensitivity reactions reproducible in all patients
questions.answer: Unpredictable reactions not explained by usual pharmacologic action
questions.explanation: Idiosyncratic reactions are uncommon and patient-specific.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient on warfarin starts trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and presents with high INR and bleeding. The interaction is best described as
options: Reduced warfarin metabolism and increased anticoagulant effect
Induction of cytochrome P450 2C9 accelerating warfarin clearance
Direct displacement of warfarin from plasma albumin with rapid excretion
Inhibition of intestinal vitamin K absorption leading to acute deficiency
questions.answer: Reduced warfarin metabolism and increased anticoagulant effect

questions.prompt: Therapeutic index compares
questions.explanation: A narrow therapeutic index means small concentration changes can cause toxicity.

questions.prompt: A type A adverse drug reaction is generally

Selecting the most recently marketed and broad-spectrum pharmaceutical agent
Prescribing high-dose empirical therapy prior to establishing a clinical diagnosis
Relying exclusively on patient brand familiarity without considering contraindications
questions.answer: Defining the therapeutic objective and choosing the safest effective option
questions.explanation: Good prescribing links diagnosis, treatment goal, patient factors and evidence.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Medication reconciliation is important because it
options: Detects omissions, duplications, interactions and incorrect doses across care transitions
Eliminates the clinical necessity for routine therapeutic drug and laboratory monitoring
Substitutes for detailed diagnostic history taking and formal physical examination
Ensures that all prescribed medications are permanently renewed without reassessment

Expected normal cognitive decline unrelated to recent medication initiation
Acute central nervous system infection requiring immediate lumbar puncture
Paradoxical central dopaminergic hypersensitivity causing acute delirium

questions.explanation: Older adults are vulnerable to anticholinergic delirium, urinary retention and falls.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Prescribing in pregnancy should consider
options: Gestational age, fetal risk, maternal benefit and safer alternatives
Maternal symptom relief exclusively while disregarding potential fetal teratogenicity
The general rule that all pharmacological agents cross the placenta without biological harm
A complete refusal to prescribe any indicated medication regardless of maternal illness severity
questions.answer: Gestational age, fetal risk, maternal benefit and safer alternatives
questions.explanation: Risk-benefit assessment changes with trimester and disease severity.

questions.prompt: Teratogenic risk is greatest for many structural malformations during

The second trimester after organ formation
questions.explanation: Major organ formation occurs early in pregnancy.

options: Treat maternal disease with agents known to be safer in pregnancy
Withhold all antihypertensive therapy to avoid compromising uteroplacental perfusion
Routinely initiate ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers as first-line therapy
Rely solely on dietary salt restriction and strict bed rest without medical treatment

questions.explanation: Untreated severe maternal hypertension is dangerous, but drug choice must avoid known fetal harm.

questions.prompt: In liver disease, drug toxicity may increase because of impaired
options: Metabolism, protein synthesis and biliary excretion
Renal tubular acid secretion and potassium excretion
Gastric intrinsic factor secretion and ileal absorption
Pulmonary surfactant synthesis and alveolar gas diffusion

Predictable therapeutic efficacy across all receptor subtypes
Intrinsic renal clearance and baseline glomerular filtration rate
Compliance rates by simplifying daily dosing administration regimens

Double the dose of enalapril and add an over-the-counter antitussive
Switch immediately to an alternative angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor
Add oral high-dose systemic corticosteroids while continuing the ACE inhibitor

Immediate type I immunoglobulin E-mediated hypersensitivity reaction

questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Tick paralysis usually begins with symmetric lower-extremity weakness about how long after tick attachment?

questions.prompt: A child has ascending symmetric weakness, absent reflexes, normal sensation and normal lumbar puncture; a tick is found in the scalp. The key treatment is
questions.explanation: Medicine 1 states diagnosis depends on finding the tick and removal generally leads to rapid improvement.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The central obligation of the physician-patient relationship is to
options: Place the patient's welfare and informed choices at the center of care
Prioritize institutional financial profitability above clinical indications
Enforce physician treatment preferences irrespective of patient values
Eliminate clinical discussions of diagnostic uncertainty and prognosis
questions.answer: Place the patient's welfare and informed choices at the center of care
questions.explanation: Professional care combines beneficence, respect for autonomy and honest communication.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A complete clinical encounter should integrate disease diagnosis with assessment of
options: The patient's illness experience, values and functional context
Strictly laboratory biomarkers and radiographic abnormalities alone
Solely the patient insurance status and third-party reimbursement rules
Exclusively the biological pathology while disregarding social context
questions.answer: The patient's illness experience, values and functional context
questions.explanation: Good medicine treats the patient who has the disease, not only the disease label.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A 62-year-old with heart failure says she cannot take diuretics because she fears being unable to travel for work. The best next step is to
options: Explore her goals and barriers before revising the treatment plan
Document nonadherence in the chart and discontinue heart failure care
Double the morning diuretic dose without discussing daily schedule
Instruct family members to administer the medication without consent
questions.answer: Explore her goals and barriers before revising the treatment plan
questions.explanation: Adherence improves when the plan fits the patient's life and concerns.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Shared decision-making is most important when
options: More than one medically reasonable option exists with different trade-offs
An acute emergency requires immediate lifesaving protocolized action
Only one clearly superior standard-of-care treatment is available
The patient explicitly delegates all decision-making to the physician
questions.answer: More than one medically reasonable option exists with different trade-offs
questions.explanation: Preference-sensitive decisions require clear explanation of risks, benefits and alternatives.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The most useful opening question in history taking is usually one that
options: Allows the patient to describe the problem in their own words
Demands a brief binary yes-or-no answer regarding specific organ systems
Asks the patient to identify the exact medical diagnostic code for symptoms
Interrupts the narrative immediately to document formal medication names
questions.answer: Allows the patient to describe the problem in their own words
questions.explanation: An open beginning reveals symptoms, sequence and concerns that closed questions can miss.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient with newly diagnosed cancer asks, 'Am I going to die soon?' The best response is to
options: Acknowledge the fear and ask what they understand before giving clear information
Offer immediate reassurance that everything will be completely cured
Quote median five-year survival statistics without assessing readiness
Redirect the conversation away from prognosis toward scheduling tests
questions.answer: Acknowledge the fear and ask what they understand before giving clear information
questions.explanation: Serious conversations need empathy, assessment of understanding and honest information.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The main reason to summarize the patient's story back to them is to
options: Confirm accuracy and show that their concerns were heard
Shorten the formal consultation time to meet clinic quotas
Prove that the physician remembered all clinical details
Demonstrate superiority in medical vocabulary and phrasing
questions.answer: Confirm accuracy and show that their concerns were heard
questions.explanation: Reflection catches errors and strengthens therapeutic alliance.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: In chronic disease care, the physician's role includes helping the patient to
options: Develop self-management skills and realistic goals
Maintain complete passivity during therapeutic decision-making
Rely solely on acute emergency room visits for symptom flares
Avoid active home monitoring of physiologic parameters and symptoms
questions.answer: Develop self-management skills and realistic goals
questions.explanation: Long-term outcomes depend heavily on informed patient participation.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient repeatedly misses diabetes visits because clinic timing conflicts with daily wages. The most patient-centered response is to
options: Identify practical access barriers and arrange a feasible follow-up plan
Formally discharge the patient from practice for persistent nonattendance
Reprimand the patient for prioritizing employment over glycemic management
Discontinue all prescription medications until attendance can be guaranteed
questions.answer: Identify practical access barriers and arrange a feasible follow-up plan
questions.explanation: Social and logistical barriers must be addressed as part of clinical care.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A hospitalized patient refuses a recommended procedure after understanding the risks. The physician should
options: Respect the informed refusal and discuss alternative management
Proceed with the procedure regardless under emergency exception
Obtain surrogate family consent to override the competent refusal
Immediately discharge the patient without offering supportive care
questions.answer: Respect the informed refusal and discuss alternative management
questions.explanation: Capacitous patients may refuse treatment even when refusal increases risk.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A diagnostic hypothesis should be revised most strongly when
options: New findings are inconsistent with the working diagnosis
The patient expresses anxiety regarding diagnostic testing
The initial clinical impression was formed by a senior physician
A rare alternative illness is more intellectually interesting
questions.answer: New findings are inconsistent with the working diagnosis
questions.explanation: Sound reasoning updates probability as new evidence arrives.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Premature closure in diagnosis means
options: Accepting a diagnosis before adequate consideration of alternatives
Discharging a patient before finalizing outpatient documentation
Ordering excessive confirmatory investigations to confirm impressions
Revising a working hypothesis repeatedly as clinical course changes
questions.answer: Accepting a diagnosis before adequate consideration of alternatives
questions.explanation: Premature closure is a common cognitive error leading to missed diagnoses.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A 55-year-old with chest discomfort is diagnosed as gastritis without ECG despite diaphoresis and risk factors. The reasoning error is most likely
questions.explanation: Stopping at a benign explanation before excluding dangerous alternatives is premature closure.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The pretest probability of disease is mainly estimated from
options: Clinical context, history, examination and disease prevalence
The technical sensitivity and specificity of the chosen test alone
The financial cost and processing turnaround time of the laboratory
The subjective physician confidence level in laboratory technology
questions.answer: Clinical context, history, examination and disease prevalence
questions.explanation: Test interpretation depends on probability before the test is ordered.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A highly sensitive test is most useful for
options: Ruling out disease when the result is negative
Ruling in disease definitively when the result is positive
Confirming disease presence regardless of pretest probability
Determining exact disease prognosis in asymptomatic individuals
questions.answer: Ruling out disease when the result is negative
questions.explanation: Sensitive tests have few false negatives, so a negative result reduces probability.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A highly specific test is most useful for
options: Ruling in disease when the result is positive
Ruling out disease when the screening test result is negative
Screening large unselected low-prevalence populations broadly
Replacing detailed medical history taking and clinical examination
questions.answer: Ruling in disease when the result is positive
questions.explanation: Specific tests have few false positives, so a positive result is persuasive.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A low-risk patient requests a whole-body scan. The best explanation against indiscriminate testing is that it
options: May produce false positives and downstream harm without likely benefit
Guarantees discovery of fatal occult malignancies in all screened adults
Has zero technical sensitivity for detecting early anatomic abnormalities
Violates statutory medical licensing requirements in outpatient practice
questions.answer: May produce false positives and downstream harm without likely benefit
questions.explanation: Testing low-probability populations can cause overdiagnosis, anxiety and invasive follow-up.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A D-dimer is negative in a patient with low clinical probability of pulmonary embolism. The appropriate interpretation is
options: CT pulmonary angiography is mandatory for all patients
questions.explanation: A sensitive D-dimer helps exclude PE in low-probability patients.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Bayesian reasoning in clinical diagnosis means that
options: Test results are interpreted by how much they change prior probability
A positive test result establishes a definitive diagnosis irrespective of context
Prior clinical suspicion and baseline population prevalence are completely ignored
Diagnostic testing should be repeated until a confirmatory positive is obtained
questions.answer: Test results are interpreted by how much they change prior probability
questions.explanation: Likelihood ratios modify the probability estimated before testing.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient has recurrent syncope. The physician documents arrhythmia, seizure, orthostatic hypotension and structural heart disease before testing. This is an example of
options: Committing an anchoring cognitive heuristic error
Engaging in unjustified defensive testing practice
questions.explanation: A differential organizes plausible causes and guides targeted evaluation.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Valid informed consent requires disclosure, voluntariness and
options: A relative's signature in every case
questions.explanation: Consent is valid only when a capable patient understands and freely chooses.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Decision-making capacity is task-specific and includes the ability to
options: Understand, appreciate, reason about options and communicate a choice
Recite complex medical literature and memorize pharmacologic actions
Demonstrate complete absence of any diagnosed psychiatric condition
Agree unequivocally with all recommendations made by the treatment team
questions.answer: Understand, appreciate, reason about options and communicate a choice
questions.explanation: Capacity concerns the decision at hand, not a global label.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A confused patient with sepsis refuses antibiotics but cannot explain the consequences. The physician should first
options: Assess and treat reversible causes of impaired capacity while seeking surrogate input
Accept the refusal as an autonomous decision and withhold all further medical therapy
Immediately petition a civil court for permanent legal conservatorship and guardianship
Discharge the patient against medical advice once nonadherence documentation is signed
questions.answer: Assess and treat reversible causes of impaired capacity while seeking surrogate input
questions.explanation: Delirium can impair capacity and urgent care may require surrogate or emergency standards.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Confidentiality may be breached without consent when
options: There is a serious, legally recognized risk to others or mandatory reporting requirement
An immediate adult family member requests clinical details out of personal curiosity
The treating physician desires to discuss clinical findings casually with colleagues
A patient discloses mild non-injurious compliance issues during routine outpatient visits
questions.answer: There is a serious, legally recognized risk to others or mandatory reporting requirement
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is strong but not absolute when law or serious preventable harm applies.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The ethical principle of autonomy primarily protects the patient's right to
options: Make informed decisions about their own body and care
Demand clinically inappropriate or futile interventions
Prevent clinicians from documenting clinical findings
Refuse public health reporting of epidemic pathogens
questions.answer: Make informed decisions about their own body and care
questions.explanation: Autonomy requires respect for informed choices within professional and legal limits.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient with tuberculosis refuses isolation and plans to travel in a crowded bus. The physician's duty includes
options: Taking public health steps to prevent serious transmission
Preserving absolute patient confidentiality at all costs
Administering forced intravenous sedation prior to travel
Providing symptomatic antitussives and endorsing departure
questions.answer: Taking public health steps to prevent serious transmission
questions.explanation: Contagious diseases can create duties to protect others through lawful public health action.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Medical paternalism is least justified when
options: A capable patient has made an informed preference-sensitive decision
An unresponsive trauma patient requires immediate lifesaving surgery
A delirious septic patient lacks decision-making capacity in the ICU
A patient with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requires intubation
questions.answer: A capable patient has made an informed preference-sensitive decision
questions.explanation: Capable informed patients should not be overruled merely because the clinician disagrees.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Truth telling in medicine is best understood as
options: Clear, compassionate disclosure adjusted to the patient's readiness and preferences
Blunt presentation of grim survival statistics without assessing emotional state
Routine withholding of malignant diagnoses to protect patients from distress
Delegating all diagnostic communication exclusively to designated next of kin
questions.answer: Clear, compassionate disclosure adjusted to the patient's readiness and preferences
questions.explanation: Honesty and compassion are both required in difficult conversations.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A family asks the doctor not to tell a competent patient about metastatic cancer. The best response is to
options: Ask the patient how much information they want and whom they want involved
Agree with the family and document an uninformative benign condition
Reprimand the family and immediately disclose all details to the patient
Refuse to provide further clinical care unless the family consents to disclosure
questions.answer: Ask the patient how much information they want and whom they want involved
questions.explanation: The patient controls information preferences if they have capacity.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A medical student wants to post a de-identified rare case with enough details for recognition. The correct action is to
options: Avoid posting unless proper consent and institutional rules are satisfied
Post the full case details on an open social media page if name is omitted
Share the case images in an informal closed messaging group without consent
Change only the occupation and city while leaving unique anomalies visible
questions.answer: Avoid posting unless proper consent and institutional rules are satisfied
questions.explanation: Confidentiality can be breached even without names if details identify the patient.
questions.subject: General Medicine

Suppressing near-miss incident reporting to avoid negative institutional publicity
Relying exclusively on individual practitioner vigilance rather than standardized safeguards

Requires immediate punitive action against personnel
Does not warrant documentation or formal investigation
Indicates that established clinical safety safeguards failed

questions.explanation: Near misses are valuable signals for prevention.

Handled only by scolding the prescriber

questions.explanation: Learning from intercepted errors improves future safety.

Assign individual legal liability and financial restitution
Establish criminal culpability for involved clinical staff
Conceal system vulnerabilities from hospital oversight bodies
questions.answer: Identify contributory system factors and prevention strategies
questions.explanation: RCA looks beyond the final act to conditions that allowed harm.

questions.prompt: The safest handoff communication is one that

Relies entirely on unwritten informal hallway verbal conversations
Transfers clinical responsibility without discussing active pending laboratory results
Focuses exclusively on room assignments while omitting contingency contingency plans
questions.answer: Uses structured, concise transfer of diagnosis, status, risks and pending tasks
questions.explanation: Structured handoffs reduce omissions during transitions of care.

questions.topicTitle: Quality, Safety and Systems of Care
questions.prompt: A postoperative patient deteriorates overnight after abnormal vitals were not escalated during shift change. The best quality intervention is
options: Create a reliable escalation and handoff process for abnormal vital signs
Instruct nursing staff to be more attentive during overnight vital checks
Discontinue recording vital signs overnight to avoid unnecessary alarms
Mandate intensive care unit admission for all postoperative patients routinely
questions.answer: Create a reliable escalation and handoff process for abnormal vital signs
questions.explanation: A dependable trigger and communication process addresses the system failure.

questions.prompt: Clinical practice guidelines are best used as
options: Evidence-based aids adapted to the individual patient's context
Inflexible mandates that supersede individual physician judgment in every case
Legally binding administrative directives establishing statutory malpractice standards
Rigid protocols that remove the necessity of discussing patient values and preferences
questions.answer: Evidence-based aids adapted to the individual patient's context
questions.explanation: Guidelines support but do not replace individualized clinical reasoning.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.topic: Quality, Safety and Systems of Care
questions.topicTitle: Quality, Safety and Systems of Care
questions.prompt: Checklists improve safety mainly by
options: Reducing omission of critical steps in complex workflows
Replacing formal clinical training and diagnostic decision-making
Serving solely as retrospective documentation for billing audits
Eliminating the need for team communication during operative procedures
questions.answer: Reducing omission of critical steps in complex workflows
questions.explanation: Checklists protect against predictable memory and coordination failures.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.explanation: Insertion bundles reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections.

questions.prompt: Open disclosure after a harmful medical error should include
options: Honest explanation, apology where appropriate and steps to reduce future harm
Minimization of the occurrence and denial of institutional involvement
Passive concealment unless the patient or family initiates legal discovery
Altering clinical documentation retrospectively to obscure causative factors
questions.answer: Honest explanation, apology where appropriate and steps to reduce future harm
questions.explanation: Transparency maintains trust and supports learning after harm.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Professionalism in medicine includes competence, integrity, accountability and
questions.explanation: Medicine is a social profession with duties beyond technical skill.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Lifelong learning is essential because medical practice
options: Changes as evidence, technology and population needs evolve
Remains completely static following completion of residency training
Relies entirely on empirical tradition rather than emerging clinical trials
Is unaffected by epidemiological shifts or evolving antimicrobial patterns
questions.answer: Changes as evidence, technology and population needs evolve
questions.explanation: Continuing competence requires updating knowledge and skills.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A physician realizes a new drug they commonly prescribe has important updated safety restrictions. The professional response is to
options: Review the evidence and adjust practice promptly
Continue current prescribing habits unchanged until formal regulatory fines
Dismiss the updated alert as an unnecessary administrative inconvenience
Advise existing patients to discontinue all medications without consultation
questions.answer: Review the evidence and adjust practice promptly
questions.explanation: Professional competence requires responding to credible new safety information.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Conflict of interest is problematic because it can
options: Bias judgment or undermine trust even when no harm is intended
Represent intentional clinical fraud and criminal negligence in every case
Affect prescribing decisions only when substantial cash transactions occur
Improve patient adherence by demonstrating pharmaceutical alignment
questions.answer: Bias judgment or undermine trust even when no harm is intended
questions.explanation: Financial and nonfinancial interests can influence decisions or perception.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: The best response to a pharmaceutical gift that may influence prescribing is to
options: Follow institutional policy and preserve independent clinical judgment
Accept the financial gift if it falls below mandatory legal limits
Prescribe the sponsor proprietary product to maintain relationships
Conceal the gift from institutional compliance committees and patients
questions.answer: Follow institutional policy and preserve independent clinical judgment
questions.explanation: Managing conflicts protects trust and decision quality.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient cannot afford the first-line medicine. Professional care requires the physician to
options: Discuss affordable effective alternatives and access options
Prescribe the expensive agent regardless and blame nonadherence on patient
Withhold treatment completely until the first-line drug becomes affordable
Advise the patient to borrow medications from relatives with similar symptoms
questions.answer: Discuss affordable effective alternatives and access options
questions.explanation: Cost is a real determinant of treatment success and should be addressed.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Cultural humility in clinical practice means
options: Eliciting the patient's beliefs and avoiding assumptions while providing evidence-based care
Applying generalized cultural stereotypes to accelerate diagnostic decision-making
Assuming complete mastery of all cultural and ethnic health practices across populations
Deferring all evidence-based therapies in favor of unverified traditional remedies
questions.answer: Eliciting the patient's beliefs and avoiding assumptions while providing evidence-based care
questions.explanation: Respectful care asks rather than assumes and still explains medical reasoning.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: A patient with limited English nods to a surgical consent discussion but cannot explain the operation. The best next step is
options: Use a trained medical interpreter and reassess understanding
Accept nodding as valid legal consent and proceed with surgery
Ask an accompanying minor child to translate complex operative risks
Have the patient sign English consent forms using hand gestures
questions.answer: Use a trained medical interpreter and reassess understanding
questions.explanation: Language access is necessary for valid informed consent.
questions.subject: General Medicine

questions.prompt: Team-based care is important because complex illness often requires
options: Coordinated contributions from multiple health professionals
Autonomous isolated decision-making by a single attending physician
Subordinating nursing and pharmacy evaluations to medical documentation
Eliminating multidisciplinary discharge planning in favor of physician notes
questions.answer: Coordinated contributions from multiple health professionals
questions.explanation: Good outcomes depend on communication across disciplines and settings.

questions.prompt: A junior doctor is asked to perform a procedure they have never done unsupervised. The professional response is to
options: Seek supervision and disclose their level of experience
Proceed with the procedure independently to demonstrate clinical confidence
Ask the patient for permission to practice without informing senior staff
Sign off the procedure documentation under the name of an absent senior

questions.explanation: Recognizing limits and seeking help protects the patient and supports learning.

options: Current and previous cigarette smoking with pack-years
Cumulative dietary sodium intake during childhood
Frequency of routine dental cleanings and flossing
History of seasonal cutaneous insect bite reactions

questions.prompt: Initial chest imaging in many respiratory disorders generally begins with ultrasound or

Catheter-directed pulmonary angiography with transvenous pressure monitoring
High-resolution positron emission tomography combined with whole-body CT
Immediate invasive diagnostic mediastinoscopy with node biopsy
questions.answer: A plain chest radiograph, preferably posteroanterior and lateral films
questions.explanation: Chapter 278 recommends chest ultrasound or plain chest radiography as early imaging in most respiratory evaluations.

questions.prompt: A bedside ultrasound rapidly detects pneumothorax, pleural effusion and consolidation in an acutely dyspneic patient. This use is supported in which diagnostic chapter?
options: Approach to the Patient with Disease of the Respiratory System
Approach to the Patient with Primary Renal Tubular Disease
Evaluation and Management of Severe Malignant Hypertension
Approach to the Patient with Progressive Neuromuscular Atrophy

questions.explanation: Medicine 1 describes FEV1/FVC as typically reduced in airflow obstruction, though severe air trapping may sometimes mask this.

questions.answer: Cells and organisms from alveolar spaces
questions.explanation: Chapter 280 explains that wedging the bronchoscope and instilling saline allows BAL sampling of alveolar cells and organisms.

Isolated seasonal allergic rhinoconjunctivitis without lower airway symptoms
Normal spirometry with preserved forced expiratory volume in one second

questions.explanation: Medicine 1 lists poorly controlled asthma with frequent bronchodilator use, poor ICS adherence and previous near-fatal admissions as death-risk factors.

questions.prompt: A child with eczema and allergic rhinitis has recurrent wheeze. Which risk background from Medicine 1 best explains the asthma risk?
questions.explanation: Asthma commonly coexists with atopic dermatitis and allergic rhinitis, with allergic rhinitis present in many asthmatic patients.

questions.prompt: Mast cells in asthma are activated by allergens mainly through
options: Loss of surfactant protein A only

Diffuse noncaseating granulomatous inflammation of the alveolar interstitium

questions.explanation: Medicine 1 defines emphysema as alveolar destruction with enlargement of air spaces.

The mainstem left and right bronchi

Daily systemic oral steroids, chronic inhaled antibiotics and long-term bed rest
Routine maintenance theophylline, continuous cough suppressants and prophylactic sedatives

questions.prompt:
A MAN MET WITH A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT, WHICH RESULTED IN PARALYSIS OF BOTH HIS UPPER AND
LOWER LIMBS. HE HAS NOT PASSED URINE AND TENDERNESS IS ELICITED IN THE CERVICAL REGION. WHAT
WILL YOU ADVISE CONCERNING RADIOGRAPHY?
options:
THE PATIENT SHOULD NOT BE SHIFTED AND PORTABLE X-RAY MACHINE SHOULD BE USED AFTER NECK
STABILIZATION.
INSTRUCT THE RADIOGRAPHER TO TAKE CERVICAL AND CHEST X-RAY.

INSTRUCT THE RADIOGRAPHER TO TAKE CERVICAL X-RAY AP AND LATERAL VIEW WITHOUT ANY CERVICAL
SUPPORT.
ORDER A CERVICAL X-RAY AND SHIFT THE PATIENT FROM THE TROLLEY BY HIMSELF.
questions.answer:
THE PATIENT SHOULD NOT BE SHIFTED AND PORTABLE X-RAY MACHINE SHOULD BE USED AFTER NECK
STABILIZATION.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SITUATION SUGGESTS A CERVICAL SPINE INJURY DUE TO TRAUMA. THE PATIENT SHOULD NOT
BE SHIFTED AND A PORTABLE X-RAY MACHINE SHOULD BE USED FOR RADIOGRAPHY AFTER NECK STABILIZATION.
MANAGEMENT IN A TRAUMA PATIENT WITH A SUSPECTED CERVICAL FRACTURE INVOLVES THE FOLLOWING STEPS:
- SPINAL IMMOBILIZATION WITH A RIGID CERVICAL COLLAR AND A LONG SPINE BOARD IS THE IMMEDIATE STEP IN
THE MANAGEMENT OF BLUNT/PENETRATING CERVICAL TRAUMA CASES.
- IT IS FOLLOWED BY A GROSS ASSESSMENT OF SPINAL CORD FUNCTION BY ELICITING EXTREMITY MOVEMENT.
TENDERNESS OVER THE INJURED VERTEBRAE OR THE PRESENCE OF A DEFORMITY IS INDICATIVE OF AN ASSOCIATED
FRACTURE.
- IMAGING IS DONE BY X-RAY OR CT. PORTABLE X-RAY MACHINES ARE PREFERRED TO AVOID FURTHER INJURY
WHILE MOBILIZING THE PATIENT. THEY ARE USEFUL IN VISUALIZING THORACIC AND LUMBAR VERTEBRAE BUT
NOT THE CERVICOTHORACIC JUNCTION. CERVICAL CT HAS BEEN MADE THE MODALITY OF CHOICE IN MOST
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS OWING TO THE HIGH QUALITY OF IMAGES THAT CAN BE OBTAINED.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH RENAL CALCULUS OF > 4 CM OF THE STAGHORN TYPE. SPECIFY THE BEST
MANAGEMENT.
questions.explanation:
THE BEST MANAGEMENT FOR STAGHORN RENAL CALCULUS OF >4 CM IS PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY
(PCNL).
THE INITIAL MANAGEMENT OF RENAL STONES DEPENDS ON THE STONE SIZE AND INCLUDES CONSERVATIVE
MANAGEMENT, EXTRACORPOREAL SHOCKWAVE LITHOTRIPSY (ESWL), AND PCNL. PCNL IS PREFERRED FOR
STONES > 2CM IN SIZE AND FOR STAGHORN CALCULI, WHILE ESWL IS USED TO TREAT RENAL STONES OF SIZE
0.6 TO 1.5 CM. PCNL IS INDICATED IN
- RENAL STONES >2 CM
- STAGHORN CALCULUS
- FAILED SHOCKWAVE LITHOTRIPSY (SWL) OR RETROGRADE INTRARENAL SURGERY (RIRS) FOR RENAL CALCULI
- LOWER POLE RENAL STONES WITH ANATOMY THAT IS UNFAVORABLE FOR ESWL
4651
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION C: URETEROSCOPIC REMOVAL IS ATTEMPTED FOR FAILED SWLS OR PCNLS, AND IS NOT THE FIRST
CHOICE IN THE SURGICAL MANAGEMENT OF RENAL STONES.
OPTION D: RIRS IS A MINIMALLY INVASIVE PROCEDURE SIMILAR TO URETEROSCOPIC REMOVAL, WHERE THE
KIDNEY IS ACCESSED USING A SLIM AND FLEXIBLE URETEROSCOPE IN A RETROGRADE MANNER VIA THE URETERIC
ORIFICE. IT IS INDICATED FOR LOWER POLE RENAL STONES < 2 CM.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: ALL OF THESE CAN BE DONE TO TRANSPORT A POLYTRAUMA PATIENT WHO IS CONSCIOUS EXCEPT?
options: STRAP THEIR THORAX, ABDOMEN AND LOWER LIMBS ON A STRETCHER
PLACE IN PRONE POSITION TO PREVENT ASPIRATION
PUT PATIENT ON LATERAL POSITION AND SHIFT HIM IMMEDIATELY
ROLL THE PATIENT ONTO A HARD BOARD
questions.answer: PUT PATIENT ON LATERAL POSITION AND SHIFT HIM IMMEDIATELY
questions.explanation:
PATIENTS WITH POLYTRAUMA ARE SHIFTED INTO A SUPINE OR PRONE POSITION (NOT IN A LATERAL POSITION) BY
LAYING THEM OVER A FIRM SURFACE TO RESTRICT SPINAL MOVEMENT.
AS PER ATLS GUIDELINES, IN PATIENTS WITH TRAUMA, AIRWAY MANAGEMENT IS FIRST DONE ALONG WITH
CERVICAL SPINE STABILIZATION. ALL TRAUMA PATIENTS UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE ARE CONSIDERED TO HAVE AN
INJURED VERTEBRAL COLUMN.
THE PATIENTS ARE PLACED SUPINE ON A FIRM SURFACE WITHOUT ROTATING OR BENDING THE SPINAL COLUMN
AND A RIGID CERVICAL COLLAR (PHILADELPHIA COLLAR) IS APPLIED. ASPIRATION CAN BE PREVENTED BY PUTTING
THE PATIENT IN THE PRONE POSITION AND STRAPPING CAN BE DONE TO PROVIDE FURTHER STABILIZATION.
LONG SPINE BOARDS WITH STRAPS ARE HELPFUL IN THE RAPID TRANSPORT OF THE PATIENT FROM ONE PLACE TO
ANOTHER. THE PATIENT CAN BE PUT ON THE LONG SPINE BOARD BY LOG-ROLLING (A TECHNIQUE WHERE FOUR
PEOPLE HOLD THE PATIENT AND ROLL THE PATIENT LIKE A LOG WITHOUT ALLOWING ROTATION OR BENDING OF THE
SPINE).
CONSCIOUS AND ALERT PATIENT INDIRECTLY MEANS THAT THEY DON’T NEED INTUBATION AND THEIR AIRWAY IS
PATENT. IF THE PATIENT IS UNCONSCIOUS ALWAYS CHECK THE AIRWAY AND IF NEEDED, ENDOTRACHEAL
INTUBATION MUST BE DONE IMMEDIATELY BY VARIOUS METHODS. PREFERABLY BY DIRECT LARYNGOSCOPY AND
INTUBATION.
4652

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: SELECT THE CONDITION.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS A RESECTED SPECIMEN OF A GALLBLADDER WITH A POLYP ON THE INNER SURFACE.
SPECIMEN OF GALLBLADDER CARCINOMA WOULD INCLUDE AN EN-BLOC DISSECTION OF THE GALL BLADDER,
SURROUNDING LIVER TISSUE AND REGIONAL LYMPH NODES (OPTION D). IN SPECIMENS OF CHOLESTEROLOSIS,
ALSO KNOWN AS STRAWBERRY GALLBLADDER, THE GALL BLADDER WOULD APPEAR YELLOW AND COARSELY GRANULAR
DUE TO THE PRESENCE LIPID NODULES (OPTIONS A AND B).
GALL BLADDER POLYPS ARE USUALLY INCIDENTAL FINDINGS DURING ABDOMINAL IMAGING. MOST OF THEM ARE
BENIGN AND COMPRISE CHOLESTEROL POLYPS, ADENOMYOMAS OR INFLAMMATORY POLYPS. ADENOMATOUS
POLYPS ARE THE MOST COMMON NEOPLASTIC POLYPS. THE MAJORITY OF PATIENTS WITH POLYPS ARE STABLE
AND SMALLER POLYPS ARE KEPT UNDER OBSERVATION. CHOLECYSTECTOMY IS DONE FOR SYMPTOMATIC PATIENTS
(BILIARY COLIC, PANCREATITIS), PATIENTS >50 YEARS, SESSILE POLYPS WITH THICKENING >4 MM AND
POLYPS >10 MM.
THE RISK FACTORS FOR MALIGNANCY IN AN ADENOMATOUS POLYP INCLUDE AGE >50 YEARS, SIZE >10
MM, SESSILE POLYP, DOCUMENTED INCREASE IN SIZE, AND COEXISTENCE WITH GALLSTONES.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION D: THE GALLBLADDER IN A PATIENT WITH CARCINOMA IS REMOVED VIA AN EN-BLOC DISSECTION WITH
SURROUNDING LIVER TISSUE ALONG WITH REGIONAL LYMPH NODES. THE GIVEN IMAGE BELOW SHOWS A CUT
SURFACE OF THE RESECTED GALLBLADDER WITH A TUMOR AT THE NECK ALONG WITH LIVER BED INVOLVEMENT
(MARKED BY THE RED ARROW).
OPTIONS A AND B: CHOLESTEROLOSIS (STRAWBERRY GALLBLADDER) IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE ACCUMULATION OF
LIPIDS (TRIGLYCERIDES, CHOLESTEROL PRECURSORS AND CHOLESTEROL ESTERS) IN THE LAMINA PROPRIA OF THE
GALLBLADDER WALL. THE NODULES ARE LESS THAN 1 MM IN DIAMETER AND THERE IS MUCOUS VILLOUS
HYPERPLASIA, WHICH GIVES IT A COARSE, YELLOW AND GRANULAR APPEARANCE, GIVING IT A STRAWBERRY-LIKE
APPEARANCE. THE GIVEN IMAGES BELOW SHOW CHOLESTEROLOSIS.
4653

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: FR IN SIZE OF FOLEY'S CATHETER REFERS TO:
questions.explanation:
THE FRENCH (FR) MEASUREMENT UNIT REFERS TO THE OUTER DIAMETER.
AS PER THE FRENCH SYSTEM, THE OUTER CIRCUMFERENCE EQUALS 3 TIMES THE OUTER DIAMETER. ONE FRENCH
UNIT (1 FR) EQUALS 1 MM OF THE OUTER CIRCUMFERENCE AND 0.3 MM OF THE OUTER DIAMETER. THEREFORE,
THE OUTER DIAMETER IN MM CAN BE DETERMINED BY DIVIDING THE FR SIZE BY 3.
EXAMPLE: AN 18 FR WOULD HAVE A CIRCUMFERENCE OF 18 MM AND AN OUTER DIAMETER OF 6 MM.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A SCHOOL BUS FULL OF CHILDREN MET WITH AN ACCIDENT. AS THE DOCTOR IN CHARGE OF TRIAGE, WHICH OF THESE WILL YOU ATTEND TO FIRST?
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENT WITH AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION, CATEGORIZED AS RED, SHOULD BE ATTENDED TO FIRST.
TRIAGE IS USED TO CLASSIFY THE PRIORITY OF TREATMENT. IT IS CARRIED OUT AT THE SITE OF THE DISASTER TO
DETERMINE THE PRIORITY FOR IMMEDIATE MEDICAL ATTENTION, TRANSPORTATION, AND ADMISSION TO THE
HOSPITAL. TRIAGE DECISIONS ARE MADE BY DECIDING WHICH INJURIES CONSTITUTE THE GREATEST IMMEDIATE
THREAT TO LIFE. IN GENERAL, AIRWAY PROBLEMS ARE MORE RAPIDLY LETHAL THAN BREATHING PROBLEMS >
CIRCULATION PROBLEMS > NEUROLOGIC INJURIES.
THE INTERNATIONALLY ACCEPTED FOUR-COLOR CODED SYSTEM IS COMMONLY USED. IT INCLUDES:
- RED - HIGH-PRIORITY ATTENTION OR TRANSFER
- YELLOW - MEDIUM PRIORITY
4654
- GREEN - AMBULATORY PATIENTS
- BLACK - DEAD OR MORIBUND PATIENTS

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH PARAMETER IS THE BEST GUIDE TO MONITOR THE ADEQUACY OF FLUID RESUSCITATION IN A PATIENT.
questions.explanation:
URINE OUTPUT IS THE BEST MEASURE OF ORGAN PERFUSION AND THE BEST MONITOR FOR ADEQUACY OF FLUID
RESUSCITATION.
ADEQUATE END-ORGAN PERFUSION IS BEST INDICATED BY URINE OUTPUT OF >0.5 TO 1 ML/KG/H. HOWEVER,
IT DOES NOT GIVE A MINUTE-TO-MINUTE VALUE.
THE LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS IS AN IMPORTANT MARKER FOR CEREBRAL PERFUSION.
THE ONLY CLINICAL INDICATORS OF PERFUSION OF THE GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT AND MUSCULAR BEDS ARE
MEASURES OF LACTIC ACIDOSIS (LACTATE AND BASE DEFICIT) AND MIXED VENOUS OXYGEN SATURATION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CENTRAL VENOUS PRESSURE (CVP) IS THE MEAN PRESSURE IN THE SUPERIOR VENA CAVA, USED FOR
ESTIMATION OF PRELOAD AND RIGHT ATRIAL PRESSURE. NORMAL CVP RANGES FROM 2 TO 7 MM HG (3 TO 9 CM
H2O). A SICK OR INJURED PATIENT WITH A CVP <3 MM HG IS PRESUMED TO BE VOLUME DEPLETED AND
MAY BE GIVEN FLUIDS WITH RELATIVE SAFETY. HOWEVER, CVP IS UNRELIABLE IN ASSESSING VOLUME STATUS OR
LEFT VENTRICULAR FUNCTION WITH RESPECT TO RESUSITATION.
OPTIONS C AND D: BLOOD PRESSURE AND OXYGEN SATURATION DO NOT REFLECT BODY FLUID LEVELS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS THE MOST COMMON PRESENTATION OF ABDOMINAL DESMOID TUMOR?
questions.explanation:
EXPLANATION:
THE MOST COMMON PRESENTATION OF AN ABDOMINAL DESMOID TUMOR IS AN ABDOMINAL MASS.
DESMOID TUMORS, ALSO KNOWN AS FIBROMATOSIS, AGGRESSIVE FIBROMATOSIS OR DESMOID-TYPE
FIBROMATOSIS ARE LOCALLY AGGRESSIVE TUMORS THAT LACK METASTATIC POTENTIAL. DESMOID TUMORS CAN BE
SPORADIC IN ORIGIN OR ASSOCIATED WITH FAMILIAL ADENOMATOUS POLYPOSIS.
THESE TUMORS ARISE FROM FIBRO-APONEUROTIC TISSUE AND TYPICALLY ARE MANIFESTED AS A SLOWLY GROWING
MASS. THEY PRESENT AS FIRM, NON-PAINFUL, NON-TENDER MASSES IN THE ABDOMINAL WALL, SHOULDER, HIP
AND LIMBS, MESENTERY, AND PELVIS. THEY ARE ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH TRAUMA, PREGNANCY, AND ORAL
CONTRACEPTIVE USAGE.
THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR A DESMOID TUMOR IS MRI. IT IS SUPERIOR TO CT IN DEFINING THE
PATTERN AND THE EXTENT OF INVOLVEMENT AND CAN DETERMINE RECURRENCE AFTER SURGERY. DIAGNOSIS IS
ESTABLISHED BY A BIOPSY WITH IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, WHICH STAINS POSITIVE FOR BETA-CATENIN, ACTIN
AND VIMENTIN, AND NEGATIVE FOR DESMIN, CYTOKERATIN AND S-100.
TREATMENT:
- AN INITIAL OBSERVATION IS PREFERRED FOR STABLE, ASYMPTOMATIC, PRIMARY OR RECURRENT DESMOIDS,
ESPECIALLY IF SURGERY CAN CAUSE HIGH MORTALITY.
4655
- SURGICAL RESECTION WITH NEGATIVE MARGIN CLEARANCE IS RESERVED FOR PATIENTS WITH SMALL ABDOMINAL
WALL TUMORS ASSOCIATED WITH PAIN OR AN INCREASE IN SIZE.
- TAMOXIFEN AND NSAIDS ARE USED AS FIRST-LINE MEDICAL THERAPY. OTHER SYSTEMIC TREATMENT OPTIONS
ARE LOW-DOSE CHEMOTHERAPY, TYROSINASE KINASE INHIBITORS, AND FULL-DOSE CHEMOTHERAPY
- RADIOTHERAPY IS PREFERRED FOR CANDIDATES UNFIT FOR SURGERY, PATIENTS REFUSING SURGERY AND WHEN
SURGICAL RESECTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH MORBIDITY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 10-YEAR-OLD CHILD CAME WITH COMPLAINTS OF PAIN OVER THE RIGHT LOWER QUADRANT AND LOWER
BACK PAIN. UPON EXAMINATION, THE PATIENT HAD PAIN OVER THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE HIP ON PASSIVE
EXTENSION WITH A MASS IN THE RIGHT LUMBAR REGION POINTING TOWARDS THE GROIN. SPECIFY THE
MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL HISTORY OF LOWER BACK PAIN, MASS IN THE RIGHT LUMBAR REGION POINTING TOWARDS THE
GROIN AND PAIN ON PASSIVE EXTENSION OF THE IPSILATERAL HIP IS SUGGESTIVE OF A PSOAS ABSCESS.
PSOAS ABSCESS IS A RETROPERITONEAL ABSCESS, CAUSED DUE TO VARIOUS ETIOLOGIES. PREVIOUSLY,
TUBERCULOSIS OF THE SPINE WAS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE SECONDARY TO SPREADING INFECTION FROM THE
DIGESTIVE OR URINARY TRACT, WHICH CAN CAUSE PSOAS ABSCESS. NOWADAYS, CROHN’S DISEASE IS THE MOST
COMMON CAUSE. PATIENTS PRESENT WITH FLANK PAIN, FEVER AND CHILLS, MALAISE AND WEIGHT LOSS. THEY
CAN HAVE REFERRED PAIN TO THE HIP, GROIN OR KNEE. WHEN THE SWELLING EXTENDS ACROSS THE GROIN AND
BELOW THE INGUINAL LIGAMENT ALONG THE COURSE OF THE ILIOPSOAS, IT BECOMES CROSS FLUCTUANT ACROSS THE
INGUINAL LIGAMENT.
IMAGING IS DONE BY A CT SCAN, WHICH SHOWS A LOW-DENSITY MASS WITH SURROUNDING INFLAMMATION
AND INFILTRATION OF SURROUNDING FAT AND GAS OR AIR-FLUID LEVELS.
4656
TREATMENT IS DONE BY PERCUTANEOUS CT-GUIDED DRAINAGE AND APPROPRIATE ANTIBIOTICS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: PYELONEPHRITIS IS USUALLY ASSOCIATED WITH A HISTORY OF URINARY TRACT INFECTION AND SUDDEN
ONSET OF PAIN IN THE FLANK AND HYPOCHONDRIUM, NOT THE LUMBAR REGION.
OPTION C: APPENDICITIS (RETROCAECAL) CAN PRESENT WITH PAIN ON PASSIVE EXTENSION OF THE HIP (PSOAS
SIGN), BUT THE PRESENCE OF A MASS IN THE RIGHT LUMBAR REGION POINTING TOWARDS THE GROIN MAKES IT
AN UNLIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
OPTION D: TESTICULAR TORSION IS A SURGICAL EMERGENCY CONDITION PRESENTING WITH SUDDEN ONSET PAIN
IN THE SCROTUM, GROIN AND LOWER ABDOMEN, TENDERNESS, REDNESS AND EDEMA OF THE SCROTAL SKIN.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH LAYER IS INVOLVED IN BLISTER FORMATION IN A SUPERFICIAL PARTIAL THICKNESS BURN.
questions.explanation:
THE PAPILLARY DERMIS IS INVOLVED IN BLISTER FORMATION IN A SUPERFICIAL PARTIAL-THICKNESS BURN.
FIRST-DEGREE BURNS INVOLVE ONLY THE EPIDERMIS, WITH PAIN, REDNESS, AND MILD SWELLING.
SECOND-DEGREE (PARTIAL THICKNESS) BURNS INVOLVE THE EPIDERMIS AND SOME PARTS OF THE DERMIS (ALSO
KNOWN AS PARTIAL-THICKNESS BURNS). FURTHER DIVIDED INTO:
- SUPERFICIAL SECOND-DEGREE BURNS - INVOLVES THE UPPER PART OF THE DERMIS (PAPILLARY) AND SHOWS
PAIN, BLISTERS, AND SEVERE SWELLING.
- DEEP SECOND-DEGREE BURNS - EXTENDS UP TO THE RETICULAR LAYER OF THE DERMIS AND APPEARS MORE
PALE AND MOTTLED, DOES NOT BLANCH TO TOUCH, BUT REMAINS PAINFUL TO PINPRICK.
THIRD-DEGREE OR FULL-THICKNESS BURNS INVOLVE THE FULL THICKNESS OF THE DERMIS AND SUBCUTANEOUS
TISSUE.
FOURTH-DEGREE BURNS INVOLVE DEEP STRUCTURES SUCH AS MUSCLE AND BONE.
4657

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: PROPER FUNCTIONING OF ICD TUBE IS INDICATED BY _____.
options: CONTINUOUS AIR BUBBLES COMING OUT OF THE UNDERWATER DRAIN
OSCILLATION OF WATER COLUMN IN THE TUBE
questions.answer: OSCILLATION OF WATER COLUMN IN THE TUBE
questions.explanation:
OSCILLATION OF THE WATER COLUMN LEVEL (MOVING UP AND DOWN DURING RESPIRATION) WITHIN THE TUBE IN
THE WATER SEAL CHAMBER IS INDICATIVE OF A FUNCTIONING (PATENT) ICD TUBE.
DURING SPONTANEOUS RESPIRATION, THE WATER LEVEL RISES WITH INSPIRATION AND FALLS WITH EXPIRATION.
WHEREAS DURING POSITIVE PRESSURE VENTILATION, THE OPPOSITE OCCURS. THIS OSCILLATION IS ALSO KNOWN
AS TIDALING.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CONTINOUS BUBBLING INDICATES AN AIR LEAK IN THE DRAINAGE SYSTEM, WHICH SHOULD BE
CORRECTED
OPTION B: CHEST X-RAY IS USEFUL FOR ASSESSING THE POSITION OF THE ICD TUBE INSIDE THE CHEST, NOT ITS
FUNCTIONING.
OPTION C: AUSCULTATION IS NOT USEFUL FOR ASSESSING THE FUNCTIONING OF AN ICD TUBE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A TRAUMA PATIENT SUFFERS A RENAL LACERATION WITH URINE EXTRAVASATION. HE IS MANAGED
CONSERVATIVELY. HOWEVER, AFTER A FEW DAYS, HE PRESENTS WITH A URINOMA. THE NEXT BEST
MANAGEMENT FOR THIS PATIENT WOULD BE?
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENT WITH A HISTORY OF GRADE IV RENAL INJURY (RENAL LACERATION WITH URINE EXTRAVASATION) WHO
DEVELOPS A PERSISTENT URINOMA (A MASS FORMED BY ENCAPSULATED EXTRAVASATED URINE) SHOULD BE
MANAGED WITH THE PLACEMENT OF AN INTERNAL URETERAL STENT.
4658
IN PATIENTS NOT CURED BY URETERAL STENTING, PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROSTOMY OR TRANSCUTANEOUS DRAIN
MAY BE REQUIRED.
MANAGEMENT OF RENAL INJURIES
BLUNT TRAUMA IS THE MAIN CAUSE OF RENAL INJURIES AND IS SELF-LIMITING. BLUNT TRAUMA IS MOSTLY
TREATED CONSERVATIVELY. MOST PENETRATING INJURIES REQUIRE SURGICAL RENAL EXPLORATION.
- GRADING OF INJURY THROUGH CECT
- IF HEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE
- CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT - BEDREST & HEMODYNAMIC MONITORING
- IN GRADE IV, A REPEAT CT SCAN TO ENSURE THE EXTRAVASATION OF URINE HAS RESOLVED.
- IF HEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE
- SURGICAL EXPLORATION AND REPAIR
- IN GRADE V, NEPHRECTOMY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS CONSIDERED BALANCED RESUSCITATION?
options: MAINTAIN PH BY ENSURING ACID-BASE BALANCE
FLUID RESUSCITATION BY GIVING COLLOIDS AND CRYSTALLOIDS
questions.explanation:
PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION IS A PART OF BALANCED RESUSCITATION IN TRAUMA MANAGEMENT TO AVOID
BLEEDING.
DAMAGE CONTROL RESUSCITATION (DCR) I.E. BALANCED RESUSCITATION IS USED IN THE SETTINGS OF MAJOR
TRAUMA. IT AIMS TO CONTROL HEMORRHAGE AND PREVENT COAGULOPATHY PRIOR TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE
TRAUMA TRIAD OF DEATH (HYPOTHERMIA, ACIDOSIS, AND COAGULOPATHY). THE COMPONENTS OF DCR
INCLUDE:
- PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION UNTIL DEFINITIVE SURGICAL CONTROL
- MINIMIZE CRYSTALLOID BASED RESUSCITATION
- EARLY USE OF BLOOD PRODUCTS (PRBCS, FFP, PLATELETS, CRYOPRECIPITATE) IN THE RATIO OF 1:1:1
- USE OF HEMOSTATIC AGENTS SUCH AS TRANEXAMIC ACID, RECOMBINANT FACTOR 7A, PROTHROMBIN COMPLEX
CONCENTRATES
DCR HAS THE FOLLOWING ADVANTAGES:
- MINIMIZES THE IMPACT OF TRAUMA-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY
- LIMITS BLOOD PRODUCT WASTE
- REDUCES THE COMPLICATIONS THAT OCCUR WITH AGGRESSIVE CRYSTALLOID RESUSCITATION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A 25-YEAR-OLD PATIENT PRESENTED WITH NECK SWELLING WHICH MOVES WITH DEGLUTITION AS DISPLAYED BELOW. WHAT IS YOUR DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
A THYROGLOSSAL CYST IS THE ONLY MIDLINE NECK SWELLING THAT MOVES WITH DEGLUTITION. THIS IS BECAUSE
THE THYROID GLAND IS FIXED TO THE HYOID.
THYROGLOSSAL DUCT CYST:
IT IS A CONGENITAL MIDLINE NECK SWELLING THAT TYPICALLY PRESENTS DURING CHILDHOOD OFTEN NOTICED AFTER
AN UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION. IT REPRESENTS THE PERSISTENCE OF THE TRACK OF THE THYROID GLAND AND
CAN BE FOUND ADJACENT TO THE MIDLINE. THE THYROID GLAND DESCENDS EARLY IN FETAL LIFE FROM THE BASE
OF THE TONGUE TOWARDS ITS POSITION IN THE LOWER NECK. AT THE TIME OF DESCENT, THE HYOID BONE HAS NOT
BEEN FORMED AND THE TRACK OF THE THYROID GLAND IS VARIABLE, PASSING IN FRONT, THROUGH, OR BEHIND THE
EVENTUAL POSITION OF THE HYOID BODY.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF THYROGLOSSAL CYST:
- CLASSICALLY THE CYST MOVES UPWARDS ON SWALLOWING AND ON TONGUE PROTRUSION. THIS INDICATES
ATTACHMENT TO THE HYOID BONE.
- SWELLING IS SMOOTH, SOFT, FLUCTUANT (CYSTIC), NONTENDER, MOBILE, OFTEN TRANSILLUMINANT.
- THYROID FOSSA IS EMPTY, IF THERE IS NO THYROID IN THE NORMAL LOCATION.
4660
COMPLICATIONS OF THYROGLOSSAL CYST:
- THE MOST COMMON COMPLICATION IS INFECTION.
- THYROGLOSSAL FISTULA IS AN ACQUIRED CONDITION THAT EITHER FOLLOWS INFECTION OF THE CYST WHICH BURSTS
OPEN OR DUE TO INADEQUATE REMOVAL OF THE CYST.
- 1% OF THYROGLOSSAL DUCT CYSTS ARE FOUND TO BE MALIGNANT OF WHICH THE MOST COMMON TYPE
OF CANCER IS PAPILLARY (85%).
NECK SWELLINGS THAT MOVE WITH DEGLUTITION ARE:
- THYROID SWELLINGS
- SUBHYOID BURSITIS
- DERMOID CYSTS ATTACHED TO THE HYOID BONE
HOWEVER, ONLY THE THYROGLOSSAL CYST MOVES WITH TONGUE PROTRUSION. THIS IS BECAUSE THE DUCT
EXTENDS FROM THE FORAMEN CAECUM OF THE TONGUE TO THE ISTHMUS OF THE GLAND.
SISTRUNK’S OPERATION IS PERFORMED TO EXCISE THE CYST AND PREVENT A RECURRENCE. IT INVOLVES THE
EXCISION OF THE WHOLE THYROGLOSSAL TRACT, INVOLVING REMOVAL OF THE BODY OF THE HYOID BONE,
AND SUPRAHYOID TRACT THROUGH THE TONGUE BASE TO THE VALLECULA AT THE SITE OF THE PRIMITIVE FORAMEN
CAECUM ALONG WITH THE CORE OF TISSUE ON EITHER SIDE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 28-YEAR-OLD PATIENT WAS BROUGHT TO THE CASUALTY WARD WITH HIGH FEVER AND PAIN ABDOMEN. HE
HAD A HISTORY OF BLOODY DIARRHEA FOR SEVERAL MONTHS. HIS PAST HISTORY WAS NEGATIVE FOR
LONG-TERM MEDICATIONS AND PREVIOUS SURGERIES. THE ABDOMINAL X-RAY IMAGE OBTAINED IS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO AND THE RADIOGRAPH ARE SUGGESTIVE OF TOXIC MEGACOLON.
TOXIC MEGACOLON MAY PRESENT WITH FEVER, ABDOMINAL PAIN, AND ABDOMINAL DISTENSION. ABDOMINAL
RADIOGRAPHY SHOWS TRANSVERSE OR RIGHT COLONIC DILATION OF >6 CM AND LOSS OF HAUSTRATIONS. IT IS
USUALLY ASSOCIATED WITH ULCERATIVE COLITIS AS INDICATED BY HISTORY OF CHRONIC BLOODY DIARRHOEA.
IT CAN BE TRIGGERED BY ELECTROLYTE IMBALANCE AND NARCOTICS WHICH INTERFERE WITH GUT MOTILITY.
FEATURES OF SECONDARY BACTERIAL INFECTON AND SEPSIS MAY BE PRESENT. IT CAN BE COMPLICATED BY
INTESTINAL PERFORATION.
IT USUALLY RESOLVES WITH SUPPORTIVE TREATMENT (CORRECTING ELECTROLYTE IMBALANCE, FLUIDS, AND BOWEL
REST) AND MEDICAL THERAPY WHICH INCLUDES GLUCOCORTICOIDS, ANTI-INFLAMMATORY DRUGS, AND
ANTIBIOTICS. HOWEVER, AN URGENT COLECTOMY IS INDICATED IN PATIENTS WHO DO NOT SHOW SIGNS OF
IMPROVEMENT.
INDICATIONS FOR URGENT SURGERY INCLUDE:
- FRANK INTRAPERITONEAL PERITONITIS, SECONDARY TO PERFORATION
- LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE OR INCREASING TRANSFUSION REQUIREMENTS
- WORSENING SYSTEMIC TOXICITY
- WORSENING COLONIC DILATATION
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: VOLVULUS OCCURS WHEN THE AIR-FILLED SEGMENT OF THE COLON TWISTS AROUND THE MESENTERY.
THE SIGMOID COLON IS THE MOST COMMONLY INVOLVED PART OF THE LARGE INTESTINE (90%). THE PATIENT
4661
CAN PRESENT WITH ABDOMINAL DISTENSION, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. X-RAY ABDOMEN SHOWS A BENT INNER
TUBE OR COFFEE BEAN APPEARANCE.
OPTION C: OGILVIE SYNDROME, ALSO KNOWN AS COLONIC PSEUDO-OBSTRUCTION IS A FUNCTIONAL DISORDER
WITH COLONIC DILATATION WITHOUT MECHANICAL OBSTRUCTION. IT OCCURS COMMONLY IN HOSPITALIZED
PATIENTS AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH NARCOTICS, BED REST AND COMORBID DISEASE. X-RAY SHOWS DILATATION OF
THE COLON (PREDOMINANTLY TRANSVERSE COLON) WITH ABSENT MECHANICAL OBSTRUCTION.
OPTION D: PNEUMATOSIS INTESTINALIS IS THE PRESENCE OF GAS WITHIN THE BOWEL WALL SEEN IN ANY PART OF
THE GI TRACT BUT MOST COMMONLY IN THE JEJUNUM. IT IS A PATHOGNOMIC FEATURE OF NECROTIZING
ENTEROCOLITIS. X-RAY OF THE ABDOMEN WILL SHOW INTRAMURAL GAS IN THE BOWEL.
4662

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A USG CAN DETECT LYMPH NODE METASTASES IN A PATIENT WITH BREAST CANCER AND CLINICALLY
NEGATIVE LYMPH NODES BY WHAT PERCENTAGE?
questions.explanation:
A USG CAN DETECT LYMPH NODE METASTASIS IN A PATIENT WITH CLINICALLY NEGATIVE LYMPH NODES BY
50-60%.
THE CLINICAL DETERMINATION OF AXILLARY LYMPH NODE METASTASES HAS AN ACCURACY OF ONLY 33%.
ULTRASOUND (USG) IS MORE SENSITIVE THAN PHYSICAL EXAMINATION ALONE IN DETERMINING AXILLARY
LYMPH NODE INVOLVEMENT DURING THE PRELIMINARY STAGING OF BREAST CARCINOMA.
FINE-NEEDLE ASPIRATION CYTOLOGY (FNAC) OR CORE BIOPSY OF SONOGRAPHICALLY INDETERMINATE OR
SUSPICIOUS LYMPH NODES CAN PROVIDE A MORE DEFINITIVE DIAGNOSIS THAN USG ALONE.
ULTRASONOGRAPHY CAN ALSO BE UTILIZED TO IMAGE THE REGIONAL LYMPH NODES IN PATIENTS WITH BREAST
CANCER. THE SENSITIVITY FOR THE STATUS OF AXILLARY NODES RANGES FROM 35% TO 82% AND SPECIFICITY
RANGES FROM 73% TO 97%.
THE FEATURES OF A LYMPH NODE INVOLVED WITH CANCER ON USG INCLUDE:
- CORTICAL THICKENING
- CHANGE IN SHAPE OF THE NODE TO A MORE CIRCULAR APPEARANCE
- SIZE LARGER THAN 10 MM
- ABSENCE OF A FATTY HILUM
- HYPOECHOIC INTERNAL ECHOES

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A YOUNG BOY WAS BROUGHT TO THE CASUALTY WITH A HISTORY OF FEVER AND ABDOMINAL PAIN. UPON EXAMINATION, HE WAS FEBRILE AND HIS PULSE RATE WAS 104 BEATS/MIN. THE CT SCAN IMAGE IS
DISPLAYED BELOW. WHICH OF THESE SIGNS IS NOT SEEN IN THIS DISEASE?
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENT'S HISTORY AND RADIOLOGICAL FINDINGS ARE INDICATIVE OF ACUTE APPENDICITIS. BALLANCE SIGN IS
NOT SEEN IN ACUTE APPENDICITIS.
4663
FINDINGS ON CT THAT ARE SUGGESTIVE OF ACUTE APPENDICITIS INCLUDE:
- APPENDICEAL DILATATION (>6 MM IN DIAMETER)
- APPENDICEAL WALL THICKENING (>3 MM) AND ENHANCEMENT
BALLANCE SIGN IS SEEN DUE TO A RUPTURED SPLEEN. THE BALLANCE SIGN IS POSITIVE IF THERE IS A FIXED
DULLNESS TO PERCUSSION IN THE LEFT FLANK AND SHIFTING DULLNESS TO PERCUSSION IN THE RIGHT FLANK. THE
FIXED DULLNESS IS DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF COAGULATED BLOOD NEAR THE LACERATED SPLEEN WHILE THE
SHIFTING DULLNESS IS DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF BLOOD IN THE PERITONEAL CAVITY.
OPTION A: DEEP TENDERNESS AT MCBURNEY'S POINT, KNOWN AS MCBURNEY'S SIGN, IS A SIGN OF ACUTE
APPENDICITIS. MCBURNEY'S POINT IS A POINT AT ONE-THIRD OF THE DISTANCE FROM THE ANTERIOR SUPERIOR
ILIAC SPINE AND UMBILICUS.
OPTION B: ROVSING SIGN IS SEEN IN APPENDICITIS. DEEP PALPATION OF THE LEFT ILIAC FOSSA MAY CAUSE
PAIN IN THE RIGHT ILIAC FOSSA.
OPTION C: PSOAS SIGN IS SEEN IN APPENDICITIS. OCCASIONALLY, AN IN■AMED APPENDIX LIES ON THE PSOAS
MUSCLE, AND THE PATIENT WILL LIE WITH THE RIGHT HIP ■EXED, FOR PAIN RELIEF.
