questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: HELLER’S OPERATION IS DONE FOR _____.
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON SURGICAL PROCEDURE FOR ACHALASIA CARDIA IS LAPROSCOPIC HELLER MYOTOMY IN
CONJUGATION WITH PARTIAL FUNDOPLICATION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT TRUE WITH RESPECT TO BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS?
options: IT IS THE INTESTINAL METAPLASIA OF ESOPHAGUS
MUCUS SECRETING FOVEOLAR CELLS ARE CHARACTERISTIC
ALICIAN BLUE IS USED IN THE STAINING OF BIOPSY SPECIMEN
IT IS A REVERSIBLE CELL ADAPTATION
questions.answer: MUCUS SECRETING FOVEOLAR CELLS ARE CHARACTERISTIC
questions.explanation:
MUCUS-SECRETING GOBLET CELLS (NOT FOVEOLAR CELLS) ARE CHARACTERISTIC OF BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS, AS THERE
IS INTESTINAL METAPLASIA OF THE ESOPHAGUS. FOVEOLAR CELLS ARE THE MUCUS-SECRETING CELLS IN THE
STOMACH.
BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS IS A COMPLICATION OF CHRONIC GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE (GERD), AND IT
IS ESTIMATED TO OCCUR IN ABOUT 10% OF INDIVIDUALS WITH SYMPTOMATIC GERD. SYMPTOMS INCLUDE
HEARTBURN, REGURGITATION AND SOMETIMES DYSPHAGIA. OBESE WHITE MEN OVER THE AGE OF 60
YEARS REPRESENT THE HIGHEST-RISK GROUP.
INTESTINAL METAPLASIA IN THE ESOPHAGUS OCCURS DUE TO CHRONIC IRRITATION OF THE ESOPHAGUS IN GERD
(OPTION A) SINCE INTESTINAL EPITHELIUM IS BETTER SUITED TO HANDLING GASTRIC ACID EXPOSURE. HENCE,
MUCUS-SECRETING GOBLET CELLS ARE CHARACTERISTIC OF BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS. SINCE ALL METAPLASIA ARE
REVERSIBLE, BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS IS ALSO REVERSIBLE (OPTION D). ONLY 0.2 TO 1% OF BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS
LEADS TO DYSPLASIA AND ADENOCARCINOMA.
4807
ALICIAN BLUE IS USED IN THE STAINING OF THE BIOPSY SPECIMEN, AS IT STAINS THE GOBLET CELLS (OPTION C).
MUCICARMINE IS THE SPECIFIC STAIN.
SEATTLE PROTOCOL IS USED FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: MODIFIED SHOCK INDEX IS CALCULATED USING?
questions.explanation:
- MODIFIED SHOCK INDEX = HR/MAP
- ORIGINAL SHOCK INDEX = HR/SBP
THE SHOCK INDEX IS A HEMODYNAMIC STABILITY INDICATOR. IN PATIENTS WITH SHOCK, IT IS A
BETTER PREDICTOR OF MORTALITY THAN BLOOD PRESSURE OR HEART RATE ALONE. A SHOCK INDEX >0.9 IS
INDICATIVE OF HIGHER MORTALITY.
4808
THE MODIFIED SHOCK INDEX IS A MORE SENSITIVE INDICATOR OF TISSUE PERFUSION THAN THE ORIGINAL SHOCK
INDEX. IN CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS, THE DBP DECREASES EARLIER THAN SBP, HENCE, THE MODIFIED SHOCK
INDEX USING MAP IS BETTER SUITED TO ASSESS THE SEVERITY OF SHOCK.
4809

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH RENAL CALCULUS OF > 4 CM OF THE STAGHORN TYPE. SPECIFY THE BEST
MANAGEMENT.
questions.explanation:
THE BEST MANAGEMENT FOR STAGHORN RENAL CALCULUS OF >4 CM IS PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY
(PCNL).
THE INITIAL MANAGEMENT OF RENAL STONES DEPENDS ON THE STONE SIZE AND INCLUDES CONSERVATIVE
MANAGEMENT, EXTRACORPOREAL SHOCKWAVE LITHOTRIPSY (ESWL), AND PCNL. PCNL IS PREFERRED FOR
STONES > 2CM IN SIZE AND FOR STAGHORN CALCULI, WHILE ESWL IS USED TO TREAT RENAL STONES OF SIZE
0.6 TO 1.5 CM. PCNL IS INDICATED IN
- RENAL STONES >2 CM
- STAGHORN CALCULUS
- FAILED SHOCKWAVE LITHOTRIPSY (SWL) OR RETROGRADE INTRARENAL SURGERY (RIRS) FOR RENAL CALCULI
- LOWER POLE RENAL STONES WITH ANATOMY THAT IS UNFAVORABLE FOR ESWL
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION C: URETEROSCOPIC REMOVAL IS ATTEMPTED FOR FAILED SWLS OR PCNLS, AND IS NOT THE FIRST
CHOICE IN THE SURGICAL MANAGEMENT OF RENAL STONES.
4709
OPTION D: RIRS IS A MINIMALLY INVASIVE PROCEDURE SIMILAR TO URETEROSCOPIC REMOVAL, WHERE THE
KIDNEY IS ACCESSED USING A SLIM AND FLEXIBLE URETEROSCOPE IN A RETROGRADE MANNER VIA THE URETERIC
ORIFICE. IT IS INDICATED FOR LOWER POLE RENAL STONES < 2 CM.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
YOU ARE DOING AN EMERGENCY LAPAROTOMY FOR A CASE OF INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION. INDICATE WHICH ORGAN WILL
YOU FIRST VISUALIZE TO KNOW IF THIS IS A CASE OF SMALL BOWEL OR LARGE BOWEL OBSTRUCTION.
questions.explanation:
THE CECUM IS THE FIRST ORGAN TO BE VISUALIZED TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THE SMALL AND LARGE BOWEL IN
CASES OF INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION.
DISTENSION OF THE CECUM WILL CONFIRM LARGE BOWEL INVOLVEMENT. THE IDENTIFICATION OF A COLLAPSED
DISTAL SEGMENT OF THE LARGE BOWEL AND ITS SEQUENTIAL PROXIMAL ASSESSMENT WILL LEAD TO THE
IDENTIFICATION OF THE CAUSE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE BEST POSITION FOR A CONSCIOUS PATIENT TO BE IN DURING THE INSERTION OF A RYLE'S TUBE.
questions.explanation:
THE BEST POSITION FOR A CONSCIOUS PATIENT TO BE IN DURING THE INSERTION OF RYLE'S TUBE (RT) IS SITTING
WITH NECK FLEXION. THE DESCRIBED POSITION HELPS IN DIRECTING THE RT TOWARDS THE ESOPHAGUS AND
ALSO PREVENTS IT FROM COILING IN THE OROPHARYNX OR ENTERING THE TRACHEA.
RT, ALSO KNOWN AS NASOGASTRIC (NG) TUBE, MEASURES 120-125 CM. IT HAS 4 MARKINGS AT 40CM
(CARDIA), 50CM (BODY), 60CM (PYLORUS), AND 70 CM (DUODENUM) TO INDICATE THE APPROXIMATE
POSITION AFTER THE PLACEMENT.
INDICATIONS FOR NG TUBE:
- FEEDING IN PATIENTS WITH DYSPHAGIA, DECREASED APPETITE, OR THOSE WHO ARE NIL PER OS (NPO) FOR
MEDICAL OR SURGICAL REASONS.
- ASPIRATION OF GASTRIC FLUID
- GASTRIC DECOMPRESSION IN CASES OF INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION AND PARALYTIC ILEUS.
- ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME
- BOWEL IRRIGATION
THE ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATIONS FOR AN NG TUBE ARE SEVERE MIDFACE TRAUMA, RECENT NASAL SURGERY,
AND BASILAR SKULL FRACTURES
STEPS FOR THE CORRECT INSERTION OF RT IN AN ADULT:
- EXAMINATION OF THE PATIENT’S NOSTRIL FOR ANY ANATOMICAL ABNORMALITIES AND THEN INSTILLATION WITH
10 ML OF 1% LIGNOCAINE
- NEX METHOD IS USED TO MEASURE THE LENGTH OF THE RT: PLACE THE EXIT PORT OF THE TUBE AT THE TIP OF
THE NOSE. EXTEND THE TUBE TO THE EARLOBE, AND THEN TO THE XIPHISTERNUM.
- THE PATIENT IS ASKED TO SIT UPRIGHT WITH PARTIAL NECK FLEXION. THE TIP OF THE RYLE’S TUBE IS
LUBRICATED AND PASSED ALONG THE FLOOR OF THE NASAL PASSAGE UNTIL A RESISTANCE IS FELT(CORRESPONDS TO
NASOPHARYNX)
- THE PATIENT IS SUBSEQUENTLY ASKED TO SWALLOW WATER TO GUIDE THE TUBE THROUGH THE ESOPHAGUS INTO
THE STOMACH UNTIL THE MARKED LENGTH (BASED ON THE NEX METHOD).
4710
- NG TUBE IS FINALLY TAPED TO SECURE IT IN PLACE.
CONFIRMATION OF THE CORRECT POSITION IS DONE BY:
- AUSCULTATION IN THE EPIGASTRIC AREA WHILE INJECTING A BOLUS OF AIR
- X-RAY CHEST TO LOCATE THE LEAD MARKERS
- ASPIRATION OF CONTENTS AND SUBSEQUENTLY CONFIRMING GASTRIC ORIGIN (PH <6 INDICATES GASTRIC
PLACEMENT)

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: PICK FROM THE FOLLOWING THE USUAL CAUSE OF THYROID STORM IN THYROIDECTOMY:
options: ROUGH HANDLING OF THYROID DURING SURGERY
questions.explanation:
THE USUAL CAUSE OF THYROID STORM IN THYROIDECTOMY IS INADEQUATE PATIENT PREPARATION BEFORE
SURGERY. PATIENT PREPARATION PRE-OPERATIVELY INVOLVES ENSURING A EUTHYROID STATE.
ROUGH HANDLING OF THE THYROID IN THYROIDECTOMY DOES NOT CAUSE A THYROID STORM. THOUGH A
SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF THYROGLOBULIN IS STORED IN THE ACINAR CELLS, THEY ARE INACTIVE UNLESS CONVERTED
TO THYROXINE (T3 AND T4).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THESE COLORED CANNULA WILL YOU USE TO ACHIEVE MAXIMUM FLOW RATE, IN A
PATIENT WHO NEEDS A LARGE AMOUNT OF FLUIDS?
questions.explanation:
GREY COLORED CANNULA IS USED TO ACHIEVE MAXIMUM FLOW RATE IN A PATIENT WHO NEEDS A LARGE AMOUNT
OF FLUIDS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WHO WAS ADMITTED AFTER A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT IS PUT ON MECHANICAL VENTILATION. HE
OPENS HIS EYES ON VERBAL COMMAND AND MOVES ALL FOUR LIMBS SPONTANEOUSLY. CALCULATE HIS
GCS.
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENTS GCS IS EYES-3, VERBAL-NT, MOTOR-6.
IT IS CALCULATED AS FOLLOWS:
4711
- EYE OPENING: OPENING TO VERBAL COMMAND - 3
- VERBAL RESPONSE: IN THE CASE OF ENDOTRACHEAL INTUBATION, THE VERBAL RESPONSE SCORE IS NOTED AS NT
(NON-TESTABLE)
- MOTOR RESPONE: MOVEMENT OF ALL 4 LIMBS SPONTANEOUSLY - 6
TOTAL GCS SCORE IS NOT RECORDED SINCE ONE OF THE COMPONENTS IS NON-TESTABLE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WAS BROUGHT TO THE CASUALTY AFTER A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT (RTA) WITH CHEST TRAUMA.
HE IS CONSCIOUS AND SPEAKS SINGLE WORDS. HE HAS A RESPIRATORY RATE OF 44 CYCLES PER MIN AND A
BP OF 90/40 MMHG. THERE IS A HYPER-RESONANCE ON PERCUSSING THE RIGHT SIDE OF HIS CHEST.
WHAT WILL BE YOUR NEXT, IMMEDIATE STEP?
options: INSERT NEEDLE IN APPROPRIATE INTERCOSTAL SPACE
questions.answer: INSERT NEEDLE IN APPROPRIATE INTERCOSTAL SPACE
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF CHEST TRAUMA WITH A HYPER RESONANT NOTE ON THE RIGHT SIDE SUGGESTS
PNEUMOTHORAX. HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY IN THIS PATIENT SUGGESTS TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX AND THIS
IS MANAGED BY IMMEDIATE DECOMPRESSION BY INSERTION OF A NEEDLE IN THE APPROPRIATE PLACE.
PNEUMOTHORAX REFERS TO THE PRESENCE OF EXCESS AIR IN THE PLEURAL SPACE. ENTRAPMENT OF AIR OCCURS
BY:
- PRIMARY SPONTANEOUS PNEUMOTHORAX - DUE TO THE SPONTANEOUS RUPTURE OF APICAL PLEURAL BLEBS OR
CYSTIC SPACES IMMEDIATELY BELOW THE VISCERAL PLEURA.
- SECONDARY PNEUMOTHORAX - DUE TO THE RUPTURE OF DILATED CYSTIC SPACES IN LUNG DISEASES LIKE
CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD)
- TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX - DUE TO A ONE-WAY VALVE MECHANISM THAT DIRECTS AIRFLOW INTO THE PLEURAL
SPACE LEADING TO A HIGHER THAN ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE ENVIRONMENT. THIS LEADS TO THE AFFECTED LUNG
BEING UNABLE TO EXPAND APPROPRIATELY AND LEADS TO HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY.
TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX IS A SURGICAL EMERGENCY AND THE EXCESSIVE PRESSURE HAS TO BE IMMEDIATELY
RELIEVED. A CHEST X-RAY IS NOT REQUIRED BEFORE EMERGENCY DECOMPRESSION AS IT IS A CLINICAL
DIAGNOSIS, BUT AN X-RAY SHOULD BE DONE FOLLOWING CHEST TUBE INSERTION (OPTION D). TENSION
PNEUMOTHORAX IS MANAGED BY IMMEDIATE NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION IN THE 5TH ICS (ADULTS), FOLLOWED
BY DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT WITH A CHEST TUBE INSERTED IN THE SAME SPACE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: INTUBATION IS PERFORMED WHEN THE PATIENT IS UNRESPONSIVE POST CHEST TUBE INSERTION.
OPTION C: WHILE IV FLUIDS ARE A PART OF THE RESUSCITATION PROTOCOL, THE MANAGEMENT OF TENSION
PNEUMOTHORAX TAKES HIGHER PRECEDENCE AS THE NEXT IMMEDIATE STEP.
NOTE: ACCORDING TO ATLS 10TH EDITION
- IN ADULTS, NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY OR NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION LOCATION IS CHANGED TO THE 5TH ICS
ANTERIOR TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE FROM THE 2ND ICS MIDCLAVICULAR LINE.
- IN THE PEDIATRIC AGE GROUP, THE NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY LOCATION REMAINS AT THE 2ND ICS
MIDCLAVICULAR LINE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS USED FOR WOUND INFECTION GRADING?
questions.explanation:
SOUTHAMPTON WOUND GRADING SYSTEM IS USED TO SCORE THE SEVERITY OF WOUND SITE INFECTION.
4712
SOUTHAMPTON WOUND GRADING SYSTEM:
- GRADE 0 - NORMAL HEALING
- GRADE I - NORMAL HEALING WITH DIFFERENT GRADES OF ERYTHEMA
- GRADE II - ERYTHEMA WITH OTHER SIGNS OF INFLAMMATION AT DIFFERENT PARTS OF THE WOUND.
- GRADE III - CLEAR OR SEROSANGUINOUS DISCHARGE AT DIFFERENT SITES
- GRADE IV - PUS DISCHARGE
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: AMERICAN SOCIETY OF ANESTHESIOLOGISTS (ASA) GRADING IS USED IN PRE-ANESTHETIC CHECKUPS
TO ASSESS A PATIENT'S PHYSICAL HEALTH AND FITNESS FOR ANESTHESIA AND SURGERY.
OPTION B: SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE SYNDROME (SIRS) IS A SET OF CLINICAL CRITERIA USED TO
IDENTIFY AND MONITOR CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH HIGH-GRADE BURNS, SEVERE TRAUMA, AND OTHER MAJOR
SURGERIES.
OPTION D: ACUTE PHYSIOLOGY AND CHRONIC HEALTH EVALUATION II (APACHE II) IS A SCORING SYSTEM
USED TO ASSESS THE SEVERITY AND PREDICT THE OUTCOME OF PANCREATITIS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE MOST COMMON MEDIASTINAL TUMOR?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON MEDIASTINAL TUMORS IN DESCENDING ORDER OF INCIDENCE ARE THYMOMA (25%),
GERM CELL TUMOR (13%), LYMPHOMA, MESENCHYMAL, AND THYROID.
THE MASAOKA CLASSIFICATION AND TNM STAGING ARE USED IN THE STAGING OF THYMOMA.
THE MOST COMMON MEDIASTINAL TUMOR IN CHILDREN IS THE NEUROGENIC TUMOR.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
ON THE 5TH POSTOPERATIVE DAY POST CABG, THE PATIENT DEVELOPS TACHYPNEA AND HYPOTENSION.
SPECIFY THE MOST PROBABLE CAUSE.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF TACHYPNOEA AND HYPOTENSION IN A POST-OP DAY 5 PATIENT WHO
UNDERWENT CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS GRAFTING (CABG) POINTS TOWARDS LUNG COLLAPSE (ATELECTASIS) -
TYPE 3 RESPIRATORY FAILURE.
ATELECTASIS IS THE MOST COMMON RESPIRATORY COMPLICATION IN A POST-OPERATIVE PATIENT.
THE FACTORS PREDISPOSING TO ATELECTASIS ARE GENERAL ANESTHESIA, UPPER ABDOMINAL SURGERY, AND
THORACIC SURGERY. THEY COMMONLY PRESENT WITH TACHYPNOEA AND DECREASED OXYGEN SATURATION. ON
EXAMINATION, THE BREATH SOUNDS ARE BRONCHIAL IN NATURE AND REDUCED IN INTENSITY.
LUNG ATELECTASIS CAN BE REVERSED (WITHIN 24H-48H) WITH EARLY MOBILIZATION, DEEP BREATHING (5
SEQUENTIAL BREATHS FOR 5S), INCENTIVE SPIROMETRY, AND CHEST PHYSIOTHERAPY.
OTHER POSTOPERATIVE SYSTEMIC COMPLICATIONS INCLUDE:
- PNEUMONIA AND MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION : FIRST FEW DAYS AFTER SURGERY
- VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM, KIDNEY FAILURE, AND URINARY TRACT INFECTION: DAYS 4 TO 7
- SUPERFICIAL AND DEEP SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS: 2ND POST-OP WEEK
4713
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: FOR A DIAGNOSIS OF SEPSIS, SEPSIS 3 CRITERIA NEEDS TO BE SATISFIED:
- A DOCUMENTED INFECTION
- AN ACUTE INCREASE IN >2 SOFA POINTS
OPTION B: ACUTE KIDNEY FAILURE IS DEFINED AS A DECREASE IN URINE OUTPUT (<0.5 ML/KG/H FOR 6-12H)
AND A RISE IN SERUM CREATININE VALUES ( >1.5X BASELINE OR >0.3 MG/DL).
OPTION D: ACUTE CARDIAC FAILURE HAS FEATURES OF HYPOTENSION AND TACHYCARDIA, WITH PERIPHERAL SIGNS
OF HYPOPERFUSION CHARACTERIZED BY COLD CLAMMY EXTREMITIES.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS BASED ON THE BELOW CLINICAL IMAGE OF THE BREAST?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS A THROMBOSED SUBCUTANEOUS CORD ATTACHED TO THE SKIN OF THE BREAST WHICH IS THE
PATHOGNOMIC FEATURE OF MONDOR'S DISEASE.
MONDOR’S DISEASE IS THE THROMBOPHLEBITIS OF THE SUPERFICIAL VEINS OF THE BREAST AND ANTERIOR CHEST
WALL. IT MAY ALSO OCCUR IN THE ARM OR PENIS. ON RAISING THE ARM, THE SKIN OVER THE CHEST GETS
STRETCHED AND A NARROW, SHALLOW GROOVE ALONGSIDE THE CORD IS SEEN. IT IS TREATED BY RESTRICTING ARM
MOVEMENTS AND USUALLY SUBSIDES WITHIN A FEW MONTHS WITHOUT RECURRENCE, COMPLICATIONS, OR
DEFORMITY.
THE DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS TO BE CONSIDERED IS LYMPHATIC PERMEATION FROM AN OCCULT CARCINOMA OF
THE BREAST.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: PAGET’S DISEASE IS A TYPE OF DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU ARISING FROM THE NIPPLE AND
COMMONLY PRESENTS AS NIPPLE EROSION.
OPTION B: ZUSKA’S DISEASE, ALSO CALLED RECURRENT PERIDUCTAL MASTITIS, IS A CONDITION OF RECURRENT
RETROAREOLAR INFECTIONS AND ABSCESSES. SMOKING HAS BEEN IMPLICATED AS A RISK FACTOR FOR THIS
CONDITION. MANAGED SYMPTOMATICALLY BY ANTIBIOTICS COUPLED WITH INCISION AND DRAINAGE AS
NECESSARY.
OPTION D: TIETZE’S SYNDROME REFERS TO THE BENIGN INFLAMMATION OF ONE OR MORE COSTAL CARTILAGES.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: THE MOST COMMONLY INVOLVED ARTERY IN PSEUDOANEURYSM FORMATION:
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMONLY INVOLVED ARTERY IN PSEUDOANEURYSM IS THE FEMORAL ARTERY.
A TRUE ANEURYSM INVOLVES ALL THREE VESSEL WALL LAYERS, WHILE A PSEUDOANEURYSM INVOLVES ONLY THE
INTIMAL AND MEDIAL LAYERS. PSEUDOANEURYSMS ARE MOST COMMONLY IATROGENIC DUE TO REPEATED
ARTERIAL PUNCTURE FOR BLOOD SAMPLING OR CATHETERIZATION PROCEDURES WHICH INJURE THE ARTERIAL WALL.
THE MOST COMMONLY USED ARTERY IN ENDOVASCULAR SURGERIES IS THE FEMORAL ARTERY, AND HENCE, ALSO
THE MOST COMMONLY INVOLVED IN THE FORMATION OF PSEUDO ANEURYSMS.
ANEURYSMS ARE USUALLY PULSATILE ON PALPATION AND A SYSTOLIC BRUIT CAN BE HEARD ON AUSCULTATION.
4714
DOPPLER ULTRASOUND REVEALS A BIDIRECTIONAL, 'TO-AND-FRO' FLOW OF BLOOD WHICH IS KNOWN AS THE
YIN-YANG SIGN.
TREATMENT OPTIONS INCLUDE ENDOVASCULAR STENT INSERTION, ULTRASOUND-GUIDED THROMBIN INJECTION,
AND SURGICAL REPAIR.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: AORTIC ANEURYSM CAN BE TYPES - THORACIC OR ABDOMINAL. THEY ARE USUALLY SEEN IN
HERITABLE CONDITIONS LIKE MARFAN SYNDROME OR VASCULAR-TYPE EHLERS-DANLOS.
OPTION C: THE MOST COMMON PERIPHERAL ANEURYSM IS THE POPLITEAL ANEURYSM (80% OF THE CASES)
FOLLOWED BY THE FEMORAL ANEURYSM.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A CHRONIC ALCOHOLIC PATIENT CAME TO THE EMERGENCY WITH PAIN IN THE EPIGASTRIUM RADIATING TO
THE BACK AND RECURRENT VOMITING. UPON EXAMINATION, GUARDING WAS PRESENT IN THE UPPER
EPIGASTRIUM. THE ERECT CHEST X-RAY WAS NORMAL. SPECIFY THE NEXT STEP.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO OF THE PATIENT PRESENTING WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN, RECURRENT VOMITING, AND
UPPER EPIGASTRIC GUARDING IN A CHRONIC ALCOHOLIC IS HIGHLY SUGGESTIVE OF ACUTE PANCREATITIS. THE
NORMAL ERECT CHEST X-RAY INDICATES THAT THERE IS NO PNEUMOPERITONEUM (EFFECTIVELY RULING OUT
PERFORATION). THE NEXT STEP IS TO SEND BLOOD SAMPLES FOR SERUM LIPASE LEVELS.
WHILE CONTRAST-ENHANCED COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CECT) OF THE ABDOMEN (OPTION D) IS THE BEST
INVESTIGATION TO RULE OUT A CASE OF ACUTE PANCREATITIS, IT IS NOT THE NEXT STEP AFTER AN ABDOMINAL
X-RAY.
ACUTE PANCREATITIS IS OFTEN CAUSED BY GALLSTONES (70%) OR ALCOHOLISM (25%). THE CARDINAL SYMPTOM
IS ACUTE-ONSET SEVERE PAIN IN THE UPPER QUADRANT OF THE ABDOMEN. THE PATIENT USUALLY PRESENTS IN
SHOCK (HYPOTENSION AND TACHYCARDIA) AND TACHYPNOEA. SOME MAY ALSO PRESENT WITH SIGNS OF
BLEEDING INTO THE FASCIAL PLANES LEADING TO DISCOLORATION OF THE SITES INVOLVED:
- CULLEN’S SIGN: AROUND THE UMBILICUS
- GREY TURNER’S SIGN: FLANKS
- FOX SIGN: INGUINAL REGION
4715
- BRYANT’S SIGN: SCROTUM
THE DIAGNOSIS IS OFTEN CLINICAL WITH A LABORATORY DIAGNOSIS OF SERUM LIPASE PREFERRED OVER SERUM
AMYLASE. THE SEVERITY OF THE ACUTE PANCREATITIS IS ASSESSED USING THE RANSON AND GLASGOW SCORING
SYSTEM ( ≥3 AT 48H OF ONSET OF PAIN ). APACHE, SOFA, SAPS, AND MODS CAN ALSO BE USED TO ASSESS
THE SEVERITY OF PANCREATITIS IN INTENSIVE CARE (ICU) SETTINGS.
PANCREATITIS IS MANAGED CONSERVATIVELY WITH INITIAL NASOGASTRIC DRAINAGE FOLLOWED BY INTRAVENOUS
FLUIDS, ANALGESIA, AND FREQUENT MONITORING OF VITAL SIGNS, URINE OUTPUT, AND BLOOD GASES.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: UPPER GASTROINTESTINAL INTESTINAL (GI) ENDOSCOPY IS PERFORMED BY PASSING A FLEXIBLE
ENDOSCOPE AND IS THE BEST METHOD FOR EXAMINING THE UPPER GASTROINTESTINAL MUCOSA. IT DOESN'T
HELP US DIAGNOSE PANCREATITIS.
OPTION B: THE ALCOHOL BREATH TEST IS USED AS A SCREENING TEST TO MEASURE THE CONCENTRATION OF
ALCOHOL IN A PERSON'S BREATH, BUT DOESN'T HELP US DIAGNOSE PANCREATITIS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE BEST WAY TO MANAGE THE WOUND DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS A SUPERFICIAL INJURY TO THE SKIN, AN ABRASION. CLEANING AND DRESSING IS THE
APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT OF AN ABRASION.
WOUND CLEANING IS THE REMOVAL OF BACTERIA AND PARTICLES TO DECREASE THE CHANCES OF INFECTION. IT
INCLUDES THE “TIME” ACRONYM:
- T - TISSUE : ASSESSMENT AND DEBRIDEMENT OF NON-VIABLE TISSUE OR FOREIGN MATERIAL
- I - INFLAMMATION/INFECTION : ASSESS THE ETIOLOGY OF EACH WOUND
- M - MOISTURE BALANCE : ASSESS THE ETIOLOGY OF WOUND EXUDATE
- E - EDGE OF THE WOUND : ASSESS THE EDGE AND SURROUNDING SKIN
WOUND IRRIGATION OR TOILET IS WASHING THE WOUND WITH NORMAL SALINE.
WOUND DEBRIDEMENT IS PERFORMED USING A SURGICAL BLADE OR FINE SCISSORS TO REMOVE ANY
DEVITALIZED, NONVIABLE TISSUE OR ANY EMBEDDED FOREIGN BODY (OPTION B).
SKIN GRAFTING IS REQUIRED ONLY IN SITUATIONS OF WONUDS WITH LARGER AREAS SOFT TISSUE LOSS (OPTIONS C
AND D).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: DEVICE DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE IS USED FOR WHICH PURPOSE?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS A LEUKOREDUCTION FILTER WHICH IS USED FOR FILTERING OUT DONOR WBCS. THIS HELPS IN
REDUCING THE INCIDENCE OF TRANSFUSION-RELATED REACTIONS BY REMOVING WBC MICROAGGREGATES. THE
OPTIMUM TIME FOR PERFORMING LEUKOREDUCTION IS BEFORE THE STORAGE OF BLOOD.
POTENTIAL BENEFITS INCLUDE REDUCED RISK OF:
- SENSITIZATION TO HLA ANTIGENS (IMPORTANT FOR TRANSPLANT PATIENTS & PREVENTING PLATELET
REFRACTORINESS)
4716
- FEBRILE NON-HEMOLYTIC TRANSFUSION REACTIONS (FNHTR)
- CMV TRANSMISSION
NOTE: CMV ALSO HAS AN AFFINITY FOR MONOCYTES AND MACROPHAGES (TYPES OF WBCS). REDUCTION IN
WBCS IS THE CAUSE FOR THE DECREASE IN CMV TRANSMISSION (ACCIDENTAL BENEFIT), AND THUS, THE MAIN
PURPOSE OF A LEUKOREDUCTION FILTER IS NOT THE PREVENTION OF CMV TRANSMISSION (OPTIONS A AND C).
POSSIBLE REDUCED RISK OF:
- TRANSFUSION-ASSOCIATED GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE (TA- GVHD)
- TRANSFUSION-RELATED IMMUNO-MODULATORY (TRIM) EFFECTS
- TRANSMITTING VARIANT CREUTZFELDT-JAKOB DISEASE
OTHER METHODS OF LEUCODEPLETION ARE:
- SPECIFIC LEUCODEPLETION FILTERS (MOST EFFICIENT)
- WASHING
- FREEZING
- BUFFY COAT REMOVAL
- MICRO-AGGREGATE FILTRATION
- LOW LEUCOCYTE APHERESIS DEVICES

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
IN A CHILD WITH A UNILATERAL UNDESCENDED TESTIS, A DIAGNOSTIC LAPAROSCOPY IS PERFORMED WHICH
SHOWED THE BLIND-ENDING TESTICULAR VESSELS ON THE RIGHT SIDE. SPECIFY THE NEXT BEST STEP.
questions.explanation:
IN NON-PALPABLE TESTIS CASES, LAPAROSCOPICALLY ENCOUNTERING BLIND-ENDING VAS DEFERENS AND
TESTICULAR VESSELS PRIOR TO ENTERING THE INTERNAL RING IS SUFFICIENT TO DIAGNOSE A VANISHING TESTIS. IN
SUCH CASES, NO FURTHER EXPLORATION IS REQUIRED.
CRYPTORCHIDISM IS THE FAILURE OF THE DESCENT OF THE INTRA-ABDOMINAL TESTES INTO THE SCROTAL SAC. IT IS
THE MOST COMMON CONGENITAL ABNORMALITY OF THE GENITOURINARY TRACT. THE DESCENT OF THE TESTES
CAN ARREST ANYWHERE, AND THE MOST COMMON SITE IS THE INGUINAL REGION.
PHASES OF TESTICULAR DESCENT:
- TRANSABDOMINAL PHASE: TESTES COME TO LIE IN THE LOWER ABDOMEN OR PELVIS, AND THIS DESCENT IS
REGULATED BY MULLERIAN-INHIBITING SUBSTANCES.
- INGUINOSCROTAL PHASE: TESTES DESCEND ALONG THE INGUINAL CANAL AND REACH THE SCROTAL SAC, AND THIS
PHASE OF THE DESCENT IS REGULATED BY ANDROGEN-INDUCED CALCITONIN GENE-RELATED PEPTIDE FROM THE
GENITOFEMORAL NERVE.
THE EXACT PATHOGENESIS REMAINS UNKNOWN; HOWEVER, DEFICIENCY IN GONADOTROPINS AND
MULLERIAN-INHIBITING SUBSTANCE (MIS) AND INCREASED EXPRESSION OF ESTRADIOL IN THE PLACENTA ARE
THOUGHT TO PLAY A ROLE.
CRYPTORCHIDISM IS HISTOPATHOLOGICALLY CHARACTERIZED BY THE FOLLOWING:
- TESTICULAR ATROPHY: THICKENING OF THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE, ARRESTED GERM CELL DEVELOPMENT,
MARKED HYALINIZATION
4717
- TUBULES SHOWING SERTOLI CELLS BUT NO SPERMATOGENESIS
- INCREASE IN THE INTERSTITIAL LEYDIG CELLS
IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH TESTICULAR ATROPHY AND DYSFUNCTION, WHICH RESULT IN STERILITY. CRYPTORCHID
TESTES CARRY A 3–5-FOLD HIGHER RISK FOR TESTICULAR CANCER (USUALLY SEMINOMA).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT A COMPONENT OF QSOFA?
questions.explanation:
QSOFA SCORE (QUICKSOFA) IS A BEDSIDE PROMPT THAT MAY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED INFECTION
WHO ARE AT GREATER RISK FOR A POOR OUTCOME OUTSIDE THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU).
IT USES THREE CRITERIA, ASSIGNING ONE POINT EACH FOR
- LOW BLOOD PRESSURE (SBP≤100 MMHG),
- HIGH RESPIRATORY RATE (≥22 BREATHS PER MIN)
- ALTERED MENTATION (GLASGOW COMA SCALE, <15).
THE SCORE RANGES FROM 0 TO 3 POINTS. THE PRESENCE OF 2 OR MORE QSOFA POINTS IS A SIMPLE PROMPT
TO IDENTIFY INFECTED PATIENTS OUTSIDE THE ICU WHO ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP SEPSIS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE DOES NOT CLASSIFY AS LOCALLY ADVANCED BREAST CANCER?
questions.explanation:
A BREAST TUMOR OF SIZE > 5 CM (NOT 4 CM) IS CLASSIFIED AS LOCALLY ADVANCED BREAST CARCINOMA
(LABC).
4718
INVASIVE BREAST CARCINOMA IS OF 3 TYPES:
- EARLY BREAST CARCINOMA (EBC) - TNM COMBINATION OF T1 TO T2, N0 TO N1, AND M0
- LOCALLY ADVANCED BREAST CARCINOMA (LABC) - T4N0M0, T3N1M0, TANYN2-3M0
- ADVANCED BREAST CARCINOMA (ABC) - TANYNANYM1
LOCALLY ADVANCED BREAST CANCER (LABC) INCLUDES:
- BREAST TUMORS MORE THAN 5 CM IN DIAMETER
- CANCERS THAT INVOLVE THE SKIN OR THE UNDERLYING MUSCLES OF THE CHEST (T4 OF TNM STAGING)
- CANCERS THAT INVOLVE MULTIPLE LOCAL LYMPH NODES (AXILLARY OR SUB CLAVICULAR)
- INFLAMMATORY BREAST CANCER - A RAPIDLY GROWING TYPE OF CANCER THAT MAKES THE BREAST APPEAR RED
AND SWOLLEN

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: ALL OF THESE ARE FEATURES OF SIRS EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
RESPIRATORY RATE > 20/MINUTE OR (NOT AND) PACO2 < 32 MMHG (NOT <35 MMHG) WOULD BE
A FEATURE OF SIRS (SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE SYNDROME).
SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE SYNDROME (SIRS) IS AN EXAGGERATED DEFENSE RESPONSE OF THE BODY
TO A NOXIOUS STRESSOR (INFECTION, TRAUMA, SURGERY, ACUTE INFLAMMATION, ISCHEMIA, OR REPERFUSION) TO
LOCALIZE AND THEN ELIMINATE THE ENDOGENOUS OR EXOGENOUS SOURCE OF THE INSULT.
SIRS IS DIAGNOSED WHEN ANY TWO OF THE FOLLOWING ARE PRESENT:
- HYPERTHERMIA (>38 DEGREE CELSIUS) OR HYPOTHERMIA (<36 DEGREE CELSIUS)
- TACHYPNOEA (>20/MIN) OR PACO2 < 32 MMHG
- TACHYCARDIA (>90/MIN)
- WHITE CELL COUNT >12 X 109/LITER OR <4 X 109/LITER OR >10% BAND FORMS
SEPSIS IS SIRS WITH A DOCUMENTED INFECTION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE MOST COMMON NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR OF THE PANCREAS?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR OF THE PANCREAS IS INSULINOMA (4 PER MILLION).
INSULINOMA IS AN INSULIN-PRODUCING TUMOR OF THE PANCREAS, WITH MORE THAN 90% OF THEM BEING
BENIGN. IT OCCURS IN >40 YEARS IN PATIENTS WITHOUT MEN 1 SYNDROME AND <40 YEARS IN PATIENTS
WITH MEN 1. IT PRESENTS WITH SYMPTOMS OF HYPOGLYCEMIA SUCH AS WEAKNESS, HEADACHES, SWEATING,
FAINTNESS, SEIZURES, AND ALTERED BEHAVIOR. THESE OCCUR AFTER FASTING OR EXERTION AND IMPROVE AFTER
GLUCOSE INTAKE.
THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR INSULINOMA IS THE DETERMINATION OF 72-HOUR FASTING
GLUCOSE AND SERUM INSULIN LEVELS. C-PEPTIDE AND PROINSULIN LEVELS ARE ALSO ELEVATED.
MEDICAL MANAGEMENT INCLUDES:
4719
- FREQUENT CARBOHYDRATE-RICH MEALS
- SOMATOSTATIN ANALOGS LIKE OCTREOTIDE ARE EFFECTIVE IN CONTROLLING SYMPTOMS DUE TO EXCESS INSULIN
SECRETION. THEY SHOULD BE USED WITH CAUTION AS THEY CAN SUPPRESS COUNTERREGULATORY HORMONES,
SUCH AS GROWTH HORMONE (GH), GLUCAGON, AND CATECHOLAMINES, AND PRECIPITOUSLY WORSEN
HYPOGLYCEMIA.
- DIAZOXIDE CAN BE USED IN THE INITIAL MANAGEMENT OF INSULINOMA AS IT INHIBITS INSULIN RELEASE. ITS
SIDE EFFECTS INCLUDE SODIUM RETENTION AND NAUSEA.
- EVEROLIMUS HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE HIGHLY EFFECTIVE IN IMPROVING GLYCEMIC CONTROL IN PATIENTS WITH
INSULINOMA OWING TO ITS ANTITUMOR EFFECT AND INDUCTION OF INSULIN RESISTANCE.
ENUCLEATION AND PANCREATECTOMY ARE THE DEFINITIVE SURGICAL MANAGEMENT OF INSULINOMA.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: GASTRINOMA HAS AN INCIDENCE OF 0.5 TO 4 IN A MILLION.
OPTIONS B & D: SOMATOSTATINOMA AND VIPOMA ARE MUCH RARER THAN GASTRINOMA.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
AFTER PAROTIDECTOMY PATIENTS REPORTS LOSS OF SENSATION WHILE SHAVING. WHICH NERVE IS
MOST LIKELY AFFECTED?
questions.explanation:
AFTER PAROTID SURGERY, THE NERVE INVOLVED IN THE LOSS OF SENSATION WHILE SHAVING IS THE GREAT
AURICULAR NERVE.
THE GREAT AURICULAR NERVE (GAN) ORIGINATES FROM THE SECOND AND THIRD NERVE ROOTS OF THE CERVICAL
PLEXUS (C2-C3). IT SUPPLIES THE SKIN OVER THE LOWER PINNA, PRE-AURICULAR REGION, AND ANGLE OF THE
MANDIBLE (IMAGE BELOW). THE MAIN TRUNK PASSES OVER THE STERNOCLEIDOMASTOID AND INTO THE
ANTEROSUPERIOR PORTION OF THE PAROTID GLANDS AND BRANCHES INTO THE ANTERIOR AND POSTERIOR GAN.
THE ANTERIOR BRANCH OF GAN IS OFTEN INJURED DURING PAROTID SURGERY DURING THE INITIAL ELEVATION OF
THE SKIN FLAP.
WHEN GAN IS INJURED, IT CAN CAUSE REDUCED SENSATIONS IN THE EARLOBE, PRE-AURICULAR SKIN, AND THE
ANGLE OF THE MANDIBLE THAT CAN INTERFERE WITH HABITS SUCH AS SHAVING, WEARING EARRINGS, ETC.
4720
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE AURICULOTEMPORAL NERVE, A BRANCH OF THE MANDIBULAR NERVE (V3 OF TRIGEMINAL)
SUPPLIES THE POSTERIOR PART OF THE TEMPLE, TRAGUS, AND ADJOINING AURICLE. IT DOES NOT SUPPLY THE AREA
WHERE A PERSON IS LIKELY TO SHAVE. HOWEVER, THE INJURY TO THE AURICULOTEMPORAL NERVE RESULTING IN
ABERRANT REGENERATION WOULD RESULT IN FREY'S SYNDROME (GUSTATORY SWEATING).
OPTION C: THOUGH THE FACIAL NERVE IS THE MOST COMMON NERVE AFFECTED DURING PAROTIDECTOMY, ANY
DAMAGE WOULD RESULT IN FACIAL PARALYSIS AND NOT LOSS OF SENSATION OF THE FACE.
OPTION D: THE MANDIBULAR NERVE IS A BRANCH OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE (CRANIAL NERVE V) THAT SUPPLIES
THE SKIN OVER THE MANDIBLE, LOWER LIP, AND CHEEK. HOWEVER, THEY ARE NOT INJURED DURING
PAROTIDECTOMY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: ABCDE RULE APPLIES FOR:
questions.explanation:
ABCDE ALGORITHM IS USED TO DIAGNOSE MELANOMA.
IT COMPRISES OF:
- ASYMMETRY
- BORDER IRREGULARITY
- COLOR VARIEGATION
- DIAMETER OF MORE THAN 6 MM
- EVOLUTION OR CHANGE
MELANOMA IS A MALIGNANT TUMOR ARISING FROM MELANOCYTES AT THE EPIDERMAL-DERMAL JUNCTION.
THOUGH IT REPRESENTS ONLY 4% OF SKIN CANCERS, IT ACCOUNTS FOR 80% OF DEATHS (HIGH MORTALITY RATE).
IT PRESENTS AS A PIGMENTED LESION THAT HAS ENLARGED, ULCERATED, OR BLED.
HISTOPATHOLOGICAL CONFIRMATION IS THE GOLD STANDARD IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF MELANOMA. IT IS DIVIDED
INTO FOUR MAIN TYPES: NODULAR MELANOMA (NM), SUPERFICIAL SPREADING MELANOMA (SSM), LENTIGO
MALIGNA MELANOMA (LMM), AND ACRAL LENTIGINOUS MELANOMA (ALM).
THE TREATMENT CONSISTS OF WIDE LOCAL EXCISION OF THE TUMOR AND FOLLOW-UP TO DETECT ANY LOCAL
RECURRENCE AROUND THE SCAR AND EXCLUDING NODAL SPREAD.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: SELECT THE FOLLOWING INSTRUMENT?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN INSTRUMENT IS A UNIPOLAR CAUTERY/MONOPOLAR CAUTERY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: THE BIPOLAR CAUTERY CONTAINS TWO TIPS, UNLIKE UNIPOLAR CAUTERY WHICH HAS ONLY ONE TIP.
THE CURRENT FLOWS BETWEEN THESE TWO TIPS AND HENCE IT DOES NOT NEED A RETURN ELECTRODE, UNLIKE THE
UNIPOLAR CAUTERY.
4721
OPTION C: THE HARMONIC SCALPEL (SHOWN BELOW) IS A SURGICAL INSTRUMENT USED TO SIMULTANEOUSLY CUT
AND CAUTERIZE TISSUE. ULTRASONIC ENERGY IS USED IN HARMONIC SCALPEL WHERE ULTRASONIC ENERGY IS
CONVERTED TO MECHANICAL ENERGY AT THE ACTIVE BLADE.
OPTION D: LIGASURE VESSEL SEALING SYSTEM (SHOWN BELOW) IS A BIPOLAR APPARATUS FOR SEALING VASCULAR
TISSUE. IT APPLIES A HIGH COAPTIVE PRESSURE DURING THE GENERATION OF TISSUE TEMPERATURE UNDER
1000°C, HYDROGEN CROSS-LINKS ARE FIRST RUPTURED AND THEN RENATURED, RESULTING IN A VASCULAR SEAL
THAT HAS HIGH TENSILE STRENGTH.
4722

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: RADICAL NECK DISSECTION SPARES WHICH OF THESE STRUCTURES?
questions.explanation:
DIGASTRIC MUSCLE IS SPARED IN RADICAL NECK DISSECTION (RND). RND IS USED IN THE TREATMENT OF
MALIGNANT LESIONS OF THE NECK WITH LOCAL SPREAD OR METASTASIS.
IN 1905, CRILE DESCRIBED RND WHERE LEVEL I-V LN, STERNOCLEIDOMASTOID (SCM), INTERNAL JUGULAR
VEIN (IJV), AND XI CRANIAL NERVE (SPINAL ACCESSORY NERVE) ARE REMOVED.
IN 1962, SUAREZ DESCRIBED MODIFIED RND (MRND) WHERE LEVEL I-V LNS ARE REMOVED AND THE
FOLLOWING ARE PRESERVED:
- MRND I - XI CRANIAL NERVE
- MRND II - XI CRANIAL NERVE AND IJV
- MRND III - XI CRANIAL NERVE, IJV, AND SCM
NOTE: RND WITH AN ADDITIONAL LN/MUSCLE/NERVE IS CALLED EXTENDED RND.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A PATIENT COMES WITH ACTIVE VARICEAL BLEEDING. WHICH OF THESE IS NOT DONE?
questions.explanation:
PLATELET TRANSFUSION IS NOT DONE IN THE CASE OF ACTIVE VARICEAL BLEEDING UNLESS COAGULOPATHY IS
CONFIRMED AS THE CAUSE. PLATELET TRANSFUSIONS ARE INDICATED ONLY IN PATIENTS WITH A PLATELET COUNT OF
<50,000/MICROL OR IN PATIENTS WITH EVIDENCE OF MICROVASCULAR BLEEDING.
VARICEAL HEMORRHAGE IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY. VARICES USUALLY PRESENT WITH THE ACUTE
ONSET LARGE-VOLUME HAEMATEMESIS, THE LOWER ESOPHAGUS BEING THE MOST COMMON SITE FOR VARICEAL
BLEEDING.
THE SITES FOR PORTOSYSTEMIC ANASTOMOSIS ARE:
- LEFT GASTRIC VEIN TO DISTAL OESOPHAGEAL VEINS: OESOPHAGEAL AND GASTRIC VARICEAL BLEEDING
4723
- SUPERIOR RECTAL VEINS TO MIDDLE AND INFERIOR RECTAL VEINS: HEMORRHOIDS AND RECTAL BLEEDING
- LEFT BRANCH OF THE PORTAL VEIN TO PERIUMBILICAL VEINS: CAPUT-MEDUSAE
- THE RIGHT BRANCH OF THE PORTAL VEIN TO RETROPERITONEAL VEINS DRAINING INTO AZYGOS, HEMIAZYGOS,
LUMBAR, INTERCOSTAL, AND PHRENIC VEINS
- OMENTAL AND COLONIC VEINS NEAR HEPATIC AND SPLENIC ■EXURES TO RETROPERITONEAL VEINS NEAR
HEPATIC AND SPLENIC ■EXURES
MEDICAL MANAGEMENT OF VARICEAL BLEEDING INCLUDES BLOOD TRANSFUSION (OPTION B) AND DRUG THERAPY
WITH SOMATOSTATIN ANALOGS LIKE OCTREOTIDE (OPTION C). SHORT-TERM ANTIBIOTICS LIKE CEFTRIAXONE ARE
KNOWN TO DECREASE BACTERIAL INFECTION AND INCREASE SURVIVAL.
SURGICAL MEASURES ARE PREFERRED IF MEDICAL MANAGEMENT FAILS. THEY INCLUDE BALLOON TAMPONADE,
ENDOSCOPIC BANDING (OPTION D), TRANSJUGULAR INTRAHEPATIC PORTOSYSTEMIC SHUNT (TIPS),
PORTOSYSTEMIC SHUNTS, SPLENECTOMY, AND GASTRIC REVASCULARIZATION
NOTE: SUGIURA PROCEDURE IS THE NON-SHUNT SURGICAL MANAGEMENT OF REFRACTORY OESOPHAGEAL VARICEAL
BLEEDING. IT IS A PROCEDURE OF DE-VASCULARIZING THE DISTAL ESOPHAGUS AND STOMACH.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A CHILD PRESENTS WITH PAIN AND SWELLING IN THE RIGHT SIDE OF HIS SCROTUM AND TESTICULAR TORSION
IS SUSPECTED. WHICH IS THE MOST APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT?
options: IMMEDIATE EXPLORATION ON BOTH SYMPTOMATIC AND ASYMPTOMATIC SIDE
IMMEDIATE EXPLORATION ON SYMPTOMATIC SIDE ONLY
DELAYED EXPLORATION ON BOTH SYMPTOMATIC AND ASYMPTOMATIC SIDE
DELAYED EXPLORATION ON SYMPTOMATIC SIDE ONLY
questions.answer: IMMEDIATE EXPLORATION ON BOTH SYMPTOMATIC AND ASYMPTOMATIC SIDE
questions.explanation:
IN A CASE OF SUSPECTED TESTICULAR TORSION, IMMEDIATE EXPLORATION NEEDS TO BE DONE ON BOTH THE
SYMPTOMATIC AS WELL AS THE ASYMPTOMATIC SIDE. AFTER THE DE-TORSION, THE ADEQUACY OF THE BLOOD
FLOW HAS TO BE ASSESSED BY DOPPLER.
IN TESTICULAR TORSION, THE BLOOD SUPPLY TO THE TESTICLE IS COMPROMISED DUE TO THE TWISTING OF THE
SPERMATIC CORD WITHIN THE TUNICA VAGINALIS, RESULTING IN ISCHEMIA OF THE EPIDIDYMIS AND THE TESTIS.
THE PATIENT USUALLY PRESENTS WITH ACUTE ONSET PAIN AND SWELLING OF THE SCROTUM. ON EXAMINATION,
THE CREMASTERIC REFLEX IS LOST, AND THE SCROTUM LOOKS ASYMMETRICAL.
PREHN’S SIGN IS USED TO DIFFERENTIATE EPIDIDYMITIS FROM TESTICULAR TORSION. PREHN’S SIGN IS SAID TO BE
POSITIVE WHEN THE PAIN GETS RELIEVED ON LIFTING THE TESTIS, AND IT IS SEEN IN EPIDIDYMO-ORCHITIS.
4724
AT THE TIME OF SURGICAL EXPLORATION, CONTRALATERAL TESTES ALSO MUST BE EXPLORED AND FIXED TO THE
DARTOS FASCIA IN ORDER TO PREVENT POSSIBLE TORSION OCCURRING IN THIS TESTES.
MORE THAN 80% OF THE TESTIS CAN BE SALVAGED IF SURGERY IS PERFORMED WITHIN 6 HOURS. IF THE TESTIS IS
FOUND TO BE NECROSED ON SCROTAL EXPLORATION, ORCHIDECTOMY OF THE NECROSED TESTIS AND ORCHIDOPEXY
OF THE CONTRALATERAL TESTIS IS DONE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE INSTRUMENT DISPLAYED BELOW THAT IS USED TO CREATE A PNEUMOPERITONEUM .
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWING A LONG, SLENDER LAPAROSCOPIC INSTRUMENT IS VERESS NEEDLE. IT IS USED IN
DIRECT PUNCTURE LAPAROSCOPY TO PRODUCE A PNEUMOPERITONEUM.
DIRECT PUNCTURE LAPAROSCOPY (CLOSED METHOD):
- THE ABDOMINAL WALL IS GRASPED WITH TOWEL CLIPS OR FINGERS TO ELEVATE THE ABDOMINAL WALL AWAY
FROM THE UNDERLYING STRUCTURES.
- A SMALL INCISION IS MADE IN THE UMBILICUS AND THE VERESS NEEDLE IS INTRODUCED INTO THE ABDOMEN.
TWO DISTINCT POPS CAN BE FELT AS THE NEEDLE PIERCES THE ABDOMINAL WALL FASCIA AND THE PERITONEUM.
THE UMBILICUS IS THE PREFERRED LOCATION FOR INTRODUCING A VEREESS NEEDLE BECAUSE THE ABDOMINAL
WALL IS THIN AT THIS LOCATION.
CARBON DIOXIDE (CO2) GAS IS USUALLY USED AND THE MAXIMUM PRESSURE IS IN THE RANGE OF 14-15
MMHG. BUT N2O IS USED IF THE PROCEDURE IS DONE UNDER LOCAL ANESTHESIA. INSUFFLATION WITH N2O IS
STOPPED AT A PRESSURE OF 10 MMHG OR WHEN 2L OF GAS IS INSUFFLATED.
THE HASSON TROCAR IS USED TO GAIN ACCESS TO THE PERITONEAL CAVITY AND GENERATE
PNEUMOPERITONEUM BY THE OPEN DIRECT PERITONEAL ACCESS TECHNIQUE (OPTION C). THIS IS KNOWN AS
THE HASSON TECHNIQUE AND IS DONE ONLY OCCASIONALLY. IT IS PREFERRED FOR PATIENTS WHO HAVE
UNDERGONE PREVIOUS ABDOMINAL SURGERIES AS THE SMALL BOWEL MAY BE ADHERENT TO THE UNDERSURFACE
OF THE ABDOMINAL WOUND IN SUCH CASES.
4725
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: SALAH'S NEEDLE IS A TYPE OF REUSABLE BONE MARROW BIOPSY NEEDLE THAT HAS A GUARD SITUATED
2 CM FROM THE TIP AND A SIDE SCREW.
OPTION D: VON GRAEFE NEEDLE (ALSO KNOWN AS GRAEFE'S KNIFE) IS PRIMARILY USED IN OPHTHALMIC
SURGERY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS THE PRINCIPLE BEHIND THE WOUND-HEALING PROCEDURE DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE PRESENTED BELOW?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS NEGATIVE PRESSURE WOUND THERAPY USING A VACUUM-ASSISTED CLOSURE (VAC)
DEVICE TO PROMOTE HEALING IN CHRONIC WOUNDS.
PRINCIPLE: AN INTERMITTENT NEGATIVE PRESSURE OF -125 MMHG HASTENS DEBRIDEMENT AND FORMATION OF
GRANULATION TISSUE IN CHRONIC WOUNDS.
4726
INDICATIONS: CHRONIC WOUNDS (SUCH AS DIABETIC FOOT ULCERS, STAGE III AND IV PRESSURE
ULCERS), TRAUMATIC WOUNDS, FLAPS AND GRAFTS, AND DEHISCED INCISIONS.
CONTRAINDICATIONS:
- EXPOSED VITAL STRUCTURES (ORGANS, BLOOD VESSELS, OR VASCULAR GRAFTS)
- PREEXISTING INFECTION
- INADEQUATE DEBRIDEMENT OF DEVITALIZED SOFT TISSUE OR BONE INCREASES THE RISK OF INFECTION.
- THE PRESENCE OF MALIGNANCY (MARJOLIN’S ULCER).
- AN ALLERGIC REACTION TOWARDS THE ADHESIVE USED TO MAINTAIN THE VACUUM SEAL.
THOUGH NOT AN ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION, THERE IS NO APPRECIABLE BENEFIT FOR ISCHEMIC WOUNDS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: STAGE THE BEDSORE IN THE FOLLOWING IMAGE:
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS COMPLETE SKIN LOSS THAT INVOLVES MUSCLES AND SHOWS EXPOSED BONE
INDICATING A STAGE 4 PRESSURE SORE.
PRESSURE SORES ARE SKIN OR SOFT TISSUE INJURIES THAT OCCUR DUE TO PROLONGED PRESSURE OVER SPECIFIC
AREAS OF THE BODY. AN EXTERNAL PRESSURE OF >30 MMHG LEADS TO THE FORMATION OF PRESSURE SORES.
THE COMMON SITES OF PRESSURE SORES IN DECREASING FREQUENCY ARE THE ISCHIUM, GREATER TROCHANTER,
SACRUM, HEEL, MALLEOLUS (LATERAL FOLLOWED BY MEDIAL), AND OCCIPUT.
PRESSURE SORES CAN BE PREVENTED WITH GOOD SKINCARE, THE USE OF AIR-FLUIDIZED BEDS, SPECIAL
PRESSURE-DISPERSION CUSHIONS, OR FOAMS. REPOSITIONING THE PATIENT EVERY TWO HOURS CAN LESSEN THE
PRESSURE ON THE AREA.
ULCERS OF STAGES 1 AND 2 OFTEN DO NOT REQUIRE OPERATIVE MEASURES. THEY ARE MANAGED WITH REGULAR
WOUND CLEANING AND DRESSING WITH A GOOD ANTIBIOTIC COVER.
STAGE 3 AND 4 ULCERS ARE ADEQUATELY DEBRIDED, AND VACUUM-ASSISTED CLOSURE (VAC) IS USED TO
PROMOTE THE GROWTH OF GRANULATION TISSUE REQUIRED FOR SURGICAL CLOSURE. LARGE SKIN FLAPS THAT HAVE
MUSCLE WITH SENSORY INNERVATION ARE BEST FOR RECONSTRUCTION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT PRESENTED TO THE EMERGENCY ROOM AND REQUIRES A LARGE
AMOUNT OF FLUIDS TO BE TRANSFUSED. WHICH OF THESE IV CANNULA IS PREFERRED?
questions.explanation:
GREY COLOURED IV CANNULA IS REQUIRED FOR THIS PATIENT IN ORDER TO TRANSFUSE LARGE AMOUNT OF FLUIDS.
THE ATLS 10TH EDITION GUIDELINES STATE THAT 2 CANNULAE OF ATLEAST 18G SHOULD BE USED TO GAIN
VASCULAR ACCESS IN TRAUMA PATIENTS. IN THIS SCENARIO REQUIRING LARGE FLUID TRANSFUSIONS, THE GREY
(16G) CANNULA WOULD BE PREFERABLE TO THE GREEN (18G) CANNULA DUE TO THE HIGHER FLOW RATE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH A NODULE OF THE NECK PRESENTS TO THE SURGERY OPD. A JUNIOR RESIDENT PERFORMS
THE FOLLOWING METHOD TO PALPATE IT. IDENTIFY THE PROCEDURE SHOWN IN THE VIDEO BELOW.
questions.explanation:
THE VIDEO DEPICTS LAHEY’S METHOD OF PALPATION OF THE LEFT LOBE OF THE THYROID GLAND.
4727
IN LAHEY'S METHOD, FOR PALPATING THE LEFT LOBE, THE EXAMINER INITIALLY PUSHES THE RIGHT LOBE MEDIALLY
WITH THE LEFT HAND, AND THEN USING THE RIGHT HAND, THE BORDER AND CONSISTENCY OF THE LEFT LOBE IS
PALPATED.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: IN CRILE'S METHOD THE PATIENT IS ASKED TO SWALLOW, WHILE THE EXAMINER PALPATES THE GLAND
WITH THE THUMB. THIS GIVES A CLEAR INDICATION REGARDING THE SLIGHT ENLARGEMENT OF THE THYROID GLAND
OR SMALL NODULES.
OPTION C: KOCHER'S METHOD IS DONE TO DEMONSTRATE THE PRESSURE EFFECT OF THE THYROID GLAND ON THE
TRACHEA OR LARYNX. LATERAL COMPRESSION WILL RESULT IN STRIDOR.
OPTION D: PEMBERTON'S SIGN (NOT METHOD), IS ENGORGEMENT OF NECK VEINS WHEN THE PATIENT IS ASKED
TO RAISE THEIR HANDS ABOVE THE HEAD AND THE ARMS SHOULD TOUCH THE EARS. IT IS SEEN IN PATIENTS WITH
RETROSTERNAL GOITER.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE INSTRUMENT GIVEN IN THE IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE IS OF A JACKSON-PRATT DRAIN.
DRAINS ARE PLACED AT SURGICAL SITES TO FREELY DRAIN THE AIR OR FLUIDS THAT MAY ACCUMULATE. THEY
PROMOTE WOUND HEALING BY PREVENTING THE FORMATION OF UNNECESSARY CAVITIES. DRAINS CAN BE:
- OPEN : THEY ARE BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF GRAVITY
- SEMI-OPEN : THEIR ACTION IS BASED ON CAPILLARY EFFECT
- CLOSED : THEY CARRY OUT THEIR ACTIONS THROUGH SUCTION
JACKSON-PRATT DRAIN IS A CLOSED, AIR-TIGHT DRAINAGE SYSTEM THAT OPERATES BY SELF-SUCTION. THE DRAIN
IS SUTURED IN PLACE ON THE SKIN AT THE SITE OF INSERTION TO PROMOTE STABILITY. THERE ARE TWO MAIN
PARTS TO A JP DRAIN:
- HOLLOW TUBE
4728
- COLLECTION BULB
THE DRAIN SHOULD BE EMPTIED AS OFTEN AS POSSIBLE TO ALLOW THE BULB TO BE COMPRESSED FULLY IN ORDER
TO MAINTAIN SUCTION. THIS IS USUALLY DONE EVERY 4-6 HOURS THE FIRST FEW DAYS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: HEMOVAC IS ALSO A CLOSED TYPE OF SUCTION DRAIN WHICH CAN TYPICALLY HANDLE LARGER
AMOUNTS OF FLUID THAN THE JP DRAIN.
OPTION C: MINIVAC IS A CLOSED WOUND DRAINAGE SYSTEM UNDER NEGATIVE PRESSURE USED IN MINOR
SURGERIES.
OPTION D: CORRUGATED DRAIN IS AN OPEN DRAINAGE SYSTEM TO REMOVE EXCESS FLUID FROM THE OPERATED
SITE.
4729

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 65-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTS WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN FOR THE PAST 6 HOURS, BP- 89/50MMHG, RR-
24/MIN, SATURATION 92% WITH 6 L OF OXYGEN. RADIOGRAPH SHOWS EXTRALUMINAL AIR IN THE
ABDOMEN. WHICH OF THESE MUST BE DONE BEFORE SHIFTING THIS PATIENT INTO THE OT?
options: INSERT CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETER AS INITIAL IV ACCESS OF CHOICE
questions.explanation:
VOLUME RESUSCITATION WITH 1 LITER OF CRYSTALLOID INFUSION SHOULD BE DONE BEFORE SHIFTING THIS PATIENT
TO THE OT FOR AN EMERGENCY EXPLORATORY LAPAROTOMY.
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO IN A PATIENT WITH HYPOTENSION AND TACHYPNEA WITH EXTRALUMINAL GAS IN
THE ABDOMEN IS SUGGESTIVE OF PERFORATION PERITONITIS WITH HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY. THE IMMEDIATE
STEP IS VOLUME RESUSCITATION TO MAINTAIN CIRCULATING VOLUME AND ORGAN PERFUSION.
PERITONITIS IS THE INFLAMMATION OF THE PERITONEUM AND CAN BE CATEGORIZED AS LOCAL OR DIFFUSE AND
ACUTE OR CHRONIC.
CAUSES:
- GASTROINTESTINAL PERFORATION E.G. PERFORATED ULCER, APPENDIX, DIVERTICULUM
- TRANSMURAL TRANSLOCATION (NO PERFORATION), E.G. PANCREATITIS, ISCHAEMIC BOWEL, PRIMARY BACTERIAL
PERITONITIS
- EXOGENOUS CONTAMINATION, E.G. DRAINS, OPEN SURGERY, TRAUMA, PERITONEAL DIALYSIS
- FEMALE GENITAL TRACT INFECTION, E.G. PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE
- HAEMATOGENOUS SPREAD (RARE), E.G. SEPTICAEMIA
- MISCELLANEOUS- E.G. FAMILIAL MEDITERRANEAN FEVER
CLINICAL FEATURES:
- ABDOMINAL PAIN, WORSE ON MOVEMENT, COUGHING AND DEEP RESPIRATION
- CONSTITUTIONAL SYMPTOMS: ANOREXIA, MALAISE, FEVER, LASSITUDE
4746
- NAUSEA +/– VOMITING
- PYREXIA (MAY BE ABSENT)
- TACHYCARDIA
- TENDERNESS +/– GUARDING/RIGIDITY/REBOUND OF THE ABDOMINAL WALL
- PAIN/TENDERNESS ON RECTAL/VAGINAL EXAMINATION (PELVIC PERITONITIS)
- ABSENT OR REDUCED BOWEL SOUNDS
- SEPTIC SHOCK (SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE SYNDROME [SIRS] AND MULTIORGAN DYSFUNCTION
SYNDROME [MODS]) IN LATER STAGES
MANAGEMENT:
GENERAL CARE OF THE PATIENT:
- CORRECTION OF FLUID AND ELECTROLYTE IMBALANCE
- INSERTION OF A NASOGASTRIC TUBE AND URINARY CATHETER
- BROAD-SPECTRUM ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY
- APRROPRIATE ANALGESIA
SURGICAL TREATMENT: EXPLORATORY LAPAROTOMY AND REPAIR OF PERFORATION IS THE DEFINITIVE
MANAGEMENT. PRESENCE OF PERITONEAL SIGNS AND HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY ARE INDICATIONS FOR URGENT
SURGERY.
OTHER OPTIONS
OPTION A: INTUBATION IS NOT INDICATED BY THE PATIENT'S CURRENT VITAL SIGNS.
OPTION B: INITIAL VOLUME RESUSCITATION CAN BE DONE WITH THE PERIPHERAL LARGE-BORE CANNULA. A
CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETER MAY BE NEEDED IF PERIPHERAL ACCESS IS DIFICULT, VASOPRESSORS ARE
ADMINISTERED, PATIENT REQUIRES TPN.
OPTION D: A CT SCAN, WHILE HELPFUL FOR LOCATING LESION AND CONFIRMING THE DIAGNOSIS, IS NOT
INDICATED FOR A HEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE PATIENT.
NOTE:
ACCORDING TO RECENT ATLS GUIDELINES, CRYSTALLOID INFUSION SHOULD BE LIMITED TO A MAXIMUM OF 1.5
LITRES AS CRYSTALLOID RESUSCITATION BEYOND 1.5 LITERS INCREASES THE RISK OF DEATH.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH RECURRENT PAIN IN THE RIGHT HYPOCHONDRIUM, NAUSEA, AND VOMITING IS DIAGNOSED
WITH BILIARY DYSKINESIA. WHICH OF THESE IS LEAST USEFUL IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF THIS
CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
USG IS THE LEAST USEFUL INVESTIGATION IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF BILIARY DYSKINESIA OR SPHINCTER OF ODDI
DYSFUNCTION SINCE THE FINDINGS CAN BE NORMAL OR SHOW NON-SPECIFIC CHANGES SUCH AS DILATATION OF
THE COMMON BILE DUCT.
SPHINCTER OF ODDI DYSFUNCTION (SOD) IS CAUSED DUE TO A STRUCTURALLY OR PHYSIOLOGICALLY ABNORMAL
SPHINCTER WITH A HIGHER TONE, WHICH FAILS TO RELAX, CAUSING PAIN AND RECURRENT EPISODES OF
PANCREATITIS WITH NORMAL LIVER FUNCTION TESTS. THERE ARE TWO CLINICAL TYPES: BILIARY SOD AND
PANCREATIC SOD. EACH TYPE IS FURTHER CLASSIFIED INTO TYPES 1,2 AND 3.
4747
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE BEST INVESTIGATION FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF SOD IS ERCP WITH MANOMETRY OF THE BILIARY
AND PANCREATIC SPHINCTERS.
OPTION B: HIDA SCAN WILL SHOW A REDUCED GALLBLADDER EJECTION FRACTION (EF). A GALLBLADDER EF
<35% IS CONSIDERED DIAGNOSTIC OF BILIARY DYSKINESIA.
OPTION D: BILIARY-TYPE SOD SHOULD BE CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED IN POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY
SYNDROME; HENCE, POST-SURGERY FOLLOW-UP IS ESSENTIAL.
CT AND MRCP CAN DEMONSTRATE DILATATION OF THE BILIARY AND PANCREATIC DUCTS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 32-YEAR-OLD WOMAN WAS DECLARED BRAIN DEAD. HER FAMILY HAS DECIDED TO DONATE HER ORGANS.
WHO IS THE IDEAL/BEST RECIPIENT?
options: 14 YEAR OLD CHILD WITH MULTI ORGAN DYSFUNCTION SYNDROME
50 YEAR ALCOHOLIC MAN WITH LIVER CIRRHOSIS WITH 1 MONTH ABSTINENCE
70 YEAR OLD WOMAN WITH END STAGE RENAL DISEASE
32 YEAR OLD WOMAN WITH RENAL FAILURE
questions.answer: 32 YEAR OLD WOMAN WITH RENAL FAILURE
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS, A 32-YEAR-OLD WOMAN WITH RENAL FAILURE IS THE MOST SUITABLE RECIPIENT FOR
TRANSPLANTATION.
THIS IS BECAUSE THE PROGNOSIS FOR THE OTHER PATIENTS MENTIONED ABOVE IS POOR. PRIORITIZATION OF
ORGAN TRANSPLANT RECEPIENTS SHOULD BE DONE BASED ON POST-TRANSPLANT OUTCOMES.
OPTION A - 14-YEAR-OLD WITH MULTI-ORGAN DYSFUNCTION SYNDROME IS NOT SUITABLE BECAUSE THERE IS A
POOR PROGNOSIS FOR THE ONGOING ORGAN DYSFUNCTION.
OPTION B - ALCOHOLIC PATIENTS WITH JUST 1-MONTH OF ABSTINENCE ARE NOT CONSIDERED FOR A TRANSPLANT.
OPTION C - A 70-YEAR-OLD WOMAN WITH END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE IS NOT THE RIGHT CANDIDATE BECAUSE
THE CHANCES OF LONG-TERM SURVIVAL AND A SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME ARE VERY LESS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: ERCP IS LEAST USEFUL IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF _____________
questions.explanation:
ERCP IS LEAST USEFUL IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF ACUTE PANCREATITIS WITHOUT CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS.
ERCP STANDS FOR ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIO-PANCREATOGRAPHY. IT INVOLVES THE USE OF A
SIDE-VIEWING ENDOSCOPE WHICH IS PASSED THROUGH THE PYLORUS OF THE STOMACH INTO THE SECOND PART
OF THE DUODENUM TO VISUALISE THE PAPILLA. THIS IS THEN CANNULATED, AND DYE IS INJECTED INTO THE
PANCREATIC OR BILE DUCT TO VISUALISE THE PANCREATIC OR BILIARY TREE. IT CAN BE THERAPEUTIC OR
DIAGNOSTIC. IT IS THE BEST DIAGNOSTIC MODALITY FOR VIEWING THE DISTAL BILIARY TREE, BUT MRCP IS
PREFERRED AS THE DIAGNOSTIC MODALITY UNLESS A THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION IS ALSO NEEDED.
INDICATIONS OF ERCP:
- CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS
- ACUTE CHOLANGITIS
- BILIARY STRICTURE, BILIARY LEAK
- PANCREATIC DUCT STRICTURE, PANCREATIC STONES
- EXTRAHEPATIC BILIARY STRICTURES RELATED TO PRIMARY SCLEROSING CHOLANGITIS
- ENDOSCOPIC THERAPY FOR SOME PATIENTS WITH SPHINCTER OF ODDI DYSFUNCTION
4748
- BILIARY OR PANCREATIC DUCTAL SYSTEM TISSUE SAMPLING
- BALLOON DILATATION OF THE DUODENAL PAPILLA OR DUCTAL STRICTURES
- SPHINCTEROTOMY
THE MOST COMMON THERAPEUTIC INDICATION FOR ERCP IS THE RELIEF OF BILIARY OBSTRUCTION DUE TO
GALLSTONE DISEASE AND BENIGN OR MALIGNANT BILIARY STRICTURES.
CONTRAINDICATIONS OF ERCP INCLUDE PATIENTS WHO CANNOT TOLERATE ANESTHESIA, PATIENTS WITH TYPE 3
SPHINCTER OF ODDI DYSFUNCTION, LUMINAL GASTROINTESTINAL OBSTRUCTION (EXAMINATION LIMITED TO AN
AREA PROXIMAL TO THE LEVEL OF OBSTRUCTION AND UNTREATED HEMOSTATIC DISORDER (HIGH RISK OF
BLEEDING).
COMPLICATIONS OF ERCP INCLUDE DUODENAL PERFORATION, HEMORRHAGE, PANCREATITIS AND SEPSIS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: ERCP CAN HELP IN RULING OUT THE ETIOLOGY IN CASES OF RECURRENT PANCREATITIS.
OPTION B: ERCP CAN ACT AS BOTH DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC IN CASES OF UNEXPLAINED JAUNDICE.
OPTION C: ERCP CAN BE USEFUL IN CASE OF A PERIAMPULLARY MASS TO TAKE A TISSUE BIOPSY AND CYTOLOGY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE NERVE IS LEAST INJURED DURING THYROID SURGERY?
questions.explanation:
THE MARGINAL MANDIBULAR NERVE IS LEAST LIKELY TO BE INJURED DURING THYROID SURGERY AS IT IS HIGH UP
(MANDIBULAR MARGIN) THAN THE DISSECTION PLANE OF THE APPROACH TO THYROID SURGERY.
OTHER NERVES THAT MIGHT BE AT RISK OF INJURY INCLUDE:
- RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE MAY BE INJURED IF DISSECTION IS DONE BELOW THE CRICOID CARTILAGE OR NEAR
THE TRACHEOESOPHAGEAL GROOVE (OPTION A).
- ANSA CERVICALIS MAY BE INJURED IF STRAP MUSCLES ARE NOT CUT HIGH ENOUGH. (OPTION B)
- EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE MAY BE INJURED DURING LIGATION OF SUPERIOR THYROID VESSELS AS IT LIES VERY
CLOSE TO THE SUPERIOR THYROID ARTERY (OPTION C).
COMPLICATIONS OF THYROIDECTOMY:
- HEMORRHAGE - MOST COMMON COMPLICATION OVERALL; DUE TO SLIPPING OF LIGATURE
- NERVE INJURY
- EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE - HOARSENESS (MORE COMMON)
- RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE - HOARSENESS IF UNILATERAL, LIFE-THREATENING ASPIRATION AND APHONIA IF
BILATERAL
4750
- RESPIRATORY OBSTRUCTION
- LARYNGEAL EDEMA - THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF RESPIRATORY OBSTRUCTION
- BILATERAL RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE PALSY
- LARYNGOMALACIA
- TENSION HEMATOMA
- HYPOPARATHYROIDISM - INFARCTION OF PARATHYROIDS
- THYROID STORM - INADEQUATELY PREPARED FOR SURGERY
- HYPOTHYROIDISM
- RECURRENT THYROTOXICOSIS
- WOUND INFECTION, STITCH GRANULOMA, KELOID.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: EFAST IS LEAST HELPFUL IN DIAGNOSING WHICH OF THESE CONDITIONS?
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS, EFAST (FOCUSSED ASSESSMENT WITH SONOGRAPHY IN TRAUMA) IS THE LEAST
USEFUL IN DIAGNOSING RETROPERITONEAL HEMATOMA AS THE SENSITIVITY OF ULTRASOUND FOR THE DETECTION OF
RETROPERITONEAL HEMATOMAS IS EXTREMELY POOR.
COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT SCAN) IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR RETROPERITONEAL INJURY, BUT IT
CAN ONLY BE DONE IN A HEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE PATIENT.
FAST STANDS FOR FOCUSSED ASSESSMENT WITH SONOGRAPHY FOR TRAUMA. IT IS A RAPID, NON-INVASIVE
BEDSIDE TEST FOR DETECTING FREE FLUID USING SONOGRAPHY USED TO ASSESS PATIENTS FOR POTENTIAL
THORACOABDOMINAL INJURIES.
TECHNIQUE:
- THE PATIENT IS PLACED IN A SUPINE POSITION AND THE FOLLOWING REGIONS ARE SCANNED:
- SUBXIPHOID TRANSVERSE VIEW: ASSESS FOR PERICARDIAL EFFUSION AND LEFT LOBE LIVER INJURIES
- LONGITUDINAL VIEW OF THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR RIGHT LIVER INJURIES, RIGHT KIDNEY INJURY,
AND MORISON POUCH
- LONGITUDINAL VIEW OF THE LEFT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR SPLENIC INJURY AND LEFT KIDNEY INJURY
- TRANSVERSE AND LONGITUDINAL VIEWS OF THE SUPRAPUBIC REGION: ASSESS THE BLADDER AND POUCH OF
DOUGLAS

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 23-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTED WITH BURN INJURY. HE IS COVERED WITH BURNS ON HIS HEAD &
NECK, BOTH UPPER LIMBS, FRONT AND BACK OF THE CHEST. CALCULATE THE PERCENTAGE OF BURNS.
questions.explanation:
THE PERCENTAGE OF BURNS CALCULATED IN THE GIVEN PATIENT IS 45% ACCORDING TO WALLACE’S RULE OF NINE.
CALCULATION:
- BURNS ON THE HEAD&NECK WOULD ACCOUNT FOR 9% OF BURNS.
- BURNS ON BOTH UPPER LIMBS (9% FOR EACH LIMB) WOULD ADD TO 18%
- BURNS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE CHEST WOULD ACCOUNT FOR 18%
THEREFORE THE TOTAL PERCENTAGE OF BURNS IN THE GIVEN PATIENT IS 9+18+18 = 45%

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A PATIENT WITH UNILATERAL BREAST CANCER IS STARTED ON TAMOXIFEN. THIS WILL INCREASE THE RISK OF?
questions.explanation:
TAMOXIFEN INCREASES THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER BY 1-2%.
THE BENEFIT OF TAMOXIFEN IN BREAST CANCER OUTWEIGHS THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER.
TAMOXIFEN IS A SELECTIVE ESTROGEN RECEPTOR MODULATOR, APPROVED FOR THE TREATMENT OF ESTROGEN
RECEPTOR-POSITIVE (ER) BREAST CANCER. IT IS USED ONLY IN PREMENOPAUSAL WOMEN FOR 5 YEARS IN
LOW-RISK PATIENTS AND FOR 10 YEARS IN PATIENTS WITH A HIGH RISK OF RELAPSE (NODE-POSITIVE, TUMOR
>5 CM, LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION). IT IS ALSO KNOWN TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF SECOND PRIMARY
BREAST CANCER IN THE CONTRALATERAL BREAST.
TAMOXIFEN INCREASES THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN; HENCE AROMATASE
INHIBITORS ARE USED IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN. TAMOXIFEN IS ALSO NOT RECOMMENDED IN PATIENTS
WHO HAVE HAD BILATERAL MASTECTOMIES WITH ER-POSITIVE DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU. OTHER SIDE EFFECTS
OF TAMOXIFEN INCLUDE BONE PAIN, HOT FLASHES, NAUSEA, VOMITING, FLUID RETENTION AND RARELY
4753
THROMBOSIS AND CATARACT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS THE MOST APPROPRIATE MESH FOR USE IN HERNIOPLASTY?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST APPROPRIATE MESH USED IN HERNIOPLASTY IS A LIGHTWEIGHT MESH WITH LARGE PORES.
LIGHTWEIGHT MESHES GENERALLY CONTAIN LESS MATERIAL AND INDUCE A LESS-PRONOUNCED FOREIGN BODY
REACTION AND DECREASED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE, WHICH RESULTS IN BETTER TISSUE INCORPORATION,
INCREASED PROSTHESIS COMPLIANCE, AND DECREASED PATIENT DISCOMFORT AND PAIN.
MESHES WITH LARGE PORES EXHIBIT LESS INFLAMMATORY INFILTRATE, CONNECTIVE TISSUE, AND SCAR BRIDGING,
WHICH ALLOWS INCREASED SOFT TISSUE INGROWTH. THEY HAVE GREATER ELASTICITY AND FLEXIBILITY AND ALSO
SHRINK LESS RESULTING IN LESSER ADHESIONS, BETTER TISSUE INCORPORATION, AND DECREASED PATIENT
DISCOMFORT AND PAIN. SO THE BEST MESH TYPE AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS IS LIGHTWEIGHT MESH WITH
LARGE PORES.
MESHES USED IN HERNIOPLASTY CAN BE SYNTHETIC OR BIOLOGICAL DEPENDING ON THEIR COMPOSITION.
SYNTHETIC MESHES ARE MADE FROM POLYPROPYLENE, POLYESTER, OR PTFE (POLYTETRAFLUOROETHYLENE).
PTFE MESHES ARE HYDROPHOBIC WITH A LOWER RISK OF ADHESION.
BIOLOGICAL MESHES ARE ACELLULAR MATRIX MATERIALS DERIVED FROM HUMANS OR ANIMALS AND HAVE LESSER
COMPLICATIONS. BUT DUE TO POOR COLLAGEN DEPOSITION AND ABSORPTION, THEY RAPIDLY LOSE MECHANICAL
STRENGTH AND HENCE THEIR USE IS RESTRICTED TO INFECTED ENVIRONMENTS.
NOTE: TO PROMOTE BETTER TISSUE INTEGRATION, A COMPOSITE MESH WAS DEVELOPED WHICH COMBINES THE
ATTRIBUTES OF POLYPROPYLENE AND PTFE BY LAYERING THE TWO SUBSTANCES ON TOP OF ONE ANOTHER.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 30-YEAR-OLD TEACHER UNDERWENT PAROTIDECTOMY FOLLOWING WHICH SHE DEVELOPED LOWER LIP
PARALYSIS. THIS PROBABLY OCCURRED BECAUSE OF AN INJURY TO WHICH OF THESE STRUCTURES?
options: BUCCAL BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE
questions.explanation:
LOWER LIP PARALYSIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS AN INJURY TO THE MARGINAL MANDIBULAR BRANCH OF THE FACIAL
NERVE.
BRANCHES OF THE FACIAL NERVE ARE:
- TEMPORAL
- ZYGOMATIC
- BUCCAL
4754
- MARGINAL MANDIBULAR
- CERVICAL
THE FACIAL NERVE PASSES THROUGH THE PAROTID GLAND, HENCE IT MIGHT BE INJURED DURING
PAROTIDECTOMY.
IN CONTRAST TO THIS, THE UPPER LIP IS SUPPLIED BY BUCCAL BRANCHES OF THE FACIAL NERVE.
COMPLICATIONS OF PAROTIDECTOMY INCLUDE HEMATOMA FORMATION, INFECTION, DEFORMITY (UNSIGHTLY
SCARRING AND RETROMANDIBULAR HOLLOWING), TEMPORARY/PERMANENT FACIAL WEAKNESS, SIALOCELE, FACIAL
NUMBNESS, PERMANENT NUMBNESS OF THE EARLOBE DUE TO GREAT AURICULAR NERVE TRANSECTION AND
FREY'S SYNDROME.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT AN ADVERSE EFFECT SEEN AFTER A MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION?
questions.explanation:
HYPERCALCEMIA IS NOT AN ADVERSE EFFECT OF MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION.
MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION INSTEAD LEADS TO HYPOCALCEMIA AS THE ANTICOAGULANT CITRATE BINDS TO
CALCIUM. THE LETHAL TRIAD OF MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION IS ACIDOSIS, HYPOTHERMIA, AND COAGULOPATHY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE GENE MUTATIONS ARE INVOLVED IN CARCINOMA OF THE COLON?
questions.explanation:
APC, K-RAS, AND P53 GENE MUTATIONS ARE IMPLICATED IN CARCINOMA OF THE COLON.
IN THE ADENOMA TO CARCINOMA SEQUENCE, THE LOSS OF ONE NORMAL COPY OF THE TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENE
APC IS THE FIRST HIT, FOLLOWED BY THE LOSS OF THE INTACT SECOND COPY OF THE APC GENE (SECOND HIT).
OTHER CHANGES IN THE SEQUENCE INCLUDE THE MUTATION OF K-RAS AND THE INACTIVATION OF THE TUMOR
SUPPRESSOR GENE P53, LEADING TO THE EMERGENCE OF CARCINOMA. THE ACCUMULATION OF THESE
MUTATIONS IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN THEIR OCCURRENCE IN A SPECIFIC ORDER. THIS IS KNOWN AS THE
FEARON-VOGELSTEIN ADENOMA-CARCINOMA MULTISTEP MODEL OF COLORECTAL NEOPLASIA.
4755
A NUMBER OF OTHER GENES ON CHROMOSOME 18Q ARE IMPLICATED IN COLORECTAL CANCER, INCLUDING
SMAD2, SMAD4, AND DCC.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH AMONG THESE IS CORRECT CONCERNING ADEQUATE THYROID FNAC SAMPLING?
questions.explanation:
6 FOLLICULAR CLUSTERS EACH WITH 10 CELLS ARE CONSIDERED ADEQUATE THYROID FNAC SAMPLING.
THERE ARE DIFFERENT CRITERIA FOR THE ADEQUACY OF THYROID FNAC:
- SIX GROUPS WITH AT LEAST 10 CELLS IN EACH GROUP, OR
- TEN GROUPS WITH AT LEAST 20 CELLS IN EACH GROUP, ARE CONSIDERED ADEQUATE.
CYSTIC GOITRE MAY NOT YIELD THYROID FOLLICULAR CELLS, HENCE, THE ASPIRATION SHOULD BE REPEATED UNDER
USG GUIDANCE.
FNAC IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IN DISCRETE THYROID SWELLINGS; IT HAS EXCELLENT PATIENT
COMPLIANCE, SIMPLE AND QUICK TO PERFORM IN THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT AND IS READILY REPEATED.
BETHESDA CRITERIA FOR REPORTING THYROID CYTOPATHOLOGY:
4756

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE ARE USED TO STOP ESOPHAGEAL VARICEAL BLEED?
questions.explanation:
ALL THE GIVEN OPTIONS CAN BE USED TO STOP ESOPHAGEAL VARICEAL BLEEDING.
IMAGE A SHOWS THE SENGSTAKEN-BLAKEMORE TUBE. IT HAS 3 LUMENS - ONE ASPIRATION PORT AND 2
INFLATION BALLOONS. THEY ARE:
- GASTRIC ASPIRATION PORT
- GASTRIC BALLOON PORT
- ESOPHAGEAL BALLOON PORT
THE GASTRIC BALLOON IS INFLATED AND TENSION IS APPLIED TO THE GASTROESOPHAGEAL JUNCTION. IF THIS DOES
NOT CONTROL THE HAEMORRHAGE, THE ESOPHAGEAL BALLOON IS INFLATED AS WELL, COMPRESSING THE VENOUS
PLEXUS BETWEEN THEM. ONLY GASTRIC CONTENTS CAN BE ASPIRATED.
4757
IMAGE B SHOWS THE MINNESOTA TUBE. IT HAS 4 OPENINGS - 2 INFLATION TUBES AND 2 SUCTION TUBES I.E.
BOTH GASTRIC AND OESOPHAGEAL ASPIRATION PORTS ARE PRESENT, WHICH ALLOWS THE ASPIRATION OF BOTH
GASTRIC AND ESOPHAGEAL CONTENTS.
IMAGES C AND D BOTH SHOW AN UPPER GI ENDOSCOPE. THEY ARE USED TO IDENTIFY THE SOURCE OF
BLEEDING AND ONCE IDENTIFIED, SCLEROTHERAPY AND ENDOSCOPIC VARICEAL BANDING ARE PERFORMED, WHICH
HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO CONTROL HEMORRHAGE EFFECTIVELY.
BANDING HAS A LOWER RATE OF COMPLICATIONS. IF BLEEDING DOES NOT STOP BY BANDING/SCLEROTHERAPY,
BALLOON TAMPONADE SHOULD BE TRIED.

questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY, HYPER-RESONANCE ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE

WIDE-BORE NEEDLE IN THE 5TH INTERCOSTAL SPACE (ICS) FOLLOWED BY PLACING AN INTERCOSTAL DRAIN IN THE
5TH ICS.
TRAUMATIC PNEUMOTHORAX CAN BE:
- SIMPLE PNEUMOTHORAX: WITHOUT HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY
- TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX: WITH HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY
THE X-RAY GIVEN BELOW IS SHOWING A LEFT-SIDED TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX. A LARGE, WELL-DEMARCATED
AREA IS DEVOID OF LUNG MARKINGS ON THE LEFT SIDE. THE YELLOW ARROWS ARE POINTING TO THE TRACHEAL
DEVIATION AND THE MEDIASTINAL SHIFT TO THE RIGHT SIDE.
4758
MANAGEMENT:
- SIMPLE PNEUMOTHORAX: TUBE THORACOSTOMY OR CHEST TUBE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS IN THE TRIANGLE
OF SAFETY
- TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX:
- IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT: URGENT NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION OR NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY I.E. INSERTION OF

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH PAIN IN THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ON THE SECOND POSTOPERATIVE DAY
FOLLOWING A CHOLECYSTECTOMY. EVALUATION REVEALS A COLLECTION IN THE SUBHEPATIC SPACE. A BILE
LEAK WAS SUSPECTED. WHICH OF THESE IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION FOR THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY (ERCP) IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION IN A PATIENT
SUSPECTED OF POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY BILIARY LEAKS.
PATIENTS WITH POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY BILIARY LEAK USUALLY PRESENT WITH FEVER, JAUNDICE AND
ABDOMINAL PAIN. USG IS USED FOR AN INITIAL EVALUATION IN SUCH CASES AND CAN SHOW A COLLECTION IN
THE SUB-HEPATIC SPACE.
THE MOST COMMON BILE LEAK FOLLOWING CHOLECYSTECTOMY IS FROM THE CYSTIC DUCT. THIS CAN BE TREATED
BY PLACING A BILIARY ENDOPROSTHESIS (STENT) IN THE COMMON BILE DUCT ACROSS THE ORIGIN OF THE CYSTIC
DUCT.
4759
MRCP SHOWS FLUID COLLECTIONS ARISING FROM BILE LEAKS BUT CANNOT DIFFERENTIATE THESE FROM OTHER
CAUSES OF FLUID COLLECTIONS.
ERCP IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION AS IT HAS THE ADVANTAGE OF BEING BOTH DIAGNOSTIC AND
THERAPEUTIC. ERCP IS USEFUL POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY AS THERE IS A HIGH LIKELIHOOD OF A RETAINED STONE
AND STONE EXTRACTION AND/OR TEMPORARY STENTING MAY BE REQUIRED.
HIDA SCAN IS THE MOST SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION FOR BILIARY LEAKAGE.
CT SCAN CAN SHOW FOCAL FLUID COLLECTIONS, ASCITES, BILIARY OBSTRUCTION, HEPATIC ATROPHY, SIGNS OF
SECONDARY BILIARY CIRRHOSIS AND ANY VASCULAR INJURY.

DIABETIC NEUROPATHY, B12 DEFICIENCY, ALCOHOLISM, HYPOTHYROIDISM, LEPROSY, PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURY,
TRANSVERSE MYELITIS AND MYELOMENINGOCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 35-YEAR-OLD CHRONIC SMOKER PRESENTS WITH BLUISH DISCOLORATION OF THE TOE ALONG WITH
INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION. WHICH OF THESE WILL BE THE NEXT APPROPRIATE INVESTIGATION IN THE PATIENT DESCRIBED?
questions.explanation:
CHRONIC SMOKER PRESENTING WITH BLUISH DISCOLORATION OF THE TOE ALONG WITH INTERMITTENT
CLAUDICATION IS SUGGESTIVE OF PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE AND DUPLEX SCANNING WILL BE THE NEXT
APPROPRIATE INVESTIGATION.
DUPLEX SCANNING IS A MAJOR NON-INVASIVE TECHNIQUE THAT USES B-MODE ULTRASOUND TO PROVIDE AN
IMAGE OF THE VESSEL. MOST SCANNERS NOW HAVE COLOR CODING, WHICH ALLOWS DETAILED VISUALIZATION OF
BLOOD FLOW IN A VESSEL. DIFFERENT COLORS INDICATE CHANGES IN THE DIRECTION AND VELOCITY OF FLOW, WITH
AREAS OF HIGH FLOW USUALLY INDICATING STENOTIC LESIONS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CT ANGIOGRAPHY (CTA) IS MORE USEFUL IN THE EVALUATION OF VISCERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE (EG.
MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA). IT CAN BE BENEFICIAL IN PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASES WHERE A DUPLEX SCAN SHOWS
POOR IMAGES (AORTOILIAC SEGMENT INVOLVEMENT). CTA IS NOT ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED IN PERIPHERAL
ARTERY DISEASE BECAUSE OF CONCOMITANT RENAL DYSFUNCTION IN THESE PATIENTS WHICH CAN LEAD TO
CONTRAST-INDUCED NEPHROPATHY.
OPTION B: MR ANGIOGRAPHY IS TIME-CONSUMING AND EXPENSIVE, HENCE NOT DONE AS THE NEXT
INVESTIGATION. IT IS CONTRAINDICATED IN PATIENTS WITH CLAUSTROPHOBIA AND METALLIC IMPLANTS.
OPTION C: DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY (DSA) IS AN INVASIVE AND EXPENSIVE
PROCEDURE COMPARED TO OTHER INVESTIGATIONS. THE BENEFITS OF DSA ARE THAT IT PROVIDES DYNAMIC
ARTERIAL FLOW INFORMATION AND CAN BE COMBINED WITH A DEFINITIVE ENDOVASCULAR INTERVENTION WHEN
INDICATED. DSA IS INDICATED ONLY WHEN THERE IS A DISCREPANCY IN DIAGNOSIS OR INTERVENTION IS
PLANNED. COMPLICATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH DSA INCLUDE BLEEDING, HEMATOMA, FALSE ANEURYSM
FORMATION, THROMBOSIS, ARTERIAL DISSECTION, DISTAL EMBOLISATION, RENAL DYSFUNCTION, AND ALLERGIC
REACTION.
4763

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD WOMAN REPORTS SWELLING OF THE RIGHT BREAST OVER THE PAST 15
DAYS. UPON EXAMINATION, THERE WAS LOCAL RISE OF TEMPERATURE, AND THE SWELLING WAS MOBILE OVER
THE CHEST WALL. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
IN THE GIVEN SCENARIO, THE RAPID ONSET OF THE DISEASE AND THE EXAMINATION FINDINGS ARE SUGGESTIVE
OF INFLAMMATORY CARCINOMA OF THE BREAST.
INFLAMMATORY BREAST CANCER IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE SUBTYPE OF BREAST CANCER. IT MIMICS ACUTE
MASTITIS. THE HALLMARK OF INFLAMMATORY BREAST CARCINOMA IS THE DIFFUSE TUMOR INVOLVEMENT OF THE
DERMAL LYMPHATICS WITHIN THE BREAST AND THE OVERLYING SKIN, OFTEN WITHOUT A DISCRETE UNDERLYING
TUMOR MASS (PEAU D' ORANGE APPEARANCE). THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH RAPIDLY PROGRESSIVE SWELLING OF
THE BREAST, WARMTH, ERYTHEMA AND EDEMA. A BREAST LUMP MAY OR MAY NOT BE PRESENT.
A DIAGNOSIS OF INFLAMMATORY BREAST CARCINOMA SHOULD BE SUSPECTED WHEN A PATIENT WITH RAPIDLY
PROGRESSIVE SWELLING WITH INFLAMMATORY SKIN CHANGES DOES NOT RESPOND TO ANTIBIOTICS. THE IMAGING
FEATURES WITH ULTRASOUND AND A MAMMOGRAPH IS NON-SPECIFIC DUE TO THE UNDERLYING ERYTHEMA AND
EDEMA. A BIOPSY SHOULD BE DONE TO CONFIRM THE DIAGNOSIS.
TREATMENT INCLUDES COMBINED-MODALITY TREATMENT:
- NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY
- MASTECTOMY
- RADIATION THERAPY
- HORMONAL THERAPY- FOR ER-POSITIVE TUMORS
- TRASTUZUMAB FOR HER-2-POSITIVE TUMORS
OPTION B: GIANT FIBROADENOMAS OCCASIONALLY OCCUR DURING PUBERTY. THESE ARE BENIGN SOLID
ENCAPSULATED SLOW-GROWING TUMORS OVER 5 CM IN DIAMETER. IT PRESENTS AS A PAINLESS LUMP IN THE
BREAST. THEY ARE MANAGED BY EXCISION VIA A SUBMAMMARY INCISION.
OPTION C: PHYLLODES TUMORS USUALLY OCCUR IN WOMEN OVER THE AGE OF 40 YEARS BUT CAN APPEAR IN
YOUNGER WOMEN. PHYLLODES TUMOR IS MOSTLY BENIGN EVEN THOUGH IT IS ALSO CALLED CYSTOSARCOMA
PHYLLODES. IT PRESENTS AS A LARGE TUMOR WITH AN UNEVENLY BOSSELATED SURFACE. THEY ARE USUALLY
4764
MOBILE OVER THE CHEST WALL DESPITE THEIR LARGE SIZE. THIS TUMOR DOES NOT INFILTRATE THE SKIN. NIPPLE
RETRACTION IS NOT SEEN IN THIS CONDITION. BENIGN LESIONS CAN BE TREATED WITH ENUCLEATION OR WIDE
LOCAL EXCISION. MASSIVE TUMOURS, RECURRENT TUMOURS AND MALIGNANT LESIONS ARE TREATED WITH A
MASTECTOMY.
OPTION D: GALACTOCELE ARE THE MOST COMMON BENIGN BREAST LESIONS IN LACTATING WOMEN. IT IS A
CYSTIC ENLARGEMENT OF THE MAMMARY GLAND CONTAINING MILK. THEY ARE MOSTLY DETECTED DURING
LACTATION OR IN THE THIRD TRIMESTER OF PREGNANCY BUT RARELY, MAY ALSO PRESENT AFTER STOPPING
BREASTFEEDING. CLINICALLY, THE MASS IS USUALLY FIRM AND NON-TENDER AND PRESENTS AS A SOLID
TUMOUR-LIKE LESION ON PHYSICAL EXAMINATION. THE PATIENT USUALLY NOTES THE
LESION DURING LACTATION OR SOME PERIOD AFTER LACTATION. NEEDLE ASPIRATION, FOLLOWED
BY EXCISION SHOULD IT RECUR, IS THE STANDARD METHOD OF TREATING GALACTOCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A MIDDLE-AGED MAN PRESENTS WITH PROGRESSIVE DIFFICULTY IN SWALLOWING FOR BOTH SOLIDS AND
LIQUIDS FOR 8 MONTHS. BARIUM SWALLOW DONE IS DISPLAYED BELOW. WHAT OTHER INVESTIGATIONS NEED
TO BE DONE IN THE PATIENT DESCRIBED?
options: UPPER GI ENDOSCOPY AND 24 HOUR PH MONITORING
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND THE BARIUM SWALLOW SHOWING A BIRD BEAK APPEARANCE ARE SUGGESTIVE
OF ACHALASIA CARDIA.
ACHALASIA IS A PRIMARY ESOPHAGEAL MOTILITY DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE ABSENCE
OF ESOPHAGEAL PERISTALSIS AND IMPAIRED RELAXATION OF THE LOWER ESOPHAGEAL SPHINCTER (LES) IN
RESPONSE TO SWALLOWING.
MANOMETRY IS CONSIDERED THE MOST SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION TO DIAGNOSE ACHALASIA AS IT IDENTIFIES
EARLY DISEASE BEFORE ESOPHAGEAL DILATATION AND FOOD RETENTION. THE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR ACHALASIA
WITH MANOMETRY ARE IMPAIRED LOWER ESOPHAGEAL SPHINCTER (LES) RELAXATION AND ABSENT
PERISTALSIS WITH AN ELEVATED LES PRESSURE.
ENDOSCOPY IS USEFUL FOR RULING OUT PSEUDO-ACHALASIA.
NOTE: 24-HOUR PH MONITORING IS IDEAL AND MOST ACCURATE IN PATIENTS WITH THE FEATURES OF
GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 55-YEAR-OLD MAN WITH IHD PRESENTS WITH SUDDEN, SEVERE, GENERALIZED ABDOMINAL PAIN AND
MULTIPLE EPISODES OF VOMITING. UPON EXAMINATION, THE PULSE RATE IS 118BPM, RHYTHM IS
IRREGULARLY IRREGULAR, BP IS 90/60 MMHG. THE ABDOMEN APPEARS SOFT, NON-DISTENDED, AND
BOWEL SOUNDS ARE ABSENT. WHICH OF THESE COULD BE A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IN THIS SITUATION?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF A PATIENT WITH SUDDEN ONSET SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN WHICH IS
OUT-OF-PROPORTION TO THE PHYSICAL EXAMINATION FINDINGS ALONG WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION IS SUGGESTIVE OF
ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA.
MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA MAY BE ACUTE OR CHRONIC. THE SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY (SMA) IS MOST LIKELY
AFFECTED. AN EMBOLUS IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF SMA OCCLUSION. POSSIBLE SOURCES FOR SMA
EMBOISATION INCLUDE:
- LEFT ATRIUM IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION
- PREVIOUS HISTORY OF ISCHEMIC HEART DISEASE/MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION
- VEGETATIONS ON MITRAL AND AORTIC VALVES ASSOCIATED WITH ENDOCARDITIS
- AN ATHEROMATOUS PLAQUE FROM AN AORTIC ANEURYSM.
OTHER CAUSES OF MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA INCLUDE:
4765
- ATHEROSCLEROSIS OF MESENTERIC VESSELS
- VASCULITIDES
- VENOUS THROMBOSIS IN FACTOR V LEIDEN MUTATION
- NON-OCCLUSIVE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA DUE TO ALTERATIONS IN SPLANCHNIC BLOOD FLOW.
THE MOST IMPORTANT CLUE TO AN EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA IS THE SUDDEN ONSET
OF SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN IN A PATIENT WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION OR ATHEROSCLEROSIS. THE PAIN IS
TYPICALLY IN THE CENTRAL ABDOMEN AND OUT OF PROPORTION TO THE PHYSICAL FINDINGS.
ASSOCIATED CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE NAUSEA, VOMITING, DIARRHEA, ABDOMINAL DISTENSION, PERITONITIS,
AND THE PASSAGE OF BLOODY STOOLS.
THE GOLD STANDARD FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA IS ANGIOGRAPHY, AND
MANAGEMENT IS LAPAROTOMY. THE GOAL OF OPERATIVE EXPLORATION IS TO RESECT THE COMPROMISED
BOWEL AND RESTORE BLOOD SUPPLY VIA EMBOLECTOMY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: A PULSATILE ABDOMINAL MASS IS SEEN IN THE CASE OF AN ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM. ACUTE
PAIN AND HYPOTENSION OCCUR WITH RUPTURE OF THE ANEURYSM, WHICH REQUIRES AN EMERGENCY
OPERATION.
OPTIONS A AND D: ACUTE SEVERE PANCREATITIS AND PEPTIC ULCER PERFORATION HAVE NO ASSOCIATION WITH
ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. THEY USUALLY PRESENT WITH PAIN OVER THE UPPER ABDOMEN ASSOCIATED WITH
GUARDING AND RIGIDITY ON EXAMINATION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 15-YEAR-OLD GIRL PRESENTED WITH A SLOW-GROWING, RUBBERY, NON-TENDER SWELLING ON THE SIDE OF
THE NECK AS DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE. EXAMINATION SHOWS THE PRESENCE OF FRECKLES AND SKIN PATCHES
OVER THE FACE AND TRUNK. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
A LATERAL NECK MASS IN A PEDIATRIC PATIENT, WHICH IS NON-TENDER AND PRESENT IN ASSOCIATION
WITH FRECKLES, AND HYPERPIGMENTED SKIN PATCHES (CAFE-AU-LAIT SPOTS) IS SUGGESTIVE OF NEURAL TUMOR
I.E. NEUROFIBROMA.
NEUROFIBROMA IS A BENIGN TUMOR ARISING FROM THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE OF THE NERVE CONTAINING
ECTODERMAL, NEURAL AND MESODERMAL CONNECTIVE TISSUE COMPONENTS. IT CAN BE SINGLE OR MULTIPLE. IT
IS THE MOST COMMON INTRADURAL EXTRAMEDULLARY SPINAL TUMOR. NEUROFIBROMAS CAN BE LOCAL,
GENERALIZED (VON RECKLINGHAUSEN'S DISEASE) OR PLEXIFORM TYPES. PATIENTS PRESENT WITH MILD PAIN OR
A PAINLESS SWELLING USUALLY IN THE SUBCUTANEOUS OR CUTANEOUS PLANE WITH TINGLING, NUMBNESS AND
PARAESTHESIA ALONG THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE NERVE. COMPLICATIONS OF NEUROFIBROMA INCLUDE CYSTIC
DEGENERATION, EROSION INTO DEEPER PLANES, CORD COMPRESSION AND PARALYSIS (SPINAL NEUROFIBROMA)
AND SARCOMATOUS CHANGES.
TREATMENT IS EXCISION UNDER GENERAL OR REGIONAL ANESTHESIA. INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY IN
NEUROFIBROMA INCLUDE SYMPTOMATIC PATIENTS (PAIN AND PRESSURE SYMPTOMS), COSMETIC PROBLEMS
AND MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION (5%).
OPTION A: CYSTIC HYGROMA IS A TYPE OF CONGENITAL LYMPHANGIOMA. THIS SWELLING IS SOFT AND PARTIALLY
COMPRESSIBLE, WHICH SHOWS POSITIVE FLUCTUATION AND TRANSLUCENCY TEST.
OPTION B: CHEMODECTOMA OR CAROTID BODY TUMOR IS A RARE TUMOR, MOST COMMONLY PRESENT IN THE
FIFTH DECADE AND THERE IS AN ASSOCIATION WITH PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. THESE PATIENTS USUALLY PRESENT
WITH A SLOWLY ENLARGING, PAINLESS LUMP AT THE CAROTID BIFURCATION.
4766
OPTION D: A LIPOMA IS A SOFT PAINLESS SWELLING. IT SHOWS THE CHARACTERISTIC SLIP SIGN AND IS FREELY
MOBILE.

questions.explanation:

30 DEGREES HIGHER THAN THE FEET. IT IS NAMED SO, AS THE POSITION IS REVERSE OF THE TRENDELENBURG
POSITION, WHERE THE HEAD END IS LOWER AND THE FEET ARE AT A HIGHER LEVEL.
THE TRENDELENBURG AND REVERSE TRENDELENBURG POSITIONS ARE USED IN SURGERIES THAT ARE REQUIRED TO
MOVE THE ABDOMINAL VISCERA, SUCH AS THE SMALL BOWEL, AWAY FROM THE OPERATIVE FIELD. RESTRAINTS
AND SIDEBOARDS ARE PLACED TO PREVENT THE PATIENT FROM SLIDING FROM THE BED.
IN LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY, THE PATIENT IS PLACED IN A REVERSE TRENDELENBURG POSITION SLIGHTLY
ROTATED TO THE LEFT. THIS EXPOSES THE FUNDUS OF THE GALLBLADDER WHICH IS RETRACTED TOWARDS THE
DIAPHRAGM.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: LLOYD DAVIES'S POSITION IS A 30-DEGREE TRENDELENBURG POSITION WITH THE HIPS FLEXED AT 15
DEGREES. IT IS USED FOR RECTAL AND ANAL CANAL SURGERIES LIKE LOW ANTERIOR RESECTION AND
ABDOMINOPERINEAL RESECTION. IT CAN CAUSE COMPARTMENT SYNDROME OF THE CALVES.
OPTION B: JACKKNIFE POSITION IS A MODIFIED PRONE POSITION WHERE THE PATIENT'S HIPS ARE SUPPORTED
ON A PILLOW AND THE TABLE IS FLEXED AT A 90-DEGREE ANGLE WITH THE HEAD AND FEET AT A LOWER LEVEL. IT IS
NOT USED ANYMORE DUE TO THE CHEST COMPRESSION CAUSING IMPAIRED VENTILATION LEADING TO POSITIONAL
