questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A DIABETIC PATIENT PRESENTS WITH SUDDEN-ONSET PERINEAL PAIN. UPON EXAMINATION, FOUL-SMELLING
DISCHARGE, AND NECROTIC TISSUE AS SEEN IN THE IMAGE IS NOTED. WHICH OF THESE IS TRUE WITH RESPECT TO THE GIVEN CONDITION?
options: ANTI-GAS GANGRENE SERUM INDICATED FOR ALL CASES
URINARY DIVERSION IS THE NEXT STEP
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CONDITION IS LIKELY TO BE FOURNIER GANGRENE. IT IS A MIXED FLORA AEROBIC AND ANAEROBIC
INFECTION.
FOURNIER'S GANGRENE IS A POLYMICROBIAL INFECTION AND A TYPE OF NECROTIZING FASCIITIS OF THE
PERINEUM, EXTERNAL GENITALIA, AND PERIANAL REGION. RISK FACTORS INCLUDE IMMUNOCOMPROMISED
STATES SUCH AS HIV, ALCOHOLISM, AND DIABETES. THE INFECTION MAY BE PRECIPITATED BY MINOR
5048
PROCEDURES IN THE PERINEAL AREA, SUCH AS A BRUISE, SCRATCH, URETHRAL DILATATION, INJECTION OF
HEMORRHOIDS, OR OPENING OF A PERIURETHRAL ABSCESS. THE INFECTION SPREADS ALONG THE DARTOS, SCARPA,
AND COLLES FASCIA.
THE SEQUENCE OF EVENTS THAT LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF GANGRENE ARE AS FOLLOWS: A MIXED INFECTION
OF THE AEROBIC AND ANAEROBIC BACTERIA → FULMINATING INFLAMMATION
OF SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE → OBLITERATIVE ARTERITIS OF THE ARTERIOLES THAT SUPPLY THE SCROTAL SKIN →
GANGRENE.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF FOURNIER GANGRENE ARE SCROTAL PAIN, FEVER, PROSTRATION, AND PALLOR. CELLULITIS
SPREADS RAPIDLY AND MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH ESCHARS, NECROSIS, FLAKING SKIN, AND CREPITUS.
THE TESTIS IS USUALLY NOT AFFECTED.
DIAGNOSIS IS MAJORLY CLINICAL AND VERY RARELY MADE BY LABORATORY OR IMAGING FINDINGS.
THE STEPS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF THIS CONDITION:
- IV FLUIDS
- IV ANTIBIOTICS
- URGENT SURGICAL EXCISION FOLLOWED BY SKIN GRAFTING IN LATER STAGES. WIDE SURGICAL EXCISION IS OFTEN
NECESSARY.
WHEN THE INFECTION HAS BEEN CONTROLLED, A VACUUM-ASSISTED DRESSING MAY BE HELPFUL. SKIN GRAFTING
IS ESSENTIAL FOR A PATIENT SURVIVING AN ACUTE EPISODE. DESPITE THE BEST THERAPY, MORTALITY RATES ARE
AROUND 50%.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: ANTI-GAS GANGRENE SERUM IS A TREATMENT FOR GAS GANGRENE THAT IS OF HISTORICAL IMPORTANCE
AND IS NO LONGER USED. TREATMENT OF GAS GANGRENE IS NOW DONE WITH ANTIBIOTICS.
OPTION B: WHILE URINARY DIVERSION AND OTHER SUPPORTIVE MEASURES ARE USEFUL IN THE MANAGEMENT
OF THE CONDITION, IT IS NOT THE NEXT BEST STEP.
OPTION C: THE BLOOD SUPPLY OF THE TESTES IS SEPARATE FROM THAT OF THE OVERLYING SKIN, AND HENCE,
TESTES CAN BE PRESERVED DURING DEBRIDEMENT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
Which of these is the most common complication following ligation of the first vessel
during abdominoperineal resection for rectal carcinoma? (APR Abdominoperineal resection)
options: PARASYMPATHETIC - BLADDER DYSFUNCTION AND RETROGRADE EJACULATION.
SYMPATHETIC - RETROGRADE EJACULATION AND BLADDER DYSFUNCTION.
SYMPATHETIC - IMPOTENCE AND LOSS OF CUTANEOUS SENSATION IN PERINEAL REGION
questions.answer: SYMPATHETIC - RETROGRADE EJACULATION AND BLADDER DYSFUNCTION.
questions.explanation:
THE FIRST VESSEL THAT IS USUALLY LIGATED DURING ABDOMINOPERINEAL RESECTION (APR) IS THE INFERIOR
MESENTERIC ARTERY (IMA). A HIGH INFERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY LIGATION DURING ABDOMINOPERINEAL
RESECTION CAN INJURE THE SUPERIOR HYPOGASTRIC NERVE, RESULTING IN SYMPATHETIC DYSFUNCTION
AND LEADING TO RETROGRADE EJACULATION AND BLADDER DYSFUNCTION.
ABDOMINOPERINEAL RESECTION IS THE COMPLETE EXCISION OF THE RECTUM, ANAL CANAL, AND SPHINCTER
APPARATUS. THIS IS DONE WITH THE CREATION OF A PERMANENT COLOSTOMY. THIS IS COMMONLY PREFERRED
IN ELDERLY PATIENTS WITH DISTAL RECTAL CANCER WITH POOR SPHINCTER FUNCTION. IN THESE PATIENTS, THE END
COLOSTOMY OFFERS A BETTER QUALITY OF LIFE.
COMPLICATIONS:
- HIGHER RECURRENCE RATES COMPARED TO LOW ANTERIOR RESECTION.
5049
- ANASTOMOTIC LEAKS OR DEHISCENCES
- NECROSIS OF THE TRANSPOSED COLON
- BLEEDING
- STRICTURES
THE SYMPATHETIC INNERVATION OF THE RECTUM IS FROM L1, L2, AND L3, WHICH TOGETHER FORM THE
SUPERIOR HYPOGASTRIC PLEXUS. THEY DIVIDE INTO LEFT AND RIGHT HYPOGASTRIC NERVES AT THE LEVEL OF THE
SACRAL PROMONTORY SUPPLYING THE RECTUM AND THE GENITOURINARY SYSTEM. A HIGH IMA LIGATION DURING
SURGERY CAN RESULT IN SYMPATHETIC DYSFUNCTION CAUSING RETROGRADE EJACULATION.
INJURY TO THE PELVIC PLEXUS AND NERVI ERIGENTES, DURING THE DIVISION ALONG THE PELVIC SIDE WALL, CAN
CAUSE ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION, IMPOTENCE, AND ATONIC BLADDER. INJURY TO THE PERIPROSTATIC PLEXUS CAN
LEAD TO SEXUAL AND BLADDER DYSFUNCTION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS TO THE CLINIC WITH THE LESION GIVEN IN THE IMAGE. HE HAD A TRAUMATIC INJURY
TO THE CHEST ONE YEAR AGO. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWING A LARGE AREA OF SCAR TISSUE IS SUGGESTIVE OF A KELOID.
A KELOID REFERS TO EXCESS ACCUMULATION OF COLLAGEN AT THE SCAR SITE WITH GROWTH OF THE SCAR TISSUE
BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF THE ORIGINAL WOUND. IT DOES NOT REGRESS. THE PATIENT'S HISTORY OF
TRAUMATIC INJURY TO THE CHEST ONE YEAR AGO, FOLLOWED BY THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN EXPANDING SCAR, IS
SUGGESTIVE OF A KELOID. THE KELOID IS OFTEN GLOSSY IN APPEARANCE AND RUBBERY IN TEXTURE. THEY ARE
COMPOSED OF THICK BUNDLES OF COLLAGEN.
TREATMENT OF KELOIDS USUALLY INVOLVES INTRALESIONAL INJECTIONS OF TRIAMCINOLONE. MULTIPLE DOSES ARE
REQUIRED AT INTERVALS OVER SEVERAL WEEKS AND MAY RESULT IN FLATTENING BUT RARELY DOES THE WOUND
NARROW.
OPTION A: A HEMANGIOMA IS A VASCULAR TUMOR THAT ARISES FROM THE ENDOTHELIUM. THEY TYPICALLY
PRESENT AS RED OR PINKISH MACULES OR RAISED LESIONS.
OPTION B: HYPERTROPHIC SCARS, UNLIKE KELOIDS, REMAIN WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OF THE ORIGINAL WOUND
AND TEND TO REGRESS OVER TIME. SINCE THIS SCAR HAS FAILED TO REGRESS OVER 1 YEAR AND HAS GROWN
BEYOND THE ORIGINAL WOUND MARGINS, IT IS MORE LIKELY TO BE A KELOID.
OPTION D: NEUROFIBROMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS ARISING FROM SCHWANN CELLS. THEY USUALLY PRESENT AS
SOFT, FLESH-COLORED NODULES, OFTEN IN ASSOCIATION WITH NEUROFIBROMATOSIS TYPE 1, A GENETIC DISORDER.
THE PATIENT'S HISTORY OF CHEST TRAUMA AND THE APPEARANCE OF THE LESION MAKE NEUROFIBROMA AN
UNLIKELY DIAGNOSIS IN THIS CASE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 45-YEAR-OLD MALE UNDERWENT BILATERAL LAPAROSCOPIC HERNIA REPAIR FOR INGUINAL HERNIA.
POSTOPERATIVELY, HE REPORTED PAIN IN THE RIGHT THIGH. WHICH OF THESE NERVE
ENTRAPMENT LEADS TO THIS SYMPTOM?
questions.explanation:
ENTRAPMENT OF THE LATERAL CUTANEOUS NERVE OF THE THIGH IS THE MOST LIKELY CAUSE OF PAIN IN THIS
PATIENT WITH HISTORY OF LAPAROSCOPIC HERNIA REPAIR.
THE LAPAROSCOPIC APPROACH IS PREFERRED FOR BILATERAL OR RECURRENT INGUINAL HERNIAS.
TRANSABDOMINAL PREPERITONEAL (TAPP) REPAIR AND TOTAL EXTRAPERITONEAL (TEP) REPAIR ARE THE
METHODS COMMONLY USED.
5050
THE NERVES COMMONLY INJURED IN LAPAROSCOPIC REPAIR ARE THE GENITOFEMORAL AND LATERAL FEMORAL
CUTANEOUS NERVES OF THE THIGH. PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ACUTE NEUROPATHIC PAIN ALONG THE DERMATOMAL
DISTRIBUTION. INJURY TO THE LATERAL FEMORAL CUTANEOUS NERVE RESULTS IN MERALGIA PARESTHETICA.
TREATMENT CONSISTS OF REST, ICE, NSAIDS, PHYSICAL THERAPY, AND POSSIBLE LOCAL CORTICOSTEROID AND
ANESTHETIC INJECTION. DRUGS LIKE GABAPENTIN CAN BE USED.
IN LAPAROSCOPIC TAPP REPAIR, TO REDUCE THE CHANCES OF NERVE INJURY DURING MESH PLACEMENT, TACKS
ARE IDEALLY PLACED ABOVE THE ILIOPUBIC TRACT TO AVOID NERVE INJURY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: ILIOINGUINAL NERVE MAY BE COMMONLY INJURED DURING OPEN HERNIA REPAIR. IT LEADS TO
SENSORY DISTURBANCES AND PAIN OVER THE SKIN OF THE GENITALIA AND UPPER MEDIAL THIGH.
OPTION B: ILIOHYPOGASTRIC NERVE CAN BE INJURED WHILE MAKING AN INCISION IN THE RIGHT ILIAC FOSSA
DURING HERNIA SURGERY.
OPTION C: FEMORAL NERVE CAN BE COMPRESSED BY RETROPERITONEAL TUMORS OR HEMORRHAGE IN PATIENTS
ON ANTICOAGULANTS OR BLEEDING DIATHESIS. IT PRESENTS AS WASTING AND WEAKNESS OF THE QUADRICEPS
FEMORIS MUSCLE MAKING THE PATIENT DIFFICULT TO WALK. PAIN AND PARAESTHESIA ARE SEEN ALONG THE
REGION OF THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE NERVE.

PAINFUL STIMULUS. SPECIFY HIS GCS SCORE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH FEVER AND ABDOMINAL PAIN WITH JAUNDICE. INVESTIGATIONS SHOWED THE
GIVEN FINDINGS. WHICH OF THESE STATEMENTS IS TRUE CONCERNING THIS CONDITION?
options: ANGIOEMBOLIZATION IS THE TREATMENT OF CHOICE
ECHINOCOCCUS SPECIES IS INVOLVED IN ETIOLOGY
questions.answer: ECHINOCOCCUS SPECIES IS INVOLVED IN ETIOLOGY
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CT IMAGE SHOWS A CYST IN THE LIVER WITH SERPENTINE LINEAR MEMBRANES SEEN AS WAVY
MEMBRANES WITHIN THE CYST IS SUGGESTIVE OF HYDATID DISEASE.
HYDATID DISEASE OR ECHINOCOCCOSIS IS A ZOONOTIC INFECTION CAUSED BY THE ECHINOCOCCUS SPECIES
OF FLATWORMS. ITS LIFE CYCLE CONSISTS OF DOGS AS DEFINITIVE HOSTS AND HUMANS AS
ABBERANT INTERMEDIATE HOSTS. PRIMARY HYDATID CYSTS MOST COMMONLY OCCUR IN THE LIVER. MOST
PATIENTS ARE ASYMPTOMATIC BUT WHEN SYMPTOMATIC, THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH HEPATOMEGALY, PAIN,
AND OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE.
THE FIRST/INITIAL IMAGING TEST IS USG, AND A CT SCAN CAN BE USED TO DIAGNOSE THE CONDITION.
CT SCAN SHOWS THE PRESENCE OF A SPACE-OCCUPYING LESION WITH A SMOOTH OUTLINE AND SEPTA. CT SCAN
HAS AN ACCURACY OF 98% IN THE DETECTION OF HYDATID CYSTS AND HIGH SENSITIVITY TO THE DETECTION OF
DAUGHTER CYSTS AND EXTRA-HEPATIC CYSTS. ON CT IMAGING, THE SERPENT SIGN IS SEEN AS WAVY
MEMBRANES WITHIN THE CYST.
5051
THE USG OF AN ACTIVE HYDATID CYST SHOWS MULTIPLE SEPTATIONS AND A ROSETTE OR HONEYCOMB
APPEARANCE:
THE BALL OF WOOL SIGN IS SEEN ON USG WHEN THE CONTENTS SETTLE IN THE DEPENDENT PORTION OF THE CYST,
AS SEEN BELOW:
ON USG, THE WATER-LILY SIGN IS SEEN IN HYDATID INFECTIONS WHEN THERE IS DETACHMENT OF THE ENDOCYST
MEMBRANE, WHICH RESULTS IN FLOATING MEMBRANES WITHIN THE PERICYST THAT MIMIC THE APPEARANCE OF
A WATER LILY. 5052
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: WHILE SURGICAL TREATMENT OF HYDATID CYST IS USEFUL AND EFFECTIVE, ALTERNATIVES LIKE
PERCUTANEOUS ASPIRATION, INJECTION, RE-ASPIRATION (PAIR) ARE EQUALLY EFFECTIVE AND ARE CURRENTLY
USED.
OPTION B: IGG ELISA AND INDIRECT HEMAGGLUTININ ASSAY ARE USED FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF HYDATID CYST.
OPTION C: ANGIOEMBOLIZATION HAS NO ROLE IN THE TREATMENT OF HYDATID CYST.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD MALE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A SWELLING THAT HAS BEEN SLOWLY GROWING IN THE PAST 2
YEARS. UPON EXAMINATION, IT WAS VARIABLE IN CONSISTENCY AND FULLY MOBILE. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY
DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND IMAGE DEPICT A LIKELY CASE OF PAROTID TUMOR, LIKELY TO BE A
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA.
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA IS THE MOST COMMON BENIGN SALIVARY GLAND TUMOR. THE MOST COMMONLY
AFFECTED GLAND IS THE PAROTID GLAND. THE SUPERFICIAL LOBE IS MOST COMMONLY AFFECTED. IT IS ALSO
CALLED AS MIXED TUMOR SINCE IT HAS BOTH EPITHELIAL AND MESENCHYMAL COMPONENTS. IT MOST
COMMONLY AFFECTS FEMALES AROUND 40 YEARS OF AGE.
THE COMMON PRESENTING FEATURE IS A PAINLESS SWELLING BELOW, IN FRONT, OR BEHIND THE EAR. THE
INVOLVEMENT OF THE DEEP LOBE LEADS TO DUMBBELL TUMOR – SWELLING IN BOTH THE NECK AND ORAL CAVITY.
SPECIFIC FEATURES:
- SLOWLY GROWING BENIGN TUMOR
- UNICENTRIC IN ORIGIN
- POTENTIALLY MALIGNANT
- POSSIBILITY OF PROTRUSION OF FRINGES OF THE TUMOR MASS THROUGH THE CAPSULE
- RADIORESISTANT
- USUALLY AFFECTS ADULTS, FEMALES > MALES
5053
- PAINLESS SWELLING
- WELL-DEFINED MARGINS
- LOBULATED, FIRM, ELASTIC-TO-HARD CONSISTENCY
- FREE FROM DEEPER STRUCTURES
- NO FACIAL NERVE INVOLVEMENT
- THE DEEP LOBE PUSHES TONSILS AND FAUCIAL PILLARS
DIAGNOSIS IS MADE BY FNAC, WHICH IS CONSIDERED THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE. OPEN BIOPSY
CONTRAINDICATED DUE TO CHANCES OF INJURY TO THE FACIAL NERVE AND SEEDLING OF THE TUMOR
SURGERY IS THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT - SUPERFICIAL PAROTIDECTOMY (PATEY'S OPERATION). RADIOTHERAPY
IS CONSIDERED IN HIGH-GRADE MALIGNANCIES DEMONSTRATING EXTRA-GLANDULAR DISEASE, PERINEURAL
INVASION, DIRECT INVASION OF SURROUNDING TISSUE, OR REGIONAL METASTASES.
PATHOLOGY:
GROSS FEATURES:
- THE TUMORS ARE ROUNDED, WELL-DEMARCATED, MEASURING <6 CM IN GREATEST DIMENSION.
- THEY ARE USUALLY ENCAPSULATED, EXCEPT IN SOME AREAS SUCH AS THE PALATE.
- THE CUT SURFACE IS GRAY-WHITE WITH MYXOID AND BLUE TRANSLUCENT AREAS OF THE
CHONDROID (CARTILAGE-LIKE) STROMA.
MICROSCOPIC FEATURES:
- THE EPITHELIAL ELEMENTS RESEMBLE DUCTAL CELLS OR MYOEPITHELIAL CELLS. THEY ARE ARRANGED AS DUCTS,
ACINI, IRREGULAR TUBULES, STRANDS, OR SHEETS OF CELLS.
- THESE EPITHELIAL ELEMENTS ARE DISPERSED WITHIN A BACKGROUND OF LOOSE MYXOID AND HYALINE
TISSUE CONTAINING ISLANDS OF CARTILAGE AND, RARELY, FOCI OF BONE.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA OF THE SALIVARY GLAND CONSISTING OF MIXED EPITHELIAL
(LEFT) AND MESENCHYMAL CELL COMPONENTS (RIGHT).
5054
DERMOID CYSTS ARE SLOW-GROWING BENIGN LESIONS. THEY ARE MOSTLY SEEN ON THE SCALP AND SKULL. IT IS
MADE OF HAIR, TEETH, CARTILAGE, AND SKIN GLANDS. OTHER COMMON SITES ARE THE FOREHEAD,
POSTAURICULAR, AND LATERAL PART OF THE EYEBROW.
A SEBACEOUS CYST IS DERIVED FROM HAIR FOLLICLE INFUNDIBULUM OR TRAUMATIC INCLUSION. THE MOST
COMMON SITE OF A SEBACEOUS CYST IS THE POSTAURICULAR SULCUS OR BELOW AND BEHIND THE EAR LOBULE.
MALIGNANCY IS RARE.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF A SEBACEOUS CYST INCLUDE:
- BENIGN SWELLING THAT IS MOBILE, FLUCTUANT, AND FIXED TO THE SKIN. IT PRESENTS WITH A CENTRAL
PUNCTUM IN ABOUT 70% OF CASES.
- IT IS GENERALLY AN ASYMPTOMATIC, NON-TENDER SWELLING. IT CAN BE PAINFUL AND RED IF INFLAMED.
- IT MAY OOZE OUT A FOUL-SMELLING, CHEESE-LIKE DISCHARGE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A patient who is a known case of alcohol dependence syndrome presents with sudden and
unintentional weight loss. Specify the most likely diagnosis. -ALP 240 IU/L -S. Direct bilirubin - 1 mg/dL -AST/ALT -0.5 -Alpha fetoprotein- 600 ng/mL
questions.explanation:
THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IN THIS PATIENT WITH A HISTORY OF ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE, SUDDEN
UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS, AND RAISED AFP IS HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA (HCC).
HCC IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF PRIMARY LIVER CANCER. IT IS MORE COMMONLY SEEN IN MALES, AND
THE PEAK AGE GROUP IS BETWEEN 65-70 YEARS. THE MAIN RISK FACTOR FOR HCC IS CIRRHOSIS AND
ASSOCIATED CHRONIC LIVER DAMAGE DUE TO CHRONIC INFECTION BY HEPATITIS B OR C VIRUS (HBV OR HCV),
ALCOHOL ABUSE, METABOLIC SYNDROME, OR HEMOCHROMATOSIS. THE INCIDENCE OF HCC IS INCREASING
WORLDWIDE. THIS IS CONTRIBUTED BY THE INCREASE IN HCV AND HBV INFECTIONS, ALONG WITH LIFESTYLE
DISORDERS LIKE OBESITY. OBESITY IS ASSOCIATED WITH NON-ALCOHOLIC FATTY LIVER DISEASE (NAFLD). THIS
PROGRESSES ON TO NON-ALCOHOLIC STEATOHEPATITIS (NASH) CAUSING CIRRHOSIS AND HEPATOCELLULAR
CARCINOMA. THUS, NASH AND NAFLD ARE RISK FACTORS FOR HCC.
REGULAR SURVEILLANCE, INCLUDING LIVER IMAGING AND MONITORING OF ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN LEVELS, IS
RECOMMENDED FOR HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH LIVER CIRRHOSIS, CHRONIC HEPATITIS B OR
C INFECTION, OR SIGNIFICANT ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION. EARLY DETECTION OF HCC CAN IMPROVE TREATMENT
5055
OUTCOMES AND OVERALL PROGNOSIS.
VERY EARLY HCC IS TREATED BY ABLATION. EARLY HCC WITH A SINGLE NODULE IS RESECTED, BUT WHEN THERE
ARE MULTIPLE NODULES OVER 3 CM, ABLATION OR TRANSPLANTATION ARE CONSIDERED. INTERMEDIATE-STAGE
HCC IS TREATED BY CHEMOEMBOLIZATION. TRANSARTERIAL CHEMOEMBOLIZATION (TACE) IS USED FOR
MULTINODULAR LESIONS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: HEPATIC ADENOMAS ARE BENIGN LIVER TUMORS THAT ARE OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH ORAL
CONTRACEPTIVE USE AND ANABOLIC STEROID USE. THE PATIENT'S HISTORY OF ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE AND HIGH
ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN LEVELS ARE NOT CONSISTENT WITH HEPATIC ADENOMA. ADDITIONALLY, HEPATIC ADENOMAS
ARE USUALLY ASYMPTOMATIC AND DO NOT PRESENT WITH SUDDEN UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS.
OPTION B: CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA IS A CANCER THAT ARISES FROM THE BILE DUCTS WITHIN THE LIVER. WHILE
PATIENTS WITH ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE MAY HAVE AN INCREASED RISK OF CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA, THE ELEVATED
ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN LEVELS ARE NOT TYPICAL FOR THIS TYPE OF CANCER. CHOLANGIOCARCINOMAS USUALLY
PRESENT WITH JAUNDICE, PRURITUS, AND ABDOMINAL PAIN, BUT SUDDEN WEIGHT LOSS IS LESS CHARACTERISTIC.
OPTION D: ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS IS AN INFLAMMATION OF THE LIVER CAUSED BY EXCESSIVE ALCOHOL
CONSUMPTION. IT USUALLY PRESENTS WITH JAUNDICE, FEVER, AND ABDOMINAL PAIN. WHILE THE PATIENT'S
HISTORY OF ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE MIGHT SUGGEST ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS, ELEVATED ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN LEVELS
AND UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS ARE NOT TYPICAL FOR THIS CONDITION. MOREOVER, THE AST/ALT RATIO IS
USUALLY GREATER THAN 2 IN ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS, BUT IT IS 0.5 IN THIS CASE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH FEATURES OF CHRONIC PANCREATITIS WITH RECURRENT ATTACKS AND HAS A 10
MM DILATATION OF THE PANCREATIC DUCT WITH INTRADUCTAL CALCULI PRESENT. WHICH OF THESE
IS THE SURGERY OF CHOICE?
questions.explanation:
IN THIS CASE OF CHRONIC PANCREATITIS WITH RECURRENT ATTACKS, 10 MM DILATATION OF THE PANCREATIC DUCT,
AND INTRADUCTAL CALCULI, LONGITUDINAL PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY (ALSO KNOWN AS PUESTOW PROCEDURE OR
LATERAL PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY) IS THE SURGERY OF CHOICE. THIS PROCEDURE INVOLVES OPENING THE
PANCREATIC DUCT ALONG ITS LENGTH AND CONNECTING IT TO A LOOP OF THE JEJUNUM, WHICH HELPS TO DRAIN
THE OBSTRUCTED PANCREATIC DUCT AND ALLEVIATE PAIN.
PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC PANCREATITIS MAINLY EXPERIENCE PAIN DUE TO DUCTAL HYPERTENSION OR
PARENCHYMAL INFLAMMATION. ACUTE EXACERBATIONS IN DUCT PRESSURE LEAD TO RECURRENT ACUTE
ATTACKS. THE PANCREATIC DUCT DILATION OBSERVED ON PANCREATOGRAPHY FOR CHRONIC PANCREATITIS IS
CLASSICALLY DESCRIBED AS A CHAIN OF LAKES, WHICH REFLECTS THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE DILATIONS AND
STENOSES. RESPONSE TO TREATMENT HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE DEPENDENT UPON THE DEGREE OF PREOPERATIVE
PANCREATIC FIBROSIS.
LONGITUDINAL PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY, ALSO KNOWN AS THE PUESTOW PROCEDURE OR LATERAL
PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY, IS A SURGICAL TREATMENT PRIMARILY USED FOR CHRONIC PANCREATITIS WITH A
DILATED MAIN PANCREATIC DUCT AND INTRADUCTAL CALCULI.
IN LONGITUDINAL PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY, A LONGITUDINAL INCISION IS MADE ALONG THE LENGTH OF THE
MAIN PANCREATIC DUCT, TYPICALLY FROM THE TAIL TO THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS. THE DILATED PANCREATIC
DUCT IS THEN OPENED, AND ANY INTRADUCTAL CALCULI OR OBSTRUCTIONS ARE REMOVED. THE OPENED DUCT IS
THEN CONNECTED TO A LOOP OF THE JEJUNUM TO CREATE A SIDE-TO-SIDE ANASTOMOSIS. THIS ALLOWS FOR THE
DRAINAGE OF PANCREATIC SECRETIONS DIRECTLY INTO THE JEJUNUM, BYPASSING ANY NARROWED OR OBSTRUCTED
AREAS OF THE DUCT.
5056
THIS PROCEDURE CAN EFFECTIVELY RELIEVE PAIN AND IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC
PANCREATITIS. HOWEVER, IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT IT MAY NOT REVERSE THE UNDERLYING PATHOLOGY OF
CHRONIC PANCREATITIS OR PREVENT THE PROGRESSION OF THE DISEASE. IT IS ALSO NOT SUITABLE FOR ALL PATIENTS
WITH CHRONIC PANCREATITIS, PARTICULARLY THOSE WITH A NON-DILATED PANCREATIC DUCT OR ISOLATED HEAD
INVOLVEMENT.
OTHER OPTIONS:
PANCREATICODUODENECTOMY: THIS PROCEDURE, ALSO KNOWN AS WHIPPLE PROCEDURE, INVOLVES REMOVING
THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS, DUODENUM, GALLBLADDER, AND PART OF THE BILE DUCT. IT IS TYPICALLY
PERFORMED FOR PANCREATIC CANCER OR TUMORS IN THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS, NOT FOR CHRONIC
PANCREATITIS WITH DUCTAL OBSTRUCTION AND INTRADUCTAL CALCULI.
ERCP AND SPHINCTEROTOMY: ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY (ERCP) WITH
SPHINCTEROTOMY IS A PROCEDURE THAT INVOLVES OPENING THE SPHINCTER OF ODDI TO FACILITATE THE
DRAINAGE OF BILE AND PANCREATIC SECRETIONS. ALTHOUGH IT MAY PROVIDE TEMPORARY RELIEF, IT IS NOT A
DEFINITIVE TREATMENT FOR CHRONIC PANCREATITIS WITH LARGE DUCTAL DILATATION AND INTRADUCTAL CALCULI.
ERCP WITH SPHINCTEROTOMY MAY BE USEFUL IN SOME CASES OF CHRONIC PANCREATITIS FOR THE REMOVAL OF
SMALL PANCREATIC DUCT STONES, BUT FOR LARGE DUCTAL DILATATION AND INTRADUCTAL CALCULI, LONGITUDINAL
PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY IS MORE APPROPRIATE.
CORING OF PANCREAS HEAD: CORING OF THE PANCREAS HEAD, ALSO KNOWN AS PANCREATIC HEAD RESECTION OR
BEGER PROCEDURE, IS A SURGICAL TECHNIQUE USED TO TREAT CHRONIC PANCREATITIS, PARTICULARLY WHEN THE
INFLAMMATION AND FIBROSIS PREDOMINANTLY AFFECT THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS. THE PROCEDURE INVOLVES
REMOVING THE INFLAMED AND FIBROTIC TISSUE FROM THE HEAD OF THE PANCREAS WHILE PRESERVING THE
DUODENUM, BILE DUCT, AND THE MAIN PANCREATIC DUCT. LONGITUDINAL PANCREATICOJEJUNOSTOMY IS A
MORE TARGETED AND EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR THIS PATIENT'S CONDITION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A WOMAN PRESENTED WITH A BIRADS-5 BREAST LESION. WHICH OF THESE IS A GOOD
PROGNOSTIC FACTOR FOR THIS LESION?
questions.explanation:
ER POSITIVITY IS A GOOD PROGNOSTIC FACTOR IN BREAST CANCER.
THE ER AND PR ARE TWO STEROID HORMONE RECEPTORS PRESENT IN BREAST CANCER. THE EXPRESSION OF
THESE RECEPTORS INDICATES A FAVORABLE PROGNOSIS AND RESPONSE TO HORMONAL THERAPY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE MUTATIONS IN BRCA1 GENE ACCOUNT FOR UP TO 40% OF FAMILIAL BREAST CANCERS. THESE
TUMORS ARE HIGH-GRADE, HORMONE RECEPTOR–NEGATIVE, AND ANEUPLOID AND DO NOT HAVE A GOOD
PROGNOSIS.
OPTION B: P53 IS A TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENE, WHICH ON MUTATION ACTS AS AN ONCOGENE. P53 POSITIVITY
IS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGHLY MALIGNANT BREAST CANCERS AND HAS POOR SURVIVAL.
OPTION D: KI-67 IS USED TO ACCESS THE PROLIFERATIVE INDEX (ACTIVITY) OF THE TUMOR. HIGH KI-67
INDICATES A POOR PROGNOSIS.

REGION. X-RAY SHOWS WIDENED MEDIASTINUM. BP IS 110/90 MMHG IN THE RIGHT UPPER LIMB AND

AND A WIDENED MEDIASTINUM ON X-RAY POINT TOWARDS A DIAGNOSIS OF AORTIC DISSECTION.
IT IS INITIATED BY AN INTIMAL TEAR, WHICH ALLOWS BLOOD TO PENETRATE INTO THE MEDIAL LAYER, PRODUCING
A CLEAVAGE PLANE (FALSE LUMEN) BETWEEN THE INNER TWO-THIRDS AND OUTER ONE-THIRD OF THE MEDIA. THE
TRUE LUMEN IS SEPARATED FROM THE FALSE LUMEN BY AN INTIMOMEDIAL FLAP.
CLASSIFICATION OF AORTIC DISSECTION:
ACUTE AORTIC DISSECTION CAN BE CLASSIFIED BY THE ORIGINAL DEBAKEY SYSTEM, WHICH IS BASED ON THE
LOCATION OF THE PROXIMAL TEAR AND DISTAL EXTENT OF THE DISSECTION FLAP, OR THE STANFORD SYSTEM, WHICH
IS BASED ONLY ON THE LOCATION OF THE PROXIMAL TEAR.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH RIGHT HYPOCHONDRIAC PAIN. HE HAD AN EPISODE OF DIARRHEA 1 WEEK
PRIOR. CT SCAN OF THE ABDOMEN REVEALS A LIVER ABSCESS OF AROUND 25 CCS. SPECIFY THE NEXT STEP
IN MANAGEMENT.
questions.explanation:
THIS PATIENT WITH AN ABSCESS IN THE LIVER WITH A HISTORY OF DIARRHEA MOST LIKELY HAS AN AMEBIC LIVER
ABSCESS. THE INITIAL TREATMENT OF CHOICE FOR AN AMEBIC LIVER ABSCESS IS MEDICAL THERAPY
WITH METRONIDAZOLE.
INGESTION OF ENTAMOEBA HISTOLYTICA CYSTS CAUSES INTESTINAL DISEASES LIKE DIARRHEA. FOLLOWING THIS,
THE TROPHOZOITES REACH THE LIVER MOSTLY THROUGH THE PORTAL VENOUS SYSTEM AND CAUSE AMEBIC LIVER
ABSCESS. THE COMMON PRESENTING FEATURES ARE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT PAIN, TENDERNESS, FEVER,
HEPATOMEGALY, AND DIARRHEA.
CT ABDOMEN IS HELPFUL IN DIFFERENTIATING AMEBIC FROM A PYOGENIC ABSCESS. A RIM ENHANCEMENT IS
NOTED IN CASE OF A PYOGENIC ABSCESS.
THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT FOR AMEBIC ABSCESSES IS METRONIDAZOLE, WHICH IS CURATIVE IN MORE THAN
90% OF PATIENTS. LUMINAL AGENTS SUCH AS IODOQUINOL, PAROMOMYCIN, OR DILOXANIDE FUROATE CAN BE
ADMINISTERED TO TREAT THE CARRIER STATE.
ASPIRATION OF ABSCESS IS RECOMMENDED IN CASE OF
- DIAGNOSTIC UNCERTAINTY
- FAILURE TO RESPOND TO METRONIDAZOLE THERAPY
- ABSCESSES LARGER THAN 5 CM IN DIAMETER AND IN THE LEFT LIVER, SINCE THEY ARE THOUGHT TO CARRY A
HIGH RISK OF RUPTURE

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 50-YEAR-OLD PATIENT WITH A HISTORY OF TRAUMA ONE WEEK BACK PRESENTS WITH CONFUSION AND
ATAXIA. HE IS ON TREATMENT FOR ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE AND HIS LAST INTAKE WAS 2 WEEKS BACK. CT
SCAN REVEALS THE FOLLOWING FINDING. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND THE PLAIN CT SCAN SHOWING A CONCAVO-CONVEX-SHAPED HEMATOMA ON
THE LEFT SIDE WITH A MIDLINE SHIFT TO THE RIGHT IS SUGGESTIVE OF SUBDURAL HEMATOMA (SDH).
5060
AN ACUTE SDH IS THE RESULT OF THE ACCUMULATION OF BLOOD BETWEEN THE ARACHNOID MEMBRANE AND
THE DURA. IT IS USUALLY DUE TO THE RUPTURE OF BRIDGING VEINS RUNNING FROM THE CEREBRAL CORTEX TO THE
DURAL SINUSES. THE LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS IS USUALLY IMPAIRED AT PRESENTATION AND MAY DETERIORATE
FURTHER AS THE HEMATOMA EXPANDS. ELDERLY AND ALCOHOLIC PATIENTS ARE AT A HIGHER RISK OF ACUTE SDH
FORMATION AFTER HEAD TRAUMA DUE TO BRAIN ATROPHY. ON CT SCAN, ACUTE SDH APPEARS AS A
HYPERDENSE, CRESCENT-SHAPED (CONCAVO-CONVEX) LESION.
OPEN CRANIOTOMY FOR THE EVACUATION OF ACUTE SDH IS INDICATED FOR THE FOLLOWING:
- THICKNESS >1 CM
- MIDLINE SHIFT >5 MM
- GLASGOW COMA SCALE (GCS) SCORE DROPS BY TWO OR MORE POINTS FROM THE TIME OF INJURY TO
HOSPITALIZATION.
CHRONIC SUBDURAL HEMATOMA RESULTS FROM A HEMATOMA THAT EXPANDS OVER DAYS OR WEEKS BY
OSMOSIS, ULTIMATELY PRODUCING SYMPTOMS OF RAISED ICP OR FOCAL DEFICITS. ON A CT SCAN, DIFFUSE
HYPODENSITY OVERLYING THE BRAIN SURFACE WOULD BE SEEN.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS FALSE WITH RESPECT TO THE GIVEN CONDITION?
options: REPEATED RADICAL SURGERY EVERY 24 HOURS MAY BE REQUIRED TO ADEQUATELY MANAGE THIS CONDITION
THIS IS A CASE OF MELENEY'S GANGRENE
THE CONDITION IS CAUSED BY BETA HEMOLYTIC STREPTOCOCCUS AND MAY SOMETIMES BE POLYMICROBIAL
HYPERBARIC OXYGEN HAS NO ROLE IN THE TREATMENT OF THIS CONDITION
questions.answer: HYPERBARIC OXYGEN HAS NO ROLE IN THE TREATMENT OF THIS CONDITION
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE IS LIKELY THAT OF MELENEY'S GANGRENE. HYPERBARIC OXYGEN HAS BEEN SHOWN TO
REDUCE MORTALITY IN PATIENTS WITH MELENEY'S GANGRENE AND THEREFORE PLAYS A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN THE
MANAGEMENT OF THIS CONDITION.
NECROTIZING FASCIITIS OF THE ABDOMINAL WALL IS KNOWN AS MELENEY'S GANGRENE. IT PRESENTS WITH
EXTENSIVE NECROSIS OF THE ABDOMINAL WALL, THROMBOSIS OF THE MICROVASCULATURE, AND AN ACUTE
INFLAMMATORY INFILTRATE. BULLAE DEVELOP ON THE ABDOMINAL WALL, WHICH PROGRESS TO OVERT CUTANEOUS
GANGRENE. THE AFFECTED AREA IS OFTEN PAINFUL, ERYTHEMATOUS, AND EDEMATOUS, WITH POSSIBLE SYSTEMIC
SIGNS OF INFECTION SUCH AS FEVER AND MALAISE. EARLY RECOGNITION AND AGGRESSIVE TREATMENT ARE
ESSENTIAL FOR A FAVORABLE OUTCOME.
MANAGEMENT INCLUDES PROMPT SURGICAL DEBRIDEMENT OF THE NECROTIC TISSUE, BROAD-SPECTRUM
ANTIBIOTICS TO COVER THE POLYMICROBIAL NATURE OF THE INFECTION, AND SUPPORTIVE MEASURES SUCH AS
FLUID RESUSCITATION AND CORRECTION OF ELECTROLYTE IMBALANCES. IN SOME CASES, HYPERBARIC OXYGEN
THERAPY MAY BE UTILIZED AS AN ADJUNCTIVE TREATMENT TO IMPROVE TISSUE OXYGENATION AND ENHANCE THE
HEALING PROCESS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: SURGICAL EXCISION OF NECROTIC TISSUE IS OFTEN REQUIRED DAILY AS THE INFECTION TENDS TO
SPREAD BEYOND THE BORDERS OF THE DEBRIDEMENT WOUND.
OPTION C: MELENEY'S GANGRENE IS CAUSED BY BETA-HEMOLYTIC STREPTOCOCCI OR STAPHYLOCOCCUS
AUREUS AND MAY ALSO BE POLYMICROBIAL.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A SWELLING IN THE GROIN REGION AND IT IS DIAGNOSED AS A DIRECT INGUINAL
HERNIA. WEAKNESS IN WHICH OF THESE STRUCTURES IS MOST LIKELY TO CAUSE THIS CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
A DIRECT INGUINAL HERNIA IS CAUSED DUE TO WEAKNESS IN THE CONJOINT TENDON.
5061
THE INNERMOST LAYERS OF THE LATERAL ABDOMINAL WALL CONTAIN TWO MUSCLES, NAMELY INTERNAL OBLIQUE
AND TRANSVERSE ABDOMINIS. THESE MUSCLE FIBERS ARCH OVER THE DEEP INGUINAL RING FROM LATERAL TO
MEDIAL, FUSE, AND BECOME TENDINOUS FORMING THE CONJOINT TENDON. THE AREA BELOW THIS ARCH LACKS
MUSCLE AND CONTAINS EXTERNAL OBLIQUE APONEUROSIS AND FASCIA TRANSVERSALIS, MAKING IT WEAK.
DIRECT INGUINAL HERNIA IS COMMON IN ELDERLY PATIENTS. IT IS SEEN MEDIAL TO THE INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC
VESSELS, IN HESSELBACH’S TRIANGLE. THIS AREA LACKS MUSCLE AND CONTAINS ONLY FASCIA.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: PECTINEAL LIGAMENT ALSO KNOWN AS COOPER'S LIGAMENT IS A STRONG FIBROUS BAND THAT
EXTENDS LATERALLY ALONG THE PECTINEAL LINE FROM THE PECTINEAL ATTACHMENT OF THE LACUNAR LIGAMENT.
OPTION C: THE INGUINAL LIGAMENT IS EXTERNAL OBLIQUE APONEUROSIS THAT EXTENDS BETWEEN THE ANTERIOR
SUPERIOR ILIAC SPINE AND THE PUBIC TUBERCLE. ON THE POINT OF ATTACHMENT TO THE PUBIC TUBERCLE, SOME
FIBERS PASS UPWARDS BEHIND THE SUPERFICIAL INGUINAL RING AND EXTERNAL OBLIQUE APONEUROSIS TO JOIN
THE RECTUS SHEATH AND LINEA ALBA. THESE FORM THE REFLECTED PART OF THE INGUINAL LIGAMENT.
OPTION D: LACUNAR LIGAMENT IS FORMED FROM THE FIBERS OF THE MEDIAL END OF THE INGUINAL LIGAMENT
AND THE FIBERS FROM THE FASCIA LATA OF THE THIGH. IT FORMS THE MEDIAL WALL OF THE FEMORAL CANAL.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH SUDDEN ONSET OF HEMATEMESIS. HE HAS BEEN TAKING ASPIRIN FOR HIS
ARTHRITIS AND DRINKS ALCOHOL OCCASIONALLY. HE GIVES A HISTORY OF OCCASIONAL ABDOMINAL PAIN. UPON EXAMINATION, THERE IS NO ABDOMINAL MASS OR TENDERNESS. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THIS PATIENT WITH A HISTORY OF ASPIRIN USE, NOW PRESENTING WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN AND A SUDDEN ONSET
OF HEMATEMESIS MOST LIKELY HAS A BLEEDING PEPTIC ULCER.
PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE (PUD) ACCOUNTS FOR AROUND 2/3RD OF UPPER GASTROINTESTINAL BLEEDING. THE
MAJOR CAUSATIVE FACTORS ARE HELICOBACTER PYLORI AND NSAIDS. PROSTAGLANDINS PROTECT GASTRIC AND
DUODENAL MUCOSA FROM ACID AND PEPSIN. THEY INCREASE MUCIN AND BICARBONATE SECRETION
AND INCREASE MUCOSAL BLOOD FLOW. THEY ALSO PROMOTE EPITHELIAL CELL PROLIFERATION. NSAIDS LIKE
ASPIRIN DISRUPT THESE NATURALLY PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS AND INCREASE THE RISK OF PEPTIC ULCER
FORMATION IN THE STOMACH AND THE DUODENUM.
5062
THEY PRESENT WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN, BLEEDING, OR SIGNS OF PERITONITIS DUE TO PERFORATION. SIGNIFICANT
HEMORRHAGE OCCURS WHEN DUODENAL OR GASTRIC ULCERS PENETRATE BRANCHES OF THE GASTRODUODENAL OR
LEFT GASTRIC ARTERIES, RESPECTIVELY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: MALLORY-WEISS TEARS ARE PARTIAL-THICKNESS TEARS OF THE MUCOSA AND SUBMUCOSA OCCURRING
NEAR THE GASTROESOPHAGEAL JUNCTION. THEY OCCUR IN PATIENTS WITH A HISTORY OF REPEATED EMESIS AND
ARE CLASSICAL IN ALCOHOLIC PATIENTS AFTER A PERIOD OF INTENSE RETCHING AND VOMITING FOLLOWING BINGE
DRINKING.
OPTION B: ESOPHAGITIS COMMONLY OCCURS DUE TO REPEATED EXPOSURE OF MUCOSA TO THE ACIDIC GASTRIC
SECRETIONS IN GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE. IT RESULTS IN CHRONIC BLOOD LOSS AND COMMONLY
PRESENTS AS ANEMIA OR GUAIAC-POSITIVE STOOLS. ULCERATIONS OF SUPERFICIAL MUCOSA DUE TO ESOPHAGITIS
GENERALLY DO NOT BLEED ACUTELY.
OPTION D: ESOPHAGEAL VARICES COMMONLY OCCUR DUE TO PORTAL HYPERTENSION IN PATIENTS WITH
CIRRHOSIS. A HISTORY OF LIVER DISEASE OR THE STIGMATA OF PORTAL HYPERTENSION AND CIRRHOSIS WOULD
SUGGEST VARICEAL BLEEDING.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A CONSTRUCTION WORKER CAME TO THE OPD COMPLAINING OF WHITE FINGERS. HE HAS BEEN WORKING IN
THE CEMENT AND CONCRETE INDUSTRY AND HAS BEEN WORKING ON HEAVY MACHINERY DRILLS, WOOD,
AND FURNITURE POLISHING FOR 20 YEARS. SPECIFY THE MOST LIKELY ETIOLOGY FOR THIS CONDITION.
options: CANDIDAL INFECTION OF THE FINGERS DUE TO CONTINUOUS EXPOSURE TO WATER
CONTINUOUS EXPOSURE TO CEMENT AND CONCRETE
CONTINUOUS EXPOSURE TO DRILLS AND MACHINES
questions.answer: CONTINUOUS EXPOSURE TO DRILLS AND MACHINES
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL VIGNETTE SUGGESTS THE DIAGNOSIS OF RAYNAUD'S SYNDROME DUE TO CHRONIC EXPOSURE TO
DRILLS AND MACHINES (VIBRATING TOOLS).
RAYNAUD'S SYNDROME OCCURS DUE TO PERIPHERAL VASOSPASM, AND IT IS MORE COMMON IN THE UPPER
EXTREMITIES. IT MAY OCCUR DUE TO EXPOSURE TO VARIOUS STIMULI, INCLUDING COLD TEMPERATURES,
TOBACCO, OR EMOTIONAL STRESS, AND CERTAIN OCCUPATIONAL GROUPS, SUCH AS THOSE WHO USE VIBRATING
TOOLS, OR IT CAN BE SECONDARY TO SCLERODERMA, SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS, SJOGREN'S SYNDROME,
AND ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME.
THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY BEHIND RAYNAUD'S SYNDROME IS BELIEVED TO BE DUE TO INCREASED LEVELS OF
α2-ADRENERGIC RECEPTORS AND THEIR HYPERSENSITIVITY AND ALSO DUE TO AN ABNORMAL THERMOREGULATORY
RESPONSE BY THE SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM.
A RAYNAUD'S PHENOMENON ATTACK IS SUDDEN, AND IT RANGES FROM INTENSE PALLOR (WHITE ATTACK) TO
CYANOSIS (BLUE ATTACK), FOLLOWED BY REACTIVE HYPEREMIA DUE TO SUBSEQUENT RELAXATION OF BLOOD
VESSELS. IT TYPICALLY AFFECTS FINGERS (DISTAL AREAS), AND THE THUMB IS USUALLY SPARED. IF THE THUMB IS
INVOLVED, IT MAY INDICATE UNDERLYING SECONDARY ETIOLOGY. OTHER COMMON COMPLAINTS INCLUDE PIN
AND NEEDLES SENSATION, NUMBNESS, OR FINGER ACHES OR PAIN. IN SEVERE ATTACKS, DIGITAL ULCERATIONS
AND GANGRENE MAY DEVELOP.
DIAGNOSIS IS PRIMARILY BASED ON THE CLINICAL HISTORY AND PHYSICAL EXAMINATION. NAIL FOLD CAPILLARY
MICROSCOPY CAN BE HELPFUL, PARTICULARLY FOR IDENTIFYING SECONDARY RAYNAUD'S PHENOMENON
ASSOCIATED WITH CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISEASES. ANGIOGRAPHY CAN BE DONE FOR PATIENTS WITH DIGITAL
ULCERATIONS AND GANGRENE.
MANAGEMENT IS MAINLY CONSERVATIVE, AND IT INCLUDES WEARING GLOVES, USE OF ELECTRIC OR CHEMICALLY
ACTIVATED HAND WARMERS, AVOIDING OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE TO VIBRATORY TOOLS, ABSTINENCE FROM
TOBACCO, AND RELOCATING TO A WARMER, DRYER CLIMATE.
OTHER MANAGEMENT OPTIONS:
5063
- CALCIUM CHANNEL–BLOCKERS SUCH AS DILTIAZEM AND NIFEDIPINE ARE THE DRUGS OF CHOICE.
- FLUOXETINE HAS BEEN SHOWN TO REDUCE THE FREQUENCY AND DURATION OF VASOSPASTIC EPISODES.
- PROSTAGLANDINS CAN BE USED IN PATIENTS WITH SEVERE SYMPTOMS.
COMPLICATIONS, INCLUDING DIGITAL ULCERATIONS AND GANGRENE, CAN BE SURGICALLY TREATED BY
DEBRIDEMENT AND AMPUTATION, RESPECTIVELY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 5-YEAR-OLD CHILD WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL FOR PROLAPSING RECTAL MASS AND PAINLESS RECTAL
BLEEDING. HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION REVEALS ENLARGED AND INFLAMED GLANDS FILLED WITH
MUCIN. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN FEATURES ARE SUGGESTIVE OF A JUVENILE POLYP, WHICH ARE A TYPE OF HAMARTOMATOUS POLYP.
THEY ARE BENIGN GROWTHS THAT ARE COMPOSED OF A DISORGANIZED MIXTURE OF DIFFERENT TYPES OF TISSUES.
JUVENILE POLYPS ARE MALFORMATIONS OF EPITHELIUM AND LAMINA PROPRIA COMMONLY LOCATED IN THE
RECTUM. IT IS SEEN IN CHILDREN <5 YEARS OF AGE. THE TYPICAL PRESENTATION IS PAINLESS RECTAL
BLEEDING. SOMETIMES, THERE MAY BE A PROLIFERATING RECTAL MASS.
THE DISEASE MAY BE SPORADIC OR SYNDROMIC.
- SPORADIC JUVENILE POLYP OCCURS AS A SINGLE MASS AND IS CALLED A RETENTION POLYP.
- JUVENILE POLYPOSIS SYNDROME IS CHARACTERIZED BY MULTIPLE HAMARTOMATOUS POLYPS, WHICH MAY BE
PREMALIGNANT.
MORPHOLOGICALLY, BOTH OF THESE TYPES ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE.
- GROSS APPEARANCE: THEY APPEAR AS PEDUNCULATED, SMOOTH REDDISH LESIONS, AND WITH CYSTIC SPACES.
- MICROSCOPIC APPEARANCE: THE CYSTS APPEAR AS DILATED GLANDS FILLED WITH MUCIN AND INFLAMMATORY
DEBRIS.
ADENOMA: ADENOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS THAT ARISE FROM GLANDULAR TISSUE. WHILE THEY MAY PRESENT
WITH RECTAL BLEEDING, THEY ARE NOT COMMONLY SEEN IN YOUNG CHILDREN AND ARE NOT TYPICALLY
PEDUNCULATED LIKE JUVENILE POLYPS.
5064
CHORISTOMA: CHORISTOMAS ARE NON-NEOPLASTIC MASSES THAT ARISE FROM HETEROTOPIC TISSUE, I.E., TISSUES
FOUND IN ABNORMAL LOCATIONS. THEY ARE NOT ASSOCIATED WITH JUVENILE POLYPS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A patient with varicose veins reports eczema over the same region. Specify the stage of
the clinical classification according to the CEAP guidelines. CEAP-Clinical-Aetiology-Anatomy- Pathophysiology classification of chronic venous disorders
questions.explanation:
A PATIENT WITH VARICOSE VEINS AND OVERLYING ECZEMA IS CLASSIFIED AS C4A UNDER CEAP GUIDELINES.
THE CLINICAL-ETIOLOGY-ANATOMY-PATHOPHYSIOLOGY (CEAP) CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM IS USED TO CLASSIFY
CHRONIC LOWER EXTREMITY VENOUS DISEASE.
THE CLINICAL CLASS OF C4 UNDER CEAP INCLUDES CHANGES IN SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE SECONDARY
TO CHRONIC VENOUS DISEASE. IT IS FURTHER CLASSIFIED AS FOLLOWS:
- C4A - PIGMENTATION OR ECZEMA
- C4B - LIPODERMATOSCLEROSIS OR ATROPHIE BLANCHE
- C4C - CORONA PHLEBECTATICA
IMAGE A SHOWS TORTUOUS DILATED VEINS - C2, IMAGE B SHOWS ATROPHIE BLANCHE - C4B, AND IMAGE C
SHOWS FAN-SHAPED TELANGIECTASIA - C4C.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT COMES TO THE CASUALTY WITH A SEVERE HEADACHE. HIS BP WAS FOUND TO BE 160/100
MMHG. CT SCAN SHOWED A SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE. SPECIFY THE NEXT BEST STEP IN THE
MANAGEMENT OF THIS PATIENT.
questions.explanation:
IN THIS PATIENT WITH SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE (SAH), THE NEXT STEP IS TO DO AN ANGIOGRAPHY TO SEE
THE VASCULAR ANATOMY AND IDENTIFY THE SITE OF BLEED.
TRAUMA IS THE COMMONEST CAUSE OF SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE. SPONTANEOUS SAH USUALLY RESULTS
FROM THE RUPTURE OF AN ANEURYSM OR AN ARTERIO-VENOUS MALFORMATION (AVM). PATIENTS PRESENT WITH
A SUDDEN AND SEVERE HEADACHE WHICH IS DIFFERENT FROM ANY HEADACHE THEY HAVE EXPERIENCED BEFORE.
THIS IS DESCRIBED AS A THUNDERCLAP HEADACHE. OTHER SYMPTOMS INCLUDE MENINGITIC FEATURES LIKE
NECK RIGIDITY AND PHOTOPHOBIA, IMPAIRED CONSCIOUSNESS, INTRAOCULAR HEMORRHAGES, WITH OR WITHOUT
FOCAL NEUROLOGICAL DEFICITS. COMPRESSION FROM A POSTERIOR COMMUNICATING ARTERY ANEURYSM WOULD
RESULT IN THIRD NERVE PALSY.
NON-CONTRAST CT HEAD IS THE FIRST IMAGING TO BE DONE IN A SUSPECTED CASE, WHICH WOULD CONFIRM
BLEEDING IN MORE THAN 98% OF CASES. IN PATIENTS WITH HIGH SUSPICION AND A NEGATIVE CT, LUMBAR
PUNCTURE IS DONE TO DETECT HEMOGLOBIN BREAKDOWN PRODUCTS LIKE OXYHEMOGLOBIN AND BILIRUBIN.
AFTER CONFIRMING THE DIAGNOSIS, CT OR MR ANGIOGRAPHY IS DONE TO LOCATE THE ANEURYSMS OR AVM.
DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY REMAINS THE GOLD STANDARD INVESTIGATION.
THE DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT OF SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE (SAH) IS DONE SURGICALLY BY CRANIOTOMY
AND CLIPPING OR BY ENDOVASCULAR EMBOLIZATION KNOWN AS COILING. THIS PREVENTS REBLEEDING OF THE
ANEURYSM.
PATIENTS WITH SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE ARE AT RISK OF DEVELOPING COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS
REBLEEDING, CEREBRAL VASOSPASM, HYDROCEPHALUS, SEIZURES, AND HYPONATREMIA. EARLY RECOGNITION
AND MANAGEMENT OF THESE COMPLICATIONS ARE ESSENTIAL TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO SURGERY
AND NIMODIPINE, OTHER MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR SAH INCLUDE STRICT BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL,
ANALGESIA FOR HEADACHE, ANTIEMETICS, AND ANTICONVULSANTS IF SEIZURES OCCUR. MAINTAINING A CLOSE
MONITORING OF THE PATIENT'S NEUROLOGICAL STATUS, INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE, AND ELECTROLYTES IS ALSO
CRUCIAL.
OTHER OPTIONS
5068
NIMODIPINE: ALTHOUGH IT IS USED TO PREVENT CEREBRAL VASOSPASM AND DELAYED ISCHEMIC NEUROLOGICAL
DEFICITS, IT IS NOT THE IMMEDIATE NEXT STEP IN THE MANAGEMENT OF SAH. ANGIOGRAPHY IS NEEDED FIRST
TO LOCATE THE ANEURYSMS OR AVM. IT IS ADMINISTERED AFTER THE PROCEDURE.
SURGERY: ALTHOUGH SURGERY IS AN IMPORTANT MANAGEMENT OPTION FOR SAH, IT IS NOT THE IMMEDIATE
NEXT STEP. ANGIOGRAPHY MUST BE DONE FIRST TO IDENTIFY THE SITE OF THE BLEED AND PLAN FOR THE
APPROPRIATE SURGICAL OR ENDOVASCULAR INTERVENTION.
FIBRINOLYTIC THERAPY: THIS OPTION IS NOT APPROPRIATE FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF SAH AS IT MAY
EXACERBATE THE BLEEDING. FIBRINOLYTIC THERAPY IS USED IN THE TREATMENT OF ISCHEMIC STROKE, NOT
HEMORRHAGIC STROKE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 20-YEAR-OLD FEMALE PATIENT CONSUMED A CLEANING PRODUCT CONTAINING 90% SODIUM
HYDROXIDE. SHE IS HAVING COMPLETE DYSPHAGIA. SPECIFY THE BEST STEP IN MANAGEMENT.
questions.explanation:
THIS PATIENT WITH A CORROSIVE ESOPHAGEAL INJURY WITH COMPLETE DYSPHAGIA REQUIRES A FEEDING
JEJUNOSTOMY FOR ENTERAL FEEDING.
THE INJURY CAUSED BY ALKALI INGESTION IS DEEPER DUE TO THE PROCESS OF SAPONIFICATION OF FATS AND
DEHYDRATION. THE INJURY CAUSED BY ACIDS IS MORE SUPERFICIAL BECAUSE THEY CAUSE COAGULATIVE
NECROSIS WITH ESCHAR FORMATION, WHICH PREVENTS THE DEEPER PENETRATION OF THE ACID.
SEVERE CORROSIVE INJURY MAY LEAD TO ESOPHAGEAL PERFORATION, BLEEDING, STRICTURE, AND DEATH.
PATIENTS CAN DEVELOP DYSPHAGIA OR ODYNOPHAGIA, WHICH IMPLIES ESOPHAGAL DAMAGE.
MINOR INJURIES CAUSE MUCOSAL EDEMA THAT RESOLVES RAPIDLY WITH NO LATE SEQUELAE AND THESE PATIENTS
CAN BE SAFELY FED. IN CASE OF SEVERE INJURIES, A FEEDING JEJUNOSTOMY MAY BE APPROPRIATE UNTIL THE
PATIENT CAN SWALLOW SALIVA SATISFACTORILY.
MANAGEMENT OF CORROSIVE ESOPHAGITIS:
- HEMODYNAMIC STABILIZATION AND MANAGEMENT OF PATIENT'S AIRWAY
- ENDOSCOPIC EVALUATION OF INJURIES
- SURGICAL MANAGEMENT INCLUDES LAPAROTOMY FOR BLEEDING OR PERFORATION. ESOPHAGEAL REPLACEMENT
IS DONE FOR VERY LONG OR MULTIPLE STRICTURES.
STENTING IS USED IN PATIENTS WHO DO NOT RESPOND TO REPEATED DILATATIONS FOR ESOPHAGEAL STRICTURES.
THEY ARE NOT USED AS A TREATMENT IN ACUTE SETTINGS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 23-YEAR-OLD MALE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH MIDLINE SWELLING IN THE NECK. THE SWELLING MOVES
WITH DEGLUTITION AND PROTRUSION OF THE TONGUE. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF A THYROGLOSSAL CYST. IT MOVES WITH DEGLUTITION,
PROTRUSION OF THE TONGUE, AND SIDE-TO-SIDE MOVEMENT IS ALSO POSSIBLE.
A THYROGLOSSAL DUCT CYST IS A CONGENITAL MIDLINE NECK SWELLING THAT TYPICALLY PRESENTS DURING
CHILDHOOD OFTEN NOTICED AFTER AN UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION.
A THYROGLOSSAL CYST REPRESENTS THE PERSISTENCE OF THE TRACK OF THE THYROID GLAND AND CAN BE FOUND
ADJACENT TO THE MIDLINE. THE THYROID GLAND DESCENDS EARLY IN FETAL LIFE FROM THE BASE OF THE TONGUE
TOWARDS ITS POSITION IN THE LOWER NECK. AT THE TIME OF DESCENT, THE HYOID BONE HAS NOT BEEN FORMED
5069
AND THE TRACK OF THE THYROID GLAND IS VARIABLE, PASSING IN FRONT, THROUGH, OR BEHIND THE EVENTUAL
POSITION OF THE HYOID BODY.
IT CAN OCCUR ANYWHERE ALONG THE MIGRATORY COURSE OF THE DUCT:
- INFRAHYOID (MOST COMMON SITE)
- REGION OF THYROID CARTILAGE
- SUPRAHYOID
- FLOOR OF MOUTH
- BENEATH FORAMEN CECUM
CLINICAL FEATURES OF THYROGLOSSAL CYST:
- CLASSICALLY THE CYST MOVES UPWARDS ON SWALLOWING AND ON TONGUE PROTRUSION. THIS INDICATES
ATTACHMENT TO THE HYOID BONE.
- SWELLING IS SMOOTH, SOFT, FLUCTUANT (CYSTIC), NONTENDER, MOBILE, AND SHOWS TRANSILLUMINATION.
- THYROID FOSSA IS EMPTY, IF THERE IS NO THYROID IN THE NORMAL LOCATION.
COMPLICATIONS OF THYROGLOSSAL CYST:
- THE MOST COMMON COMPLICATION IS INFECTION.
- THYROGLOSSAL FISTULA IS AN ACQUIRED CONDITION THAT EITHER FOLLOWS INFECTION OF THE CYST WHICH BURSTS
OPEN OR DUE TO INADEQUATE REMOVAL OF THE CYST.
- 1% OF THYROGLOSSAL DUCT CYSTS ARE FOUND TO BE MALIGNANT OF WHICH THE MOST COMMON TYPE
OF CANCER IS PAPILLARY (85%).
HOWEVER, ONLY THE THYROGLOSSAL CYST MOVES WITH TONGUE PROTRUSION. THIS IS BECAUSE THE DUCT
EXTENDS FROM THE FORAMEN CECUM OF THE TONGUE TO THE ISTHMUS OF THE GLAND.
SISTRUNK’S OPERATION IS PERFORMED TO EXCISE THE CYST AND PREVENT A RECURRENCE. IT
INVOLVES EXCISION OF THE WHOLE THYROGLOSSAL TRACT, INVOLVING REMOVAL OF THE BODY OF THE HYOID BONE,
AND SUPRAHYOID TRACT THROUGH THE TONGUE BASE TO THE VALLECULA AT THE SITE OF THE PRIMITIVE FORAMEN
CECUM ALONG WITH THE CORE OF TISSUE ON EITHER SIDE.
FEATURES OF HOARSENESS OF VOICE, COUGH, NECK SWELLING THAT INCREASES IN SIZE ON COUGHING/VALSALVA
MANEUVER, AND A GURGLING SOUND HEARD ON PRESSING THE SWELLING ARE SUGGESTIVE OF LARYNGOCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 54-YEAR-OLD WOMAN PRESENTS WITH CERVICAL CANCER STAGE 2A. IT IS DECIDED TO GIVE NEOADJUVANT
CHEMOTHERAPY. WHAT DOES NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY MEAN?
options: CHEMOTHERAPY GIVEN BEFORE RADICAL SURGERY TO REDUCE BULK OF TUMOR
CHEMOTHERAPY GIVEN AFTER RADICAL SURGERY FOR MICROMETASTASES
questions.answer: CHEMOTHERAPY GIVEN BEFORE RADICAL SURGERY TO REDUCE BULK OF TUMOR
questions.explanation:
NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY IS DEFINED AS CHEMOTHERAPY GIVEN BEFORE THE DEFINITIVE TREATMENT
(USUALLY SURGERY) TO REDUCE THE BULK OF THE TUMOR.
NEOADJUVANT THERAPY IS A TYPE OF INDUCTION THERAPY THAT IS GIVEN BEFORE THE DEFINITIVE SURGERY
TO DOWNSTAGE THE TUMOR, REDUCE THE MORBIDITY OF TREATMENT, KNOW THE IN VIVO RESPONSE OF THE
TUMOR TO THERAPY, AND INCREASE ITS CHANCES OF SUCCESS. CHEMOTHERAPY, RADIOTHERAPY, OR HORMONAL
THERAPY CAN BE GIVEN AS NEOADJUVANT THERAPY.
OPTION A: TREATMENT THAT INVOLVES THE ADMINISTRATION OF CHEMOTHERAPY ALONG WITH RADIATION IS
CALLED CHEMORADIATION.
5070
OPTION B: HYPERTHERMIC INTRAPERITONEAL CHEMOTHERAPY (HIPEC) IS USED DURING SURGERY IN WHICH A
HYPERTHERMIC SOLUTION OF ANTICANCER DRUGS IS INFUSED DIRECTLY INTO THE ABDOMINAL CAVITY AFTER THE
DEFINITIVE SURGERY TO KILL ANY RESIDUAL TUMOR CELLS. IT IS OFTEN USED TO TREAT CANCERS THAT HAVE SPREAD
TO THE PERITONEUM.
OPTION D: TREATMENT GIVEN AFTER SURGICAL RESECTION OF THE TUMOR TO REDUCE THE RISK OF RECURRENCE
AND MICROMETASTASIS IS CALLED ADJUVANT THERAPY. ADJUVANT THERAPY CAN BE CHEMOTHERAPY, RADIATION
THERAPY, HORMONE THERAPY, TARGETED THERAPY, OR BIOLOGICAL THERAPY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A YOUNG PATIENT IS ADMITTED WITH A HISTORY OF FEVER FOR 5 DAYS. BP IS 90/60 MMHG, PR-120
BPM, RR-24 BREATHS/MIN, GCS SCORE-10; LABORATORY TESTS SHOW LEUCOCYTOSIS WITH NEUTROPHILIA
AND SERUM CREATININE LEVEL OF 2.6 MG/DL. AN INTERN DOCTOR WANTS TO CALCULATE THE QSOFA SCORE
TO PREDICT PROGNOSIS AND HOSPITALIZATION DURATION. WHICH OF THESE COMPRISES THE
QSOFA SCORE?
questions.explanation:
QSOFA SCORE COMPRISES OF SBP, RR, AND GCS.
QSOFA SCORE (QUICKSOFA) IS A BEDSIDE PROMPT THAT MAY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED INFECTION
WHO ARE AT GREATER RISK FOR A POOR OUTCOME OUTSIDE THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU).
IT USES THREE CRITERIA, ASSIGNING ONE POINT EACH FOR
- LOW BLOOD PRESSURE (SBP≤100 MMHG),
- HIGH RESPIRATORY RATE (≥22 BREATHS/MIN),
- ALTERED MENTATION (GCS SCORE, <15).
THE SCORE RANGES FROM 0 TO 3 POINTS. THE PRESENCE OF 2 OR MORE QSOFA POINTS IS A SIMPLE PROMPT
TO IDENTIFY INFECTED PATIENTS OUTSIDE THE ICU WHO ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP SEPSIS. THIS IS A SIMPLIFIED
DERIVATIVE OF SOFA SCORE. THE PRIMARY METHOD TO EVALUATE THE RISK OF ORGAN DYSFUNCTION (SEPSIS) IN
PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED INFECTION IS BY DETERMINING THE SEQUENTIAL (SEPSIS-RELATED) ORGAN FAILURE
ASSESSMENT (SOFA) SCORE, WHICH INCLUDES ASSESSMENT OF:
- CIRCULATION - SYSTOLIC BP AND NEED FOR VASOPRESSORS; PLATELET COUNT
- RESPIRATION - PAO2/FIO2 AND NEED FOR MECHANICAL VENTILATION
- MENTATION - GLASGOW COMA SCALE SCORE
- HEPATIC FUNCTION - BILIRUBIN LEVEL
- RENAL FUNCTION - CREATININE LEVEL
ORGAN DYSFUNCTION IS DEFINED BY A SOFA SCORE OF ≥2.
THE SOFA SCORE IS LIMITED BY ITS REQUIREMENT OF MULTIPLE LABORATORY TESTS WHICH MAKES IT COMPLEX
AND TIME-CONSUMING. IN ORDER TO SIMPLIFY THE SCORING PROCESS, THE "SEPSIS - 3" TASK FORCE
RECOMMENDED THE QUICK SEPSIS-RELATED ORGAN DYSFUNCTION ASSESSMENT "QSOFA" SCORE.
SOFA VS. QSOFA:
- SOFA IS A MORE COMPREHENSIVE AND ACCURATE SCORING SYSTEM, WHICH IS PARTICULARLY SUPERIOR
TO QSOFA IN THE ICU SETTING.
- QSOFA IS A SIMPLIFIED DERIVATIVE OF SOFA FOR BEDSIDE ASSESSMENT OF INDIVIDUALS AT RISK FOR
SEPSIS, PARTICULARLY USEFUL OUTSIDE THE ICU SETTING (I.E. WARD/EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT). HOWEVER,
NOTE THAT IT WAS ORIGINALLY DESIGNED AS A PREDICTIVE TOOL THAT CALCULATES THE RISK OF DEATH FROM SEPSIS
RATHER THAN A DIAGNOSTIC TOOL.
5071
THEREBY, THE BEST DESCRIPTION OF SEPSIS BASED ON "SEPSIS-3" TASK FORCE RECOMMENDATIONS WOULD BE
AS FOLLOWS:
- SUSPECTED OR DOCUMENTED INFECTION WITH SOFA SCORE OF ≥2 OR
- SUSPECTED OR DOCUMENTED INFECTION WITH QSOFA SCORE OF ≥2
ANOTHER SCORE THAT HAS BEEN USED IS THE NATIONAL EARLY WARNING SCORE (NEWS). IT RANGES FROM 0
TO 20 AND IS BASED ON RESPIRATORY RATE, OXYGEN SATURATION, USE OF SUPPLEMENTAL O2, TEMPERATURE,
SYSTOLIC BLOOD PRESSURE, PULSE RATE, AND LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS. ≥5 OUT OF 20 IS CONSIDERED A
POSITIVE SCORE.
OTHER SCORING SYSTEMS FOR SEPSIS:
THE SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE SYNDROME (SIRS) SCORE IS NO LONGER RECOMMENDED AS IS IT
NOT SPECIFIC TO INFECTION.
THE LOGISTIC ORGAN DYSFUNCTION SYSTEM (LODS) SCORE IS NOT RECOMMENDED AS IT IS COMPLEX AND
HAS TOO MANY VARIABLES.
5072

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE ARE EXTRA-ESOPHAGEAL COMPLICATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH GERD?
questions.explanation:
Source note: The source PDF omits the numbered statements or table referenced by this question.

ASTHMA, LARYNGITIS, PULMONARY FIBROSIS, AND COUGH ARE ALL EXTRA ESOPHAGEAL COMPLICATIONS IN
GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE(GERD)
EXTRAOESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOMS OF GERD ARE:
- CHRONIC COUGH
- LARYNGITIS,
- ASTHMA
- DENTAL EROSIONS (ESPECIALLY ON THE LINGUAL AND PALATAL TOOTH
SURFACES).
- PULMONARY FIBROSIS
- SINUSITIS
- PHARYNGITIS
- RECURRENT OTITIS MEDIA
EXTRAESOPHAGEAL SYMPTOMS OF GERD ORIGINATE FROM THE RESPIRATORY TRACT AND INCLUDE BOTH
LARYNGEAL AND PULMONARY ISSUES THESE SYMPTOMS CAN ARISE THROUGH TWO MECHANISMS. THE FIRST
AND MOST COMMON MECHANISM INVOLVES PROXIMAL ESOPHAGEAL REFLUX AND MICROASPIRATION OF
GASTRODUODENAL CONTENTS, WHICH CAUSE DIRECT INJURY TO THE LARYNX AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT. THE
SECOND MECHANISM INVOLVES DISTAL ESOPHAGEAL ACID EXPOSURE TRIGGERING A VAGAL NERVE REFLEX,
LEADING TO BRONCHOSPASM AND COUGH, DUE TO THE SHARED VAGAL INNERVATION OF THE TRACHEA AND
ESOPHAGUS.
THE INCIDENCE OF BARRETT'S ESOPHAGUS IS ALSO MORE IN PATIENTS WITH LONG TERM GERD, WHICH IN TURN
INCREASES THE RISK OF ADENOCARCINOMA OF ESOPHAGUS.

questions.prompt:
A 23-YEAR-OLD FEMALE REPORTED NECK SWELLING, DIFFICULTY SWALLOWING, AND

questions.prompt: A 32-year-old male is brought to the emergency department following a high-speed vehicular collision. He has a heart rate of 126 bpm, blood pressure of 88/62 mmHg, respiratory rate of 34/min, and hourly urine output of 12 mL/hr. He appears anxious and confused. According to standard trauma life support hemorrhage classification, what class of hemorrhagic shock is present?
questions.explanation: Class III hemorrhagic shock represents an acute circulating volume loss of 30–40% (1500–2000 mL in a 70-kg adult). It is clinically demarcated by marked tachycardia (HR > 120 bpm), hypotension (< 90 mmHg systolic), tachypnea (RR 30–40/min), significant oliguria (5–15 mL/hr), and mental status changes including marked anxiety and confusion.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance

questions.prompt: During massive transfusion for a patient with traumatic hemoperitoneum, diffuse microvascular oozing develops across all raw peritoneal surfaces. Core body temperature is 34.6°C, arterial pH is 7.20, and base deficit is -9 mEq/L. Which pathophysiological triad is present, and what is the mandatory immediate surgical strategy?
options: Triad of Virchow; proceed with definitive anatomical visceral resection
Lethal triad of trauma; abort definitive surgery and initiate Damage Control Surgery
Beck's triad; perform urgent transdiaphragmatic pericardiotomy
Charcot's triad; initiate urgent intraoperative biliary exploration
questions.answer: Lethal triad of trauma; abort definitive surgery and initiate Damage Control Surgery
questions.explanation: The lethal triad of trauma comprises hypothermia (< 35°C), progressive metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.25), and dilutional/consumptive coagulopathy. Once this triad develops, prolonged anatomical reconstruction leads to near 100% mortality. The mandatory principle is Damage Control Surgery (DCS): rapid surgical control of hemorrhage and contamination, temporary abdominal closure (laparostomy), and urgent transfer to the ICU for rewarming and correction of acidosis and coagulopathy.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old polytrauma patient receives 12 units of packed red blood cells over 3 hours. On continuous ECG monitoring, widening of the QRS complex, prolonged PR interval, and tall, peaked, tented T waves appear. Serum potassium is 6.8 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate first-line drug to stabilize the myocardial membrane against life-threatening arrhythmias?
options: 10% Calcium gluconate 10 mL IV over 3–5 minutes
Regular insulin 10 units with 50 mL 50% dextrose
questions.answer: 10% Calcium gluconate 10 mL IV over 3–5 minutes
questions.explanation: In acute severe hyperkalemia with cardiotoxicity (tall peaked T waves, widened QRS, prolonged PR), the immediate priority is cardioprotection. Intravenous calcium gluconate (10 mL of 10% solution administered over 3–5 minutes) antagonizes the membrane actions of hyperkalemia and restores myocardial resting membrane threshold potential without shifting serum potassium levels.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: A 56-year-old male with persistent vomiting from gastric outlet obstruction presents with severe lethargy and muscular cramps. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.54, pCO2 48 mmHg, serum sodium 132 mEq/L, potassium 2.8 mEq/L, and chloride 84 mEq/L. Urinary pH is unexpectedly measured at 5.4. What explains this paradoxical aciduria?
options: Renal tubular acidosis type I with failure of hydrogen ion excretion in the distal tubule
Preferential distal renal tubular secretion of H+ in exchange for Na+ from hypokalemia
Lactic acidosis secondary to volume depletion overwhelming urinary bicarbonate buffers
Excessive respiratory compensation with secondary proximal tubular bicarbonate retention
questions.answer: Preferential distal renal tubular secretion of H+ in exchange for Na+ from hypokalemia
questions.explanation: Gastric outlet obstruction leads to loss of HCl and water, causing hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis. As volume contraction activates aldosterone, the distal tubule attempts to reabsorb sodium. Because potassium is severely depleted, hydrogen ions are secreted in exchange for sodium instead of potassium, resulting in the excretion of acidic urine despite systemic metabolic alkalosis (paradoxical aciduria).
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance

questions.prompt: A 68-year-old female in the surgical ICU on postoperative day 3 following Hartmann's procedure for ruptured diverticulitis develops septic shock. Mean arterial pressure is 52 mmHg despite an initial 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus. Which vasopressor is the first-line agent of choice to restore organ perfusion?
questions.explanation: In septic shock refractory to fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor of choice. It acts predominantly as a potent alpha-1 adrenergic agonist with modest beta-1 inotropic properties, effectively increasing systemic vascular resistance and mean arterial pressure with significantly lower tachyarrhythmic potential compared to dopamine.

questions.prompt: In evaluating an unconscious adult polytrauma patient in shock, which clinical endpoint best reflects adequate cellular and end-organ microcirculatory perfusion during fluid resuscitation?
options: Systolic blood pressure maintained strictly above 140 mmHg at all times
Hourly urine output of at least 0.5 mL/kg/hr with clearance of serum lactate
Central venous pressure elevated to between 18 and 20 cm of water
Rapid restoration of circulating peripheral venous hematocrit above 45%
questions.answer: Hourly urine output of at least 0.5 mL/kg/hr with clearance of serum lactate
questions.explanation: Urine output (minimum 0.5 mL/kg/hr in adults, 1 mL/kg/hr in children) provides a direct, non-invasive indicator of renal and visceral microcirculatory perfusion. In conjunction with serial serum lactate clearance and base deficit normalization, it confirms the restoration of tissue oxygen delivery and aerobic metabolism.

questions.prompt: A 22-year-old male sustains a stab wound to the left anterior chest. He is restless with BP 78/50 mmHg, pulse 134 bpm, and elevated jugular venous pressure. Breath sounds are equal bilaterally on chest auscultation, and the trachea is central. Heart sounds are muffled. What is the immediate definitive emergency bedside intervention?
options: Left tube thoracostomy placed in the fifth intercostal space anteriorly
Subxiphoid pericardiocentesis or immediate emergency thoracotomy
High-pressure positive ventilation with 100% oxygen via bag-valve-mask
Rapid intravenous infusion of 2 L of 5% dextrose over ten minutes
questions.answer: Subxiphoid pericardiocentesis or immediate emergency thoracotomy
questions.explanation: Beck's triad (hypotension, raised jugular venous pressure, and muffled heart sounds) in penetrating thoracic trauma with equal bilateral breath sounds and midline trachea is diagnostic of acute cardiac tamponade. The immediate decompression of pericardial blood via ultrasound-guided subxiphoid pericardiocentesis or anterolateral emergency thoracotomy restores venous return and cardiac output.

questions.prompt: During total parenteral nutrition (TPN) administration via a subclavian central catheter in a malnourished postoperative patient with enterocutaneous fistula, which electrolyte abnormality is characteristic of refeeding syndrome and carries high risk of fatal cardiac arrest?
questions.explanation: Refeeding syndrome occurs when carbohydrate-rich nutrition stimulates endogenous insulin release in a starved patient. Insulin drives glucose, phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells for glycolysis. This leads to profound acute extracellular hypophosphatemia, triggering adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, diaphragmatic weakness, hemolytic anemia, and lethal cardiac arrhythmias.

questions.prompt: A 60-kg adult male is placed on nil-by-mouth following an uneventful open appendectomy. In calculating his daily baseline maintenance fluid and electrolyte requirements, which prescription is physiologically accurate?
options: 1000 mL water, 20 mmol sodium, 10 mmol potassium daily
2000-2500 mL water, 60-120 mmol sodium, 40-60 mmol potassium daily
4000-5000 mL water, 250 mmol sodium, 150 mmol potassium daily
3000 mL water with zero electrolytes for the first 72 hours
questions.answer: 2000-2500 mL water, 60-120 mmol sodium, 40-60 mmol potassium daily
questions.explanation: Basal maintenance requirements in an adult are: Water: 30–35 mL/kg/day (approximately 2000–2500 mL for a 60–70 kg adult); Sodium: 1–2 mmol/kg/day (60–120 mmol/day); Potassium: 0.5–1 mmol/kg/day (40–60 mmol/day). Potassium is safely commenced once adequate urine output (> 0.5 mL/kg/hr) is confirmed postoperatively.

questions.prompt: A 54-year-old male with decompensated liver cirrhosis and severe ascites develops sudden hematemesis from ruptured esophageal varices. Terlipressin is administered. In transfusing blood products, what is the target hemoglobin level recommended to avoid worsening portal venous pressure and re-bleeding?
options: Target hemoglobin of greater than 15 g/dL
questions.explanation: In acute variceal hemorrhage, a restrictive transfusion strategy targeting a hemoglobin of 7–8 g/dL is standard. Overzealous transfusion raises central venous pressure and portal venous pressure, dislodging fresh hemostatic clots at the variceal rupture site and significantly increasing re-bleeding rates and mortality.

questions.prompt: A 30-year-old male weighing 70 kg sustains full-thickness flame burns covering his entire anterior trunk, entire right upper limb, and anterior aspect of both lower limbs. According to Wallace's Rule of Nines, what is the total percentage of body surface area burned?
questions.explanation: According to Wallace's Rule of Nines: Anterior trunk = 18%; Entire right upper limb = 9%; Anterior aspect of both lower limbs = 9% each (18% total). Total Body Surface Area (TBSA) burned = 18 + 9 + 18 = 45%.

questions.prompt: For the 70-kg patient with 45% TBSA thermal burn, calculate the total fluid requirement in the first 24 hours using the Parkland formula, and determine the volume to be infused over the first 8 hours post-injury.
options: Total 6,300 mL; infuse 3,150 mL in the first 8 hours
Total 12,600 mL; infuse 6,300 mL in the first 8 hours
Total 15,400 mL; infuse 7,700 mL in the first 8 hours
Total 8,400 mL; infuse 4,200 mL in the first 8 hours
questions.answer: Total 12,600 mL; infuse 6,300 mL in the first 8 hours
questions.explanation: The Parkland formula dictates: 4 mL × Body weight in kg × % TBSA burn. Here: 4 mL × 70 kg × 45 = 12,600 mL of Ringer's lactate in the first 24 hours. Half of this total volume (6,300 mL) must be infused within the first 8 hours calculated from the exact time of burn injury, and the remaining half (6,300 mL) is infused over the subsequent 16 hours.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance

questions.prompt: A 40-year-old male sustains full-thickness circumferential burns to the right forearm. Four hours later, he complains of severe deep aching pain, paresthesias in the fingers, and progressive loss of radial pulse. Compartment pressures measure 38 mmHg. What is the urgent operative intervention?
options: Intravenous administration of high-dose mannitol without surgical release
Emergency bedside escharotomy along mid-lateral and mid-medial lines
Circumferential application of tight compressive elastic crepe bandaging
Immediate split-thickness skin autografting over the unreleased burn wound
questions.answer: Emergency bedside escharotomy along mid-lateral and mid-medial lines
questions.explanation: Circumferential full-thickness burns form an inelastic, rigid eschar. As post-burn tissue edema develops beneath the eschar, interstitial compartment pressures rise rapidly, impairing arteriolar flow and inducing compartment syndrome. Emergency escharotomy involves incising the full depth of the non-elastic burned dermis into subcutaneous fat along mid-axial neutral lines without breaching the deep muscular fascia.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance

questions.prompt: Which topical antimicrobial agent used in extensive thermal burns is known to penetrate thick eschar effectively, making it useful in infected burn wounds and auricular burns, but carries the specific adverse effect of severe burning pain and metabolic acidosis from carbonic anhydrase inhibition?
questions.explanation: Mafenide acetate diffuses rapidly through avascular eschar, making it effective for deep bacterial colonization, suppurative chondritis of the ear, and electrical burns. Its major limitation is inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in renal tubules, leading to alkaline diuresis, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, compensatory hyperventilation, and marked local application pain.

questions.prompt: An unhealed burn scar on the anterior aspect of the lower leg of 24 years duration develops a proliferative, non-healing ulcer with raised, everted, indurated borders and foul-smelling discharge. Punch biopsy reveals well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. What is the eponym for this malignancy?
questions.explanation: Marjolin's ulcer is a malignant transformation—classically aggressive squamous cell carcinoma (rarely basal cell carcinoma or melanoma)—arising in chronic, non-healing burn scars, chronic venous ulcers, or sinus tracts of chronic osteomyelitis. Characterized by dense, avascular fibrous scar tissue, it exhibits late regional lymph node metastasis, but once metastasis occurs, the prognosis is poor.

questions.prompt: In Jackson's burn wound model of local thermal injury, which concentric zone represents tissue with reversible microvascular stasis that is salvageable with prompt and adequate fluid resuscitation?
questions.explanation: Jackson's burn wound model describes three concentric zones: 1. Zone of coagulation: innermost area of irreversible cellular death and protein denaturation; 2. Zone of stasis: middle zone of compromised perfusion, microvascular thrombosis, and stasis, which can either recover with optimal fluid resuscitation and wound care or progress to irreversible necrosis; 3. Zone of hyperemia: outermost zone of minimal injury and vasodilation that spontaneously recovers.

questions.prompt: A 28-year-old female presents with an unsightly, raised, erythematous, pruritic scar over her sternum 6 months after sternotomy. The lesion projects well beyond the original boundaries of the surgical incision and invades adjacent normal dermal margins. Histological examination shows thick, disorganized, hyalinized collagen bands. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Keloids characteristically extend beyond the confines of the original wound margin and invade surrounding normal tissue without spontaneous regression, occurring preferentially over presternal skin, deltoid, and ear lobes. Hypertrophic scars remain confined within the boundaries of the original incision, contain predominantly type III collagen parallel to the epidermis, and frequently regress over 1–2 years.

questions.prompt: A burn patient with extensive 50% TBSA burns on day 10 develops sudden epigastric pain, coffee-ground vomiting, and melena with dropping hemoglobin. Endoscopy reveals acute multiple superficial punctate ulcerations and mucosal erosions in the stomach and duodenum. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Curling's ulcer refers to acute stress ulceration of the gastric and duodenal mucosa arising as a severe complication of extensive thermal burn injury, mediated by splanchnic hypoperfusion, mucosal ischemia, and decreased mucosal barrier defenses. Cushing's ulcer, by contrast, is associated with elevated intracranial pressure or severe head trauma and is driven by vagal hyperstimulation causing gastric acid hypersecretion.

questions.prompt: Which phase of normal surgical wound healing is characterized by peak fibroblast proliferation, capillary endothelial sprouting, and conversion of type III collagen to robust type I collagen?
questions.explanation: The proliferative phase (days 4 to 21) encompasses angiogenesis, fibroplasia, granulation tissue formation, and epithelialization. Fibroblasts synthesize large quantities of ground substance and extracellular matrix (primarily type III collagen initially), laying the structural lattice for subsequent wound contraction and remodeling.

questions.prompt: An electrician suffers an entry electrical burn on his right hand and an exit wound on his right heel from a 11,000-volt power line. Despite minimal skin surface burns, his urine is dark reddish-brown. Urine dipstick is positive for blood, but microscopy shows no red blood cells. What is the urgent priority to prevent acute kidney injury?
options: Immediate emergent hemodialysis within one hour of hospital admission
Aggressive crystalloid resuscitation, urinary alkalinization, and mannitol
Strict fluid restriction to 500 mL daily to prevent acute pulmonary edema
Immediate emergent bilateral lower extremity fasciotomy prior to any intravenous fluids
questions.answer: Aggressive crystalloid resuscitation, urinary alkalinization, and mannitol
questions.explanation: High-voltage electrical injury generates massive internal resistance heating and deep muscular necrosis, releasing myoglobin into the circulation. In acidic urine, myoglobin precipitates as ferrihemate casts, causing acute tubular necrosis. Management requires higher fluid rates targeting urine output of 1.5–2.0 mL/kg/hr (75–100 mL/hr in adults), intravenous sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize urine (pH > 6.5) to keep myoglobin soluble, and osmotic diuresis with mannitol.

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old agricultural laborer sustains a deep laceration on his thigh contaminated with soil. Forty-eight hours later, he presents with excruciating disproportionate pain, tachycardia out of proportion to fever, a thin watery brownish discharge with a sweetish foul odor, and palpable soft tissue crepitus. Gram stain demonstrates large Gram-positive bacilli devoid of polymorphonuclear leukocytes. What is the definitive diagnosis and primary surgical management?

Clostridial gas gangrene requiring emergent radical surgical debridement and penicillin
Cutaneous erysipelas treated with oral erythromycin and warm compression dressings
Streptococcal toxic shock treated with intravenous immunoglobulin without surgery
questions.answer: Clostridial gas gangrene requiring emergent radical surgical debridement and penicillin
questions.explanation: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis, most commonly Clostridium perfringens) is a surgical emergency characterized by rapid spread, alpha-toxin (lecithinase) tissue destruction, gas production, and absence of inflammatory cells on smear. Emergency management hinges on radical debridement of dead muscle (which fails to contract, bleed, or exhibit normal turgor), high-dose crystalline penicillin G and clindamycin, and hyperbaric oxygen.

questions.prompt: According to the CDC surgical wound classification system, into which category is an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis classified when there is controlled entry into the bile duct with no gross bile spillage?
questions.explanation: Clean-contaminated wounds (Class II) are operative wounds in which a hollow viscus (respiratory, alimentary, genital, or urinary tract) is entered under controlled conditions without unusual contamination or gross spillage. Elective cholecystectomy, gastric surgery, and appendectomy without perforation fall into this category.

questions.prompt: A 58-year-old diabetic male presents with scrotal swelling, severe perineal pain, high-grade fever, and marked toxemia. Examination reveals rapidly spreading blackened skin necrosis, extensive crepitus extending from the scrotum into the perineum and lower abdominal wall, with foul-smelling dishwater pus. What is the diagnosis and urgent course of action?
options: Fournier gangrene requiring immediate wide surgical debridement and triple antibiotics
Scrotal carbuncle managed with outpatient oral antibiotics and warm sitz baths
Acute testicular torsion treated with emergency unilateral orchiectomy
Strangulated indirect inguinal hernia requiring immediate manual reduction by taxis
questions.answer: Fournier gangrene requiring immediate wide surgical debridement and triple antibiotics
questions.explanation: Fournier's gangrene is a necrotizing fasciitis of the perineal, genital, and perianal regions, typically polymicrobial (aerobic and anaerobic synergy) in immunocompromised or diabetic patients. It causes endarteritis obliterans of the subcutaneous vessels. Immediate intervention requires aggressive resuscitation, broad-spectrum coverage, and emergency radical surgical debridement back to healthy bleeding fascia.

questions.prompt: An unimmunized 35-year-old construction worker presents 8 days after stepping on a rusty nail with lockjaw (trismus), risus sardonicus, painful reflex muscular spasms triggered by acoustic and tactile stimuli, and opisthotonos. Sensorium is completely clear. What is the mechanism of action of the causative toxin?
options: Tetanospasmin retrogradely blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release in spinal cord
Tetanolysin causes direct lysis of postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors at endplates
Botulinum neurotoxin inhibits presynaptic vesicular release of acetylcholine
Alpha-toxin causes lecithinase-mediated cellular membrane disruption and cytolysis
questions.answer: Tetanospasmin retrogradely blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release in spinal cord
questions.explanation: Clostridium tetani elaborates tetanospasmin, an exotoxin that enters motor neuron terminals and travels via retrograde intra-axonal transport to inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells) in the spinal cord and brainstem. There, it cleaves synaptobrevin, preventing the presynaptic release of the inhibitory neurotransmitters glycine and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), leading to unregulated, continuous excitatory motor discharge and reflex tetanic spasms.

questions.prompt: What is the optimal timing for the administration of single-dose intravenous prophylactic antibiotics prior to elective clean-contaminated abdominal surgery to achieve peak bactericidal tissue concentrations at the time of skin incision?
options: Within 30 to 60 minutes prior to surgical incision
24 hours prior to surgery in the ward
Immediately after the skin has been closed at the end of surgery
At induction followed by mandatory continuation for 5 postoperative days
questions.answer: Within 30 to 60 minutes prior to surgical incision
questions.explanation: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis is intended to establish peak bactericidal drug concentration in the dermis and target tissues before incisional contamination occurs. Administering the agent within 30 to 60 minutes prior to skin incision (or 120 minutes for vancomycin/fluoroquinolones due to prolonged infusion times) optimizes tissue protection. Postoperative continuation beyond 24 hours provides no benefit and fosters antimicrobial resistance.
tags: Metabolic Response, Shock and Fluid Balance
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: A 42-year-old female presents with a solitary, firm, painless thyroid nodule in the right lobe measuring 2.5 cm. Ultrasound reveals microcalcifications, marked hypoechogenicity, irregular borders, and taller-than-wide dimensions. FNAC shows ground-glass nuclei with pseudoinclusions and longitudinal nuclear grooves. What is the diagnosis and the most common mode of metastasis?
options: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with early hematogenous spread to skeleton
Papillary thyroid carcinoma with lymphatic metastasis to cervical nodes
Medullary thyroid carcinoma with direct local infiltration of strap muscles
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma with rapid angioinvasion and lung metastasis
questions.answer: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with lymphatic metastasis to cervical nodes
questions.explanation: The cytological features (Orphan Annie eye ground-glass nuclei, nuclear pseudoinclusions, and longitudinal grooves) together with microcalcifications (psammoma bodies) are diagnostic of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). PTC is the most common thyroid malignancy (80–85%) and predominantly metastasizes via lymphatic pathways to ipsilateral and central compartment (Level VI) cervical lymph nodes.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: Why can fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) NOT reliably differentiate between a follicular thyroid adenoma and a follicular thyroid carcinoma?
options: FNAC cannot assess cellular atypia or nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio
Distinction requires architectural demonstration of capsular invasion and/or vascular invasion
Follicular thyroid carcinoma does not take up standard Papanicolaou stain
Thyroid follicles contain high colloid concentrations that dissolve cytological specimens
questions.answer: Distinction requires architectural demonstration of capsular invasion and/or vascular invasion
questions.explanation: Both follicular adenoma and follicular carcinoma present with identical cytological appearances of uniform microfollicles and crowded follicular epithelial cells. The definitive diagnosis of follicular carcinoma hinges exclusively on histopathological demonstration of transcapsular invasion (full-thickness penetration of the fibrous capsule) or angioinvasion (tumor cells invading veins in or beyond the capsule), which can only be determined on formal histological sectioning of the resected specimen.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: A 35-year-old male is diagnosed with medullary thyroid carcinoma. Serum calcitonin is markedly elevated. A family history of sudden death and hypertension is reported. Which mandatory preoperative investigation must be performed prior to thyroidectomy to prevent a lethal intraoperative hypertensive crisis?
options: Plasma or urinary metanephrines to exclude pheochromocytoma
Serum calcium and intact parathyroid hormone to exclude hyperparathyroidism
Contrast CT scan of the abdomen to exclude primary adrenocortical carcinoma
Serum calcitonin doubling time to determine the risk of pulmonary metastasis
questions.answer: Plasma or urinary metanephrines to exclude pheochromocytoma
questions.explanation: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) originates from parafollicular C cells and can occur as part of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) 2A or 2B, both caused by germline RET proto-oncogene mutations. Because pheochromocytoma may coexist, all MTC patients must be screened with 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines/plasma metanephrines. If a pheochromocytoma is present, it must always be resected first before neck surgery to avoid fatal hypertensive crisis during anesthesia and neck exploration.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: During total thyroidectomy, ligating the superior thyroid vessels close to the upper pole of the gland protects which specific nerve, and what clinical impairment occurs if this nerve is inadvertently injured?
options: Recurrent laryngeal nerve causing complete ipsilateral vocal cord paralysis
External branch of superior laryngeal nerve causing loss of high pitch
Internal branch of superior laryngeal nerve causing complete loss of cough reflex
Cervical sympathetic trunk causing Horner syndrome with ptosis and miosis
questions.answer: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve causing loss of high pitch
questions.explanation: The superior thyroid artery runs in close proximity to the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (EBSLN). To safeguard this nerve, the superior vascular pedicle must be ligated individually right on the capsule at the apex of the superior thyroid pole. Injury to the EBSLN paralyzes the cricothyroid muscle (the chief tensor of the vocal fold), causing loss of high-frequency voice range, voice fatigue, and weakness of projection.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: Four hours after an uncomplicated total thyroidectomy, a patient develops sudden severe respiratory distress, stridor, and a rapidly expanding tense swelling deep to the neck incision. What is the immediate life-saving bedside action?
options: Immediate intravenous injection of 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate over ten minutes
Immediate bedside removal of sutures and evacuation of the hematoma
Endotracheal reintubation under continuous sedation in the intensive care unit
Emergency transfer to the radiology suite for ultrasound-guided needle aspiration
questions.answer: Immediate bedside removal of sutures and evacuation of the hematoma
questions.explanation: A postoperative tension hematoma deep to the investing layer of cervical fascia compresses venous drainage, causing rapid supraglottic laryngeal edema and acute airway obstruction. This is a surgical emergency. The surgeon or on-duty clinician must immediately open the wound at the bedside, cut all sutures, spread the strap muscles, and evacuate the clot to relieve venous compression, followed by transfer to the operating theater for definitive hemostasis.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: A 48-year-old female undergoes total thyroidectomy for high-risk papillary carcinoma. Six weeks postoperatively, she is scheduled for radioactive iodine (RAI, I-131) ablation. Which tumor marker is measured serially to detect persistent, recurrent, or metastatic disease during long-term follow-up?
options: Serum thyroid peroxidase and thyrotropin levels
questions.explanation: Following total thyroidectomy and radioiodine ablation, normal thyroid tissue is eliminated. In this setting, thyroglobulin (Tg) is an exquisitely sensitive tumor marker. Any detectable or rising serum Tg reflects persistent, recurrent, or metastatic thyroid carcinoma. Anti-Tg antibodies must always be measured simultaneously because their presence can falsely lower measured Tg levels.
questions.subject: General Surgery

questions.prompt: Which anatomical triangle or landmark provides the standard surgical trajectory to identify the recurrent laryngeal nerve during capsular dissection of the inferior thyroid pole?
questions.explanation: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is located in the tracheoesophageal groove, passing deep to or through the ligament of Berry and close to the branches of the inferior thyroid artery. Simon's triangle (bounded by the carotid sheath laterally, trachea/esophagus medially, and inferior thyroid artery superiorly) and Beahrs' landmark are classic surgical anatomical spaces used to identify and preserve the nerve.
questions.subject: General Surgery
