• Option A: Correct. The first letter 'S' stands for 'Sex' (specifically male sex, which carries a statistically higher lethality and completion rate for suicide).
• Option B: Incorrect. While psychosis contributes to the 'R' (Rational thinking loss), 'S' does not stand for schizophrenia.
• Option C: Incorrect. Lack of social support is represented by the second 'S' in PERSONS (Social supports lacking), not the initial 'S'.
• Option D: Incorrect. Substance/ethanol abuse is represented by the 'E' (Ethanol use) in SAD PERSONS.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: A 36-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by police after being found wandering naked in the street, yelling incoherently. In the emergency bay, he becomes acutely belligerent, exhibiting extraordinary physical strength, severe hyperthermia (41°C), tachypnea, profuse sweating, paranoia, and complete insensitivity to physical pain. Laboratory studies reveal severe metabolic acidosis and acute rhabdomyolysis. This presentation of 'Excited Delirium Syndrome' is most typically associated with acute intoxication by:
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Excited Delirium Syndrome (ExDS) is an extreme psychiatric/toxicological emergency characterized by agitated delirium, bizarre behavior, combativeness, superhuman physical strength, hyperthermia, metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, and sudden cardiorespiratory arrest. It is most commonly precipitated by severe psychostimulant intoxication (cocaine, methamphetamine, synthetic cathinones/'bath salts', or PCP) driving massive central dopamine and norepinephrine receptor overstimulation.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Psychostimulants such as synthetic cathinones ('bath salts'), methamphetamine, and cocaine precipitate hyperdopaminergic delirium, extreme agitation, hyperthermia, and fatal rhabdomyolysis/acidosis.
• Option B: Incorrect. Benzodiazepine intoxication causes CNS depression, sedation, ataxia, and respiratory depression, not hyperthermic excited delirium.
• Option C: Incorrect. Cannabis intoxication causes conjunctival injection, dry mouth, mild tachycardia, and relaxation or paranoia, but not excited delirium with lethal hyperthermia.
• Option D: Incorrect. Nitrous oxide causes euphoria, dissociation, and hypoxia; chronic use causes subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (B12 inactivation).

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Under the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 (MHCA 2017), what is an 'Advance Directive' in the context of psychiatric treatment?
options: Magistrate order commanding compulsory detention and involuntary medical intervention
Written document stating future treatment choices and nominated representative if capacity is lost
Hospital administrative directive mandating electroconvulsive therapy for uncooperative cases
Police warrant authorizing preventive psychiatric apprehension of homeless individuals
questions.answer: Written document stating future treatment choices and nominated representative if capacity is lost
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Under Chapter III (Sections 5–13) of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, every person who is not a minor has the legal right to execute an 'Advance Directive' in writing. This legal document specifies the manner in which they wish or do not wish to be cared for and treated for a mental illness, and enables them to appoint a 'Nominated Representative' to make decisions on their behalf during periods when they lack capacity to make mental healthcare decisions.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. An order issued by a magistrate for admission is a reception/court order, not an advance directive.
• Option B: Correct. An Advance Directive under MHCA 2017 is a written declaration by an adult specifying treatment preferences and appointing a nominated representative for times of diminished decision-making capacity.
• Option C: Incorrect. Advance directives are formulated by the individual/patient while competent, not unilaterally written by a treating psychiatrist.
• Option D: Incorrect. Police restraint powers are strictly governed by separate emergency procedures and do not constitute an advance directive.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Which landmark provision regarding suicide attempt in India was introduced under Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017?
options: Mandatory penal imprisonment of 1 year for any individual attempting suicide
Presumption of severe stress, decriminalizing suicide attempts with mandated rehabilitation
Immediate involuntary committal of suicide survivors to forensic psychiatric asylums
Imposition of heavy financial fines on legal heirs and immediate family members
questions.answer: Presumption of severe stress, decriminalizing suicide attempts with mandated rehabilitation
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, effectively decriminalized suicide attempts in India (which were previously punishable under Section 309 of the Indian Penal Code). The section creates a statutory presumption that any person who attempts to commit suicide shall be presumed, unless proven otherwise, to have been under severe stress at the time. It explicitly prohibits prosecution and places a statutory duty on the appropriate government to provide medical care, treatment, and rehabilitation.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. Section 309 of the IPC historically provided for up to 1 year of imprisonment; Section 115 of the MHCA 2017 was enacted specifically to abolish and prevent this penalization.
• Option B: Correct. Section 115 provides a legal presumption of severe stress, decriminalizing attempted suicide and mandating state-funded healthcare, support, and rehabilitation.
• Option C: Incorrect. Individuals who attempt suicide are treated in general healthcare settings and not subjected to forensic psychiatric confinement.
• Option D: Incorrect. There is no financial penalization of the family; rather, the government is obligated to support the individual.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Under Section 95 of the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, which of the following psychiatric procedures or practices is completely and unequivocally prohibited across all settings?
options: Modified Electroconvulsive Therapy in adult patients
Electroconvulsive Therapy without the use of muscle relaxants and anesthesia
Prescription of atypical antipsychotics to elderly patients
questions.answer: Electroconvulsive Therapy without the use of muscle relaxants and anesthesia
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Section 95(1) of the MHCA 2017 outlines explicit statutory prohibitions to safeguard the rights and bodily integrity of persons with mental illness. Under Section 95(1)(a), the administration of electroconvulsive therapy without the use of muscle relaxants and anesthesia (Direct ECT) is strictly prohibited. Additionally, Section 95 prohibits tying or chaining mentally ill individuals, and performing ECT on minors without prior approval from the Mental Health Review Board.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. Modified ECT (with anesthesia and muscle relaxants) is a legally recognized and permitted therapeutic intervention for adults under the Act.
• Option B: Correct. Direct ECT (unmodified ECT) is unconditionally banned under Section 95(1)(a) of the MHCA 2017, and its administration constitutes a punishable criminal offense under the Act.
• Option C: Incorrect. Prescribing atypical antipsychotics to elderly patients is guided by clinical indication, not prohibited by statutory mental health legislation.
• Option D: Incorrect. Independent voluntary admission is the primary promoted route of hospital admission under Section 85 and 86 of the Act.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: A 35-year-old man during a psychotherapy session reveals detailed, credible plans to murder his former business partner tomorrow morning, describing the exact firearm he purchased and the victim's residential address. In psychiatric medical ethics, the legal duty of a mental health professional to breach confidentiality to protect or warn an identifiable third party facing imminent violent harm was established by which famous legal precedent?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: While physician-patient confidentiality is a cornerstone of medical ethics, it is not absolute. In the landmark 1976 legal case Tarasoff v. Regents of the University of California, the Supreme Court of California established that mental health professionals have a 'Duty to Protect' (or 'Duty to Warn'). When a therapist determines that a patient presents a serious and imminent danger of violence to an identifiable third party, the protective privilege ends where public peril begins, mandating warning the intended victim and notifying law enforcement.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. The Tarasoff ruling established the legal and ethical duty of mental health clinicians to breach confidentiality to warn and protect an identifiable potential victim from imminent serious harm.
• Option B: Incorrect. Roe v. Wade was a landmark US constitutional case concerning reproductive rights and abortion, not psychiatric confidentiality.
• Option C: Incorrect. Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals defined the evidentiary standard for the admissibility of expert scientific testimony in court.
• Option D: Incorrect. Miranda v. Arizona established procedural safeguards (Miranda rights) required by police during custodial interrogation.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Under Section 84 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the defense of legal insanity is grounded in which historic nineteenth-century legal doctrine formulated in England?
options: The American Law Institute (ALI) Model Penal Code Standard
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Section 84 of the IPC (and corresponding provisions in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) states: 'Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.' This statute directly adopted the English 'McNaughten Rules' (1843), which establish a cognitive test requiring proof of a defect of reason from disease of the mind preventing knowledge of the nature and quality of the act or knowledge of right from wrong (legal insanity vs. mere medical insanity).

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Section 84 of the IPC is based entirely on the cognitive limb of the McNaughten Rules of 1843.
• Option B: Incorrect. The Durham Rule (1954) stated an accused is not criminally responsible if their unlawful act was the product of mental disease; it was broader and rejected in Indian jurisprudence.
• Option C: Incorrect. The Irresistible Impulse test excuses crimes driven by an uncontrollable volition despite knowing the act was wrong; Indian law does not recognize irresistible impulse alone under Section 84.
• Option D: Incorrect. The ALI Model Penal Code combines cognitive and volitional prongs and is an American statutory standard, not the foundation of the IPC.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: A 78-year-old wealthy widower with mild vascular cognitive impairment wishes to execute a new will distributing his estate. A psychiatrist is requested to assess his 'Testamentary Capacity'. According to the classic legal standard established in Banks v. Goodfellow (1870), which of the following is NOT an essential criterion for establishing testamentary capacity?
options: Understanding the nature of executing a will and its overall legal effects
Appreciating the extent and character of the property being bequeathed
Requirement of complete absence of psychiatric or physical illness
Recognizing natural claims of dependents expected to benefit from the estate
questions.answer: Requirement of complete absence of psychiatric or physical illness
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Testamentary capacity is the legal mental capacity to execute a valid will. The classic legal test laid down in Banks v. Goodfellow (1870) requires that the testator: (1) understands the nature and consequences of executing a will, (2) understands the extent and nature of their property/assets, (3) understands who the natural beneficiaries are and their claims upon the estate, and (4) is free from any morbid delusions that directly dictate or influence the testamentary disposition. Mild cognitive impairment or psychiatric illness does not automatically invalidate testamentary capacity if these four criteria are satisfied.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. Understanding the nature and effect of executing a will is an indispensable criterion under Banks v. Goodfellow.
• Option B: Incorrect. Understanding the extent and nature of one's property is an essential requirement.
• Option C: Correct. A testator does not need an intact, flawless memory or perfect mental health; individuals with mild dementia or mental illness can execute a valid will provided they meet the specific criteria and their dispositions are not driven by insane delusions.
• Option D: Incorrect. Appreciating the claims of natural beneficiaries (e.g., family members who would reasonably expect inheritance) is an explicit requirement of the legal test.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: What quasi-judicial bodies are established under Chapter XI of the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, in every state to protect the rights of persons with mental illness, register advance directives, and review admissions and treatment decisions?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, mandated the establishment of Mental Health Review Boards (MHRBs) across districts or groups of districts in every state. The Board is headed by a District Judge (or qualified judicial officer) and includes representatives of the district administration, psychiatrists, other medical practitioners, and persons with mental illness or their caregivers. The MHRB functions as a localized watchdog to register and adjudicate advance directives, review supported admissions exceeding 30 days, inspect facilities, and hear complaints regarding rights violations.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Mental Health Review Boards (MHRBs) are the primary district-level quasi-judicial statutory bodies constituted under the MHCA 2017 to safeguard patient rights and oversee admissions.
• Option B: Incorrect. The Central Mental Health Authority operates at the national policy and registration level, not as the localized review board.
• Option C: Incorrect. Consumer forums handle consumer service disputes under the Consumer Protection Act, not statutory mental health reviews.
• Option D: Incorrect. While Human Rights Commissions protect fundamental rights, MHRBs are the specific statutory bodies created under the MHCA 2017.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: A 22-year-old unmarried woman with schizophrenia is admitted to a psychiatric facility. Her family members approach the treating team demanding that she undergo surgical tubal ligation (sterilization) because they believe she cannot manage motherhood. Under Section 95(1)(c) of the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, what is the legal provision regarding sterilization of a person with mental illness?
options: Sterilization is permissible if nominated legal representatives sign written consent
Sterilization is strictly prohibited as a treatment for or due to mental illness
Sterilization is mandatory for female psychiatric inpatients admitted over 30 days
Sterilization can be ordered by the hospital superintendent without judicial review
questions.answer: Sterilization is strictly prohibited as a treatment for or due to mental illness
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Section 95(1)(c) of the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, explicitly prohibits performing sterilization procedures on women or men when such sterilization is intended as a treatment for mental illness or is being performed solely by reason of the person having a mental illness. This protects psychiatric patients from non-consensual eugenic practices and violations of bodily autonomy.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. Consent from family or a nominated representative cannot override this statutory prohibition.
• Option B: Correct. Under Section 95(1)(c) of the MHCA 2017, surgical sterilization of a person with mental illness as a treatment for mental illness or on the grounds of mental illness is completely prohibited.
• Option C: Incorrect. The law contains no provision for mandatory sterilization; in fact, such practices are illegal and punishable under the Act.
• Option D: Incorrect. A medical superintendent has no legal authority to sanction sterilization for reasons of mental illness.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In medical ethics, what are the four classic prima facie principles formulated by Tom Beauchamp and James Childress in 'Principles of Biomedical Ethics'?
options: Sanctity of life, Quality of life, Utility, and Duty
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: The universal framework for biomedical ethics developed by Beauchamp and Childress rests on four core prima facie principles: (1) Autonomy (respecting the decision-making capacity and self-determination of individuals), (2) Non-maleficence (primum non nocere; the duty to do no harm), (3) Beneficence (acting in the best interest of the patient; doing good), and (4) Justice (fair distribution of healthcare resources, benefits, and burdens without discrimination).

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Autonomy, Non-maleficence, Beneficence, and Justice constitute the classic Beauchamp and Childress ethical quartet.
• Option B: Incorrect. Confidentiality, veracity, and fidelity are derivative ethical rules/virtues, and paternalism is a practice often in conflict with autonomy, not one of the four foundational principles.
• Option C: Incorrect. These are concepts in philosophical bioethics, but not the four classic principles of biomedical ethics.
• Option D: Incorrect. Consent, competence, and capacity are clinical-legal constructs, not the four ethical principles.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.chapterTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topic: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.topicTitle: Legal and Ethical Issues in Psychiatry
questions.prompt: A 45-year-old woman with severe recurrent depressive disorder and psychotic features is admitted under Section 89 of the MHCA 2017 as a 'Supported Admission'. According to the provisions of Section 89, what is the MAXIMUM initial period of admission permitted under this section before a re-assessment and formal application for an extension is required?
options: Indefinitely until the family withdraws support
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Under Section 89 of the Indian Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, an individual with mental illness who lacks mental capacity to make independent treatment decisions and who satisfies criteria of high support needs/risk can be admitted under 'Supported Admission' upon application by their Nominated Representative and certification by two mental health professionals (at least one being a psychiatrist). The Act strictly limits this initial supported admission to a maximum period of 30 days. Beyond 30 days, if continued supported admission is necessary, Section 90 mandates rigorous re-examination and reporting to the Mental Health Review Board.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Section 89 permits supported admission for an initial maximum period of up to 30 days.
• Option B: Incorrect. 180 days is not an initial statutory admission period under the MHCA 2017.
• Option C: Incorrect. Admissions cannot be authorized for a year at a time under supported admission provisions without periodic statutory scrutiny.
• Option D: Incorrect. Indefinite institutional confinement without mandatory time-bounded legal reviews is illegal under the human-rights framework of the MHCA 2017.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In public health and community psychiatry, which level of prevention is exemplified by conducting school-based stress management workshops and community crisis intervention following natural disasters to reduce the initial incidence of new psychiatric disorders?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: The levels of prevention framework (Caplan's public health model) divides interventions into: (1) Primary Prevention—interventions aimed at preventing the development or initial onset of new cases of disease (decreasing incidence), such as stress reduction, prenatal care, and crisis intervention; (2) Secondary Prevention—early detection, screening, and prompt treatment to decrease duration and prevalence; and (3) Tertiary Prevention—rehabilitation and disability limitation to reduce impairment and handicap.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Interventions that build resilience, target risk factors, and prevent the emergence of new psychiatric cases reduce incidence and constitute primary prevention.
• Option B: Incorrect. Secondary prevention targets individuals who already have early or asymptomatic illness, focusing on screening, early diagnosis, and prompt treatment.
• Option C: Incorrect. Tertiary prevention focuses on rehabilitation, social skills training, and vocational reintegration for chronic established conditions.
• Option D: Incorrect. Quaternary prevention refers to identifying patients at risk of over-medicalization and protecting them from unnecessary or harmful medical interventions.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In what year was India's National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) originally launched, making India one of the earliest developing nations to formulate a comprehensive national policy integrating mental health with primary healthcare?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) of India was launched in 1982 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. Its vision was to ensure availability and accessibility of basic mental healthcare for all, particularly the underprivileged; to integrate mental health with general health services; and to promote community participation and human resources development.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. 1972 predated the formal adoption of the national mental health programme.
• Option B: Correct. The NMHP was officially formulated and launched in 1982.
• Option C: Incorrect. 1996 marks the year the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) was launched as a decentralized operational arm of the NMHP based on the Bellary model.
• Option D: Incorrect. 2017 was the year the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, was passed by the Indian Parliament, replacing the Mental Health Act, 1987.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: The District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) in India was developed based on the successful decentralized community mental health operational model pioneered in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: In the 1980s, researchers at the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, conducted a landmark rural community mental health project in Bellary district, Karnataka (the 'Bellary Model'). This project demonstrated that primary care medical officers and multipurpose healthcare workers could be successfully trained to identify and manage common and severe mental disorders in rural primary health centres (PHCs). This success led to the nationwide adoption of the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) in 1996.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. The Bellary model was the pioneering district-level pilot project that provided the operational blueprint for the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) across India.
• Option B: Incorrect. Mysore was not the location of the primary pilot model for DMHP.
• Option C: Incorrect. Mangalore is an academic hub, but was not the pioneering site for the DMHP community model.
• Option D: Incorrect. Belgaum was not the origin of this community psychiatry delivery framework.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Launched under the National Mental Health Programme by the Government of India in October 2022, what is 'Tele-MANAS'?
options: National 24x7 toll-free digital tele-mental health counseling helpline network
Robotic surgical system for stereotactic psychosurgery in remote districts
Central police biometric tracking database for monitoring psychiatric offenders
Commercial internet portal dispensing schedule H psychiatric pharmaceuticals
questions.answer: National 24x7 toll-free digital tele-mental health counseling helpline network
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Tele-MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States) was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, on World Mental Health Day (October 10, 2022). Operating via a 24x7 toll-free helpline number (14416 / 1800-891-4416), Tele-MANAS is a two-tier system: Tier 1 comprises state-level tele-mental health cells with trained counselors and clinical psychologists providing immediate psychological first-aid; Tier 2 provides referral to psychiatrists at medical colleges or DMHP teams for specialized tele-consultation or physical care.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Tele-MANAS is India's national, free, 24x7 tele-mental health counseling service network operating across states in multiple regional languages.
• Option B: Incorrect. Tele-MANAS is a telephonic/digital tele-counseling and consultation service; it does not involve surgical robotic interventions.
• Option C: Incorrect. Tele-MANAS is a universal healthcare service, not a forensic penal tracking system.
• Option D: Incorrect. Tele-MANAS is an official public health government service and does not operate as a commercial online pharmacy.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In family studies of schizophrenia, high 'Expressed Emotion' (EE) within the family environment is a potent predictor of psychiatric relapse. Which three key relational dimensions define High Expressed Emotion?
options: Critical comments, Hostility, and Emotional Over-involvement
Parental neglect, emotional detachment, and social abandonment
Financial exploitation, physical punishment, and rigid schedules
Constructive boundary setting, balanced praise, and autonomy support
questions.answer: Critical comments, Hostility, and Emotional Over-involvement
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Expressed Emotion (EE), first operationalized by George Brown and colleagues using the Camberwell Family Interview, measures the emotional climate and attitudes expressed by family caregivers toward a relative with schizophrenia or other chronic psychiatric disorders. High EE is defined by: (1) high frequency of Critical Comments (disapproval, resentment), (2) Hostility (rejection of the patient as a person), and (3) Emotional Over-involvement (intrusive, smothering, self-sacrificing behavior). High EE increases relapse rates significantly (up to 2–3 fold).

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Critical comments, hostility, and emotional over-involvement are the three defining criteria of High Expressed Emotion.
• Option B: Incorrect. While neglect and physical abuse represent domestic trauma and maltreatment, they do not define the specific construct of Expressed Emotion.
• Option C: Incorrect. Over-medication and schedule rigidity are institutional or systemic factors, not the clinical family indices of EE.
• Option D: Incorrect. Warmth, positive remarks, and appropriate boundaries are components of Low Expressed Emotion, which protects against relapse.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In community psychiatric rehabilitation, what is a 'Halfway Home'?
options: Maximum-security locked asylum for non-consensual long-term detention of chronic cases
Transitional residential facility supporting recovery between acute hospital and community
Specialized biochemical laboratory dedicated solely to therapeutic drug level monitoring
Outpatient day facility providing exclusive medically supervised opioid substitution therapy
questions.answer: Transitional residential facility supporting recovery between acute hospital and community
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: In psychiatric rehabilitation, a Halfway Home is a transitional residential facility designed to bridge the gap between acute or prolonged psychiatric hospitalization and independent community reintegration. It provides a semi-structured, homelike, supportive living environment where recovering individuals practice activities of daily living (ADL), social skills, and vocational training with gradual step-down supervision.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. Halfway homes are voluntary, open, transitional community residences, the antithesis of closed custodial asylums.
• Option B: Correct. A halfway home provides transitional, community-based residential care and psychosocial rehabilitation to support patients moving from hospital to independent home living.
• Option C: Incorrect. Halfway homes are residential rehabilitation settings, not diagnostic laboratory facilities.
• Option D: Incorrect. Acute opiate detoxification is managed in inpatient hospital addiction units, not halfway homes.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: What is the official tool developed and recommended by the Indian Psychiatric Society (IPS) and recognized for quantifying psychiatric disability for government certification and benefits in India?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: The Indian Disability Evaluation and Assessment Scale (IDEAS) was developed by the Indian Psychiatric Society (IPS) and notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, as the official instrument for measuring and certifying disability in mental illness. IDEAS evaluates four functional domains: (1) Self-care, (2) Interpersonal activities, (3) Communication and understanding, and (4) Work. Each domain is scored from 0 to 4, and the total score is combined with a score for duration of illness to calculate the Global Disability Percentage.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. IDEAS is the statutory official scale used across India for evaluating and certifying psychiatric disability.
• Option B: Incorrect. PANSS evaluates the severity of positive, negative, and general psychopathology symptoms in schizophrenia, but does not calculate legal disability percentage.
• Option C: Incorrect. HAM-D is a clinician-rated scale for assessing depression severity, not legal disability status.
• Option D: Incorrect. MMSE is a brief screening tool for global cognitive impairment and dementia, not a certified psychiatric disability scale.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, what minimum benchmark percentage of certified psychiatric disability is required for an individual to qualify for statutory government benefits, reservations, and welfare concessions in India?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Under Section 2(r) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, a 'person with benchmark disability' is defined as an individual with not less than 40% of a specified disability, as certified by an authorized medical board. Achieving the 40% benchmark disability threshold is required to access statutory entitlements, including affirmative action (employment reservations), educational quotas, disability pensions, and travel concessions.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Incorrect. 10% indicates minimal impairment that does not reach the statutory benchmark threshold.
• Option B: Incorrect. 25% represents mild-to-moderate impairment, but falls below the statutory legal benchmark.
• Option C: Correct. Under the RPwD Act, 2016, a minimum of 40% certified disability constitutes 'benchmark disability' for accessing legal reservations and social welfare schemes in India.
• Option D: Incorrect. 75% indicates severe disability; while individuals with 75% qualify, the minimum qualifying benchmark is 40%.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: The sociological shift beginning in the mid-twentieth century that led to the downsizing and closure of large custodial mental asylums in favor of psychiatric care delivered in general hospital psychiatric units (GHPUs) and community settings is termed:
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: Deinstitutionalization refers to the major health policy movement that shifted the locus of psychiatric care away from isolated, long-stay custodial psychiatric hospitals (asylums) to community-based facilities, outpatient clinics, and General Hospital Psychiatric Units (GHPUs). It was catalyzed by the discovery of effective psychotropic medications (e.g., chlorpromazine), humanitarian human-rights movements, and sociological recognition of institutionalization harms.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the recognized term for the policy and process of moving chronic mental healthcare from long-stay psychiatric institutions to community services.
• Option B: Incorrect. Trans-institutionalization is an unintended adverse consequence where discharged psychiatric patients end up in other custodial institutions (such as prisons or nursing homes) due to inadequate community mental health infrastructure.
• Option C: Incorrect. Somatization is the psychological process where psychological distress is expressed as physical bodily symptoms.
• Option D: Incorrect. Institutional neurosis describes the apathy, loss of initiative, and submissiveness resulting from prolonged residence in custodial institutions.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.prompt: In psychosocial rehabilitation of persons recovering from chronic, disabling mental illness, what type of rehabilitation facility provides structured, protective, real-work opportunities and paid task-based stipends in a non-competitive, supportive environment for individuals unable to compete in the open labor market?
questions.explanation:
Core Concept: A Sheltered Workshop is a vocational rehabilitation facility that provides adapted, supportive employment for individuals with significant chronic psychiatric or intellectual disabilities who cannot cope with the demands of the open, competitive job market. Tasks (such as packaging, assembling, printing, crafts) are graduated to the person's functional capacity, fostering self-worth, social skills, structure, and modest economic compensation.

Option Analysis:
• Option A: Correct. Sheltered workshops provide protected, tailored vocational tasks and stipends in a supportive setting to foster productivity and psychosocial rehabilitation.
• Option B: Incorrect. Inpatient forensic units house mentally ill individuals who have committed criminal offenses under court mandates, focusing on security and treatment rather than voluntary community employment.
• Option C: Incorrect. ECT suites are clinical procedural environments for administering biological therapy, not vocational rehabilitation.
• Option D: Incorrect. Crisis stabilization units provide short-term (24–72 hour) emergency psychiatric intervention, not long-term vocational training.

questions.prompt: THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SLIDE PROVIDED BELOW IS SUGGESTIVE OF:

THE GIVEN SLIDE SHOWS A ROW OF TOMBSTONES APPEARANCE, WHICH IS CLASSICALLY SEEN IN PEMPHIGUS
VULGARIS.
IN THIS CONDITION, THERE IS A SUPRABASAL SPLITTING OF THE EPIDERMIS LEADING TO BLISTER FORMATION. THE
BASAL LAYER REMAINS ADHERENT TO THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE AND GIVES THE RESEMBLANCE TO A ROW OF
TOMBSTONES AS SHOWN IN THE HISTOLOGY IMAGE BELOW.
PEMPHIGUS VULGARIS IS A CHRONIC IMMUNOBULLOUS DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE PRESENCE OF
ANTIBODIES AGAINST DESMOSOMAL PROTEINS, DESMOGLEINS 1 AND 3 EXPRESSED IN THE SKIN AND MUCOSA.
CLINICALLY, THE PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ILL-DEFINED, IRREGULAR, SLOW-TO-HEAL ORAL LESIONS AND
EROSIONS. FLACCID BLISTERS FILLED WITH CLEAR FLUID MAY ARISE ON NORMAL SKIN OR AN ERYTHEMATOUS BASE.
THE RUPTURE OF SUCH BLISTERS PRODUCES PAINFUL EROSIONS AND HEALS WITHOUT SCARRING.
NIKOLSKY'S SIGN IS POSITIVE WHICH IS ELICITED BY APPLYING FIRM TANGENTIAL SLIDING PRESSURE WITH A
FINGER ON LESIONAL OR PERILESIONAL SKIN. THIS LEADS TO THE SEPARATION OF THE NORMAL■LOOKING
EPIDERMIS FROM THE DERMIS, PRODUCING EROSION.
DIRECT IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE IS CONSIDERED THE MOST ACCURATE CONFIRMATORY TEST OF THIS CONDITION. IT
SHOWS INTERCELLULAR IGG AND C3 DEPOSITION ON THE SURFACE OF KERATINOCYTES THROUGHOUT THE
EPIDERMIS IN NORMAL, PERILESIONAL SKIN, IN A CHARACTERISTIC FISHNET/CHICKENWIRE APPEARANCE AS SEEN
BELOW.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A 23-YEAR-OLD PATIENT CAME WITH COMPLAINTS OF NON-SCARRING ALOPECIA IN THE VERTEX REGION OF
HIS HEAD. HISTOLOGICAL EXAMINATION SHOWS LOSS OF HAIR WITH HAEMORRHAGE INTO THE FOLLICULAR
AREAS AND MILD PERINUCLEAR LYMPHOCYTIC INFILTRATE. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO DEPICTING A YOUNG ADULT PRESENTING WITH NON-SCARRING ALOPECIA IN THE VERTEX
REGION AND HISTOLOGY SHOWING PERIFOLLICULAR HEMORRHAGE IS SUGGESTIVE OF TRICHOTILLOMANIA
(TRICHOTILLOSIS).
TRICHOTILLOMANIA HAS TO BE DIFFERENTIATED FROM ALOPECIA AREATA (OPTION A). TRICHOTILLOMANIA
PRESENTS WITH INCOMPLETE HAIR LOSS WITHIN A PATCH WITH VARYING LENGTHS OF HAIR WHEREAS ALOPECIA
AREATA SHOWS SMOOTH HAIRLESS PATCH WITH SPARING OF WHITE HAIRS. REGULAR PITTING OF NAILS
AND EXCLAMATION MARK HAIRS ARE SEEN IN ALOPECIA AREATA. WHEN THE DIAGNOSIS IS UNCERTAIN, A SCALP
BIOPSY CAN BE DONE. PERIFOLLICULAR HEMORRHAGE IS CHARACTERISTIC OF TRICHOTILLOMANIA WHILE
PERIBULBAR LYMPHOCYTIC INFILTRATE IS DIAGNOSTIC OF ALOPECIA AREATA.
TRICHOTILLOMANIA IS CLASSIFIED UNDER OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE AND RELATED DISORDERS. IT IS CHARACTERIZED
BY RECURRENT BODY-FOCUSED REPETITIVE BEHAVIOR (HAIR PULLING) AND REPEATED ATTEMPTS TO DECREASE OR
STOP THE BEHAVIOR. IT IS COMMONLY SEEN IN FEMALES. THE HAIR LOSS IS COMMONLY SEEN OVER THE VERTEX
BUT CAN INVOLVE EYELASHES, EYEBROWS, AND BEARD.
THE MOST EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR TRICHOTILLOSIS IS HABIT-REVERSAL TRAINING (HRT).
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: TELOGEN EFFLUVIUM IS DIFFUSE HAIR LOSS RESULTING IN NON-SCARRING ALOPECIA DUE TO LOSS OF
TELOGEN HAIRS DUE TO FEVER, PREGNANCY, HYPOTHYROIDISM OR ANEMIA.
OPTION C: TINEA INFECTION SHOWS PATCHY HAIR LOSS, RESULTING IN NON-SCARRING/SCARRING ALOPECIA. EASY
PLUCKABILITY, BROKEN HAIRS AND WOOD'S LAMP POSITIVITY ARE FEATURES.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE DISEASES IS UNLIKELY TO PRESENT WITH SKIN LESIONS ON THE SHIN?
questions.explanation:

HYPOTHYROIDISM IS UNLIKELY TO PRESENT WITH SKIN LESIONS ON SHIN. MYXEDEMA (SEVERE
HYPOTHYROIDISM) AND PRETIBIAL MYXEDEMA ARE DIFFERENT ENTITIES. PRETIBIAL MYXEDEMA IS THE
INFILTRATIVE DERMOPATHY (MUCIN DEPOSITION) SEEN OVER SHIN IN GRAVE'S DISEASE, A TYPE OF
HYPERTHYROIDISM.
OTHER OPTIONS :

OPTION A: SARCOIDOSIS: ERYTHEMA NODOSUM MAY BE SEEN ON THE ANTERIOR LEG.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: THE FOLLOWING IMAGE DEPICTS:
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS RAISED, BROWNISH THREAD-LIKE LESIONS IN THE INTERDIGITAL DISTRIBUTION
(BURROWS), TYPICALLY SEEN IN SCABIES.
SCABIES IS AN ECTOPARASITIC INFECTION CAUSED IN HUMANS BY SARCOPTES SCABIEI. IT IS TRANSMITTED BY
CLOSE PERSONAL CONTACT. PRURITIS WITH NOCTURNAL EXACERBATION AND CONTACT CASES WITHIN A FAMILY
SHOULD RAISE THE SUSPICION OF SCABIES. TYPICAL LOCATIONS OF LESIONS ARE THE FINGER WEBS, THE FLEXOR
SURFACES OF THE WRISTS, THE ELBOWS, THE AXILLAE, THE BUTTOCKS AND GENITALIA AND THE BREASTS OF WOMEN
(CIRCLE OF HEBRA). IN ADULTS, THE FACE IS OFTEN SPARED. PRURITIC PAPULES AND NODULES ON MALE
GENITALIA AND BREASTS SERVE AS VALUABLE DIAGNOSTIC CLUES IN THE ABSENCE OF BURROWS.
DERMOSCOPY OF THE BURROWS SHOWS JET■WITH■CONTRAIL APPEARANCE. MICROSCOPY OF SCRAPING FROM
BURROWS CAN BE DONE TO DEMONSTRATE MITES.
A SINGLE OVERNIGHT APPLICATION OF 5% PERMETHRIN CREAM FROM NECK TO TOE IN ADULTS AND FROM HEAD
TO TOE IN CHILDREN IS THE DRUG OF CHOICE FOR THE TREATMENT OF SCABIES IN ALL AGES INCLUDING INFANTS (AT
LEAST 2 MONTHS OLD) AND PREGNANT WOMEN. ALL FAMILY MEMBERS, EVEN IF ASYMPTOMATIC, NEED TO BE
TREATED SIMULTANEOUSLY FOR THIS CONDITION TO PREVENT REINFECTION. ORAL IVERMECTIN CAN ALSO BE USED.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A FEMALE CAME WITH COMPLAINTS OF BONE AND JOINT PAIN. NSAIDS WERE PRESCRIBED. AFTER A FEW
DAYS, SHE PRESENTS AGAIN COMPLAINING VESICOBULLOUS LESIONS HEALING TO GIVE A BROWNISH
DISCOLORATION OVER THE FACE (UPPER LIP AREA) AS DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE. THIS MOST PROBABLY
SUGGESTS A DIAGNOSIS OF
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENT HAS A HISTORY OF CONSUMPTION OF NSAIDS, FOLLOWING WHICH THERE IS AN APPEARANCE OF
VESICULOBULLOUS LESIONS ON THE LIPS, EVOLVING TO GIVE A BROWNISH DISCOLOURATION. THE MOST PROBABLE
DIAGNOSIS IS FIXED DRUG ERUPTION (FDE).
3532
A STRONG DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS IS POST-CHIKUNGUNYA PIGMENTATION (PCP) OF THE FACE SEEN ON THE
NOSE AND CHEEKS (CHIK SIGN). HOWEVER, THIS IS NOT THE ANSWER BECAUSE THERE IS NO ANTECEDENT
HISTORY OF FEVER, MYALGIA OR OTHER SYMPTOMS SUGGESTIVE OF CHIKUNGUNYA. PCP OFTEN APPEARS AS
THE FEVER SUBSIDES AND MAY PERSIST FOR ABOUT 3-6 MONTHS. PCP MIMICS MELASMA AND MAY BE
MISDIAGNOSED IF PROPER HISTORY IS NOT TAKEN.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS CHIK SIGN:
FIXED DRUG ERUPTION (FDE) IS A TYPE OF DELAYED HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION. IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY
WELL-DEFINED BROWN, HYPERPIGMENTED PLAQUES THAT MAY FOLLOW VESICULOBULLOUS LESIONS. THEY OCCUR
ON LIPS, HANDS, LEGS, FACE, GENITALIA, AND ORAL MUCOSA, AND CAN CAUSE A BURNING SENSATION. THEY
USUALLY PRESENT 30 MIN TO 8 H AFTER DRUG EXPOSURE AND RECUR AT THE SAME LOCATION ON RE-EXPOSURE.
NSAIDS, PARACETAMOL AND CO■TRIMOXAZOLE ARE THE MOST COMMON DRUGS CAUSING FDE.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: IN WHICH OF THE LISTED OPTIONS IS DENSE IRREGULAR COLLAGEN FOUND?
questions.explanation:
DENSE IRREGULAR COLLAGEN IS FOUND IN DERMIS.
IRREGULAR CONNECTIVE TISSUE IS OF THREE TYPES: LOOSE, DENSE AND ADIPOSE. DENSE CONNECTIVE TISSUE IS
LOCATED IN REGIONS WHICH ARE UNDER CONSISTENT MECHANICAL STRESS AND WHERE PROTECTION IS REQUIRED
FOR THE ENSHEATHED ORGANS. THE ABUNDANT COLLAGEN FIBRES IN THE DERMIS RUN IN A HAPHAZARD
MANNER. THIS PROTECTS THE SKIN.
IT IS USUALLY PRESENT IN :
- RETICULAR LAYER OF THE DERMIS
- SUPERFICIAL CONNECTIVE TISSUE SHEATHS OF THE MUSCLE AND NERVES
- ADVENTITIA OF LARGE VESSELS
- CAPSULES OF VARIOUS ORGANS AND GLANDS (E.G, TESTIS, SCLERA, PERIOSTEUM, PERICHONDRIUM)
ON THE OTHER HAND, DENSE REGULAR COLLAGEN FIBRES ARE FOUND IN TENDONS.
3533

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH HAIR LOSS AND ITCHING OF THE SCALP ALONG WITH MILD DISCHARGE. WHICH OF THESE IS USEFUL FOR DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE PATIENT HAS A HISTORY OF ITCHING AND MILD DISCHARGE AND EXAMINATION SHOWS A WELL-DEMARCATED
PATCH OF ALOPECIA, WITH SCALING AND BROKEN HAIR SHAFTS. THIS IS CHARACTERISTIC OF TINEA CAPITIS.
THOUGH THE DIAGNOSIS IS CLINICAL, A KOH MOUNT IS USED FOR CONFIRMATION.
SCRAPINGS FROM THE EDGE OF A LESION ARE TRANSFERRED TO A SLIDE, TO WHICH KOH IS ADDED. IT IS THEN
EXAMINED UNDER THE MICROSCOPE FOR THE PRESENCE OF HYPHAE, AS SHOWN BELOW.
TINEA CAPITIS IS A DERMATOPHYTE INFECTION PRIMARILY OCCURRING IN CHILDREN. CLINICAL FEATURES OF TINEA
CAPITIS ARE PATCHY HAIR LOSS, SCALING, TENDER LYMPHADENOPATHY, AND IN SEVERE CASES, THERE MIGHT BE
PUSTULES AND CRUSTING OF THE AFFECTED AREA ALONG WITH SINUS FORMATION.
THE CLINICAL VARIANTS OF TINEA CAPITIS ARE:
- ENDOTHRIX - A NON-INFLAMMATORY TYPE IN WHICH MULTIPLE BLACK DOTS ARE PRESENT WITHIN THE AREAS OF
ALOPECIA. IT IS MOST COMMONLY CAUSED BY T. TONSURANS AND T. VIOLACEUM.
3534
- ECTOTHRIX - A MILD INFLAMMATORY TYPE IN WHICH SINGLE OR MULTIPLE SCALY PATCHES WITH HAIR LOSS ARE
SEEN. MICROSPORUM AUDOUINII, M.CANIS, M.EQUINNUM, AND M.FERRUGINEUM CAUSE ECTOTHRIX
INFECTION.
- KERION - A SEVERE INFLAMMATORY TYPE THAT PRESENTS WITH AN INFLAMMATORY MASS WITH THICK
CRUSTING AND MATTING OF HAIR WITH PUS AND SINUS FORMATION. IT IS COMMONLY CAUSED BY T.
VERRUCOSUM AND T. MENTAGROPHYTES.
- FAVUS - IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE PRESENCE OF YELLOWISH, CUP■SHAPED CRUSTS KNOWN AS SCUTULA THAT
DEVELOP AROUND HAIR FOLLICLES. IT IS CAUSED BY T. SCHOENLEINII
3535
TREATMENT:
- TERBINAFINE: <10 KG- 62.5 MG; 10-20 KG - 125 MG; >20 KG- 250 MG, ALL GIVEN DAILY FOR 4
WEEKS.
- ITRACONAZOLE: 2-4 MG/KG/DAY FOR 4-6 WEEKS.

questions.prompt: SELECT THE CONDITION DISPLAYED BELOW:

THE IMAGE SHOWS A CHILD WITH A WELL-CIRCUMSCRIBED, BLACK, HETEROGENOUS LESION COVERED WITH HAIR.
THIS IS CHARACTERISTIC OF A CONGENITAL MELANOCYTIC NEVUS (CMN). THEY MAY BE PRESENT AT BIRTH OR
DEVELOP SHORTLY THEREAFTER. THEY ARE BENIGN AND CAN BE BROWN, BLACK, PURPLISH, OR RED, AND ARE
USUALLY A PALPABLE LESION.
THEY CAN BE CLASSIFIED BASED ON SIZE: SMALL (<1.5 CM), MEDIUM (1.5-19.9 CM), AND LARGE OR GIANT
(>20 CM). LARGER CMN HAVE A HIGHER RISK OF DEVELOPING MALIGNANT MELANOMA.
MANAGEMENT OF CMN DEPENDS ON THE SIZE AND LOCATION OF THE LESION. SMALLER NEVI MAY BE
OBSERVED, WHILE LARGER NEVI OR THOSE AT A HIGHER RISK FOR COMPLICATIONS MAY REQUIRE SURGICAL
EXCISION, PARTICULARLY IF THERE IS A CONCERN FOR MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION.
COMPLICATIONS OF CMN INCLUDE NEUROLOGICAL ABNORMALITIES (INTRAPARENCHYMAL MELANOSIS IS THE
COMMONEST FINDING), MALIGNANT MELANOMA, AND OTHER TUMORS LIKE RHABDOMYOSARCOMA.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE NERVES IS BIOPSIED FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF PURE NEURITIC LEPROSY?
questions.explanation:
SUPERFICIAL SENSORY BRANCH OF THE RADIAL NERVE IS MOST COMMONLY USED FOR NERVE BIOPSY IN NEURITIC
LEPROSY.
ALTHOUGH ANY NERVE INVOLVED WOULD SHOW THE PATHOLOGY, IT IS PRUDENT TO BIOPSY A BRANCH OF A
SENSORY NERVE, RATHER THAN A MIXED NERVE OR MAJOR NERVE TRUNK. SO, THE ULNAR NERVE WILL NOT BE THE
BEST ANSWER DESPITE IT BEING THE MOST COMMON PERIPHERAL NERVE INVOLVED IN NEURITIC LEPROSY.
THE COMMON NERVES AND SITES WHERE NERVE BIOPSY IS PERFORMED IN LEPROSY ARE AS FOLLOWS:
- SUPERFICIAL SENSORY RADIAL NERVE BRANCH AT THE WRIST
- ULNAR CUTANEOUS NERVE NEAR THE ULNAR BORDER OF THE BASE OF THE HAND
- SURAL NERVE NEAR THE ANKLE
NOTE: NERVE BIOPSY IS THE GOLD STANDARD FOR CONFIRMATION OF PURE NEURITIC LEPROSY.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH COMPONENT OF CEMENT CAUSES ALLERGIC DERMATITIS AMONG CONSTRUCTION WORKERS IN INDIA.
questions.explanation:
3543
CHROMATE IS THE MOST FREQUENT ALLERGEN IN CEMENT CAUSING OCCUPATIONAL CONTACT DERMATITIS. THE
MOST COMMON ALLERGEN CAUSING ALLERGIC CONTACT DERMATITIS IN INDIA IS NICKEL. IT IS COMMONLY FOUND
IN ARTIFICIAL JEWELRY. HOWEVER, AMONG CONSTRUCTION WORKERS, CHROMATE IS MORE COMMON THAN
NICKEL. THE REPORTED PREVALENCE OF ALLERGIC CONTACT DERMATITIS (ACD) TO CHROMATE AMONG
CONSTRUCTION WORKERS IS USUALLY MORE THAN 10%.
ALLERGIC CONTACT DERMATITIS (ACD) IS AN INFLAMMATORY CONDITION CAUSED DUE TO A DELAYED
HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION (TYPE 4 HYPERSENSITIVITY) TO A SPECIFIC ALLERGEN THAT COMES INTO DIRECT
CONTACT WITH THE SKIN. SOME COMMON ALLERGENS INCLUDE NICKEL (FOUND IN ARTIFICIAL JEWELRY),
PPD/PARA PHENYLENE DIAMINE (IN HAIR DYE), CHROMATE (IN CEMENT), RUBBER OR LATEX, COSMETICS, ETC.
PATCH TEST IS USED FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF ACD.
PATIENTS USUALLY PRESENT WITH PRURITUS, ERYTHEMA, SWELLING, PAPULES, AND PAPULOVESICLES. IN SEVERE
CASES, LARGE VESICLES OR BLISTERS MAY FORM DUE TO THE DISRUPTION OF THE INTERCELLULAR BRIDGES. IF
EXPOSURE PERSISTS THE AFFECTED AREA BECOMES DRY, SCALY, AND THICKER WITH LICHENIFICATION AND
FISSURING DEVELOPS LATER. THERE IS INVOLVEMENT OF THE COVERED AREAS AS WELL AS THE EXPOSED AREAS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THESE IS A DRUG USED IN THE TREATMENT OF TINEA CRURIS FOR WHICH WIDESPREAD
RESISTANCE IS FOUND TO BE DEVELOPING?
questions.explanation:
THE USE OF TERBINAFINE AS THE AGENT OF CHOICE FOR TINEA CRURIS AND CORPORIS HAS BEEN LIMITED LATELY
DUE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESISTANCE.
TINEA CRURIS (ALSO KNOWN AS JOCK ITCH) IS A DERMATOPHYTE INFECTION INVOLVING THE CRURAL FOLD. THE
MOST COMMON CAUSE IS TRICHOPHYTON RUBRUM.
T. RUBRUM ISOLATES HAVE BEEN FOUND TO EXHIBIT RESISTANCE AGAINST TERBINAFINE.
NOTE: THE QUESTION IS BASED ON RESEARCH PAPERS ABOUT TRICHOPHYTON RUBRUM STRAINS EXHIBITING
PRIMARY RESISTANCE TO TERBINAFINE.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT CAME WITH A HISTORY OF FEVER, BODY ACHE, AND JOINT PAIN. HE WAS GIVEN NSAIDS. A FEW
DAYS LATER, HE DEVELOPED BROWNISH PIGMENTATION OVER THE NOSE. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN HISTORY OF FEVER, JOINT PAIN, AND CENTROFACIAL HYPERPIGMENTATION POINTS TOWARD A
DIAGNOSIS OF CHIKUNGUNYA. POST CHIKUNGUNYA PIGMENTATION (PCP) USUALLY APPEARS AFTER THE FEVER
SUBSIDES AND PERSISTS FOR ABOUT 3-6 MONTHS. HYPERPIGMENTATION ASSOCIATED WITH CHIKUNGUNYA
FEVER IS MACULAR AND MOST COMMONLY AFFECTS THE NOSE AND CHEEKS.
ANOTHER CLOSE DIFFERENTIAL IS FIXED DRUG ERUPTIONS (FDE). FDE HAS A SHORTER LATENCY, USUALLY
PRESENTS 30 MIN TO 8 H AFTER DRUG EXPOSURE, AND RECURS AT THE SAME LOCATION ON RE-EXPOSURE. IT
PRESENTS WITH HYPERPIGMENTED PLAQUES THAT MAY BE PRECEDED BY VESICULOBULLOUS LESIONS.
HYPERPIGMENTATION OF THE CENTROFACIAL REGION (NOSE AND CHEEKS) MIMICS MELASMA AND MAY BE
MISDIAGNOSED IF PROPER HISTORY IS NOT TAKEN.
NOSE PIGMENTATION IS STRIKING IN CASES OF CHIKUNGUNYA FEVER AND IS TERMED CHIK SIGN. THE IMAGE
BELOW SHOWS CHIK SIGN ON THE NOSE:
3544
FDE IS A TYPE OF DELAYED HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION. THEY OCCUR ON LIPS, HANDS, LEGS, FACE, GENITALIA,
AND ORAL MUCOSA, AND CAN CAUSE A BURNING SENSATION. NSAIDS, PARACETAMOL AND CO■TRIMOXAZOLE
ARE THE MOST COMMON DRUGS CAUSING FDE. NSAID■INDUCED FDE MAINLY AFFECTS THE GENITALS AND
LIPS.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS FDE ON UPPER LIP AREA:

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A MOTHER HAS A PEARLY WHITE PAPULE ON HER FOREHEAD (AS DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE PRESENTED BELOW) WHICH HER
INFANT ALSO DEVELOPS. SPECIFY THE CAUSE.
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS PEARLY WHITE UMBILICATED WART-LIKE LESIONS WITH A CHARACTERISTIC DIMPLE AT THE
CENTER, SUGGESTIVE OF MOLLUSCUM CONTAGIOSUM, WHICH IS CAUSED BY POX VIRUS.
THE AGE OF PEAK INCIDENCE IS BETWEEN 2 AND 5 YEARS. IN CHILDREN, IT IS MAINLY CAUSED BY THE TYPE I
MOLLUSCUM CONTAGIOSUM VIRUS (MCV-1). THERE IS A RELATIVELY HIGHER INCIDENCE OF MCV■2 TYPE IN
3545
ADULTS AND HIV INFECTION. SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED MOLLUSCUM CONTAGIOSUM MAY BE PRESENT OVER THE
GENITAL AREA.
IT HAS AN INCUBATION PERIOD OF 2 WEEKS TO 6 MONTHS. WIDESPREAD AND REFRACTORY LESIONS ARE SEEN
MOST COMMONLY IN HIV OR PATIENTS ON IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE THERAPY.
IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE PRESENCE OF INTRACYTOPLASMIC EOSINOPHILIC INCLUSION BODIES CALLED
HENDERSON-PATTERSON BODIES OR MOLLUSCUM BODIES. PSEUDO-KOEBNER PHENOMENON IS SEEN, THAT IS,
NEW LESIONS DEVELOP ALONG LINES OF TRAUMA.
TREATMENT IS USUALLY NOT REQUIRED, AND LESIONS ARE LIKELY TO RESOLVE SPONTANEOUSLY. STIMULATION OF
THE IMMUNE RESPONSE CAN BE DONE AFTER DESTRUCTIVE OR INFLAMMATORY THERAPIES WITH SALICYLIC ACID,
TRICHLOROACETIC ACID, AND IMIQUIMOD. CRYOTHERAPY WHEN DONE NEEDS TO BE REPEATED AT 3-4 WEEK
INTERVALS. EXTENSIVE LESIONS ARE TREATED WITH AN ANTIVIRAL AGENT LIKE CIDOFOVIR.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH THE OCCURRENCE OF BLISTERING AND PEELING OF OVER >30% OF BODY
SURFACE AREA IS USUALLY CAUSED BY:
questions.explanation:
BLISTERING AND PEELING INVOLVING GREATER THAN 30% OF THE BODY SURFACE AREA POINTS TO THE DIAGNOSIS
OF TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS (TEN). TEN IS PRIMARILY DRUG■INDUCED, WITH A CULPRIT DRUG BEING
DEMONSTRATED IN APPROXIMATELY 85% OF CASES.
STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME (SJS) AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS (TEN) ARE BOTH SEVERE
MUCOCUTANEOUS REACTIONS, CHARACTERIZED BY BLISTERING AND EPITHELIAL SLOUGHING. THE TWO TERMS
DESCRIBE PHENOTYPES WITHIN A SEVERITY SPECTRUM, WHERE SJS IS THE LESS EXTENSIVE FORM AND TEN IS
THE MORE EXTENSIVE
COMMON DRUGS THAT CAN CAUSE SJS/TEN ARE:
- ALLOPURINOL
- NSAIDS- OXICAM GROUP
- ANTI-EPILEPTICS - PHENOBARBITAL, PHENYTOIN, CARBAMAZEPINE, LAMOTRIGINE
- ANTIBIOTICS - PENICILLINS, CEPHALOSPORINS, SULFAMETHOXAZOLE, SULFASALAZINE, NEVIRAPINE

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: A 23 YEAR OLD PATIENT PRESENTS WITH LESIONS IN THE GROIN AS DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE PRESENTED BELOW. WHICH OF THESE CANNOT BE A CAUSE OF THESE LESIONS?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS A WELL-CIRCUMSCRIBED, ANNULAR PLAQUE IN THE GROIN REGION WHICH IS CHARACTERISTIC
OF TINEA CRURIS. TINEA CRURIS IS A DERMATOPHYTOSIS. TRICHOPHYTON, MICROSPORUM AND
EPIDERMOPHYTON ARE DERMATOPHYTES WHEREAS ASPERGILLUS IS NOT.
DERMATOPHYTES INCLUDE 3 GENERA:
- TRICHOPHYTON SPECIES INFECT SKIN, HAIR, AND NAILS AND INCLUDE T. RUBRUM, T. MENTAGROPHYTES, T.
TONSURANS, T. SCHOENLEINII, AND T. VIOLACEUM.
- MICROSPORUM CONTAINS M. GYPSEUM, M. CANIS, AND M. NANUM. THESE INFECT ONLY HAIR AND SKIN
(NOT NAILS).
- FLOCCOSUM IS THE ONLY SPECIES IN THE GENUS EPIDERMOPHYTON, IT INFECTS ONLY SKIN AND NAILS (NOT
HAIR).
ASPERGILLUS SPP. PRODUCE LARGE NECROTIC LESIONS LIKE ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM, AND SOMETIMES SMALL
PAPULES AND COLD ABSCESSES.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH MULTIPLE NODULOCYSTIC LESIONS ON THE FACE. WHICH AMONG THESE
IS THE DRUG OF CHOICE IN THIS CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE NODULOCYSTIC LESIONS IMPLIES THAT THIS IS A CASE OF SEVERE
ACNE. ISOTRETINOIN IS THE FIRST-LINE DRUG FOR THE TREATMENT OF SEVERE ACNE (NODULAR ACNE AND ACNE
CONGLOBATA).
SYSTEMIC RETINOIDS ARE HIGHLY TERATOGENIC AND ARE ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANT WOMEN,
THOSE PLANNING TO BECOME PREGNANT, OR BREASTFEEDING MOTHERS. TWO NEGATIVE PREGNANCY TESTS (ON
SEPARATE OCCASIONS) ARE REQUIRED FOR FEMALES OF CHILDBEARING AGE BEFORE STARTING ACITRETIN OR
ISOTRETINOIN.
3547
BASELINE EVALUATION OF SERUM LIPIDS, TRANSAMINASES, AND COMPLETE BLOOD COUNTS SHOULD BE DONE
BEFORE STARTING ANY SYSTEMIC RETINOIDS. THESE VALUES SHOULD BE CHECKED MONTHLY FOR THE FIRST 3–6
MONTHS AND ONCE EVERY 3 MONTHS THEREAFTER. MONTHLY PREGNANCY TESTS SHOULD BE DONE WHILE ON THE
DRUG.
NOTE: FEMALE PATIENTS SHOULD AVOID CONCEPTION FOR 3 YEARS AFTER DISCONTINUING ACITRETIN TREATMENT
FOR CUTANEOUS PSORIASIS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE TYPE OF CONNECTIVE TISSUE PRESENT IN THE AREA INDICATED BY THE ARROW IN THE PROVIDED IMAGE.
questions.explanation:
THE AREA MARKED IS THE RETICULAR DERMIS. IT IS MADE UP OF DENSE IRREGULAR CONNECTIVE TISSUE.
IT IS FOUND IN THE REGIONS THAT ARE UNDER CONSIDERABLE MECHANICAL STRESS AND WHERE PROTECTION IS
GIVEN TO ENSHEATHED ORGANS. IT IS USUALLY PRESENT IN:
- RETICULAR DERMIS
- SUPERFICIAL CONNECTIVE TISSUE SHEATHS OF THE MUSCLE AND NERVES
- ADVENTITIA OF LARGE VESSELS
- CAPSULES OF VARIOUS ORGANS AND GLANDS (E.G., TESTIS, SCLERA, PERIOSTEUM, PERICHONDRIUM)
ON THE OTHER HAND, DENSE REGULAR COLLAGEN FIBERS ARE FOUND IN TENDONS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SLIDE PROVIDED BELOW IS SUGGESTIVE OF:
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN SLIDE SHOWS A ROW OF TOMBSTONES APPEARANCE, WHICH IS CLASSICALLY SEEN IN PEMPHIGUS
VULGARIS.
IN THIS CONDITION, THERE IS A SUPRABASAL SPLITTING OF THE EPIDERMIS LEADING TO BLISTER FORMATION. THE
BASAL LAYER REMAINS ADHERENT TO THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE AND GIVES THE RESEMBLANCE TO A ROW OF
TOMBSTONES AS SHOWN IN THE HISTOLOGY IMAGE BELOW.
3548
PEMPHIGUS VULGARIS IS A CHRONIC IMMUNOBULLOUS DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE PRESENCE OF
ANTIBODIES AGAINST DESMOSOMAL PROTEINS, DESMOGLEINS 1 AND 3 EXPRESSED IN THE SKIN AND MUCOSA.
CLINICALLY, THE PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ILL-DEFINED, IRREGULAR, SLOW-TO-HEAL ORAL LESIONS AND
EROSIONS. FLACCID BLISTERS FILLED WITH CLEAR FLUID MAY ARISE ON NORMAL SKIN OR AN ERYTHEMATOUS BASE.
THE RUPTURE OF SUCH BLISTERS PRODUCES PAINFUL EROSIONS AND HEALS WITHOUT SCARRING.
NIKOLSKY'S SIGN IS POSITIVE WHICH IS ELICITED BY APPLYING FIRM TANGENTIAL SLIDING PRESSURE WITH A
FINGER ON LESIONAL OR PERILESIONAL SKIN. THIS LEADS TO THE SEPARATION OF THE NORMAL■LOOKING
EPIDERMIS FROM THE DERMIS, PRODUCING EROSION.
DIRECT IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE IS CONSIDERED THE MOST ACCURATE CONFIRMATORY TEST OF THIS CONDITION. IT
SHOWS INTERCELLULAR IGG AND C3 DEPOSITION ON THE SURFACE OF KERATINOCYTES THROUGHOUT THE
EPIDERMIS IN NORMAL, PERILESIONAL SKIN, IN A CHARACTERISTIC FISHNET/CHICKENWIRE APPEARANCE AS SEEN
BELOW.
3549

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A 15-YEAR-OLD GIRL PRESENTS WITH ITCHY LESIONS ON HER ARM AS SHOWN. HER FAMILY HISTORY IS
POSITIVE FOR ASTHMA. WHAT COULD BE THE MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO DEPICTING PRURITIC LESIONS AT A FLEXURAL SITE ALONG WITH A FAMILY HISTORY OF
ATOPY (ASTHMA) IS SUGGESTIVE OF ATOPIC DERMATITIS (AD) OR ATOPIC ECZEMA (AE). THE SCRATCH
MARKS AND EXCORIATIONS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE ARE DUE TO PRURITIS, WHICH IS THE HALLMARK FEATURE OF
3579
AD.
AD IS A CHRONIC RELAPSING INFLAMMATORY CONDITION. IT PRESENTS WITH ERYTHEMATOUS MACULES,
PAPULES AND VESICLES THAT OFTEN START IN EARLY CHILDHOOD, USUALLY LESS THAN 2 YEARS OLD. THE LESIONS
LATER BECOME EXCORIATED AND LICHENIFIED. IT IS FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH DRYNESS OF THE SKIN
AND SECONDARY INFECTIONS. IN INFANCY, THE LESIONS INITIALLY APPEAR ON FACE (SPARING THE NAPKIN AREA)
AND LATER ON EXTENSOR ASPECT OF KNEES AND ELBOWS AS THE CHILD STARTS CRAWLING. IN LATER CHILDHOOD
AND IN ADULTS, THE PRINCIPAL SITE OF INVOLVEMENT IS FLEXURES.
THE FILAGGRIN MONOMERS IN KERATINOCYTES IN THE EPIDERMIS BIND AND AGGREGATE KERATIN BUNDLES AND
INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS TO FORM THE EPIDERMAL BARRIER. ANY DAMAGE/DYSFUNCTION OF THIS BARRIER IS
ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED RISK OF DEVELOPING AD. DAMAGE TO THIS BARRIER CAN BE DUE TO
ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS (DETERGENTS, HARD WATER, UV LIGHT) OR LOCAL INFLAMMATORY
REACTIONS. DYSFUNCTION OF THE BARRIER CAN BE DUE TO GENETIC MUTATION OF THE FLG GENE LEADING TO
REDUCED FILAGGRIN PRODUCTION OR LOCAL IMMUNOMODULATORY EFFECTS LEADING TO REDUCED FILAGGRIN
EXPRESSION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: SEBORRHEIC DERMATITIS IS A CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY SKIN CONDITION CHARACTERIZED BY
ERYTHEMA, PRURITUS, SCALING, FLAKING, OR CRUSTING OF THE SKIN. IT IS OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH MALASEZZIA
FUNGAL INFECTION. A MILDER FORM OF SEBORRHEIC DERMATITIS OF THE SCALP IS COMMONLY KNOWN AS
DANDRUFF.
OPTION C: ALLERGIC CONTACT DERMATITIS (ACD) IS AN INFLAMMATORY CONDITION CAUSED DUE TO A DELAYED
HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION (TYPE 4 HYPERSENSITIVITY) TO A SPECIFIC ALLERGEN THAT COMES INTO DIRECT
CONTACT WITH THE SKIN.PATIENTS USUALLY PRESENT WITH PRURITUS, ERYTHEMA, SWELLING,
PAPULES, AND PAPULOVESICLES. SOME COMMON ALLERGENS INCLUDE NICKEL (FOUND IN ARTIFICIAL JEWELRY),
PPD/PARA PHENYLENE DIAMINE (IN HAIR DYE), CHROMATE (IN CEMENT), RUBBER OR LATEX, COSMETICS, ETC.
PATCH TEST (IMAGE BELOW) IS USED FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF ACD.
3580
OPTION D: ERYSIPELAS IS A BACTERIAL SKIN INFECTION CAUSED BY STREPTOCOCCUS PYOGENES (GROUP A
STREPTOCOCCUS) CHARACTERIZED BY RAISED, ERYTHEMATOUS SHARPLY DEMARCATED RAPIDLY SPREADING SKIN
LESIONS, ALONG WITH SYSTEMIC SYMPTOMS LIKE FEVER AND CHILLS. THE SKIN MAY ALSO HAVE A PEAU
D'ORANGE OR ORANGE PEEL-LIKE APPEARANCE.
questions.assetNote: Pending Medicomm atlas conversion from the original PDF image; preserve question image order.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS A PRIMARY SKIN LESION?
questions.explanation:
PURPURA IS A PRIMARY SKIN LESION. CRUST, ATROPHY, AND INDURATION ARE SECONDARY LESIONS.
IT IS A CONDITION WITH RED OR PURPLE DISCOLORED SPOTS ON THE SKIN THAT DO NOT BLANCH ON APPLYING
PRESSURE. THE SPOTS ARE CAUSED BY BLEEDING UNDERNEATH THE SKIN. IT IS SEEN:
- VASCULITIS
- THROMBOCYTOPENIA
3581
- VITAMIN C DEFICIENCY
OPTION A: CRUSTS OR SCABS CONSIST OF DRIED-UP DISCHARGE FROM THE LESIONS.
OPTION B: ATROPHY REFERS TO LOSS OF TISSUE. THERE MAY BE FINE WRINKLING AND INCREASED TRANSLUCENCY
IF THE PROCESS IS SUPERFICIAL.
OPTION D: INDURATION REFERS TO DERMAL THICKENING THAT CLINICALLY PRESENTS AS SKIN THAT FEELS THICKER
AND FIRMER THAN NORMAL ON PALPATION.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE STATEMENTS IS FALSE CONCERNING SCLEREDEMA?
options: THE DERMIS IS 3–4 TIMES THICKER THAN NORMAL
ERYTHEMA AND PEAU D’ORANGE APPEARANCE OF THE SKIN CAN BE SEEN
CAN OCCUR IN ASSOCIATION WITH DIABETES
ASSOCIATED WITH SCLERODACTYLY OR RAYNAUDS PHENOMENON
questions.answer: ASSOCIATED WITH SCLERODACTYLY OR RAYNAUDS PHENOMENON
questions.explanation:
SCLEREDEMA IS NOT ASSOCIATED WITH SCLERODACTYLY OR RAYNAUDS PHENOMENON. SCLEREDEMA
AND SCLERODERMA ARE DIFFERENT ENTITIES. IN CONTRAST TO SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS (SCLERODERMA), SCLEREDEMA
IS NOT ASSOCIATED WITH SCLERODACTYLY, RAYNAUD PHENOMENON, NAIL FOLD CAPILLARY CHANGES, OR SERUM
3582
AUTOANTIBODIES.
IN SCLEREDEMA, THE DERMIS IS 3–4 TIMES THICKER THAN NORMAL DUE TO AN INCREASE IN TYPE 1 COLLAGEN
SYNTHESIS BY DYSFUNCTIONAL FIBROBLAST. HOWEVER, FIBROBLAST PROLIFERATION IS NOT SEEN.
ERYTHEMA AND A PEAU D’ORANGE APPEARANCE OF THE SKIN ARE COMMONLY OBSERVED. THE HANDS AND
FEET ARE CHARACTERISTICALLY SPARED.
DIABETIC SCLEREDEMA IS THE MOST COMMON TYPE. IN DIABETIC SCLEREDEMA, THE ACCUMULATION OF
COLLAGEN MAY BE DUE TO IRREVERSIBLE NON■ENZYMATIC GLYCOSYLATION OF COLLAGEN AND RESISTANCE TO
DEGRADATION BY COLLAGENASE. IT CAN ALSO OCCUR POST-STREPTOCOCCAL INFECTIONS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE PIGMENTATION ABNORMALITY IN THE IMAGE DISPLAYED BELOW.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWING HYPERPIGMENTED LESION ON SHOULDER ASSOCIATED WITH HYPERTRICHOSIS IS
SUGGESTIVE OF BECKER'S NAEVUS.
IT IS AN EPIDERMAL MELANOCYTIC NAEVUS WITH AGGREGATION OF MELANOCYTE CLUSTERS IN THE EPIDERMIS. IT
IS OFTEN HAIRY. THE ONSET IS AROUND ADOLESCENCE WHEN THERE IS AN INCREASED SENSITIVITY TO ANDROGENS
ESPECIALLY IN THE DISTRIBUTION OF OUTER ARMS, SCAPULAR AREA AND CHEST.
A TRIAD OF FEATURES CAN BE SEEN:
- HYPERPIGMENTATION
- HYPERTRICHOSIS
- ACNE
OPTION A: MONGOLIAN SPOTS ARE SLATE BLUE AREAS IN THE LUMBOSACRAL REGION THAT SPONTANEOUSLY
REGRESS BEFORE PUBERTY.
OPTION B: NAEVUS OF ITO IS UNILATERAL HYPERPIGMENTATION IN THE ACROMIOCLAVICULAR DISTRIBUTION. IT IS
NOT KNOWN TO HAVE HYPERTRICHOSIS OR ACNE.
3583
OPTION C: CONGENITAL MELANOCYTIC NEVI ARE COMMON MOLES THAT BECOME RAISED AND HAVE A
CEREBRIFORM APPEARANCE AND CAN BE HAIRY. THEY CAN OCCUR ANYWHERE. THE ONSET IS AT BIRTH OR SOON
AFTER BIRTH

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: SPECIFY THE MOST COMMON CAUSATIVE ORGANISM FOR VERRUCA VULGARIS.
questions.explanation:
VERRUCA VULGARIS OR COMMON WART IS MOST COMMONLY CAUSED BY HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS-2 (HPV-2)
BUT IS ALSO RELATED TO TYPES 1, 4, 27, AND 57.
COMMON WARTS ARE USUALLY ASYMPTOMATIC. THEY SHOW ACANTHOSIS, HYPERKERATOSIS,
AND PAPILLOMATOSIS AND PRESENT AS FIRM PAPULES WITH A ROUGH HORNY SURFACE. THE MOST COMMONLY
AFFECTED SITES ARE ON THE BACKS OF THE HANDS AND FINGERS, AND, IN CHILDREN ON THE
KNEES. PSEUDO-KOEBNER PHENOMENON MAY BE OBSERVED.
3584
TREATMENT IS USUALLY WITH TOPICAL AGENTS SUCH AS SALICYLIC ACID, CAUSTICS, GLUTARALDEHYDE, FORMALIN,
OR WITH LASER, CRYOTHERAPY, SURGICAL REMOVAL.
VERRUCA VULGARIS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: CUTIS MARMORATA OCCURS DUE TO ______
questions.explanation:
CUTIS MARMORATA REFERS TO THE PINKISH-BLUE MOTTLED OR MARBLED APPEARANCE WHEN SUBJECTED TO COLD
TEMPERATURES.
IT IS SEEN THROUGHOUT INFANCY AND IN 50% OF CHILDREN. IT IS CAUSED BY SIMULTANEOUS DILATION AND
CONTRACTION OF THE SUPERFICIAL CAPILLARIES. REWARMING RESTORES THE SKIN TO NORMAL. THIS IS A
PHYSIOLOGICAL FINDING AND REQUIRES NO TREATMENT. HOWEVER, PERSISTENT CUTIS MARMORATA MAY BE
SEEN IN TRISOMIES 18 AND 21.
NOTE: CUTIS MARMORATA TELANGIECTATICA CONGENITA IS A DISTINCT VASCULAR DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER AND
IS EASILY DISTINGUISHED AS IT IS FIXED (IT DOES NOT DISAPPEAR ON REWARMING), AND IT MAY BE ASSOCIATED
WITH A VARIETY OF OTHER ANOMALIES SUCH AS LIMB GROWTH OR RENAL ANOMALIES.
3585

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: VARICELLA-ZOSTER VIRUS REMAINS DORMANT IN THE:
questions.explanation:
VARICELLA-ZOSTER VIRUS (VZV) IS A HUMAN HERPESVIRUS THAT CAUSES VARICELLA (CHICKENPOX) AS A
PRIMARY INFECTION AND THEN REMAINS IN A LATENT FORM IN THE DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA FOR A VARIABLE PERIOD
AFTER WHICH IT CAN REACTIVATE TO CAUSE HERPES ZOSTER (SHINGLES).
3586

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A 5-YEAR-OLD BOY HAD PAINFUL SORES IN THE MOUTH WITH A RASH OVER THE HANDS ALONG WITH FEVER.
INDICATE WHICH OF THESE IS THE CAUSATIVE AGENT.
questions.explanation:
THE PRESENCE OF FEVER, ALONG WITH PAINFUL SORES IN THE MOUTH AND SMALL, TENSE VESCICLES WITH
SURROUNDING ERYTHEMA ON THE PALMS AND SOLES IN A CHILD POINT TOWARDS THE DIAGNOSIS OF
HAND-FOOT-MOUTH DISEASE. THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF WHICH WORLDWIDE IS COXACKIEVIRUS A16.
SPREAD IS BY DROPLETS OR FAECAL CONTAMINATION AND THE INCUBATION PERIOD IS 7 DAYS. THE FEVER IS
GENERALLY MILD, AND IS FOLLOWED BY THE APPEARANCE OF LESIONS. THE CHARACTERISTIC LESIONS ARE SLIGHTLY
OVAL, WITH A GREY BLISTER ROOF AND A NARROW RIM OF ERYTHEMA. THE ORAL LESIONS ARE APHTHOID AND ARE
LESS PAINFUL THAN APHTHOUS ULCERS.
ONLY SYMPTOMATIC TREATMENT IS GIVEN. THE LESIONS GENERALLY DISAPPEAR IN 7 - 10 DAYS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
THE FOLLOWING LESION IS SEEN IN A 25-YEAR-OLD MAN WHO CAME TO A PRIMARY HEALTH CENTRE 5 DAYS
AFTER HE HAD UNPROTECTED SEXUAL INTERCOURSE. ON PALPATION THE ULCERS WERE PAINFUL.
SUPPURATIVE INGUINAL LYMPHADENOPATHY WAS PRESENT ON THE RIGHT SIDE. THE PATIENT HAS NO
PREVIOUS HISTORY OF DRUG ALLERGY. INDICATE WHICH KIT WILL BE USED FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF THIS PARTICULAR
SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASE.
questions.explanation:
THE APPEARANCE OF PAINFUL GENITAL ULCERS, ALONG WITH UNILATERAL SUPPURATIVE INGUINAL
LYMPHADENOPATHY, 5 DAYS AFTER UNPROTECTED SEXUAL INTERCOURSE BEST FITS THE SYMPTOM CLUSTER OF A
NON - HERPETIC GENITAL ULCER. THE TREATMENT OF WHICH IS KIT 3 / WHITE KIT IN CASE OF NO PENICILLIN
ALLERGY.
THE ABOVE-SHOWN CLINICAL IMAGE AND THE FINDINGS ARE CONSISTENT WITH A DIAGNOSIS OF CHANCROID.
SOFT CHANCRE/CHANCROID:
- THE CAUSATIVE ORGANISM IS HAEMOPHILUS DUCREYI.
- THE INCUBATION PERIOD IS 3 TO 10 DAYS.
- IT PRESENTS WITH MULTIPLE PAINFUL ULCERS ON GENITALS.
- IT MAY BE ACCOMPANIED BY UNILATERAL PAINFUL, SUPPURATIVE INGUINAL LYMPHADENOPATHY.
- TREATMENT: INJ. BENZATHINE PENICILLIN 2.4 MILLION UNITS + TAB. AZITHROMYCIN 1 GM SINGLE DOSE
NOTE: IN THE SYNDROMIC APPROACH TO SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS, KIT ASSIGNMENT BASED ON THE
IDENTIFICATION OF A CLUSTER OF SYMPTOMS RATHER THAN MAKING AN ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS IS GIVEN EMPHASIS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH FEVER AND JOINT PAIN DEVELOPED PIGMENTATION ON THE NOSE AFTER A FEW DAYS OF
TAKING NSAIDS AS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL HISTORY OF FEVER AND JOINT PAIN AND THE IMAGE SHOWING HYPERPIGMENTED MACULES
ON NOSE (CHIK SIGN) IS SUGGESTIVE OF CHIKUNGUNYA.
POST-CHIKUNGUNYA PIGMENTATION (PCP) MOST COMMONLY AFFECTS THE NOSE AND CHEEKS. IT OFTEN
APPEARS AS THE FEVER SUBSIDES AND MAY PERSIST FOR ABOUT 3-6 MONTHS.
PCP MIMICS MELASMA AND MAY BE MISDIAGNOSED IF PROPER HISTORY IS NOT TAKEN.
ANOTHER CLOSE DIFFERENTIAL IS FIXED DRUG ERUPTIONS (FDE). FDE IS A TYPE OF DELAYED HYPERSENSITIVITY
REACTION. IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY WELL-DEFINED BROWN, HYPERPIGMENTED PLAQUES THAT MAY FOLLOW
VESICULOBULLOUS LESIONS. THEY OCCUR ON LIPS, HANDS, LEGS, FACE, GENITALIA, AND ORAL MUCOSA, AND CAN
CAUSE A BURNING SENSATION.THEY USUALLY PRESENT 30 MIN TO 8 H AFTER DRUG EXPOSURE AND RECUR AT THE
SAME LOCATION ON RE-EXPOSURE. NSAIDS, PARACETAMOL AND CO■TRIMOXAZOLE ARE THE MOST COMMON
3556
DRUGS CAUSING FDE.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: INDICATE WHICH CELL IS NOT PRESENT IN THE LAYER MARKED D.
questions.explanation:
THE LAYER MARKED AS D IS STRATUM BASALE. LANGERHAN'S CELLS ARE NOT PRESENT IN STRATUM BASALE.
LANGERHAN'S CELLS ARE PREDOMINANTLY PRESENT IN STRATUM SPINOSUM.
KERATINOCYTES, MELANOCYTES, AND MERKEL DISCS ARE ALL SEEN IN STRATUM BASALE:
(OPTION A) KERATINOCYTES ARE PREDOMINANT CELLS OF THE EPIDERMIS AND CONSTITUTE THE MAJORITY OF THE
STRATUM BASALE.
(OPTION B) MERKEL DISCS ARE TYPE 1 SLOW-ADAPTING TOUCH RECEPTORS.
3557
(OPTION C) MELANOCYTES ARE DENDRITIC CELLS WHICH ARE DERIVED FROM THE NEURAL CREST CELLS. THE
MELANOSOMES SYNTHESIZED BY THE MELANOCYTES MIGRATE TO THE ADJACENT KERATOCYTES THROUGH THE
DENDRITIC PROCESSES

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt: TOPICAL STEROIDS ARE MOST EFFECTIVE IN:
questions.explanation:
TOPICAL STEROIDS ARE THE DRUG OF CHOICE IN THE TREATMENT OF ECZEMATOUS DERMATITIS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
- STEROIDS CAUSE ATROPHY AND HENCE IS CONTRAINDICATED IN PATIENTS WITH DERMAL ATROPHY.
- HERPES INFECTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH IMMUNOSUPPRESSION SO STEROIDS ARE NOT USEFUL.
- ROUTINE STEROID USE NOT RECOMMENDED IN ROSEA AS IT CAN WORSEN THE CONDITION.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
YOU HAVE ORDERED A PATCH TEST FOR AN 8-YEAR-OLD BOY WITH A HISTORY OF ALLERGIC CONTACT
DERMATITIS. AFTER THE APPLICATION OF THE PATCH, WHEN SHOULD YOU ASK HIM TO RETURN FOR
REMOVAL?
questions.explanation:
IN PATCH TESTING, THE PATCH IS REMOVED AFTER 48 HOURS TO EXAMINE THE SITE OF REACTION.
PATCH TESTING IS A TEST TO DETECT SENSITIVITY TO A SPECIFIC ALLERGEN. A BATTERY OF SUSPECTED ALLERGENS IS
APPLIED TO THE PATIENT’S BACK UNDER OCCLUSIVE DRESSINGS OR PATCHES. IT IS ALLOWED TO REMAIN IN
CONTACT WITH THE SKIN FOR 48 HOURS.
- 48 HOURS: PATCH REMOVAL FOR INITIAL READING TO DETECT DELAYED HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION.
- 72-96 HOURS: FINAL READING DONE FOR CONFIRMATION.
NOTE: SINCE THE QUESTION IS REGARDING THE TIMING OF PATCH REMOVAL AND NOT REGARDING THE FINAL
DIAGNOSIS, 48 HOURS IS THE ANSWER.
3558

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WAS TREATED WITH STEROIDS FOR PSORIASIS. ON STOPPING THE TREATMENT, HE DEVELOPS
FEVER, MALAISE, AND LESION AS SEEN IN THE IMAGE PRESENTED BELOW. SPECIFY THE MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO POINTS TOWARDS THE DIAGNOSIS OF PUSTULAR PSORIASIS.
PUSTULAR PSORIASIS IS A TYPE OF PSORIASIS CHARACTERIZED BY TINY PUS-FILLED LESIONS (PUSTULES) HAVING A
CHARACTERISTIC LAKES OR SHEETS OF PUS APPEARANCE (SEEN IN THE IMAGE).
THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A HISTORY OF FEVER AND MALAISE ALONG WITH THE PRESENCE OF PUSTULES ON A
CIRCUMSCRIBED, FIERY RED, EDEMATOUS OR SCALING PLAQUE. THE PUS IS USUALLY STERILE. SUDDEN
WITHDRAWAL OF SYSTEMIC STEROIDS IS USUALLY THE TRIGGER FOR THIS CONDITION.
PUSTULAR PSORIASIS CAN BE DIVIDED INTO:
- LOCALIZED PUSTULAR PSORIASIS
- GENERALIZED PUSTULAR PSORIASIS:
- ACUTE GENERALIZED PUSTULAR PSORIASIS (VON ZUMBUSCH)
- SUBACUTE ANNULAR AND CIRCINATE PUSTULAR PSORIASIS
- ACUTE GENERALIZED PUSTULAR PSORIASIS OF PREGNANCY (IMPETIGO HERPETIFORMIS)
TREATMENT: ACITRETIN (ORAL RETINOID) IS THE DRUG OF CHOICE FOR PUSTULAR PSORIASIS. HOWEVER, IT IS
CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY. SYSTEMIC STEROIDS ARE USED INSTEAD. CYCLOSPORINE IS THE SECOND-LINE
DRUG.
NOTE: SYSTEMIC STEROIDS ARE NEVER USED FOR THE TREATMENT OF PSORIASIS EXCEPT IN THE CASE OF
IMPETIGO HERPETIFORMIS WHERE THEY ARE FIRST-LINE AGENTS.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH FLACCID BULLOUS LESIONS INVOLVING THE ORAL CAVITY AND THE SKIN. HE HAS
LESIONS AS DISPLAYED BELOW. ACANTHOLYTIC CELLS ARE SEEN ON TZANCK SMEAR. SPECIFY THE MOST
PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
FLACCID LESIONS, MUCOSAL INVOLVEMENT, AND THE PRESENCE OF ACANTHOLYTIC CELLS ARE SUGGESTIVE OF
PEMPHIGUS VULGARIS.
OPTION A: THERE IS NO MUCOSAL INVOLVEMENT IN PEMPHIGUS FOLIACEUS.
OPTION C: DERMATITIS HERPETIFORMIS PRESENTS WITH MULTIPLE SMALL VESICLES AND NO ACANTHOLYSIS.
OPTION D: BULLOUS PEMPHIGOID PRESENTS WITH TENSE BULLAE AND NO ACANTHOLYSIS.
