questions.prompt: A CHILD PRESENTS WITH CYANOSIS. HIS CHEST RADIOGRAPH IS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND CHEST X-RAY SHOWING A "COEUR EN SABOT" OR BOOT-SHAPED HEART ARE
SUGGESTIVE OF TETRALOGY OF FALLOT (TOF).
TOF IS A CYANOTIC CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE WITH THE FOLLOWING FOUR COMPONENTS:
- OBSTRUCTION TO RIGHT VENTRICULAR OUTFLOW (PULMONARY STENOSIS)
- MALALIGNMENT TYPE OF VENTRICULAR SEPTAL DEFECT (VSD)
- DEXTROPOSITION OF THE AORTA SO THAT IT OVERRIDES THE VENTRICULAR SEPTUM (OVERRIDING OF THE AORTA),
AND
- RIGHT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY (RVH)
IN TOF, THE HYPERTROPHIED RIGHT VENTRICLE CAUSES THE ROUNDED APICAL SHADOW TO BE UPTILTED SO THAT
IT IS SITUATED HIGHER ABOVE THE DIAPHRAGM THAN NORMAL. ON X-RAY, THIS APPEARS AS A BOOT-SHAPED
HEART OR COEUR EN SABOT, AS SHOWN BELOW:
3989
OPTION B: EBSTEIN ANOMALY IS A RARE CYANOTIC CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE WITH DIMINISHED PULMONARY
BLOOD FLOW DUE TO ABNORMALITY OF THE TRICUSPID VALVE.
IN THE EBSTEIN ANOMALY, THERE IS SEVERE RIGHT-SIDED CARDIOMEGALY DUE TO AN ELONGATED AND ENLARGED
RIGHT ATRIUM, WHICH LEADS TO AN ELEVATED APEX GIVING A BOX-SHAPED HEART, AS SHOWN BELOW:
OPTION C: TRANSPOSITION OF GREAT ARTERIES (TGA) CAN PRESENT FROM BIRTH TO INFANCY WITH CYANOSIS,
DECREASED EXERCISE TOLERANCE, AND POOR PHYSICAL DEVELOPMENT TGA IS THE MOST SPECIFIC HEART
DISEASE IN INFANTS OF DIABETIC MOTHERS.

APPEARANCE OF THE HEART:

CONNECTION OF PULMONARY VEINS INSTEAD OF JOINING TO THE LEFT ATRIUM RESULTING IN PULMONARY VENOUS

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
AN HIV PATIENT PRESENTED WITH A HEADACHE AND ALTERED SENSORIUM. CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING
STATEMENTS AND IDENTIFY THE ESSENTIAL CRITERIA FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE MRI BRAIN LABELED AS B SHOWS MULTIPLE CYSTICERCI WITHIN THE BRAIN
SUGGESTING NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS. AMONG THE GIVEN STATEMENTS, THE ESSENTIAL CRITERIA FOR THE DIAGNOSIS
OF NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS INCLUDE 1 AND 4 (OPTION B), I.E.,
- BRAIN BIOPSY SHOWING THE PARASITE.
3991
- NEURORADIOLOGIC DEMONSTRATION OF CYSTIC LESIONS WITH SCOLEX (MRI LABELED B IN THIS CASE).
NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS IS A CONDITION CAUSED BY THE LARVAE OF TAENIA SOLIUM.
CRITERIA FOR DIAGNOSIS OF NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS:
1. ABSOLUTE CRITERIA
- DEMONSTRATION OF CYSTICERCI BY HISTOLOGIC OR MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION OF A BIOPSY TAKEN FROM THE
BRAIN OR SPINAL CORD LESION.
- VISUALIZATION OF THE PARASITE IN THE EYE BY FUNDUSCOPY
- NEURORADIOLOGIC DEMONSTRATION OF CYSTIC LESIONS CONTAINING A CHARACTERISTIC SCOLEX
2. NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA
- MAJOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA: CYSTIC LESIONS WITHOUT A DISCERNIBLE SCOLEX, MULTILOBULATED CYSTIC
LESIONS IN THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE, TYPICAL SMALL ENHANCING LESIONS, TYPICAL PARENCHYMAL BRAIN
CALCIFICATIONS
- CONFIRMATIVE NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA: RESOLUTION OF CYSTIC LESIONS SPONTANEOUSLY OR AFTER CYSTICIDAL
DRUG THERAPY AND MIGRATION OF VENTRICULAR CYSTS DOCUMENTED ON SEQUENTIAL NEUROIMAGING STUDIES
- MINOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA: OBSTRUCTIVE HYDROCEPHALUS OR ABNORMAL ENHANCEMENT OF BASAL
LEPTOMENINGES
3. CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA
- MAJOR CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA: DEMONSTRATION OF ANTIBODIES TO CYSTICERCI OR CYSTICERCI ANTIGEN IN
CEREBROSPINAL FLUID BY ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY; HOUSEHOLD CONTACT WITH AN INDIVIDUAL
INFECTED WITH T. SOLIUM; EVIDENCE OF CYSTICERCOSIS OUTSIDE THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (E.G.,
CIGAR-SHAPED SOFT-TISSUE CALCIFICATIONS)
- MINOR CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA: CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS SUGGESTIVE OF NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS;
RESIDENCE IN A CYSTICERCOSIS-ENDEMIC AREA; FREQUENT TRAVEL TO A CYSTICERCOSIS-ENDEMIC AREA
DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED BY:
- ONE ABSOLUTE CRITERION
- TWO MAJOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA PLUS ANY CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA
- ONE MAJOR AND ONE CONFIRMATIVE NEUROIMAGING CRITERION PLUS ANY CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA
- ONE MAJOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERIA PLUS TWO CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA (INCLUDING AT LEAST ONE MAJOR
CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERION), WITH THE EXCLUSION OF OTHER PATHOLOGIES PRODUCING SIMILAR
NEUROIMAGING FINDINGS
A PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS IS SUPPORTED BY THE FULFILLMENT OF
- ONE MAJOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERION PLUS ANY TWO CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERIA
- ONE MINOR NEUROIMAGING CRITERION PLUS AT LEAST ONE MAJOR CLINICAL/EXPOSURE CRITERION
OTHER OPTIONS: THE MRI LABELED AS A SHOWS VENTRICULOMEGALY IN BRAIN ATROPHY.

HYDATID DISEASE OR ECHINOCOCCOSIS IS A ZOONOTIC INFECTION CAUSED BY THE ECHINOCOCCUS SPECIES
OF FLATWORMS. ITS LIFE CYCLE CONSISTS OF DOGS AS DEFINITIVE HOSTS AND HUMANS AS ACCIDENTAL
INTERMEDIATE HOSTS.
PRIMARY HYDATID CYSTS MOST COMMONLY OCCUR IN THE LIVER. MOST PATIENTS ARE ASYMPTOMATIC BUT
WHEN SYMPTOMATIC, THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH HEPATOMEGALY, PAIN, AND OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE.
THE FIRST/INITIAL IMAGING TEST IS USG, AND CT SCAN CAN BE USED TO DIAGNOSE THE CONDITION.
CT SCAN SHOWS THE PRESENCE OF A SPACE-OCCUPYING LESION WITH A SMOOTH OUTLINE AND SEPTA. CT SCAN
HAS AN ACCURACY OF 98% IN THE DETECTION OF HYDATID CYSTS AND HIGH SENSITIVITY TO THE DETECTION OF
DAUGHTER CYSTS AND EXTRA-HEPATIC CYSTS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHOLE-BODY CT SCAN PROTOCOL FOR A TRAUMA PATIENT INCLUDES ALL, EXCEPT ______.
questions.explanation:
THE WHOLE-BODY CT OF A TRAUMA PATIENT DOES NOT INCLUDE CT LIMBS.
WHOLE-BODY CT OR TRAUMA CT OR PANSCAN IS INCREASINGLY BEING USED IN THE CONTEXT OF TRAUMA
PATIENTS WITH A DANGEROUS MECHANISM OF INJURY:
- NON-CONTRAST CT OF HEAD
- NON-CONTRAST CT OF NECK
- CONTRAST-ENHANCED CT OF CHEST (ARTERIAL PHASE)
3999
- CONTRAST-ENHANCED CT OF ABDOMEN (PORTAL VENOUS PHASE)
THE PURPOSE OF THE SCAN IS TO RAPIDLY EVALUATE LIFE-THREATENING INJURIES AND ACCURATELY DIAGNOSE
KNOWN AND UNKNOWN INJURIES.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH HEMATURIA AND A MASS IN THE RIGHT KIDNEY ON A CT SCAN, AS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE CT IMAGE SHOWING RENAL LESIONS THAT HAS HYPO-ATTENUATING COMPONENTS CONSISTENT WITH
MACROSCOPIC FAT IS HIGHLY SUGGESTIVE OF RENAL ANGIOMYOLIPOMA.
ANGIOMYOLIPOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS THAT OCCUR SPORADICALLY OR IN ASSOCIATION WITH TUBEROUS
SCLEROSIS. THE MEAN AGE OF PRESENTATION IS 43 YEARS AND THERE IS A FEMALE PREDILECTION. IT CAN
PRESENT AS SPONTANEOUS RETROPERITONEAL HEMORRHAGE, ESPECIALLY WITH LARGER TUMORS. THE PATIENT
CAN PRESENT WITH FLANK PAIN, PALPABLE MASS, HEMATURIA, URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS, HYPERTENSION, OR
RENAL FAILURE.
IMAGING IN RENAL ANGIOMYOLIPOMA: DEMONSTRATION OF MACROSCOPIC FAT IS THE MAIN PART OF MAKING A
DIAGNOSIS. USG MAY SHOW HYPERECHOIC LESIONS IN THE CORTEX WITH POSTERIOR ACOUSTIC SHADOWING. IN
PATIENTS WITH TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS, THE ENTIRE KIDNEY IS AFFECTED AND PRODUCES AN ECHOGENIC
APPEARANCE WITH LOSS OF NORMAL CORTICOMEDULLARY JUNCTION.
CT FINDINGS:
- CORTICAL LESIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE MACROSCOPIC FAT (LESS THAN -20 HU)
- ABSENCE OF OSSIFICATION OR CALCIFICATION
- THE PRESENCE OF MACROSCOPIC FAT IS STRONGLY SUGGESTIVE OF THIS CONDITION, BUT NOT PATHOGNOMONIC
AS RCC MAY RARELY DEMONSTRATE MACROSCOPIC FAT.
- APPROXIMATELY 5% MAY BE FAT-POOR.
MRI: IT IS AN EXCELLENT TOOL TO DEMONSTRATE INTRAMURAL FAT COMPONENTS. TWO SEQUENCES ARE USED:
- FAT-SATURATED TECHNIQUES
- PHASE-IN AND PHASE-OUT IMAGING THAT SHOWS INDIA INK ARTIFACTS AT THE JUNCTION BETWEEN FAT AND
NON-FAT COMPONENTS.
DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY: THEY ARE HYPERVASCULAR LESIONS SHOWING A 'SUNBURST APPEARANCE'
IN THE ARTERIAL PHASE AND AN 'ONION PEEL APPEARANCE' IN THE VENOUS PHASE.
THEY USUALLY DO NOT REQUIRE ANY INTERVENTION. MTOR INHIBITORS LIKE EVEROLIMUS CAN BE USED TO
DECREASE THE SIZE OF THE LESION.
4000
OTHER OPTIONS:
RENAL CELL CARCINOMA (RCC): IT IS THE MOST COMMON MALIGNANT TUMOR OF THE KIDNEY. IT USUALLY
OCCURS IN THE AGE GROUP 50-70 YEARS AND MACROSCOPIC HEMATURIA IS SEEN IN ABOUT 60% OF THE CASES.
IT IS A DIFFERENTIAL FOR ANGIOMYOLIPOMA BUT IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT MACROSCOPIC FAT IS ALMOST
ALWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH OSSIFICATION OR CALCIFICATION.
RENAL ONCOCYTOMA: THEY ARE RELATIVELY BENIGN IN NATURE AND USUALLY PRESENT IN THE 6TH TO 7TH
DECADE. AN IMPORTANT POINT REGARDING THIS TUMOR IS ITS SIMILARITY WITH RCC AND HENCE IT IS VERY
DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THEM PREOPERATIVELY. A SHARP CENTRAL STELLATE SCAR MAY BE SEEN IN
ONE-THIRD OF THE CASES. BUT RCC MAY ALSO SHOW THIS STELLATE SCAR APPEARANCE IN SOME CASES.
4001
RENAL CYST: IT IS A BROADER TERM THAT INCLUDES THE CYSTIC LESIONS OF THE KIDNEY. THEY CAN BE SIMPLE
CYSTS THAT ARE BENIGN. COMPLEX OR COMPLICATED CYSTIC LESIONS NEEDS EVALUATION AND CAN BE
MALIGNANT. BOSNIAK CLASSIFICATION OF RENAL CYSTS IS GIVEN ABOVE.

questions.prompt: EGG SHELL CALCIFICATION IS SEEN IN ALL THESE, EXCEPT _______.
questions.explanation:
EGGSHELL CALCIFICATION IS NOT SEEN IN THE CASE OF METASTATIC LYMPH NODES.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A 55-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTS WITH HEMATURIA AND A MASS IN THE LEFT KIDNEY ON A CECT SCAN, AS
DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE HISTORY OF AN ELDERLY MALE PRESENTING WITH PAINLESS HEMATURIA, RENAL MASS, AND AN AXIAL RENAL
CORTICAL PHASE CECT IMAGE SHOWING RENAL LESIONS WITH IRREGULAR ENHANCEMENT IS SUGGESTIVE OF
RENAL CELL CARCINOMA (RCC).
RENAL CELL CARCINOMA (RCC) IS THE MOST COMMON MALIGNANT TUMOR OF THE KIDNEY. IT USUALLY OCCURS
IN THE AGE GROUP 50–70 YEARS AND MACROSCOPIC HEMATURIA IS SEEN IN ABOUT 60% OF THE CASES. IT
USUALLY PRESENTS WITH PAINLESS GROSS HEMATURIA, FLANK PAIN, OR PAINLESS FLANK MASS.
CONTRAST-ENHANCED CT IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR RCC. ON CT, SMALL LESIONS ENHANCE
HOMOGENEOUSLY, WHEREAS LARGER LESIONS HAVE IRREGULAR ENHANCEMENT DUE TO AREAS OF NECROSIS. THE
CLEAR CELL SUBTYPE MAY SHOW MUCH STRONGER ENHANCEMENT IS A DIFFERENTIAL FOR ANGIOMYOLIPOMA.
STILL, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO NOTE THAT MACROSCOPIC FAT IS ALMOST ALWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH OSSIFICATION OR
CALCIFICATION.
T1-WEIGHTED MRI IS OFTEN HETEROGENEOUS DUE TO NECROSIS, HEMORRHAGE, AND SOLID
COMPONENTS. T2-WEIGHTED MRI IS HYPERDENSE FOR CLEAR CELL RCC AND HYPODENSE FOR PAPILLARY RCC.
THUS, A T2-WEIGHTED MRI CAN BE USED FOR HISTOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS. CONTRAST-ENHANCED MRI IS THE
INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR DETECTING VASCULAR INVASION OF RCC.
4003
OTHER OPTIONS:
RENAL ANGIOMYOLIPOMA: ANGIOMYOLIPOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS THAT OCCUR SPORADICALLY OR IN
ASSOCIATION WITH TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS. THE MEAN AGE OF PRESENTATION IS 43 YEARS, AND THERE IS A
FEMALE PREDILECTION. CT FINDINGS SHOW CORTICAL LESIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE MACROSCOPIC FAT (LESS THAN
-20 HU) AND ABSENCE OF OSSIFICATION OR CALCIFICATION.
RENAL ONCOCYTOMA: THEY ARE RELATIVELY BENIGN IN NATURE AND USUALLY PRESENT IN THE 6TH TO 7TH
DECADE. AN IMPORTANT POINT REGARDING THIS TUMOR IS ITS SIMILARITY WITH RCC, AND HENCE, IT IS VERY
DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THEM PREOPERATIVELY. A SHARP CENTRAL STELLATE SCAR MAY BE SEEN IN
ONE-THIRD OF THE CASES. BUT RCC MAY ALSO SHOW THIS STELLATE SCAR APPEARANCE IN SOME CASES.
4004
RENAL CYST: IT IS A BROADER TERM THAT INCLUDES THE CYSTIC LESIONS OF THE KIDNEY. THEY CAN BE SIMPLE
CYSTS THAT ARE BENIGN. COMPLEX OR COMPLICATED CYSTIC LESIONS NEEDS EVALUATION AND CAN BE
MALIGNANT. BOSNIAK CLASSIFICATION OF RENAL CYSTS IS GIVEN ABOVE.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WHO WAS DIAGNOSED WITH PROSTATE CANCER IS BEING INVESTIGATED. THE BONE SCAN IS
REPORTED AS A SUPER SCAN WITH INCREASED UPTAKE IN THE BONES AND REDUCED ACTIVITY IN THE
KIDNEY AND SOFT TISSUE. SPECIFY THE REASON FOR THIS SUPER SCAN APPEARANCE.
options: INCREASED UPTAKE DUE TO DIFFUSE METASTASIS
DECREASED UPTAKE BY ADRENAL GLANDS AND KIDNEY
questions.answer: INCREASED UPTAKE DUE TO DIFFUSE METASTASIS
questions.explanation:
THE SUPER SCAN APPEARANCE IS DUE TO INCREASED UPTAKE DUE TO DIFFUSE METASTASIS.
DIFFUSE OSTEOBLASTIC METASTATIC DISEASES SUCH AS CARCINOMA BREAST AND PROSTATE CARCINOMA LEAD TO A
GENERALIZED INCREASE IN THE SKELETAL UPTAKE RELATIVE TO SOFT TISSUE AND ABSENT OR FAINT RENAL ACTIVITY
ON A BONE SCAN. THIS IS KNOWN AS A SUPER SCAN. IT MAY ALSO BE SEEN IN GENERALIZED BONE DISEASES
SUCH AS HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.
CARCINOMA OF THE PROSTATE IS THE MOST COMMON MALIGNANT TUMOR IN MEN OVER THE AGE OF 65 YEARS.
MOST CANCERS ARE CLINICALLY SILENT AND ARE DETECTED ON ROUTINE RECTAL EXAMINATION OR PSA
MEASUREMENTS. GROSSLY, MALIGNANT TISSUE IS GRITTY AND FIRM IN CONSISTENCY (IN CONTRAST TO THE
SPONGY APPEARANCE OF BENIGN TISSUE) AND THUS MORE READILY PALPABLE ON DIGITAL RECTAL
EXAMINATION. THEY USUALLY ARISE IN THE PERIPHERAL ZONE OF THE GLAND.
LOCAL EXTENSION MOST COMMONLY INVOLVES THE PERIPROSTATIC TISSUE, SEMINAL VESICLES, AND THE BASE OF
THE URINARY BLADDER. METASTASIS SPREADS VIA THE LYMPHATICS TO THE OBTURATOR NODES AND THE
PARA-AORTIC NODES. HEMATOGENOUS SPREAD OCCURS CHIEFLY THROUGH THE BONES TO THE AXIAL
SKELETON AND RARELY TO THE VISCERA. THE BONY METASTASIS IS BLASTIC IN ORIGIN AND INVOLVES THE LUMBAR
SPINE, PROXIMAL FEMUR, PELVIS, THORACIC SPINE, AND RIBS IN DECREASING ORDER OF FREQUENCY.
PROGNOSIS AND STAGING: THE GLEASON GRADING SYSTEM CORRELATES WITH THE PATHOLOGICAL STAGE, SPREAD,
AND PROGNOSIS. MEASUREMENT OF SERUM PSA LEVELS MAY BE USEFUL TO ASSIST WITH THE DIAGNOSIS AND
MANAGEMENT.
4006

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE IMAGING MODALITY PROVIDED BELOW.
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE IMAGING MODALITY IS A PET CT SCAN.
PET (POSITRON-EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY) CT SCAN IS A HYBRID TECHNIQUE THAT COMBINES PET AND CT
SCAN THAT IS USED FOR TARGETED IMAGING OF TUMOR PHYSIOLOGY AND BIOLOGY. IT IS BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE
THAT TUMOR CELLS GENERALLY HAVE HIGH METABOLIC ACTIVITY COMPARED WITH NORMAL TISSUES.
A SMALL DOSE OF THE RADIOPHARMACEUTICAL AGENT 18F-FLUORODEOXYGLUCOSE (FDG). THIS ENTERS CELLS
AND IS PHOSPHORYLATED TO FDG 6-PHOSPHATE WHICH CANNOT BE METABOLIZED FURTHER. SINCE IT IS A
HIGHLY POLAR MOLECULE, IT CANNOT EASILY DIFFUSE BACK OUT OF THE CELL. AFTER INTRAVENOUS INJECTION OF
4008
FDG, IT CONTINUOUSLY ACCUMULATES IN THE METABOLICALLY ACTIVE CELL.
THE MAIN ADVANTAGE OF PET-CT IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF DISTANT METASTATIC DISEASE NOT SEEN ON CT
ALONE. THE DISADVANTAGES OF PET SCANS ARE RADIATION BURDEN, POORER SPATIAL RESOLUTION WHEN USED
ALONE, AND HIGH COST.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW SCAN REFERS TO THE PERFUSION MRI THAT USES GADOLINIUM AS CONTRAST
AND PROVIDES INFORMATION ABOUT THE CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW AND VOLUME.
OPTION B: THE SESTAMIBI SCAN IS USED FOR PARATHYROID LOCALIZATION AND IS NOW CONSIDERED THE MOST
ACCURATE AND RELIABLE METHOD FOR IMAGING THE PARATHYROID GLANDS. SESTAMIBI ACCUMULATES IN
MITOCHONDRIA. PARATHYROID ADENOMAS OFTEN HAVE A HIGH CONCENTRATION OF OXYPHILIC CELLS WITH HIGH
MITOCHONDRIAL CONTENT. THESE RETAIN SESTAMIBI TRACER AND ADENOMAS ARE THEREFORE ASSOCIATED WITH
A SLOW WASHOUT WHEN COMPARED WITH THE THYROID GLAND.
OPTION D: THE FULL BODY MDCT SCAN REFERS TO THE MULTIDETECTOR CT SCAN WHICH IS AN ADVANCED CT
IMAGING TECHNIQUE THAT USES MULTIPLE DETECTOR ELEMENTS THAT PROVIDE IMPROVEMENT IN SPEED,
QUALITY, AND SCOPE.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT IS BROUGHT TO THE CASUALTY FOLLOWING A ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT. UPON EXAMINATION, THE
PATIENT IS CONSCIOUS, BP IS 90/60 MM HG, RESPIRATORY RATE IS 40 BREATHS PER MINUTE, AND PULSE
RATE IS 120 BPM. THE X-RAY IS DISPLAYED BELOW. SPECIFY THE NEXT BEST STEP IN MANAGEMENT.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN X-RAY FEATURES SHOWING A WELL-DEMARCATED AREA DEVOID OF LUNG MARKINGS ON THE LEFT SIDE
WITH TRACHEAL DEVIATION AND THE MEDIASTINAL SHIFT TO THE RIGHT SIDE, ALONG WITH THE CLINICAL
SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX. THE NEXT BEST STEP IN THE MANAGEMENT IS CHEST
TUBE INSERTION.
TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX IS A CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT SHOULD NEVER BE DELAYED WHILE
WAITING FOR RADIOLOGICAL CONFIRMATION. IMAGING MODALITIES USED ARE ULTRASOUND–EXTENDED FOCUSED
ASSESSMENT WITH SONAR FOR TRAUMA (EFAST), CHEST X-RAY, AND SPIRAL CT.
A TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX DEVELOPS WHEN THERE IS A TEAR EITHER IN THE PARIETAL OR VISCERAL PLEURA.
THIS TEAR ACTS AS A ONE-WAY VALVE I.E., AIR ENTERS FROM THE LUNG OR CHEST WALL THROUGH IT DURING
INSPIRATION BUT HAS NO WAY TO ESCAPE DURING EXPIRATION. THIS ULTIMATELY LEADS TO THE COLLAPSE OF
THE AFFECTED LUNG.
IT USUALLY OCCURS FOLLOWING PENETRATING OR BLUNT CHEST TRAUMA, IATROGENIC LUNG INJURY, OR
MECHANICAL POSITIVE PRESSURE VENTILATION.
IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY:
- CHEST PAIN
- TACHYPNEA AND ACUTE DYSPNEA
- SUDDEN ONSET HEMODYNAMIC COMPROMISE (TACHYCARDIA, HYPOTENSION, LOW O2 SATURATION, LOSS OF
CONSCIOUSNESS)
- NECK VEIN DISTENTION
- TRACHEAL DEVIATION AWAY FROM THE SIDE OF THE INJURY
- DECREASED CHEST MOVEMENTS ON THE AFFECTED SIDE
4009
- HYPER-RESONANCE ON PERCUSSION ON THE AFFECTED SIDE
- ABSENCE OR DECREASED BREATH SOUNDS ON THE AFFECTED SIDE
THE X-RAY BELOW SHOWS A LEFT-SIDED TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX. THERE IS A LARGE, WELL-DEMARCATED AREA
DEVOID OF LUNG MARKINGS ON THE LEFT SIDE. THE YELLOW ARROWS ARE POINTING TO THE TRACHEAL DEVIATION
AND THE MEDIASTINAL SHIFT TO THE RIGHT SIDE.
MANAGEMENT OF TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX:
- IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT- NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION OR NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY I.E. INSERTION OF A
WIDE-BORE NEEDLE IN THE 5TH ICS ANTERIOR TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE
- DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT- TUBE THORACOSTOMY OR CHEST TUBE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS IN THE TRIANGLE
OF SAFETY, IDENTIFIED AS A TRIANGLE THAT LIES ANTERIOR TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE ABOVE THE NIPPLE, BELOW,
AND LATERAL TO THE PECTORALIS MAJOR MUSCLE.
THE IMAGES BELOW SHOW THE TRIANGLE OF SAFETY AND TECHNIQUE OF CHEST DRAIN INSERTION.
4010
OTHER OPTIONS:
- PERICARDIOCENTESIS IS DONE IN CASES OF CARDIAC TAMPONADE WHICH IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE PRESENCE
OF HYPOTENSION, DISTENDED JUGULAR VEINS, AND MUFFLED HEART SOUNDS (BECK'S TRIAD). THE BREATH
SOUNDS ARE ABSENT IN TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX WHILE THEY ARE PRESENT IN CARDIAC TAMPONADE.
- SURGERY FOR PNEUMOTHORAX CAN BE PERFORMED BY VIDEO-ASSISTED THORACOSCOPIC SURGERY (VATS) OR
AS AN OPEN PROCEDURE (THORACOTOMY) IN CASES OF SPONTANEOUS PNEUMOTHORAX FAILING TO SETTLE
DESPITE CHEST DRAINAGE. PLEURAL ADHESION IS ACHIEVED BY CHEMICAL PLEURODESIS WHERE TALC IS USED
AND IS INSUFFLATED INTO THE CHEST CAVITY.
4011

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH DYSURIA AND PAIN IN THE BACK. HIS LUMBAR SPINE X-RAY SHOWS THE
BELOW FINDING. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND X-RAY SHOWING DIFFUSE CALCIFICATION OF BOTH KIDNEYS ARE SUGGESTIVE
OF NEPHROCALCINOSIS WHICH IS SEEN IN HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.
NEPHROCALCINOSIS IS THE DEPOSITION OF CALCIUM IN THE KIDNEY PARENCHYMA OR TUBULES WHICH IS SEEN
IN CONDITIONS CAUSING HYPERCALCEMIA LIKE HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF HYPERPARATHYROIDISM:
- BONES:
- PATHOLOGICAL FRACTURES
- SUBPERIOSTEAL BONE RESORPTION - 2ND AND 3RD DIGITS, MOST COMMON IN THE RADIAL ASPECT
- SALT AND PEPPER SKULL
- OSTEITIS FIBROSA CYSTICA OR VONRECKLING HAUSEN’S DISEASE OF BONE
- STONES
- MULTIPLE AND RECURRENT RENAL STONES - MOST COMMON
- NEPHROCALCINOSIS
- ABDOMINAL GROANS - COLICKY DUE TO PANCREATITIS
- PSYCHIATRIC OVERTONES - RAISED PTH CAUSING CNS DEPRESSION AND PSYCHIATRIC SYMPTOMS
- BAND KERATOPATHY
- FEATURES OF HYPERCALCEMIA -
- VOMITING
- CONFUSION
- ECG CHANGES: INCREASED PR INTERVAL, SHORTENED QT INTERVAL
INVESTIGATIONS DONE IN PRIMARY HYPERPARATHYROIDISM:
- ULTRASONOGRAPHY OF THE NECK IS A SAFE AND WIDELY USED TECHNIQUE FOR THE LOCALIZATION OF ABNORMAL
PARATHYROID GLANDS.
- NUCLEAR MEDICINE SCANNING WITH RADIOLABELED SESTAMIBI IS ALSO A WIDELY USED TECHNIQUE.
SESTAMIBI ACCUMULATES IN PARATHYROID ADENOMAS. THIS RADIONUCLIDE IS CONCENTRATED IN THE THYROID
AND PARATHYROID TISSUE BUT USUALLY WASHES OUT OF NORMAL THYROID TISSUE IN UNDER AN HOUR. IT
PERSISTS IN ABNORMAL PARATHYROID TISSUE.
- DUAL-ENERGY RADIOGRAPHIC ABSORPTIOMETRY IS A USEFUL TOOL TO DEMONSTRATE SKELETAL INVOLVEMENT IN
PRIMARY HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.
4025

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE FINDING IN THE GIVEN ULTRASOUND IMAGE.
questions.explanation:
THE ULTRASOUND EXAMINATION OF THE GALLBLADDER SHOWS A PHRYGIAN CAP. IT IS A NORMAL ANATOMICAL
VARIANT.
PHRYGIAN CAP REFERS TO AN ANATOMICAL VARIANT OF THE GALLBLADDER, WHERE, THE FUNDUS OF THE
GALLBLADDER FOLDS ON ITSELF, OR IS SEPARATED FROM THE BODY BY A PARTIAL OR COMPLETE SEPTUM. A TRUE
SEPTUM IS UNCOMMON AND IS USUALLY AN APPARENT SEPTUM DUE TO THE GALLBLADDER WALL FOLDING. IT IS
AN INCIDENTAL FINDING THAT MAY BE SEEN ON CT, MRI, OR ULTRASOUND. IT CAUSES NO SYMPTOMS.
THE PHRYGIAN CAP IS NAMED SO, DUE TO THE RESEMBLANCE OF THE ULTRASONOGRAPHIC APPEARANCE TO A
HAT OR CAP THAT IS WORN BY THE INHABITANTS OF ANCIENT PHRYGIA CIRCA 1200 BC.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: BANANA SIGN ON USG IS ASSOCIATED WITH WHICH OF THESE CONDITIONS?

THE BANANA SIGN ON USG IS SEEN IN SPINA BIFIDA.
BANANA SIGN IS AN ABNORMAL ANTERIOR CURVATURE OF THE CEREBELLUM ALONG WITH EFFACEMENT OF THE
CISTERNA MAGNA THAT PRODUCES THIS APPEARANCE. IT IS SEEN IN SPINA BIFIDA AND IS ALSO ASSOCIATED
WITH ARNOLD-CHIARI MALFORMATION.
SPINA BIFIDA IS A CONGENITAL ANOMALY OCCURRING DUE TO INCOMPLETE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NEURAL TUBE.
THE MOST COMMONLY CITED SIGNS PRESENT IN SPINA BIFIDA ARE THE BANANA SIGN AND THE LEMON SIGN.
THE LEMON SIGN OCCURS DUE TO THE OVERLAPPING OF THE FRONTAL BONES DUE TO THE POSTERIOR SHIFT OF
INTRACRANIAL CONTENTS AS SHOWN BELOW.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: OMPHALOCELE IS A CONGENITAL MIDLINE ANTERIOR ABDOMINAL WALL DEFECT THROUGH WHICH THE
SOLID ABDOMINAL VISCERA OR BOWEL HERNIATES. THE HERNIATED ABDOMINAL CONTENTS ARE COVERED BY A

THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS AN ULTRASOUND IMAGE OF THE FETUS SUGGESTIVE OF AN OMPHALOCELE (ASTERISK).
OPTION C: NUCHAL TRANSLUCENCY (NT) IS USED TO ANTENATALLY SCREEN DOWNS SYNDROME (TRISOMY 21)
DURING THE FIRST TRIMESTER. NT IS THE MAXIMUM THICKNESS OF THE TRANSLUCENT AREA BETWEEN THE SKIN
AND SOFT TISSUE OVER THE FETAL SPINE AT THE BACK OF THE NECK. WHEN THE NT MEASUREMENT IS

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE IS NOT AN ADVANTAGE OF USG OVER MAMMOGRAPHY?
options: CAN BE USED FOR SCREENING MAMMOGRAPHICALLY UNDETECTABLE CLINICALLY NON PALPABLE BREAST MASS
USEFUL IN YOUNG FEMALES WITH DENSE BREAST
DIFFERENTIATES BETWEEN SOLID AND CYSTIC LESIONS IN THE BREAST
questions.answer: CAN BE USED FOR SCREENING MAMMOGRAPHICALLY UNDETECTABLE CLINICALLY NON PALPABLE BREAST MASS
questions.explanation:
USG CANNOT BE USED FOR SCREENING MAMMOGRAPHICALLY UNDETECTABLE CLINICALLY NONPALPABLE BREAST
MASS. ALTHOUGH ULTRASOUND HAS ITS ADVANTAGES IN CERTAIN SCENARIOS, MAMMOGRAPHY REMAINS THE
PRIMARY SCREENING TOOL FOR BREAST TUMOR DETECTION.
MAMMOGRAPHY IS COMPLEMENTARY TO PHYSICAL EXAMINATION AND CAN DETECT CLINICALLY NON-PALPABLE
BREAST MASS. THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF MAMMOGRAPHY IS TO DETECT SMALL BREAST TUMORS. WHILE
MAMMOGRAPHY IS TYPICALLY THE INITIAL SCREENING TOOL FOR BREAST CANCER DETECTION, THERE ARE SPECIFIC
SCENARIOS WHERE ULTRASOUND MAY BE PREFERRED OR USED IN CONJUNCTION WITH MAMMOGRAPHY.
ADVANTAGES OF USG OVER MAMMOGRAPHY INCLUDE:
- USG IS PREFERRED IN PREGNANT WOMEN, LACTATING WOMEN, AND YOUNG WOMEN SINCE BREAST TISSUE IS
DENSE (OPTION B) IN THESE POPULATIONS.
- USG CAN DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN SOLID AND CYSTIC LESIONS (OPTION C) OF THE BREAST AND IS ABLE TO
DETECT ABNORMAL AXILLARY LYMPH NODES.
- ULTRASOUND CAN ASSIST IN GUIDED BREAST BIOPSY (OPTION D) PROCEDURES.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: AN MRCP IMAGE IS DISPLAYED BELOW. WHICH AMONG THESE IS THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN MRCP IMAGE SHOWS MULTIPLE ROUND FILLING DEFECTS WITHIN THE COMMON BILE DUCT
INDICATIVE OF CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS.
CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS OR COMMON BILE DUCT STONES ARE CLASSIFIED BASED ON THEIR POINT OF ORIGIN.
CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS IS MOSTLY CLINICALLY SILENT BUT MAY PRESENT WITH BILIARY COLIC AND EVEN
OBSTRUCTIVE JAUNDICE. MANAGEMENT OF CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS INCLUDES ERCP +/- SPHINCTEROTOMY
FOLLOWED BY LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY.
4030
MRCP USES THE FLUID WHICH IS PRESENT IN THE BILIARY AND PANCREATIC DUCTS AS A CONTRAST AGENT AND
DOES NOT REQUIRE EXTERNAL CONTRAST MATERIAL ADMINISTERED INTO THE DUCTAL SYSTEM. IT IS
A NON-INVASIVE INVESTIGATION FOR EVALUATING EXTRAHEPATIC, INTRAHEPATIC BILE DUCT, AND PANCREATIC
DUCT. NO INTERVENTIONS ARE PERFORMED UNDER MRCP.
MRCP USES T2 WEIGHTED MRI AND IT RECOGNIZES SLOW-FLOWING OR STATIONARY FLUID WITHIN DUCTS,
WHICH APPEAR BRIGHTER RELATIVE TO ADJACENT SOLID TISSUES. MRCP CAN BE USED TO EVALUATE VARIOUS
CONDITIONS OF THE PANCREATICOBILIARY DUCTAL SYSTEM, EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
- CONGENITAL ANOMALIES OF THE CYSTIC AND HEPATIC DUCTS
- POST-SURGICAL BILIARY ANATOMY
- PANCREAS DIVISUM
- ANOMALOUS PANCREATICOBILIARY JUNCTION
- CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS
- BILIARY STRUCTURES
- CHRONIC PANCREATITIS
- PANCREATIC CYSTIC LESIONS
- TRAUMA TO THE BILIARY SYSTEM
MRCP IN BENIGN STRICTURES WOULD TYPICALLY SHOW SMOOTH ELONGATED TAPERING OF THE BILE DUCT, WHILE
MALIGNANCY-ASSOCIATED STRICTURES TYPICALLY SHOW ABRUPT SHOULDERING.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A CHILD WAS BROUGHT TO THE EMERGENCY WITH DROOLING AND CHOKING FOLLOWING INGESTION OF A
FOREIGN BODY. BASED ON THE PROVIDED X-RAY, WHAT OBJECT WAS MOST LIKELY SWALLOWED BY THE CHILD?
options: CAP OF A COOL DRINK BOTTLE
questions.explanation:
THE PRESENCE OF A HALO SIGN OR DOUBLE RING SIGN IS INDICATIVE OF THE FOREIGN BODY BEING A BUTTON
BATTERY. FURTHERMORE, THE PRESENCE OF IRREGULARITIES ALONG THE PERIPHERY OF THE BATTERY INDICATES
THE POSSIBILITY OF CORROSION.
BUTTON BATTERIES AND SHARP OBJECTS IN THE OESOPHAGUS AND FOREIGN BODIES ASSOCIATED WITH
RESPIRATORY SYMPTOMS ALL MANDATE URGENT ENDOSCOPIC REMOVAL.
BUTTON BATTERIES, IN PARTICULAR, ARE VERY DANGEROUS FOREIGN BODIES, WHICH MUST BE EXPEDIENTLY
REMOVED BECAUSE THEY CAN CAUSE:
- MUCOSAL INJURY IN 1-HOUR CONTACT TIME
- INVOLVE ALL LAYERS OF THE OESOPHAGUS IN 4 HOURS
INJURY IS THOUGHT TO BE SECONDARY TO ELECTROCHEMICAL BURNS FROM ELECTRICAL DISCHARGE. CHEMICAL
BURNS FROM ELECTROLYTE ALKALI LEAKAGE AND PRESSURE NECROSIS ALSO MAY CONTRIBUTE TO MUCOSAL INJURY.
ASYMPTOMATIC BLUNT OBJECTS AND COINS LODGED IN THE OESOPHAGUS CAN BE OBSERVED FOR UP TO 24 HR
IN ANTICIPATION OF PASSAGE INTO THE STOMACH.
ANOTHER AP AND LATERAL X-RAY DEMONSTRATING THE PRESENCE OF A BUTTON BATTERY IN THE OESOPHAGUS IS
AS SHOWN BELOW.
4032
4033

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A 2-MONTH-OLD INFANT IS BROUGHT TO THE OPD WITH A PARIETAL SWELLING PRESENT SINCE BIRTH. THE
X-RAY IMAGE IS PROVIDED BELOW. WHAT COULD BE THE PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
IN THE GIVEN CLINICAL PICTURE, THE SWELLING OVER THE INFANT'S HEAD IS LIKELY TO BE A CEPHALHEMATOMA.
CEPHALOHEMATOMA IS A COLLECTION OF BLOOD IN BETWEEN THE PERICRANIUM AND THE FLAT BONE
(SUBPERIOSTEAL) OF THE SKULL, USUALLY UNILATERAL AND OVER A PARIETAL BONE. IT IS NEVER PRESENT AT BIRTH
BUT GRADUALLY DEVELOPS AFTER 12–24 H. THE SWELLING IS LIMITED BY THE SUTURE LINES OF THE SKULL AS THE
PERICRANIUM IS FIXED TO THE MARGINS OF THE BONE.
4014
THE ARROW MARK IN THE IMAGE REPRESENTS CEPHALOHEMATOMA.
NOTE: CEPHALHEMATOMA IS MORE LIKELY TO BE IDENTIFIED SOON AFTER BIRTH, AND ITS PRESENCE AS A
DEFINED AREA OF SWELLING THAT DOES NOT CROSS SUTURE LINES IS MORE CONSISTENT WITH THIS DIAGNOSIS.
SUBGALEAL HEMATOMA OCCURS BETWEEN THE GALEA APONEUROTICA AND THE PERIOSTEUM. IT IS COMMONLY
CAUSED BY BIRTH TRAUMA, PARTICULARLY FORCEPS OR VACUUM-ASSISTED DELIVERY. SUBGALEAL HEMATOMA CAN
CROSS SUTURE LINES AND TYPICALLY PRESENTS AS A SOFT, FLUCTUANT SWELLING ON THE SCALP.
CAPUT SUCCEDANEUM IS AN EDEMA OF THE SCALP THAT CAN CROSS SUTURE LINES. IT IS USUALLY PRESENT AT
BIRTH OR DEVELOPS SHORTLY AFTER DUE TO PRESSURE ON THE PRESENTING PART OF THE HEAD DURING LABOR. IT
GENERALLY RESOLVES WITHIN A FEW DAYS.
ENCEPHALOCELE IS A NEURAL TUBE DEFECT THAT RESULTS IN A SAC-LIKE PROTRUSION OF THE BRAIN AND ITS
MENINGES THROUGH AN OPENING IN THE SKULL. IT IS A CONGENITAL CONDITION AND IS TYPICALLY DIAGNOSED
AT BIRTH OR VIA PRENATAL ULTRASOUND.
4015

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN AND STERILE PYURIA, AND THE X-RAY SHOWED THE
FOLLOWING FEATURES. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
A PATIENT WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN AND STERILE PYURIA, WITH THE GIVEN X-RAY SHOWING DIFFUSE ALVEOLAR
CALCIFICATION IN THE RIGHT RENAL REGION POINT TOWARDS A DIAGNOSIS OF A PUTTY KIDNEY.
THE PUTTY KIDNEY IS A CHARACTERISTIC FINDING OF GENITOURINARY TUBERCULOSIS (TB), SPECIFICALLY RENAL
TB. THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS A HOMOGENOUS AND GROUND-GLASS-LIKE CALCIFICATION OF THE KIDNEY
APPEARING LIKE PUTTY. IT IS CAUSED BY THE DISSEMINATION OF THE ORGANISM THROUGH THE BLOODSTREAM
AND IS THUS ALWAYS A SECONDARY TB. THERE IS EITHER REINFECTION OR REACTIVATION OF OLD TB.
GENITOURINARY TB IS A CAUSE OF STERILE PYURIA. DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED WITH A TUBERCULIN TEST, OR AT
LEAST 3 CONSECUTIVE EARLY-MORNING SPECIMENS OF URINE ARE EXAMINED FOR ACID-FAST BACILLI. THEY ARE
STAINED WITH A ZIEHL-NEELSEN STAIN AND SUBSEQUENTLY CULTURED.
CT IS THE MOST SENSITIVE MODALITY AND IS THE PREFERRED MEANS OF VISUALIZING RENAL CALCIFICATIONS. CT
UROGRAPHY IS DONE TO ASSESS THE VARIOUS STAGES OF RENAL TB AND ITS MANIFESTATIONS, WHICH ARE AS
FOLLOWS:
- EARLY:
- PAPILLARY NECROSIS
- PROGRESSIVE:
- MULTIFOCAL STRICTURES
- GENERALIZED OR FOCAL HYDRONEPHROSIS
- MURAL THICKENING AND ENHANCEMENT
- POORLY ENHANCING RENAL PARENCHYMA
- END-STAGE:
- PROGRESSIVE HYDRONEPHROSIS
- AMORPHOUS DYSTROPHIC CALCIFICATION THAT INVOLVES THE ENTIRE KIDNEY - PUTTY KIDNEY
TREATMENT INVOLVES SHORT-COURSE THERAPY WITH ANTITUBERCULAR DRUGS LIKE PYRAZINAMIDE, ISONIAZID,
AND RIFAMPICIN. PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY, NEPHRECTOMY, OR RECONSTRUCTIVE SURGERY IS OFTEN DONE.
OPTION B: NEPHROCALCINOSIS - THIS CONDITION IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE DEPOSITION OF CALCIUM IN THE
KIDNEY PARENCHYMA OR TUBULES, OFTEN SEEN IN HYPERCALCEMIC CONDITIONS LIKE HYPERPARATHYROIDISM.
HOWEVER, IT WOULD NOT EXPLAIN THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF STERILE PYURIA.
4016
OPTION C: STAGHORN CALCULI ARE LARGE KIDNEY STONES THAT FILL THE RENAL PELVIS AND EXTEND INTO THE
RENAL CALYCES, OFTEN CAUSED BY URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS WITH ORGANISMS SUCH AS PROTEUS,
PSEUDOMONAS, AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS. WHILE THESE CALCULI CAN CAUSE ABDOMINAL PAIN, THEY USUALLY DO
NOT RESULT IN STERILE PYURIA, AS THEY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH INFECTION.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS A STAGHORN CALCULUS OF THE LEFT KIDNEY.
OPTION D: PSOAS CALCIFICATION - THIS REFERS TO CALCIFICATION WITHIN THE PSOAS MUSCLE AND IS OFTEN
SEEN AFTER ACUTE RENAL FAILURE AND RHABDOMYOLYSIS. IT IS NOT ASSOCIATED WITH STERILE PYURIA AND IS
NOT THE CAUSE OF THE PATIENT'S SYMPTOMS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A WOMAN WITH ENDOMETRIAL CARCINOMA IS UNDERGOING RADIOTHERAPY. WHICH OF THESE IS
TRUE?
options: INTENSITY IS INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL TO THE SQUARE OF THE DISTANCE FROM THE SOURCE
SMALL BLOOD VESSELS ARE MOST RADIORESISTANT
RAPIDLY PROLIFERATING CELLS ARE MOST RADIORESISTANT
SMALL INTESTINAL MUCOSA IS MOST RADIO-RESISTANT
questions.answer: INTENSITY IS INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL TO THE SQUARE OF THE DISTANCE FROM THE SOURCE
questions.explanation:
4017
THE TRUE STATEMENT IS THAT THE INTENSITY OF RADIATION IS INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL TO THE SQUARE OF THE
DISTANCE FROM THE SOURCE IN BRACHYTHERAPY.
RADIOTHERAPY IS A COMMON TREATMENT MODALITY FOR VARIOUS CANCERS, INCLUDING ENDOMETRIAL
CARCINOMA. IT WORKS BY TARGETING RAPIDLY DIVIDING CANCER CELLS WITH IONIZING RADIATION, WHICH CAN
DAMAGE THE DNA OF THESE CELLS AND LEAD TO CELL DEATH. RADIOTHERAPY CAN BE DELIVERED EXTERNALLY
(EXTERNAL BEAM RADIOTHERAPY) OR INTERNALLY (BRACHYTHERAPY). IN BRACHYTHERAPY, RADIOACTIVE SOURCES
ARE PLACED WITHIN OR ADJACENT TO THE TUMOR, LEADING TO A HIGH RADIATION DOSE DELIVERED DIRECTLY TO
THE TUMOR WHILE MINIMIZING DAMAGE TO SURROUNDING HEALTHY TISSUE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: LARGER BLOOD VESSELS ARE MORE RADIORESISTANT THAN MICROVASCULATURE.
OPTION C: PERMANENT NON-DIVIDING CELLS ARE MORE RADIORESISTANT THAN RAPIDLY PROLIFERATING CELLS.
OPTION D: SMALL INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL CELLS (INTESTINAL CRYPTS), WHICH DIVIDE RAPIDLY WITH NO
DIFFERENTIATION ARE THE MOST RADIOSENSITIVE.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A HISTORY OF FEVER AND COUGH FOR THE PAST 3-5 DAYS. HIS EXAMINATION
FINDINGS REVEAL CREPITATIONS. CHEST X-RAY IS PROVIDED BELOW. SPECIFY THE PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS.
options: APICAL SEGMENT OF RIGHT LOWER LOBE CONSOLIDATION
POSTERIOR SEGMENT OF RIGHT LOWER LOBE CONSOLIDATION
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF FEVER, COUGH, AND CREPITATIONS SUGGESTS FEATURES OF
PNEUMONIA. THE CHEST X-RAY SHOWING OPACITIES WITH OBSCURATION OF THE RIGHT CARDIAC BORDER IS
SUGGESTIVE OF RIGHT MIDDLE LOBE CONSOLIDATION.
THIS LOSS OF CLEAR DEMARCATION BETWEEN THE NORMAL LUNG AND ITS SURROUNDING SOFT STRUCTURES (HEART,
DIAPHRAGM) IS CALLED THE SILHOUETTE SIGN. IT OCCURS DUE TO LOSS OF CONTRAST BETWEEN LUNGS AND SOFT
TISSUE WHEN THE LUNG PARENCHYMA IS NO LONGER FILLED WITH AIR. THIS SIGN MAY BE SEEN IN
CONSOLIDATION, ATELECTASIS, OR MASS LESIONS.
IN THE FOLLOWING IMAGES:
- LEFT IMAGE - RED LINE INDICATES THE NORMAL DEMARCATION BETWEEN THE RIGHT HEART BORDER AND
MIDDLE LOBE OF THE RIGHT LUNG
- RIGHT IMAGE - LOSS OF DEMARCATION I.E, POSITIVE SILHOUETTE SIGN DUE TO RIGHT MIDDLE
LOBE CONSOLIDATION
4018
POSITIVE SILHOUETTE SIGN AND CORRESPONDING ANATOMICAL SITE OF PATHOLOGY:
- RIGHT HEART BORDER - RIGHT MIDDLE LOBE OR MEDIAL RIGHT LOWER LOBE
- LEFT HEART BORDER - LINGULA SEGMENTS OF THE LEFT UPPER LOBE
- LEFT HEMIDIAPHRAGM OR DESCENDING AORTA - LEFT LOWER LOBE
- AORTIC KNUCKLE - LEFT UPPER LOBE (POSTERIOR SEGMENT)
- RIGHT HEMIDIAPHRAGM - RIGHT LOWER LOBE
- RIGHT PARATRACHEAL STRIPE - RIGHT UPPER LOBE
OTHER OPTIONS:
APICAL SEGMENT OF RIGHT LOWER LOBE CONSOLIDATION: IN THIS CASE, THE CHEST X-RAY WOULD SHOW AN
OPACITY OR CONSOLIDATION IN THE APICAL SEGMENT OF THE RIGHT LOWER LOBE. THE CONSOLIDATION WOULD BE
LOCATED IN THE LOWER PART OF THE RIGHT LUNG, TOWARDS THE APEX. THE RIGHT HEART BORDER, HOWEVER,
WOULD REMAIN VISIBLE, AS IT IS NOT ADJACENT TO THE APICAL SEGMENT OF THE RIGHT LOWER LOBE.
POSTERIOR SEGMENT OF RIGHT LOWER LOBE CONSOLIDATION: A CHEST X-RAY REVEALING CONSOLIDATION IN THE
POSTERIOR SEGMENT OF THE RIGHT LOWER LOBE WOULD SHOW AN OPACITY IN THE LOWER PART OF THE RIGHT
LUNG, MORE POSTERIORLY. THIS WOULD NOT AFFECT THE VISIBILITY OF THE RIGHT HEART BORDER, AS IT IS NOT
ADJACENT TO THE POSTERIOR SEGMENT OF THE RIGHT LOWER LOBE. IN A POSTEROANTERIOR (PA) CHEST X-RAY,
THIS CONSOLIDATION MAY BE DIFFICULT TO APPRECIATE, BUT IT WOULD BE MORE EVIDENT IN A LATERAL VIEW.
LOCULATED PLEURAL EFFUSION: IN A CHEST X-RAY SHOWING A LOCULATED PLEURAL EFFUSION, THERE WOULD BE A
FLUID COLLECTION WITHIN THE PLEURAL SPACE. THIS FLUID COLLECTION WOULD APPEAR AS A WELL-DEFINED
OPACITY, TYPICALLY WITH A CONVEX BORDER FACING THE LUNG PARENCHYMA. IT MAY APPEAR AS A LENTICULAR
SHAPE, CONFORMING TO THE SPACE BETWEEN THE LUNG AND CHEST WALL OR DIAPHRAGM. THE LOCULATED
PLEURAL EFFUSION WOULD NOT CREATE A SILHOUETTE SIGN WITH THE RIGHT HEART BORDER, AS IT IS LOCATED IN
THE PLEURAL SPACE RATHER THAN THE LUNG PARENCHYMA.
4019

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE STATEMENTS IS CORRECT ABOUT CT SCAN?
options: CT CONSISTS OF UNFILTERED X-RAY BEAMS
IT IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR GALLSTONES
questions.explanation:
THE CORRECT STATEMENT IS THAT THE CT SCORE OF WATER IS 0.
ON CT, EACH IMAGE CONSISTS OF A MATRIX OF DATA POINTS (PIXELS) THAT ARE ASSIGNED A NUMBER THAT
REPRESENTS THE X-RAY ATTENUATION(µ) AT THAT POINT IN THE BODY. CT NUMBER IS A SCALED VERSION OF µ
THAT IS NORMALISED TO THE X-RAY ATTENUATION OF WATER (µW).
CT = 1000 × (µ/µW − 1)
THE RESULTING NUMBERS ARE CALLED ‘HOUNSFIELD UNITS’(HU). DUE TO THIS NORMALISATION, WATER IS
ASSIGNED 0 HU, AND AIR IS ASSIGNED A CT NUMBER OF −1000 HU.
CT NUMBERS:
- WATER = 0 HU
- SOLID SOFT TISSUES ARE CENTRED AROUND 0 HU
- LUNGS = -1000 HU
4036
- AIR = −1000 HU
- DENSE CORTICAL BONE = +1000 HU
- ACUTE BLOOD CLOT = 60-90 HU
- FAT = -100 HU
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT) IMAGING INVOLVES THE USE OF A NARROW BEAM OF X-RAYS THAT
ARE EMITTED FROM A ROTATING X-RAY TUBE.CT SCANNERS TYPICALLY USE A COMBINATION OF X-RAY BEAMS AT
DIFFERENT ENERGIES AND FILTERS TO REDUCE SCATTER AND IMPROVE IMAGE QUALITY. THEREFORE, THE X-RAY
BEAMS USED IN CT IMAGING ARE OFTEN FILTERED TO ENHANCE IMAGE CONTRAST AND REDUCE RADIATION DOSE
TO THE PATIENT.
OPTION C: THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR GALLSTONES IS AN ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND AND NOT A CT
ABDOMEN. AN ULTRASOUND CAN ASSESS FOR COMPLICATIONS OF GALLSTONES, SUCH AS INFLAMMATION OF THE
GALLBLADDER (CHOLECYSTITIS) OR OBSTRUCTION OF THE BILE DUCTS. IN CASES WHERE ULTRASOUND FINDINGS ARE
INCONCLUSIVE OR FURTHER CHARACTERISATION IS NEEDED, OTHER IMAGING MODALITIES SUCH AS CT SCAN OR
MAGNETIC RESONANCE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY (MRCP) MAY BE USED.
OPTION D: THE MSV (MILLISIEVERT) VALUE FOR A NON-CONTRAST COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (NCCT) SCAN OF
THE HEAD TYPICALLY RANGES FROM AROUND 1 TO 2 MSV. THIS RADIATION DOSE CAN VARY DEPENDING ON
FACTORS SUCH AS THE SPECIFIC CT SCANNER USED, THE SCANNING PROTOCOL, AND THE INDIVIDUAL PATIENT
CHARACTERISTICS. HOWEVER, IN GENERAL, NCCT HEAD SCANS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH RELATIVELY LOW RADIATION
DOSES COMPARED TO OTHER MEDICAL IMAGING PROCEDURES.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: IN WHICH OF THE LISTED OPTIONS IS 'MOUNT FUJI SIGN' SEEN?
questions.explanation:
'MOUNT FUJI SIGN' IS SEEN IN TENSION PNEUMOCEPHALUS.
MOUNT FUJI SIGN REFERS TO THE PRESENCE OF AIR (PNEUMOCEPHALUS) BETWEEN THE TIPS OF THE FRONTAL
LOBES GIVING THE APPEARANCE OF MOUNT FUJI.
TENSION PNEUMOCEPHALUS OCCURS WITH SUBDURAL AIR CAUSING A MASS EFFECT OVER THE UNDERLYING BRAIN
PARENCHYMA, OFTEN FROM A BALL VALVE MECHANISM CAUSING ONE-WAY ENTRY OF AIR INTO THE SUBDURAL
SPACE.
THE APPEARANCE OF THIS SIGN OFTEN WARRANTS IMMEDIATE SURGERY TO PREVENT PERMANENT DAMAGE.
THE CT IMAGE BELOW SHOWS THE MOUNT FUJI SIGN.
4037

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH A STAB WOUND OVER THE RIGHT CHEST. THE SUPINE X-RAY IMAGE OF THE
PATIENT IS PROVIDED BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE HISTORY OF STAB INJURY TO THE RIGHT CHEST AND THE X-RAY SHOWING OPACITY OF THE RIGHT HEMITHORAX,
WITH A SLIGHT TRACHEAL DEVIATION TOWARDS THE OPPOSITE SIDE, INDICATES A DIAGNOSIS OF RIGHT
HEMOTHORAX.
IN A PLAIN CHEST RADIOGRAPH, IT'S DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE AN ACUTE HEMOTHORAX FROM OTHER
COLLECTIONS OF PLEURAL FLUID AS THEY ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE. AS BLOOD CLOTS, IT OFTEN LEADS TO
LOCALISATION, OCCASIONALLY FORMING A FIBRIN BODY. PLEURAL THICKENING AND CALCIFICATION ARE
ACKNOWLEDGED AS POTENTIAL CONSEQUENCES.
THE FOLLOWING ARE THE FINDINGS COMMONLY SEEN IN A CASE OF HEMOTHORAX:
- BLUNTING OF COSTOPHRENIC ANGLE: HEMOTHORAX RESULTS IN THE ACCUMULATION OF BLOOD IN THE PLEURAL
CAVITY, CAUSING THE LUNG TO COLLAPSE PARTIALLY. THIS CAN LEAD TO THE BLUNTING OR OBLITERATION OF THE
COSTOPHRENIC ANGLE ON THE AFFECTED SIDE.
- INCREASED OPACITY: THE PRESENCE OF BLOOD IN THE PLEURAL SPACE LEADS TO INCREASED OPACITY OR
DENSITY IN THE AFFECTED HEMITHORAX. THIS CAN MANIFEST AS A HOMOGENOUS SHADOWING THAT OBSCURES
THE LUNG MARKINGS.
- MEDIASTINAL SHIFT: DEPENDING ON THE VOLUME OF BLOOD IN THE PLEURAL CAVITY, THERE MAY BE A
MEDIASTINAL SHIFT TOWARDS THE OPPOSITE SIDE. HOWEVER, IN MILD TO MODERATE HEMOTHORAX, THIS MAY
NOT BE READILY APPARENT ON SUPINE X-RAYS.
- AIR-FLUID LEVEL: IN CASES WHERE THERE IS CONCURRENT PNEUMOTHORAX (AIR IN THE PLEURAL CAVITY), AN
AIR-FLUID LEVEL MAY BE VISIBLE, WITH THE BLOOD LAYERING DEPENDENTLY AND THE AIR LAYER SUPERIORLY.
- UNILATERAL FINDINGS: THE ABNORMALITIES WILL TYPICALLY BE LIMITED TO ONE SIDE OF THE CHEST,
CORRESPONDING TO THE SIDE OF THE HEMOTHORAX.
IN CASES OF SUSPECTED HEMOTHORAX, A LATERAL DECUBITUS OR CHEST X-RAY IN ERECT POSITION MAY BE MORE
SENSITIVE FOR DETECTION. ADDITIONALLY, OTHER IMAGING MODALITIES SUCH AS ULTRASOUND OR COMPUTED
TOMOGRAPHY (CT) SCANS CAN PROVIDE MORE DETAILED INFORMATION ABOUT THE PRESENCE AND EXTENT OF A
4038
HEMOTHORAX.
OTHER OPTIONS:
THE FOLLOWING IMAGE IS CHARACTERISTIC OF A PNEUMOTHORAX (LEFT-SIDED) WITH RADIOLUCENCY OVER THE
LEFT LUNG, LUNG COLLAPSE, AND MEDIASTINAL SHIFT ON X-RAY.
THE GIVEN RADIOGRAPH IS A CASE OF DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA THAT SHOWS ELEVATION OF THE LEFT
HEMIDIAPHRAGMATIC LINE ALONG WITH THE BOWEL LOOPS AND STOMACH SEEN IN THE PLEURAL CAVITY.
THE FOLLOWING IS AN IMAGE OF A RIGHT-SIDED PULMONARY CONTUSION POST-BLUNT CHEST TRAUMA. NOTE THE
INCREASED OPACITY JUST BELOW THE HORIZONTAL FISSURE.
4039

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE CONTRAST AGENTS IS SAFE TO USE IN RENAL FAILURE PATIENTS?
questions.explanation:
ULTRASOUND CONTRAST AGENTS ARE GAS-FILLED MICROBUBBLES THAT ARE ADMINISTERED INTRAVENOUSLY TO THE
SYSTEMIC CIRCULATION. HENCE, CONSIDERED AS LOW RISK IN PATIENTS WITH RENAL IMPAIRMENT.
ULTRASOUND CONTRAST AGENTS ARE USED TO ENHANCE THE VISIBILITY OF BLOOD VESSELS, ORGANS, AND TISSUES
DURING ULTRASOUND IMAGING. THESE AGENTS TYPICALLY CONSIST OF TINY GAS-FILLED MICROBUBBLES
ENCAPSULATED WITHIN A SHELL. WHEN INJECTED INTRAVENOUSLY, THEY FLOW THROUGH THE BLOODSTREAM AND
RESONATE IN RESPONSE TO ULTRASOUND WAVES, PRODUCING STRONG ECHOES THAT ENHANCE THE ULTRASOUND
IMAGE.
PERFLUTREN/OPTISON IS AN ULTRASOUND CONTRAST AGENT. LEVOVIST (CONSISTING OF GALACTOSE
MICROPARTICLES, AIR BUBBLES, AND PALMITIC ACID) IS ANOTHER EXAMPLE OF AN ULTRASOUND CONTRAST AGENT.
SULFUR HEXAFLUORIDE WITH A PHOSPHOLIPID SHELL IS ALSO USED AS AN ULTRASOUND CONTRAST AGENT.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: GADOLINIUM CONTRAST USED IN MRI IS PREDOMINANTLY EXCRETED THROUGH THE KIDNEY. IN
RENAL FAILURE, IT GETS ACCUMULATED IN THE BODY AND RELEASES GADOLINIUM IONS. SINCE THE ION IS TOXIC,
THE BODY TRIES TO CONTAIN IT BY FIBROSIS RESULTING IN MULTISYSTEM PAINFUL FIBROSIS CALLED NEPHROGENIC
SYSTEMIC FIBROSIS.
OPTION B: IODINATED IONIC CONTRAST AGENTS INCREASE THE RISK OF CONTRAST-INDUCED NEPHROPATHY(CIN).
HENCE ALTERNATIVE IMAGING METHODS, WITHOUT IODINATED CONTRAST MEDIA, SHOULD BE CHOSEN IN
PATIENTS WITH CONSIDERABLY IMPAIRED RENAL FUNCTION (CKD 4 OR 5).
OPTION C: NON-IONIC CONTRAST AGENTS HAVE A LOWER RISK OF CAUSING ADVERSE REACTIONS COMPARED TO
IONIC CONTRAST AGENTS. THEY ARE GENERALLY BETTER TOLERATED BY PATIENTS, WITH FEWER INCIDENCES OF
ALLERGIC REACTIONS AND NEPHROTOXICITY. HOWEVER, USG CONTRAST AGENTS ARE AMONG THE SAFEST IN RENAL
FAILURE PATIENTS.
4040

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THESE STRUCTURES IS THE ARROW POINTING TO?
questions.explanation:
THE STRUCTURE POINTED BY THE ARROW MARK IN THE GIVEN CHEST X-RAY PA VIEW IS THE POSTERIOR END OF
THE RIB.
IN THE CHEST X-RAY PA VIEW, RIBS APPEAR AS LIGHT GREY STRIPS. THE ANTERIOR PART OF THE RIB IS MORE
OBLIQUE AND THE MEDIAL PART CANNOT BE DEMONSTRABLE AS IT ENDS WITH COSTAL CARTILAGE. THE POSTERIOR
PART OF THE RIB IS MORE HORIZONTAL, HYPERDENSE AND THE ATTACHMENT OF THE RIB WITH THE VERTEBRA CAN
BE EASILY MADE OUT.
NORMAL CHEST X-RAY RIB IDENTIFICATION

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THESE RADIOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS ARE USED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF CEREBRAL
ANEURYSM?
questions.explanation:
4041
COILING IS THE RADIOLOGICAL INTERVENTION USED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF CEREBRAL ANEURYSM.
ANEURYSMS OCCUR AT THE BIFURCATIONS OF THE LARGE TO MEDIUM-SIZED INTRACRANIAL ARTERIES. RUPTURE IS
INTO THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE IN THE BASAL CISTERNS. APPROXIMATELY 85% OF THE ANEURYSMS OCCUR IN
THE ANTERIOR CIRCULATION, MAINLY ON THE CIRCLE OF WILLIS.
MOST UNRUPTURED INTRACRANIAL ANEURYSMS ARE COMPLETELY ASYMPTOMATIC. WHEN THE ANEURYSM
RUPTURES, 45% OF CASES PRESENT WITH SUDDEN ONSET SEVERE HEADACHE, DESCRIBED AS THE WORST
HEADACHE OF THE PATIENT'S LIFE. OTHER FEATURES INCLUDE NECK RIGIDITY AND TRANSIENT LOSS OF
CONSCIOUSNESS.
DIAGNOSIS -
CT SHOWS HYPERATTENUATING MATERIAL FILLING THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE. CT ANGIOGRAPHY HAS A HIGH
SENSITIVITY FOR ANEURYSMS AND AVMS, BUT DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY REMAINS THE GOLD
STANDARD.
TREATMENT -
EARLY ANEURYSM REPAIR PREVENTS RE-RUPTURE. AT MANY CENTERS, DEFINITIVE REPAIR IS CARRIED OUT WITHIN
24 H OF THE BLEED IN ALL PATIENTS WHO ARE STABLE ENOUGH TO TOLERATE THE PROCEDURE. AN ANEURYSM CAN
BE “CLIPPED” BY A NEUROSURGEON OR “COILED” BY AN ENDOVASCULAR APPROACH. SURGICAL REPAIR INVOLVES
PLACING A METAL CLIP ACROSS THE ANEURYSM NECK, THEREBY IMMEDIATELY ELIMINATING THE RISK OF
REBLEEDING. THIS APPROACH REQUIRES CRANIOTOMY (OPTION D) AND BRAIN RETRACTION, WHICH IS
ASSOCIATED WITH NEUROLOGIC MORBIDITY.
ENDOVASCULAR TECHNIQUES INVOLVE PLACING PLATINUM COILS WITHIN THE ANEURYSM VIA A CATHETER THAT IS
PASSED FROM THE FEMORAL ARTERY. THE ANEURYSM IS PACKED TIGHTLY TO ENHANCE THROMBOSIS AND OVER
TIME IS WALLED OFF FROM THE CIRCULATION.
INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE SHOULD BE MEASURED AND THE CEREBRAL PERFUSION PRESSURE TARGETED AT 60–70
MMHG.
DELAYED CEREBRAL ISCHEMIA REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY FOLLOWING
ANEURYSMAL SAH. TREATMENT WITH THE CALCIUM CHANNEL ANTAGONIST NIMODIPINE (60 MG PO EVERY 4
H) IMPROVES OUTCOME, PERHAPS BY PREVENTING ISCHEMIC INJURY RATHER THAN REDUCING THE RISK OF
VASOSPASM.
4042
THE IMAGE BELOW IS AN ARTERIOGRAM SHOWING A COILED ANEURYSM (INDICATED BY YELLOW ARROWS) OF THE
POSTERIOR CEREBRAL ARTERY WITH A RESIDUAL ANEURYSMAL SAC.
OTHER OPTIONS :
OPTION B - SCLEROTHERAPY IS USED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF VENOUS INSUFFICIENCY.
OPTION D - STENTING IS EMPLOYED MAINLY FOR STENOTIC VASCULAR LESIONS.
4043

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTED WITH CHEST PAIN AND HOARSENESS FOR ONE MONTH, AND ON A CT ANGIOGRAM,
THE FOLLOWING IMAGE IS SEEN, WHAT IS THE POSSIBLE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CT SHOWS SACCULAR ANEURYSM OF THE DISTAL AORTA. THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF CHEST PAIN
AND HOARSENESS SUPPORTS THE DIAGNOSIS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: STENOSIS OF THE AORTIC ARCH WOULD SHOW A NARROWING RATHER THAN AN ANEURYSMAL DILATION,
AND IT IS MORE LIKELY TO PRESENT WITH SYMPTOMS RELATED TO DECREASED BLOOD FLOW TO THE UPPER BODY.
OPTION B: AORTIC DISSECTION WOULD USUALLY PRESENT WITH A TEARING CHEST PAIN THAT RADIATES TO THE
BACK AND WOULD SHOW A DOUBLE LUMEN OR FALSE LUMEN ON IMAGING. THE BELOW IMAGE SHOWS STANFORD
TYPE A AORTIC DISSECTION:
OPTION D: COARCTATION OF THE AORTA TYPICALLY PRESENTS WITH HYPERTENSION IN THE UPPER LIMBS AND
WEAK OR ABSENT PULSES IN THE LOWER LIMBS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
THIS IS THE RADIOGRAPH OF A CHILD WITH A FOREIGN BODY IN THE OESOPHAGUS. SPECIFY THE SIGN SEEN
IN THIS.
questions.explanation:
THE PRESENCE OF A HALO SIGN OR DOUBLE RING SIGN IS INDICATIVE OF THE FOREIGN BODY BEING A BUTTON
BATTERY.
BUTTON BATTERIES AND SHARP OBJECTS IN THE OESOPHAGUS AND FOREIGN BODIES ASSOCIATED WITH
RESPIRATORY SYMPTOMS ALL MANDATE URGENT ENDOSCOPIC REMOVAL.
BUTTON BATTERIES, IN PARTICULAR, ARE VERY DANGEROUS FOREIGN BODIES, WHICH MUST BE EXPEDIENTLY
REMOVED BECAUSE THEY CAN CAUSE:
4054
- MUCOSAL INJURY IN 1-HOUR CONTACT TIME
- INVOLVE ALL LAYERS OF THE OESOPHAGUS IN 4 HOURS
INJURY IS THOUGHT TO BE SECONDARY TO ELECTROCHEMICAL BURNS FROM ELECTRICAL DISCHARGE. CHEMICAL
BURNS FROM ELECTROLYTE ALKALI LEAKAGE AND PRESSURE NECROSIS ALSO MAY CONTRIBUTE TO MUCOSAL INJURY.
ASYMPTOMATIC BLUNT OBJECTS AND COINS LODGED IN THE OESOPHAGUS CAN BE OBSERVED FOR UP TO 24 HR
IN ANTICIPATION OF PASSAGE INTO THE STOMACH.
ANOTHER AP AND LATERAL X-RAY DEMONSTRATING THE PRESENCE OF A BUTTON BATTERY IN THE OESOPHAGUS IS
AS SHOWN BELOW.
OTHER OPTIONS
OPTION A: THUMB SIGN IS SEEN IN ACUTE EPIGLOTTITIS.
OPTION B: A STEEPLE SIGN IS SEEN IN CROUP OR LARYNGOTRACHEOBRONCHITIS.
4055
OPTION D: STRING SIGN ON THE BARIUM ENEMA IS IN ILEOCECAL TUBERCULOSIS.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS THE STRING SIGN OF KANTOR ASSOCIATED WITH CROHN'S DISEASE.
4056

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A ONE-MONTH HISTORY OF LETHARGY, HEADACHE, FEVER, AND VOMITING.
SHORTLY AFTER BEING ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL, THE PATIENT TRAGICALLY PASSES AWAY. RADIOLOGICAL
IMAGING REVEALS MULTIPLE CYSTIC LESIONS IN THE CEREBRUM WITH INVASION INTO THE VENTRICLES AND
SUBARACHNOID SPACE. SPECIFY THE LIKELY CAUSE.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO ALONG WITH CT SHOWING CYSTIC LESIONS IN THE BRAIN, PARTICULARLY WITHIN
THE CEREBRUM, VENTRICLES, AND SUBARACHNOID SPACE IS CLEARLY SUGGESTIVE OF NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS.
NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS IS A FORM OF CYSTICERCOSIS CAUSED BY TAENIA SOLIUM.
IT USUALLY PRESENTS WITH SEIZURES AND SYMPTOMS OF INCREASED INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE, INCLUDING
HEADACHE, NAUSEA, VOMITING, VISION CHANGES, DIZZINESS, ATAXIA, OR CONFUSION. PAPILLEDEMA MAY
DEVELOP SECONDARY TO HYDROCEPHALUS.
DIAGNOSIS IS DONE BY DEMONSTRATING EGGS OF TAENIA IN FAECAL EXAMINATION.
A BIOPSY OF THE BRAIN OR SPINAL CORD LESION OR FUNDOSCOPIC VISUALIZATION OF SUBRETINAL CYSTICERCUS
CAN ALSO BE DONE.
IMAGING SHOWS A SCOLEX WITHIN A CYSTIC LESION, CYSTIC LESIONS WITH OR WITHOUT ENHANCEMENT (E.G.,
RING ENHANCEMENT), NODULAR CALCIFICATIONS, FOCAL ENHANCING LESIONS, OR MULTILOBULATED CYSTIC LESIONS
IN THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE.
TREATMENT OF INTESTINAL T. SOLIUM INFECTION IS BY A SINGLE DOSE OF PRAZIQUANTEL. NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS
IS TREATED WITH ANTI-EPILEPTIC DRUGS, ANTICYSTICIDAL DRUGS LIKE ALBENDAZOLE OR PRAZIQUANTEL, AND
STEROIDS GIVEN BEFORE ANTICYSTICIDAL THERAPY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: ASTROCYTOMA IS A TYPE OF GLIAL CELL TUMOUR IN THE BRAIN, RANGING FROM LOW TO HIGH GRADE.
THEY DO NOT TYPICALLY PRESENT AS MULTIPLE CYSTIC LESIONS AND ARE MORE LIKELY TO APPEAR AS A SINGLE
MASS WITH VARIABLE ENHANCEMENT ON IMAGING.
OPTION C: ARTERIOVENOUS MALFORMATION (AVM) IS A CONGENITAL VASCULAR ANOMALY CHARACTERIZED BY A
TANGLE OF ABNORMAL BLOOD VESSELS CONNECTING ARTERIES AND VEINS. AVMS ARE MORE LIKELY TO CAUSE
HEMORRHAGE OR SEIZURES AND TYPICALLY APPEAR AS HIGHLY VASCULAR LESIONS ON IMAGING, NOT AS CYSTIC
LESIONS.
4057
OPTION D: WHILE METASTASES CAN PRESENT AS MULTIPLE LESIONS ON IMAGING, THEY USUALLY APPEAR SOLID
RATHER THAN CYSTIC MASSES AND OFTEN ENHANCE WITH CONTRAST.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT REPORTS SEVERE HEADACHE. NCCT AND CT ANGIOGRAPHY IMAGES ARE AS BELOW.
SPECIFY THE LIKELY ETIOLOGY.
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS OF SEVERE HEADACHE WITH CT REVEALING BLOOD IN THE BASAL CISTERN POINT
TO A DIAGNOSIS OF SUBARACHNOID HAEMORRHAGE (SAH).
SUBARACHNOID HAEMORRHAGE (SAH) IS BLEEDING INTO THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE, WHICH IS THE AREA
BETWEEN THE ARACHNOID MEMBRANE AND THE PIA MATER SURROUNDING THE BRAIN. THE DIAGNOSIS IS
SUSPECTED WHEN A HYPERATTENUATING MATERIAL IS SEEN FILLING THE SUBARACHNOID SPACE. MOST
COMMONLY THIS IS APPARENT AROUND THE CIRCLE OF WILLIS, ON ACCOUNT OF THE MAJORITY OF BERRY
ANEURYSMS OCCURRING IN THIS REGION (65%), OR IN THE SYLVIAN FISSURE (30%).
THE MODIFIED FISHER SCALE IS A METHOD FOR GRADING SAH AS SEEN ON NON-CONTRAST CT (NCCT). THE
HUNT AND HESS SCALE DESCRIBES THE SEVERITY OF SAH AND IS USED AS A PREDICTOR OF SURVIVAL.
XANTHOCHROMIA ON CSF IS INDICATIVE OF SAH IN CASE OF A NEGATIVE CT SCAN.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: ARTERIOVENOUS MALFORMATION (AVM) IS A CONGENITAL VASCULAR ANOMALY CHARACTERIZED BY A
TANGLE OF ABNORMAL BLOOD VESSELS CONNECTING ARTERIES AND VEINS. AVMS ARE MORE LIKELY TO CAUSE
HAEMORRHAGE OR SEIZURES AND TYPICALLY APPEAR AS HIGHLY VASCULAR LESIONS ON IMAGING, NOT AS CYSTIC
LESIONS.
OPTION C: INTRAPARENCHYMAL HEMORRHAGE RESULTS FROM DAMAGE TO LENTICULOSTRIATE ARTERIES.
HYPERDENSITY WITHIN THE BRAIN PARENCHYMA IS SEEN ON CT.
OPTION D: ACUTE SUBDURAL HAEMORRHAGE RESULTS FROM THE ACCUMULATION OF BLOOD BETWEEN THE
ARACHNOID MEMBRANE AND THE DURA. THE TEARING OF A BRIDGING VEIN FROM THE CEREBRAL CORTEX TO THE
DURAL SINUSES IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF ACUTE SDH. ON HEAD CT SCAN, ACUTE SDH APPEARS AS A
HYPERDENSE, CRESCENT-SHAPED (CONCAVO-CONVEX).

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
AN ELDERLY WOMAN WITH A KNOWN HISTORY OF MYASTHENIA GRAVIS PRESENTS WITH SYMPTOMS
INCLUDING FATIGUE, FACIAL CONGESTION, DILATED NECK VEINS, AND BREATHLESSNESS, WHICH ARE
INDICATIVE OF SUPERIOR VENA CAVA (SVC) OBSTRUCTION. SPECIFY THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE DIAGNOSIS OF MYASTHENIA GRAVIS ALONG WITH THE CT SCAN IMAGE SHOWING AN ANTERIOR MEDIASTINAL
MASS, IS SUGGESTIVE OF THYMOMA.
THYMOMA IS THE MOST COMMON MEDIASTINAL TUMOR AND IS DERIVED FROM THE THYMUS GLAND.
THYMOMAS VARY IN BEHAVIOUR FROM BENIGN TO AGGRESSIVELY INVASIVE. SUPERIOR VENA CAVA OBSTRUCTION
IS A POSSIBLE COMPLICATION OF MEDIASTINAL MASS.
MASOAKA CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM IS USED TO STAGE THYMOMAS.
MYASTHENIA GRAVIS IS OFTEN RELATED TO THYMOMAS. SYMPTOMS OF MYASTHENIA GRAVIS CAN IMPROVE
AFTER EXCISION OF THE THYMUS GLAND EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF A THYMOMA.
COMPLETE THYMECTOMY IS THE TREATMENT FOR THYMOMA. IT CAN BE PERFORMED BY TWO APPROACHES:
- A MEDIAN STERNOTOMY APPROACH
4058
- A TRANSCERVICAL APPROACH WITH OR WITHOUT AN ADDITIONAL VATS PROCEDURE (VIDEO-ASSISTED
THORACOSCOPIC SURGERY) FOR SMALLER THYMOMAS
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: LIPOMAS ARE BENIGN AND SLOW-GROWING, LESS LIKELY TO CAUSE SIGNIFICANT COMPRESSION OF
THE SVC AND PRODUCE THE ACUTE SYMPTOMS DESCRIBED.
OPTION B: ECTOPIC THYROID TISSUE CAN BE FOUND IN THE MEDIASTINUM, BUT IT IS TYPICALLY ASYMPTOMATIC
AND DOES NOT USUALLY CAUSE SVC OBSTRUCTION.
OPTION D: GERM CELL TUMOURS CAN OCCUR IN THE MEDIASTINUM AND CAUSE SVC OBSTRUCTION, BUT THEY
ARE LESS COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH MYASTHENIA GRAVIS COMPARED TO THYMOMAS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A 4-WEEK-OLD INFANT PRESENTED TO THE ER WITH PROJECTILE VOMITING. USG ABDOMEN FINDINGS OF
THE INFANT ARE PROVIDED BELOW. WHAT IS PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS IS CONGENITAL HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS SINCE THE CERVIX SIGN AND
NIPPLE SIGN ARE SIGNS OF CONGENITAL HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS ON USG.
- DOUBLE-LAYERED HYPERTROPHIC MUCOSA PROTRUDES INTO THE STOMACH, CREATING THE SO-CALLED NIPPLE
SIGN.
- THE SONOGRAPHIC APPEARANCE OF THE HYPERTROPHIED PYLORUS RESEMBLES THAT OF THE UTERINE CERVIX
AND IS SOMETIMES REFERRED TO AS THE CERVIX SIGN.
HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS MOST PRESENTS WITH NON-BILIOUS PROJECTILE VOMITING. IT IS COMMON
BETWEEN 2 AND 8 WEEKS OF AGE. HYPERTROPHY OF THE CIRCULAR MUSCLE OF THE PYLORUS RESULTS IN
CONSTRICTION AND OBSTRUCTION OF THE GASTRIC OUTLET. MALE INFANTS ARE AT A HIGHER RISK.
CLINICALLY, AN OLIVE-SHAPED MASS IS PALPABLE IN THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT OR EPIGASTRIUM. WHEN THE
INFANT IS GIVEN A TEST FEED, VISIBLE PERISTALSIS IS USUALLY OBSERVED MOVING FROM LEFT TO RIGHT ACROSS
THE ABDOMEN.
INFANTS WITH HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS DEVELOP A CHARACTERISTIC METABOLIC ABNORMALITY-
HYPOCHLORAEMIC HYPOKALAEMIC METABOLIC ALKALOSIS. PERSISTENT VOMITING RESULTS IN LOSS OF
4059
HYDROCHLORIC ACID LEADING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF METABOLIC ALKALOSIS (DUE TO LOSS OF H+) AND
HYPOCHLOREMIA (DUE TO LOSS OF CL-).
ULTRASOUND EXAMINATION IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR THIS CONDITION. THE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR
PYLORIC STENOSIS ARE A MUSCLE THICKNESS OF ≥4 MM AND A PYLORIC LENGTH OF ≥16 MM. THE CERVIX SIGN
AND NIPPLE SIGN ARE SIGNS SEEN ON USG.
AS FOR THE MANAGEMENT, THE CHILD SHOULD BE REHYDRATED AND THE METABOLIC ABNORMALITY HAS TO BE
CORRECTED BEFORE PROCEEDING TO SURGERY. THE RAMSTEDT PYLOROMYOTOMY REMAINS THE STANDARD
SURGICAL PROCEDURE FOR ITS TREATMENT.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
AN INFANT PRESENTS WITH RESPIRATORY DISTRESS. HE HAS A PREVIOUS HISTORY OF RECURRENT
RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO ALONG WITH THE IMAGE IS SUGGESTIVE OF CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS OF THE
AIRWAY.
CONGENITAL PULMONARY AIRWAY MALFORMATION (CPAM) IS A CONDITION WHERE MORE NORMAL LUNG TISSUE
IS MIXED WITH HAMARTOMATOUS OR DYSPLASTIC LUNG TISSUE, USUALLY CONFINED TO ONE LOBE. THE LESION
MOST LIKELY ORIGINATES FROM A MALDEVELOPMENT OF TERMINAL BRONCHIOLAR STRUCTURES CAUSED BY AN
EMBRYOLOGIC INJURY THAT OCCURRED PRIOR TO THE 35TH DAY OF GESTATION.
PNEUMOTHORAX, RECURRENT RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS, AND RESPIRATORY DISTRESS CAN ALL MANIFEST IN
PATIENTS DURING THE NEWBORN OR EARLY INFANCY PERIOD. ONE COULD MISTAKE THE LESION FOR A
DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA. UNTIL MID-CHILDHOOD, WHEN EPISODES OF RECURRENT OR PERSISTENT PULMONARY
INFECTION OR CHEST PAIN OCCUR, PATIENTS WITH SMALLER LESIONS TYPICALLY ARE ASYMPTOMATIC.
TREATMENT INCLUDES ASPIRATION OF MACROCYSTIC LESIONS, EXCISION OF THE AFFECTED LOBE FOR MICROCYSTIC
LESIONS, AND INFREQUENTLY, OPEN FOETAL SURGERY FOR SEVERELY AFFECTED INFANTS. FOR PATIENTS WITH
SYMPTOMS IN THE POSTNATAL PERIOD, SURGERY IS RECOMMENDED.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: LUNG ABSCESS REPRESENTS NECROSIS AND CAVITATION OF THE LUNG FOLLOWING MICROBIAL
INFECTION.
CHEST X-RAY FEATURES OF LUNG ABSCESS INCLUDE A LUNG CAVITY WITH AN AIR-FLUID LEVEL AND A THICK AND
IRREGULAR CAVITY WALL WITH SURROUNDING PULMONARY INFILTRATE. THE IMAGE SHOWING THE LUNG ABSCESS IS
GIVEN BELOW:
4060
OPTION C: CONGENITAL DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA (CDH) IS A BIRTH DEFECT OF THE DIAPHRAGM.
MALFORMATION OF THE DIAPHRAGM ALLOWS THE ABDOMINAL ORGANS TO PUSH INTO THE CHEST CAVITY,
HINDERING PROPER LUNG FORMATION AND RESULTING IN PULMONARY HYPOPLASIA.
THE MOST COMMON TYPE OF CDH IS A BOCHDALEK HERNIA, WHICH IN MOST CASES INVOLVES THE LEFT SIDE.
CDH IS A LIFE-THREATENING PATHOLOGY IN INFANTS AND A MAJOR CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY DUE TO
TWO COMPLICATIONS: PULMONARY HYPOPLASIA AND PULMONARY HYPERTENSION. THE IMAGE OF BOCHDALEK
HERNIA IS GIVEN BELOW:
OPTION D: PYOPNEUMOTHORAX IS A PLEURAL COLLECTION OF PUS AND GAS, ALSO REFERRED TO AS EMPYEMIC
HYDROPNEUMOTHORAX OR INFECTED HYDROPNEUMOTHORAX. IT COULD BE COMPARED TO A THORACIC
EMPYEMA VARIATION THAT CONTAINS GAS. CHEST PAIN AND FEVER ARE TYPICALLY THE PATIENT'S INITIAL
COMPLAINTS.
X-RAY SHOWS GAS-FLUID LEVEL. IT COULD HAVE LOCULATIONS. THERE APPEARS TO BE A LOSS OF SILHOUETTE
AROUND THE DIAPHRAGM DOME. THE THICK PLEURAL LINING IS STRONGLY INDICATIVE OF THE
4061
PYOPNEUMOTHORAX.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A YOUNG PATIENT PRESENTS WITH NASAL POLYPS AND RHINOSINUSITIS. X-RAY AND CLINICAL IMAGES ARE
AS BELOW. SPECIFY THE DIAGNOSIS.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO ALONG WITH AN X-RAY SHOWING DEXTROCARDIA, CT SHOWING MAXILLARY
POLYP, AND ENDOSCOPY SHOWING NASAL POLYP IS SUGGESTIVE OF KARTAGENER'S SYNDROME.
PRIMARY CILIARY DYSKINESIA (ALSO CALLED IMMOTILE CILIA SYNDROME) IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE DISORDER
AFFECTING CILIARY MOTILITY. WHEN A PATIENT HAS BRONCHIECTASIS, CHRONIC SINUSITIS, AND SITUS INVERSUS
TRIAD, HE IS KNOWN TO HAVE KARTAGENER SYNDROME. IT OCCURS DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF PROTEIN DYNEIN IN
THE A TUBULES OF THE RESPIRATORY MUCOSA.
THE DISEASE IS USUALLY DIAGNOSED BASED ON THE CLINICAL PICTURE AND SHOULD BE EVALUATED IN LATER
STAGES WHEN A CHILD PRESENTS WITH RECURRENT LOWER AND UPPER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS. OTHER
FEATURES OF PRIMARY CILIARY DYSKINESIA INCLUDE CONGENITAL HEART DISEASES AND NEONATAL
HYDROCEPHALUS. MALE PATIENTS WITH THIS CONDITION TEND TO BE INFERTILE, DUE
TO ASTHENOSPERMIA (IMMOTILE SPERMATOZOA DUE TO IMPAIRED SPERM FLAGELLA FUNCTION).
TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY IS THE GOLD STANDARD INVESTIGATION TO ANALYZE CILIA. THERE IS NO
SPECIFIC TREATMENT FOR THIS CONDITION AND IS MANAGED ACCORDING TO THE SYMPTOMS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CHURG STRAUSS SYNDROME CLINICALLY PRESENTS WITH ASTHMA, FEVER AND EOSINOPHILIA.
OPTION C: YOUNG'S SYNDROME CLINICALLY PRESENTS WITH INFERTILITY (AZOOSPERMIA) AND BRONCHIECTASIS.
OPTION D: CYSTIC FIBROSIS IS AN AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE CONDITION DUE TO A MUTATION OF THE CFTR GENE
ON CHROMOSOME 7. CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE RECURRENT SINOPULMONARY INFECTION, INTESTINAL
OBSTRUCTION, PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY, AND MALE INFERTILITY. DIAGNOSIS IS MADE BY ELEVATED SWEAT
CHLORIDE LEVELS, ABNORMAL NASAL POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE, AND GENETIC TESTING FOR CFTR MUTATION.
4062

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
PROVIDED BELOW IS A USG TAKEN AT APPROXIMATELY 8 WEEKS OF GESTATION. WHICH ANOMALY CAN BE
OBSERVED HERE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN ULTRASOUND IMAGE SHOWS AN OPEN DEFECT IN THE CALVARIA AND SKIN. THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH
THE DIAGNOSIS OF ANENCEPHALY.
ANENCEPHALY RESULTS FROM INCOMPLETE CLOSURE OF THE NEURAL TUBE. IT IS ONE OF THE EARLIEST DETECTABLE
CONGENITAL DEFECTS THAT CAN BE DETECTED AS EARLY AS 10 TO 11 WEEKS OF GESTATION. SCREENING CAN ALSO
BE DONE BY SERUM ESTIMATION OF MATERNAL SERUM ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN (MSAFP). THE FOLLOWING ARE THE
RADIOLOGICAL SIGNS SEEN IN ANENCEPHALY.
- FROG EYE SIGN - ABSENCE OF CRANIAL CALVARIA, PROMINENT ORBITS THEREBY RESEMBLING THE FACE OF A
FROG.
- SHOWER CAP SIGN - THE ABSENCE OF THE CRANIUM COULD LEAD TO THE PROTRUSION OF A DISORGANIZED
MASS OF BRAIN TISSUE. THIS RESEMBLES A SHOWER CAP GIVING RISE TO A CHARACTERISTIC TRIANGULAR FACIAL
APPEARANCE.
NEURAL-TUBE DEFECTS CAN BE PREVENTED WITH PRE-CONCEPTIONAL SUPPLEMENTATION OF FOLIC ACID. A DOSE
OF 4 MG DAILY IS RECOMMENDED IN SUBSEQUENT PREGNANCIES.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE DIAGNOSIS FROM THE GIVEN CT SCAN.
questions.explanation:
THE CT SCAN SHOWING BALLOONING OF THE LEFT RENAL PELVIS WITH MODERATE HYDRONEPHROSIS OF THE
AFFECTED KIDNEY INDICATING A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS OF URETEROPELVIC JUNCTION OBSTRUCTION (UPJ)OF THE LEFT
SIDE.
PUJ OBSTRUCTION REFERS TO A BLOCKAGE OR NARROWING AT THE JUNCTION WHERE THE RENAL PELVIS
TRANSITIONS INTO THE URETER, LEADING TO IMPAIRED DRAINAGE OF URINE FROM THE KIDNEY.
INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY IN PATIENTS WITH UPJ OBSTRUCTION INCLUDE:
- ON THE DIURETIC RENOGRAM, UPJO WITH LESS THAN 40% IN THE SPLIT FUNCTION OF THE AFFLICTED KIDNEY.
- RENAL PARENCHYMAL ATROPHY IN THE PRESENCE OF SEVERE BILATERAL UPJO.
- DESPITE PREVENTIVE MEDICINES, RECURRING URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS.
- OBSTRUCTIVE UPJO THAT IS SYMPTOMATIC OR LINKED WITH AN ABDOMINAL MASS
HYDRONEPHROSIS MAY BE DETECTED ON ANTENATAL ULTRASOUND; IT CAN, HOWEVER, BE TRANSIENT OR MILD
AND RESOLVES ON ITS OWN. RE-EVALUATION SHOULD BE DONE AFTER BIRTH AND IN CASES PRESENTING WITH
SYMPTOMS OF RECURRENT UTI, PALPABLE FLANK MASS OR PAIN, URINARY OBSTRUCTION, AND IN CASES OF
FAILURE TO THRIVE.
IF THE HYDRONEPHROSIS IS PERSISTENT, ITS SEVERITY IS GRADED BY THE EXTENT OF THE DILATATION OF THE
PELVICALYCEAL SYSTEM AND PARENCHYMAL THICKNESS. IT NEEDS TO BE ASCERTAINED WHETHER THE OTHER
KIDNEY IS INVOLVED, THE LOWER URETER IS DILATED, THE BLADDER WALL IS THICKENED, AND WHETHER
EMPTYING OF THE BLADDER IS INCOMPLETE. BASED ON THESE FINDINGS, A DIAGNOSIS CAN BE MADE.
IN CASES OF HYDRONEPHROSIS, LONG-STANDING URINE STASIS AND PRESSURE MAY DAMAGE THE KIDNEYS.
THE CAUSES OF UPJ OBSTRUCTION ARE
- INTRINSIC (DUE TO AN ADYNAMIC OR STENOTIC SEGMENT OF THE PROXIMAL URETER) OR
- EXTRINSIC (E.G. COMPRESSION BY ACCESSORY RENAL ARTERIES). THIS NEEDS TO BE CORRECTED PRIMARILY.
THE RENAL ANATOMY AND FUNCTION CAN BE ASSESSED USING RADIOSCINTIGRAPHY STUDIES.
THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR UPJ OBSTRUCTION IS 99MTC-MERCAPTOACETYL-TRIGLYCINE (MAG3)
SCAN. MICTURATING CYSTOURETHROGRAM IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IN VESICOURETERIC REFLUX.
99MTC-DIMERCAPTOSUCCINIC ACID (DMSA) SCAN IS USED FOR ASSESSING RENAL SCARRING.
TREATMENT OF INTRINSIC UPJ OBSTRUCTION IS DONE SURGICALLY IF RENAL FUNCTION IS COMPROMISED OR IF
THERE IS BILATERAL INVOLVEMENT OF THE KIDNEYS. IN OTHER CASES, SERIAL FOLLOW-UP WITH ULTRASONOGRAPHY
IS DONE TO ASSESS THE SPONTANEOUS RESOLUTION OF HYDRONEPHROSIS.
SURGICAL OPTIONS INCLUDE PYELOPLASTY WHICH ENTAILS THE SURGICAL DIVISION OF THE OBSTRUCTION AND THE
CREATION OF A FUNNEL-SHAPED ANASTOMOSIS. ADDITIONALLY, A TEMPORARY STENT AND A DRAIN MAY BE
INSERTED. IT IS NECESSARY TO DO FURTHER SERIAL ULTRASOUNDS AND MAG-3 IMAGING IN ORDER TO ENSURE
PROPER MONITORING AND EVALUATION. THIS PROCEDURE IS NOW COMMONLY BEING PERFORMED VIA
LAPAROSCOPY AND ALSO WITH ROBOTIC ASSISTANCE. CONGENITAL PUJ OBSTRUCTION IS TREATED SURGICALLY BY
ANDERSON HYEN'S PYELOPLASTY.
BELOW ARE CT SCANS OF A LEFT PUJ OBSTRUCTION BEFORE(LEFT) AND AFTER(RIGHT) SURGERY.
4066
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: A RENAL CYST WOULD APPEAR AS A FLUID-FILLED, WELL-DEMARCATED STRUCTURE WITHIN THE KIDNEY
BUT DOES NOT INVOLVE THE PUJ OR CAUSE OBSTRUCTION.
OPTION C: A RENAL TUMOR WOULD PRESENT AS A SOLID, ABNORMAL MASS WITHIN THE KIDNEY, NOT TYPICALLY
INVOLVING THE PUJ UNLESS THERE IS DIRECT EXTENSION.
OPTION D: MULTICYSTIC KIDNEY REFERS TO THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE CYSTS WITHIN THE KIDNEY, OFTEN
CONGENITAL, BUT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THE PUJ AND WOULD NOT RESULT IN OBSTRUCTION AT THE PUJ.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: WHAT DOES THIS IMAGE PRESENTED BELOW INDICATE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN MRCP IMAGE SHOWING SACCULAR DILATATION OF THE COMMON BILE DUCT SUGGESTS A DIAGNOSIS
OF TYPE I CHOLEDOCHAL CYST.
TODANI CLASSIFICATION:
- TYPE I- SACCULAR DILATATION OF THE WHOLE (IA) OR A SEGMENT (IB) OF THE COMMON BILE DUCT (CBD)
- TYPE II- DIVERTICULUM FROM THE CBD
- TYPE III- CHOLEDOCHOCELE THAT OPENS INTO THE DUODENUM
- TYPE IV- MULTIPLE CYSTS (BOTH INTRAHEPATIC AND EXTRAHEPATIC)
- TYPE V- MULTIPLE CYSTS THAT ARE ONLY INTRAHEPATIC (CAROLI'S DISEASE)
THE DIAGNOSIS IS MADE INITIALLY WITH A RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND, FOLLOWING WHICH A
CONFIRMATORY MRCP CAN BE CARRIED OUT TO HELP IN PRE-OPERATIVE PLANNING.
TREATMENT IS USUALLY SURGICAL WITH A ROUX-EN-Y HEPATICOJEJUNOSTOMY WITH RADICAL RESECTION OF ALL
THE BILIARY TISSUE. THERE IS A RISK OF MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION IN LONG-STANDING DISEASE, SO SURGICAL
REMOVAL IS USUALLY RECOMMENDED.
OTHER OPTIONS:
4067
OPTION B: GALL BLADDER CARCINOMA WOULD SHOW ABNORMAL GROWTHS OR MASSES IN THE GALL BLADDER
RATHER THAN CYSTIC DILATIONS OF THE BILE DUCTS.
OPTION C: CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA IS A MALIGNANCY OF THE BILE DUCTS AND WOULD PRESENT AS IRREGULAR
MASSES OR BILE DUCT STRICTURES RATHER THAN CYSTIC STRUCTURES.
OPTION D: CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS REFERS TO THE PRESENCE OF STONES IN THE BILE DUCT, WHICH WOULD
APPEAR AS FILLING DEFECTS WITHIN THE BILE DUCTS RATHER THAN CYSTIC DILATIONS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: SELECT THE CONDITION DISPLAYED IN THE IMAGE:
questions.explanation:
AS THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS, THERE ARE MULTIPLE CALCIFICATIONS WITHIN THE REGION OF THE PANCREAS,
WHICH IS CHARACTERISTIC OF CHRONIC CALCIFIC PANCREATITIS.
THIS CONDITION RESULTS FROM LONG-STANDING INFLAMMATION OF THE PANCREAS, LEADING TO THE DEPOSITION
OF CALCIUM. CHRONIC PANCREATITIS IS OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH ALCOHOL ABUSE, GENETIC FACTORS, OR
RECURRENT ACUTE PANCREATITIS. THE CALCIFICATIONS ARE A HALLMARK FEATURE AND HELP DIFFERENTIATE IT
FROM OTHER ABDOMINAL PATHOLOGIES.
IT PRESENTS WITH SYMPTOMS LIKE CHRONIC ABDOMINAL PAIN WITH A HISTORY OF ALCOHOLISM AND BULKY
STOOLS WHICH INDICATES A LACK OF PANCREATIC LIPASES SEEN IN CHRONIC DISEASE LEADING TO IMPAIRED FAT
DIGESTION AND ABSORPTION.
CHRONIC PANCREATITIS IS A PROGRESSIVE INFLAMMATORY DISEASE IN WHICH THERE IS AN IRREVERSIBLE
DESTRUCTION OF PANCREATIC TISSUE. IT IS MORE COMMON IN MALES, WITH A MALE: FEMALE RATIO OF 4:1.
THE ETIOLOGY OF CHRONIC PANCREATITIS AND PANCREATIC EXOCRINE INSUFFICIENCY CAN BE CLASSIFIED BASED
ON THE TIGAR-O CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM:
- TOXIC-METABOLIC -ALCOHOL, SMOKING, HYPERCALCEMIA, HYPERLIPIDEMIA
- IDIOPATHIC
- GENETIC- PRSS1, CFTR, AND SPINK1 GENES
- AUTOIMMUNE- AUTOIMMUNE CHRONIC PANCREATITIS, IGG4-RELATED DISEASE
- RECURRENT AND SEVERE ACUTE PANCREATITIS
- OBSTRUCTIVE- PANCREAS DIVISUM, DUCT OBSTRUCTION, MALIGNANCY
THE DIAGNOSIS CAN BE MADE USING ROSEMONT CRITERIA. IT IS BASED ON ENDOSCOPIC ULTRASONOGRAPHIC
(EUS) FINDINGS. IT IS EXPLAINED IN THE PEARL ATTACHED BELOW.
ERCP IS THE MOST SENSITIVE RADIOLOGIC TEST FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF CHRONIC PANCREATITIS.

WITH CONDITIONS LIKE ISCHEMIA.
OPTION C: HORSESHOE KIDNEY INVOLVES THE KIDNEYS AND DOES NOT CAUSE PANCREATIC CALCIFICATIONS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt:
A 6-YEAR-OLD CHILD PRESENTED WITH SEIZURES WHICH SUBSIDED WITH INJECTION MIDAZOLAM. BLOOD
INVESTIGATIONS AND LUMBAR PUNCTURE STUDIES WERE NORMAL. MRI IS DONE AND THE IMAGE IS PROVIDED BELOW. SPECIFY THE NEXT BEST INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR FURTHER ASSESSMENT.
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL HISTORY OF A CHILD ALONG WITH AN MRI SHOWING A RING-ENHANCING INTRAAXIAL LESION
OF THE BRAIN COULD LIKELY BE A TUBERCULOMA OR NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS AND MR SPECTROSCOPY WOULD BE
THE NEXT BEST INVESTIGATION FOR FURTHER ASSESSMENT.
MAGNETIC RESONANCE (MR) SPECTROSCOPY IS A NON-INVASIVE TEST BASED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF MAGNETIC
RESONANCE USED TO ANALYSE THE METABOLITE DISTRIBUTION WITHIN THE BRAIN TISSUE. IT CONTAINS N-ACETYL
ASPARTATE (NAA), A NEURONAL VIABILITY SIGNAL; CHOLINE (A COMPONENT OF CELL MEMBRANES AND A
MARKER OF CELLULAR TURNOVER); CREATINE (PRESENT IN METABOLICALLY ACTIVE TISSUES); LIPIDS (RELEASED WITH
CELL MEMBRANE DISRUPTION); AND LACTATE (A HALLMARK OF ANAEROBIC METABOLISM).
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS A NORMAL MR SPECTROSCOPY.

IN TUBERCULOMA, MR SPECTROSCOPY HAS REDUCED NAA OWING TO THE DESTRUCTION OF THE NORMAL BRAIN
PARENCHYMA AND INCREASED LEVELS OF LACTATE OR LIPIDS. IN NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS, THERE IS REDUCED NAA
AND CREATINE AND ELEVATED LACTATE, ALANINE, SUCCINATE, AND CHOLINE LEVELS.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the PRIMARY role of diagnostic imaging in clinical medicine?
options: To replace bedside clinical history taking and physical examination
To supplement clinical evaluation with structural and functional data
To provide the sole decisive basis for all therapeutic surgical steps
To eliminate the requirement for blood tests and histologic confirmation
questions.answer: To supplement clinical evaluation with structural and functional data
questions.explanation: Diagnostic imaging serves as a complement to, not a replacement for, clinical assessment. It provides anatomical and physiological data that, combined with clinical history and physical examination, guides diagnosis and management. A is incorrect because imaging can never replace the clinical encounter; physical signs and history are indispensable. C is incorrect because imaging findings must always be interpreted within the clinical context; isolated imaging findings do not dictate treatment. D is incorrect because imaging and laboratory tests are complementary modalities that address different diagnostic questions.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: A 55-year-old patient presents with chest pain. The clinician orders a chest X-ray. Which role of diagnostic imaging does this BEST illustrate?
options: Screening asymptomatic individuals for latent subclinical lesions
Monitoring long-term cellular response following cytotoxic chemotherapy
Diagnosis and differential diagnosis of symptomatic disease
Formal anatomical staging of pre-diagnosed solid visceral malignancies
questions.answer: Diagnosis and differential diagnosis of symptomatic disease
questions.explanation: In a symptomatic patient presenting with chest pain, ordering a chest X-ray is aimed at establishing a diagnosis or narrowing the differential (e.g., pneumothorax, heart failure, pneumonia, aortic dissection). A is incorrect because screening applies to asymptomatic populations to detect pre-clinical disease. B is incorrect because the patient has not yet been diagnosed or treated, so monitoring is not applicable. D is incorrect because staging is performed when malignancy has already been confirmed, not at initial presentation of chest pain.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Interventional radiology differs from diagnostic radiology primarily in that it:
options: Relies exclusively on high-frequency superficial ultrasound guidance
Provides therapeutic procedures in addition to diagnosis
Is performed exclusively by non-radiologist surgical subspecialists
Restricts all interventions to non-vascular visceral hollow organs
questions.answer: Provides therapeutic procedures in addition to diagnosis
questions.explanation: Interventional radiology uses imaging guidance to perform minimally invasive therapeutic procedures such as angioplasty, embolization, biopsy, and drainage, in addition to providing diagnostic information. A is incorrect because interventional radiology uses a wide range of guidance modalities including fluoroscopy, CT, and ultrasound. C is incorrect because interventional radiology is a recognized subspecialty performed by trained radiologists. D is incorrect because interventional radiology addresses a broad spectrum of conditions beyond vascular pathology, including tumor ablation, biliary drainage, and musculoskeletal procedures.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: A 40-year-old woman with a known breast lump undergoes mammography to assess size, margin characteristics, and lymph node involvement prior to surgery. This represents which role of imaging?
questions.explanation: When a malignancy is already suspected or confirmed, imaging to determine the extent of disease (local invasion, nodal involvement, distant metastases) constitutes staging. This information directly influences surgical planning and treatment decisions. A is incorrect because the lump is already known; screening applies to asymptomatic individuals. B is incorrect because diagnosis would refer to identifying what the lesion is, but here the clinical concern is its extent. D is incorrect because follow-up/monitoring occurs after treatment has been initiated.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Which of the following BEST describes the use of imaging in the context of disease surveillance?
options: Whole-body trauma CT pan-scan identifying occult parenchymal lacerations
Serial chest radiographs in lung cancer patients assessing chemotherapy response
Contrast-enhanced brain MRI evaluating acute stroke within therapeutic window
Real-time ultrasound guidance for core needle biopsy of suspected thyroid nodules
questions.answer: Serial chest radiographs in lung cancer patients assessing chemotherapy response
questions.explanation: Surveillance or monitoring refers to repeated imaging over time to assess how a known disease responds to treatment or evolves. Serial chest X-rays in a chemotherapy patient track tumor shrinkage or progression, representing treatment monitoring. A is incorrect because imaging in acute trauma is diagnostic, aimed at identifying injuries not previously known. C is incorrect because MRI for new-onset back pain is diagnostic workup, not surveillance. D is incorrect because ultrasound-guided biopsy is an interventional procedure, not surveillance imaging.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Which of the following represents an ABSOLUTE limitation of plain X-ray radiography?
options: Total inability to demonstrate macroscopic radiopaque soft tissue calcification
Poor soft tissue contrast resolution compared with CT
Inability to delineate cortical bone fractures or periosteal reactions
Mandatory requirement for intravenous iodinated contrast in all projections
questions.answer: Poor soft tissue contrast resolution compared with CT
questions.explanation: Plain X-ray has limited soft tissue contrast resolution, making it difficult to differentiate between adjacent soft tissue structures of similar density. This is a fundamental physical limitation. A is incorrect because plain X-ray can demonstrate calcifications, which appear as high-density (white) areas within soft tissues. C is incorrect because X-ray is excellent for imaging bone due to the high density of calcium. D is incorrect because most plain X-rays are performed without contrast; only some specialized studies (e.g., contrast enema) require contrast.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: A patient with acute renal colic is referred for imaging. Which of the following is a recognized INDICATION for non-contrast CT of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder (KUB CT) over plain KUB radiography?
options: CT exposes the patient to significantly lower radiation than plain films
CT detects radiolucent calculi missed on plain radiography
CT is completely free of any ionizing electromagnetic radiation
CT requires overnight bowel preparation with oral polyethylene glycol
questions.answer: CT detects radiolucent calculi missed on plain radiography
questions.explanation: Non-contrast CT (NCCT) of the abdomen and pelvis is the gold standard for suspected renal colic because it detects all types of calculi, including radiolucent uric acid stones that are invisible on plain KUB X-ray. This significantly increases diagnostic yield. A is incorrect because CT is generally more expensive and takes more time/resources than plain X-ray. C is incorrect because CT uses ionizing radiation; MRI is the non-ionizing cross-sectional modality. D is incorrect because plain X-ray similarly requires no significant preparation; this is not a distinguishing advantage of CT.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a CONTRAINDICATION to MRI?
options: Documented severe allergy to iodinated contrast
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic (older generation) cerebral aneurysm clips are an absolute contraindication to MRI because the strong magnetic field can cause clip displacement, leading to catastrophic hemorrhage. Modern titanium clips are MRI-compatible, but the type must be confirmed before scanning. A is incorrect because MRI (without gadolinium) is considered relatively safe in the second and third trimesters; the first trimester is more cautious but not absolutely contraindicated in urgent cases. B is incorrect because iodinated contrast is used in CT, not MRI; gadolinium-based contrast agents are used in MRI and have their own separate allergy/contraindication profile. D is incorrect because claustrophobia managed with sedation or anxiolytics is not a contraindication; open MRI systems are also available.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a LIMITATION of ultrasound compared to CT?
options: Inability to detect real-time directional vascular blood flow
Significant generation of mutagenic ionizing radiation dose
Poor acoustic penetration through bone and luminal gas
Total inability to distinguish simple fluid from solid tissue
questions.answer: Poor acoustic penetration through bone and luminal gas
questions.explanation: Ultrasound waves are reflected at interfaces with large acoustic impedance differences, such as air-soft tissue or bone-soft tissue interfaces. This severely limits visualization of structures behind bowel gas (e.g., pancreas) or within the skull and thorax. A is incorrect because the gallbladder is one of the organs best visualized by ultrasound, and US is the first-line modality for suspected gallstones. B is incorrect because ultrasound does not use ionizing radiation; it uses high-frequency sound waves, making it particularly safe in pregnancy. D is incorrect because Doppler ultrasound is widely used to assess blood flow velocity and direction in vessels.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.prompt: A 30-year-old pregnant woman at 28 weeks gestation presents with right upper quadrant pain. Which imaging modality is MOST appropriate as the FIRST-LINE investigation?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is the first-line imaging modality in pregnancy due to its lack of ionizing radiation, real-time capability, and excellent ability to evaluate the hepatobiliary system (liver, gallbladder, bile ducts) and right upper quadrant pathology such as cholelithiasis and cholecystitis. A is incorrect because CT uses ionizing radiation, which should be avoided in pregnancy when alternative, equally informative modalities are available. B is incorrect because while MRI is safe in the second/third trimester and used as second-line when US is inconclusive, it is not the first-line choice.
